Part 1: Spring Boot ki neev

1. Web basics: client, server aur HTTP

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Shuruaat: Spring Boot seekhne se pehle ek simple sawaal: jab tum browser mein URL daalte ho, tab actually hota kya hai? Poora backend development isi ek baat par khada hai: koi request bhejta hai, koi jawab deta hai. Wahin se shuru karte hain.
📖 Notes

Problem: do log baat kaise karein?

Socho tum ek restaurant mein ho. Tum (customer) waiter ko order dete ho, kitchen khana banati hai, aur waiter plate wapas laata hai. Tum kitchen mein ghuste nahi, bas ek request dete ho aur response lete ho.

Web mein bhi bilkul yahi hota hai. Ek side client hai jo kuch maangta hai, doosri side server hai jo kaam karke jawab deta hai. Dono ke beech ek common bhasha chahiye, warna koi kisi ki baat nahi samjhega. Wo bhasha hai HTTP.

Client aur Server kaun hain?

  • Client = jo request bhejta hai: Chrome, mobile app, React/Angular frontend, Postman, cURL.
  • Microservices mein ek service bhi client ban jaati hai: OrderService jab PaymentService ko call kare, tab OrderService client hai.
  • Server = jahan backend code deploy hai (jaise Tomcat par chalti Spring Boot app). Ye port par request sunta hai.
  • Server ke kaam: authenticate/authorize karna, business logic chalana, database CRUD, aur sahi HTTP response banana.

HTTP methods: kya karna hai, ye method batata hai

MethodKaamExample
GETData padhnaGET /users/5
POSTNaya resource bananaPOST /users
PUTPoora resource replace karnaPUT /users/5
PATCHSirf kuch fields updatePATCH /users/5
DELETEResource hatanaDELETE /users/5
Yaad rakhoGET, PUT aur DELETE idempotent hain: same request 10 baar bhejo, final state same. POST idempotent nahi hai: 10 baar bhejoge to 10 users ban sakte hain.

HTTP request aur response ke parts

  • Request ke 4 parts: method, URL, headers, aur optional body.
  • Response ke 3 parts: status code, headers, body.
  • Headers = extra jaankari, jaise Content-Type: application/json ya Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • GET request mein usually body nahi hoti; data URL/query params mein jaata hai.
POST https://www.codearmy.in/login
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{ "email": "student@codearmy.in", "password": "secret" }

--- response ---
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{ "status": "success", "message": "Login Successful!" }

Status codes: result ek number mein

RangeMatlabCommon
2xxSuccess200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content
3xxRedirect301, 302
4xxClient ki galti400 Bad Request, 401, 403, 404 Not Found
5xxServer ki galti500 Internal Server Error, 503
Common galti401 = 'tum kaun ho, pata nahi' (login/token nahi). 403 = 'pehchaan liya, par ijazat nahi'. Dono ko mix mat karo.

HTTP vs HTTPS

HTTP data ko plain text mein bhejta hai, beech mein koi bhi padh sakta hai. HTTPS wahi HTTP hai, par SSL/TLS se encrypt hokar jaata hai. Password, token jaisi cheezein hamesha HTTPS par.

IP address aur port: ghar ka pata aur flat number

IP address device ko pehchanta hai (ghar ka pata). Port us device par chal rahi application ko pehchanta hai (flat number). 127.0.0.1 ya localhost matlab tumhari apni machine.

Default ports: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443. Spring Boot by default 8080 par chalti hai.

Real duniya mein: reverse proxy

Browser (https, port 443)→Nginx (reverse proxy)→Spring Boot app (localhost:8080)
Real examplePublic internet se traffic 443 par Nginx leta hai, TLS wahan khatam hota hai, aur Nginx andar ki taraf request ko Spring Boot ke 8080 par forward kar deta hai. App ko public port expose nahi karna padta.

Ek request ka poora safar

  1. Browser https://shop.com/users/5 resolve karta hai (DNS se IP milta hai).
  2. IP + port 443 par connection banta hai, TLS handshake hota hai.
  3. HTTP request jaati hai: GET /users/5 + headers.
  4. Server logic chalata hai, DB se user laata hai.
  5. Response aata hai: 200 OK + JSON body. Browser/app use dikhata hai.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Client request bhejta hai, server response deta hai; bhasha HTTP hai.
  • GET padhna, POST banana, PUT poora replace, PATCH partial, DELETE hatana.
  • Request = method + URL + headers + body; response = status + headers + body.
  • 2xx success, 4xx client galti, 5xx server galti; 401 vs 403 alag hai.
  • HTTPS = HTTP + TLS encryption.
  • IP = device, port = app; Boot default 8080, Nginx 443 se forward karta hai.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q1

What is client-server architecture?

Main Definition

  • In client-server architecture, a client (browser, mobile app, Postman, or even another service) sends an HTTP request, and a server that listens for requests runs the business logic, talks to the database, and returns an HTTP response.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Client वो है जो request भेजता है (browser, mobile app, Postman) और server वो है जो उसे process करके response देता है।
  • Restaurant की तरह: customer order देता है, kitchen खाना बनाकर वापस भेजती है।
  • दोनों HTTP protocol पर बात करते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Client examples: Chrome, mobile app, React ya Angular frontend, Postman, cURL.
  • Microservices mein ek service doosri ko call kare to wo bhi client ban jaati hai (OrderService, PaymentService ko call karta hai).
  • Server ke kaam: authenticate aur authorize, database CRUD, business logic, sahi HTTP response banana.
ReferenceMDN: HTTP overview
Q2

What are the HTTP methods, and what is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?

Main Definition

  • GET reads data, POST creates a resource, PUT replaces a whole resource, PATCH updates only some fields, and DELETE removes a resource.
  • HTTP sends data in plain text, while HTTPS encrypts it in transit using SSL/TLS.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • GET data पढ़ता है, POST नया data बनाता है, PUT पूरा replace करता है, PATCH थोड़ा सा update करता है और DELETE हटाता है।
  • HTTPS असल में HTTP ही है, बस TLS से encrypted, ताकि बीच में कोई data पढ़ न सके।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
MethodKaamExample
GETData lao (state nahi badalta)Courses ki list
POSTNaya resource banaoSignup, order submit
PUTPoora resource replacePoora profile update
PATCHKuch fields updateSirf phone number badlo
DELETEResource hataoAccount delete
Extra (mera note)PUT aur DELETE idempotent hote hain: same request baar baar bhejo to final state same rehti hai. POST idempotent nahi hota.
ReferenceMDN: HTTP overview
Q3

What are the parts of an HTTP request and response, and what are the common status codes?

Main Definition

  • An HTTP request has four parts: method, URL, headers and an optional body.
  • An HTTP response has three: a status code, headers and a body.
  • Status codes show the outcome: 2xx success, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Request में method, URL, headers और optional body होती है।
  • Response में status code, headers और body आती है।
  • 2xx मतलब success, 4xx मतलब client की गलती, 5xx मतलब server की गलती।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)

200 OKSab theek

400 Bad RequestClient ka input ya syntax galat
401 / 403Authentication ya permission fail
404 Not FoundEndpoint ya resource nahi mila

POST https://www.codearmy.in/login
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{ "email": "student@codearmy.in", "password": "secret" }

{ "status": "success", "message": "Login Successful!" }
Extra (mera note)401 ka matlab hai 'tum kaun ho, pata nahi' (login nahi hua), 403 ka matlab hai 'tum ho to pehchane, par ijazat nahi'. GET request mein usually body nahi hoti.
ReferenceMDN: HTTP status codesMDN: HTTP overview
Q4

What is the difference between an IP address and a port? What is a reverse proxy?

Main Definition

  • An IP address identifies a device on a network (127.0.0.1 or localhost is the machine itself), and a port identifies the application on that device.
  • HTTP uses port 80 and HTTPS uses 443.
  • A reverse proxy like Nginx receives public traffic on 443 and forwards it internally to the app, for example Spring Boot on 8080.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • IP address बताता है कौन सी machine है, port बताता है उस machine पर कौन सा app है।
  • Building का address IP है और flat number port।
  • Reverse proxy (जैसे Nginx) सबसे आगे खड़ा होकर requests को सही backend server तक भेजता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
CheezKya pehchanta haiExample
IP addressDevice127.0.0.1 (localhost)
PortDevice par app8080 (Boot default)
Port 80HTTP traffichttp://site.com
Port 443HTTPS traffichttps://site.com

2. Java web ka safar: Servlets aur Tomcat

9 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein humne dekha ki client HTTP request bhejta hai aur server port par sunkar response deta hai. Ab sawaal ye hai ki Java mein wo server banta kaise hai? Aur Spring Boot ke zamane mein bhi Servlets kyun seekhne chahiye? Kyunki poora Spring web (Spring MVC, Boot web) Servlets ke upar hi bana hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: sirf java.net se web app banao to?

Java ke java.net package mein ServerSocket aur Socket hote hain jo localhost:8080 jaise port ko sun sakte hain. To kya isse web app ban jayegi? Banegi, par rula degi.

Socho tumhe bas ek /hello API chahiye. Socket ko jo milta hai wo sirf bytes ka stream hai. Usse ye bhi nahi pata ki ye HTTP hai, GET hai ya POST.

ServerSocket server = new ServerSocket(8080);
Socket socket = server.accept();   // raw connection mila
// ab bytes khud padho, "GET /hello HTTP/1.1" string khud todo...

Raw java.net ki 6 problems

  1. Raw stream of bytes: request bas text/bytes hai, HTTP verbs ya endpoints ka koi concept nahi.
  2. Manual parsing: method (GET/POST), URL (/hello), headers aur body string parsing se khud nikalo.
  3. Manual routing: kaunsa URL kaunsa Java method chalayega, iske liye lambe ganda if-else.
  4. Manual response formatting: status line (200, 404), headers aur body khud string mein banao.
  5. Manual multithreading: ek se zyada users ke liye thread pool khud likho, warna ek time par ek hi user.
  6. Result: business logic likhne se pehle hi 13+ server wale steps manually.

Solution: server ko do hisson mein baanto

Idea simple tha: jo kaam har app mein same hai (port sunna, HTTP parse, threads) wo ek baar likh do aur ek alag program ko de do. Wo program hai Servlet Container jaise Apache Tomcat (Jetty, Undertow bhi).

Aur jo kaam har app ka alag hai (business logic) wo ek chhoti Java class mein likho: Servlet.

  • Tomcat = ek long running Java process jo OS par port 8080 lagatar sunta hai, HTTP parse karta hai, threads manage karta hai aur HttpServletRequest/HttpServletResponse objects banata hai.
  • Servlet = special Java class jisme business logic hai. Iska object tum new se nahi banate, Tomcat banata aur manage karta hai.
Yaad rakhoAnalogy: jaise Spring ka IoC container beans ko manage karta hai, waise hi Tomcat servlets ko manage karta hai. Ye analogy Part 2 (DI/IoC) mein kaam aayegi.

Tomcat ke andar ek request ka safar

  1. Request aati hai: GET http://localhost:8080/hello.
  2. Tomcat use parse karke HttpServletRequest object banata hai aur usme method, URL, headers, params bhar deta hai.
  3. Tomcat ek khaali HttpServletResponse object bhi banata hai.
  4. URL mapping se sahi servlet (jaise HelloServlet) chunta hai aur dono objects use pass karta hai.
  5. Servlet getters (getParameter, getHeader) se data padhta hai, logic chalata hai, aur setters (setStatus, getWriter().write) se response bharta hai.
  6. Tomcat bhara hua response client ko bhej deta hai.

Servlet code: UserServlet

Servlet HttpServlet abstract class ko extend karta hai aur @WebServlet se URL par map hota hai. Dhyan do: endpoint class-level hai. Ek hi servlet /users ke GET, POST, PUT, DELETE sab sambhalta hai, doGet/doPost/doPut/doDelete override karke. Spring Boot jaise method-level mapping yahan nahi hai.

import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;
import jakarta.servlet.annotation.WebServlet;
import jakarta.servlet.http.*;
import java.io.IOException;

@WebServlet("/users")              // class-level URL
public class UserServlet extends HttpServlet {

    @Override
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
            throws ServletException, IOException {
        // Input padho (Tomcat ne request object bhar ke diya)
        String id = request.getParameter("id");
        String name = request.getParameter("name");

        // Response khud haath se banao
        response.setStatus(201);
        response.setContentType("application/json");
        response.getWriter().write("{\"message\": \"User Added Successfully\"}");
    }

    @Override
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
            throws ServletException, IOException {
        // GET /users yahan handle karo
    }
}

Servlet lifecycle: Tomcat kab kya call karta hai

Constructor (lazy, pehli request par)→init(ServletConfig) - ek baar→service(req, res) - har request→doGet / doPost / ...→destroy() - ek baar
MethodKitni baarKis kaam kaSpring mein jaisa
Constructor1 baarObject banana (default lazy)Bean constructor
init(ServletConfig)1 baarHeavy setup, resources load@PostConstruct
service(req, res)Har requestVerb check karke doGet/doPost... ko dispatch-
destroy()1 baarShutdown/undeploy par cleanup@PreDestroy
Dhyan doBy default Tomcat servlet object pehli request par banata hai (lazy). Chaho to @WebServlet(urlPatterns="/users", loadOnStartup=1) se startup par hi bana sakte ho. Aur ek servlet ka ek hi object hota hai jo saari threads share karti hain, isliye servlet mein mutable instance fields mat rakho.

WAR file aur External Tomcat (purana tareeka)

  • Pehle Tomcat alag se download karke chalana padta tha (External Tomcat).
  • WAR (Web Application Archive) = compiled .class files, servlet classes, web.xml ya annotation config, aur static files (HTML, CSS) ka bundle.
  • WAR ko Tomcat ke webapps/ folder mein copy karo, Tomcat use khud unzip karke deploy kar deta hai.
  1. pom.xml mein <packaging>war</packaging>.
  2. mvn package se .war banao.
  3. webapps/ mein copy karo.
  4. Har change par yahi dobara (aur aksar restart).

pom.xml aur provided scope

  • provided matlab: library sirf compile ke liye Maven ko chahiye.
  • Final WAR mein ye JAR bundle nahi hoti, kyunki Tomcat runtime par apni servlet library khud deta hai.
  • Bundle kar di to Tomcat ki library aur WAR wali library takra sakti hain (class loading / resolution errors).
<!-- 1. Packaging WAR -->
<packaging>war</packaging>

<dependencies>
    <!-- 2. Jakarta Servlet API -->
    <dependency>
        <groupId>jakarta.servlet</groupId>
        <artifactId>jakarta.servlet-api</artifactId>
        <version>6.0.0</version>          <!-- Boot 3 / Tomcat 10.1 = Servlet 6.0 -->
        <scope>provided</scope>           <!-- bahut important -->
    </dependency>
</dependencies>
Dhyan doVideo notes mein 6.1.0 hai. Servlet 6.1 Tomcat 11 / Spring Boot 4 wala hai. Spring Boot 3 Tomcat 10.1 use karta hai jo Servlet 6.0 (jakarta) hai. Package jakarta.servlet.* hai, purana javax.servlet.* Boot 3 mein nahi chalega.

Embedded Tomcat (Spring Boot tareeka)

External TomcatEmbedded Tomcat (Boot)
Tomcat kahanAlag installApp JAR ke andar (spring-boot-starter-web)
PackageWARExecutable fat JAR
Deploywebapps/ mein copyjava -jar app.jar
Servlet APIprovided (Tomcat deta)Starter ke saath aati hai

Raw Servlets ki kamiyaan

  • Tight coupling: servlet ke andar new UserService() khud banana padta hai.
  • Manual JSON: JSON padhna/likhna string concatenation se, ganda aur error-prone.
  • Manual response building: har method mein setStatus, setContentType, getWriter().write.
  • Manual WAR deployment: har change par package, copy, restart.
  • Bahut saare servlets ho to logging, validation, routing, response writing har jagah repeat.

Agla kadam: DispatcherServlet (Front Controller)

Spring MVC ne kaha: hazaar servlets mat banao. Ek central servlet rakho, DispatcherServlet. Tomcat saari requests pehle isko deta hai. Ye routing, JSON mapping (Jackson), common kaam khud sambhalta hai aur request ko halke controller beans tak bhejta hai. Aur new UserService() ki jagah Spring DI se dependency de deta hai.

Client→Tomcat→DispatcherServlet→@RestController method→JSON response

Poora evolution ek nazar mein

EraKya diyaDard kya bacha
java.net socketsPort sun sakte hoParsing, routing, threads sab manual
Servlets + Tomcat (1997)Container ne ports, threads, HTTP parsing le liyaTight coupling, manual JSON, WAR deploy, bahut config
Spring (IoC/DI, MVC)Loose coupling, DispatcherServletBahut saari XML/Java configuration
Spring BootStarters, auto-configuration, embedded server-
Yaad rakhoSpring Boot Spring ko replace nahi karta. Wo Spring ke modules ki configuration automate karta hai.

Spring ecosystem aur data stack

  • Spring Core: IoC, DI, beans. Baaki sab ki neev.
  • Upar: Spring MVC (web/REST), Spring Data (DB), Spring Security (auth), Spring AOP (logging, @Transactional).
  • Spring Boot: starters + auto-configuration + embedded server + application.properties + Actuator.
  • Database tak ka raasta: Spring Data JPA → Hibernate (JPA/ORM) → JDBC → DB driver → MySQL/PostgreSQL. Detail Part 5 (JPA) mein.
Common galtiProduction mein spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update/create mat rakho. validate rakho aur schema Flyway/Liquibase se manage karo.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • java.net sirf bytes deta hai: parsing, routing, response, threads sab manual.
  • Tomcat = Servlet Container (port, HTTP parse, threads); Servlet = business logic class.
  • Tomcat request se HttpServletRequest + khaali HttpServletResponse banakar servlet ko deta hai.
  • Lifecycle: constructor (lazy) → init() 1 baar → service() har request → destroy() 1 baar.
  • WAR + external Tomcat ke webapps/; servlet-api provided scope mein (Boot 3 = Servlet 6.0, jakarta).
  • Raw servlet ka dard → Spring MVC ka DispatcherServlet (Front Controller) + DI.
  • Boot Spring ko replace nahi karta, configure karta hai.

✅ Review questions (9): ab khud check karo

Q5

Why learn Servlets in the Spring Boot era, and why is a raw java.net server so hard?

Main Definition

  • The whole Spring web stack (Spring MVC and Spring Boot web) is built on top of Servlet technology, so servlets explain what happens under the hood.
  • A client sends an HTTP request and the server returns an HTTP response.
  • With only java.net (ServerSocket, Socket) you receive a raw stream of bytes and must parse, route, format and multithread everything yourself.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Spring Boot ki पूरी web building servlets की नींव पर खड़ी है, इसलिए पहले servlet समझना ज़रूरी है।
  • सिर्फ़ java.net से server बनाओ तो request बस bytes की string आती है, GET-POST, URL, headers सब खुद parse करने पड़ते हैं।
  • ये ऐसा है जैसे restaurant में waiter, cook, cashier सब काम अकेले करना।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Raw java.net server ki 6 problems
  1. Raw stream of bytes: request sirf text/bytes hai, HTTP verbs ya endpoints ka koi concept nahi.
  2. Manual parsing: method (GET/POST), URL (/hello), headers aur body khud string parsing se nikalo.
  3. Manual routing: kaunsa URL kaunsa Java method chalayega, iske liye lambe if-else.
  4. Manual response formatting: status line (200, 404), headers aur body khud string mein banao.
  5. Manual multithreading: ek se zyada users ke liye thread pool khud likho, warna ek time par ek hi user.
  6. Result: business logic likhne se pehle hi 13+ server-oriented steps.
Isliye server do hisson mein bata

Low-level kaam (port sunna, HTTP parse, threads) Servlet Container (Tomcat) ko diya gaya, aur business logic Servlet class ko. Yahi split aage chalkar Spring MVC ka base bana. Dekho Q7.

  • Client = browser, mobile app, Postman ya doosra service
  • Server = jahan backend deploy hai (Tomcat)
  • java.net socket HTTP nahi samajhta, sirf bytes
  • Business logic se pehle 13+ server-wale steps manually
Q6

How did Java web development evolve: java.net, Servlets, Spring, Spring Boot? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • First, raw java.net (ServerSocket) forced developers to parse bytes and manage threads manually.
  • Servlets and Servlet containers like Tomcat (1997) took over ports, thread pools and HTTP parsing.
  • Spring added IoC and DI for loose coupling, and Spring Boot added auto-configuration and starters to remove boilerplate.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पहले java.net से हर byte खुद parse करना पड़ता था, फिर Servlets और Tomcat ने ये low-level काम संभाल लिया।
  • Spring ने DI और DispatcherServlet दिया, और Spring Boot ने auto-configuration और embedded Tomcat देकर setup लगभग zero कर दिया।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Story: java.net se Spring Boot tak

Socho tumhe ek simple /hello API banana hai. java.net ke saath tum ServerSocket khol kar port 8080 sunte ho, par jo aata hai woh sirf bytes ka stream hai. Method, URL, headers sab string parsing se nikalne padte hain.

Har naya feature (routing, response format, threads) tumhe khud likhna padta. Business logic shuru karne se pehle hi bahut saara server code.

java.net ki problems
  • Raw bytes: request ek string/byte stream hai, koi object nahi.
  • Manual parsing: GET/POST, URL, headers, body khud nikalo.
  • Manual routing: kaunsa URL kaunsa method chalayega, lambi if-else.
  • Manual response: status line, headers, body sab khud format karo.
  • Manual threads: har user ke liye thread pool khud banao.
Har stage ne kya solve kiya
StageKya milaKya baaki raha
java.netSocket level controlSab kuch manual
Servlet + TomcatParsing, threads, HttpServletRequest/Responsenew se tight coupling, manual JSON, WAR deploy
Spring MVCDI, DispatcherServlet, @RequestMapping, JSON conversionBahut saari XML/Java config
Spring BootAuto-configuration, starters, embedded Tomcat, fat JARBas business code likho
Servlet lifecycle (Tomcat chalata hai)
  1. Pehli request par Tomcat servlet object banata hai (default lazy).
  2. init(ServletConfig) ek baar chalta hai.
  3. Har request par service() chalta hai, jo HTTP method dekh kar doGet() / doPost() ko bhejta hai.
  4. Shutdown ya undeploy par destroy() ek baar chalta hai.
Raw servlet ka sample
@WebServlet("/users")
public class UserServlet extends HttpServlet {
    @Override
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res) throws IOException {
        String name = req.getParameter("name");
        res.setStatus(201);
        res.setContentType("application/json");
        res.getWriter().write("{\"message\":\"User added\"}");
    }
}
DispatcherServlet ka idea

Bahut saare servlets mein logging, validation, JSON writing baar baar likhna padta tha. Spring MVC ne ek central servlet diya (Front Controller pattern): Tomcat har request DispatcherServlet ko deta hai, aur woh sahi @Controller method tak route karta hai.

Yaad rakhoSpring Boot mein bhi andar Servlet aur Tomcat hi chal rahe hain. Boot ne bas unhe chhupa diya hai.
  • java.net: JVM ko HTTP ya URL ka idea nahi, sirf bytes. Parsing, routing, response format aur multithreading sab manual.
  • Servlet container (Tomcat, Jetty, Undertow): request ko HttpServletRequest banata hai aur sahi Servlet tak bhejta hai.
  • Plain Servlets ka dard: hazaaron servlets, mapping config aur tight coupling, testing mushkil.
  • Spring Boot Spring ko replace nahi karta, Spring ke modules ki configuration automate karta hai.
ServerSocket server = new ServerSocket(8080);
Socket socket = server.accept();   // raw connection, ab bytes tum padho

Q7

What is a Servlet and what is a Servlet Container (Tomcat)? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A Servlet Container such as Apache Tomcat is a long-running Java process that listens on a port (8080), parses HTTP, manages threads and builds request/response objects.
  • A Servlet is a special Java class that holds the business logic for a URL.
  • The container creates and manages servlet instances and their lifecycle, just like the Spring IoC container manages beans.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Tomcat एक हमेशा चलने वाला Java process है जो port 8080 पर request सुनता है और HTTP parsing, threads सब संभालता है।
  • Servlet एक special class है जिसमें सिर्फ़ business logic होता है, उसका object हम new से नहीं बनाते।
  • जैसे IoC container beans संभालता है, वैसे ही Tomcat servlets संभालता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Tomcat ke andar ek request ka safar
  1. Request aati hai, jaise GET http://localhost:8080/hello.
  2. Tomcat use parse karke HttpServletRequest object banata hai aur usme method, URL, headers, params bhar deta hai.
  3. Tomcat ek khaali HttpServletResponse object bhi banata hai.
  4. URL mapping se sahi servlet (jaise HelloServlet) chunta hai aur dono objects use pass karta hai.
  5. Servlet getter methods (getParameter, getHeader) se data padhta hai, logic chalata hai, aur setter methods (setStatus, getWriter().write) se response bharta hai.
  6. Tomcat bhara hua response client ko bhej deta hai.
  • Tomcat = Servlet Container
  • Servlet object Tomcat banata aur manage karta hai
  • Analogy: IoC container ↔ beans, Tomcat ↔ servlets

Q8

What is the difference between embedded and external Tomcat, what is a WAR file, and why is the servlet API scope 'provided'?

Main Definition

  • In Spring Boot, embedded Tomcat ships inside the application JAR through spring-boot-starter-web.
  • Earlier, an external Tomcat was installed separately and a WAR (Web Application Archive) containing compiled classes, servlets, web.xml/annotations and static files was copied into its webapps/ folder.
  • The jakarta.servlet-api dependency uses <scope>provided</scope> because Tomcat supplies that library at runtime.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पहले Tomcat अलग से download करके उसके webapps folder में WAR file डालनी पड़ती थी, Tomcat उसे खुद unzip करके चलाता था।
  • Spring Boot में Tomcat app की JAR के अंदर ही embedded आता है।
  • provided scope का मतलब है ये library सिर्फ़ compile के लिए चाहिए, WAR में pack नहीं होगी क्योंकि Tomcat के पास अपनी copy है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • WAR = classes + servlets + web.xml + HTML/CSS ka bundle
  • External Tomcat: webapps/ mein deploy, auto unzip
  • provided: compile time haan, WAR mein nahi
  • Bundle kar diya to Tomcat ki library se conflict
<!-- pom.xml -->
<packaging>war</packaging>

<dependencies>
    <dependency>
        <groupId>jakarta.servlet</groupId>
        <artifactId>jakarta.servlet-api</artifactId>
        <version>6.1.0</version>
        <scope>provided</scope> <!-- Tomcat runtime par deta hai -->
    </dependency>
</dependencies>
Dhyan doAgar servlet-api WAR ke andar bhi chala gaya to Tomcat ki apni servlet library aur WAR wali library takra sakti hain (class loading / resolution errors).
Q9

How do you write a plain Servlet, and how are its endpoints defined?

Main Definition

  • A servlet class extends the abstract class HttpServlet and is mapped to a URL with @WebServlet("/users").
  • Endpoints in servlets are class-level: one servlet handles GET, POST, PUT and DELETE for that path by overriding doGet, doPost, doPut and doDelete.
  • The servlet reads input from HttpServletRequest and writes status, content type and body to HttpServletResponse by hand.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Servlet class HttpServlet को extend करती है और @WebServlet से उसका URL तय होता है।
  • Spring की तरह method-level mapping नहीं होती, एक servlet उस path के सारे GET, POST, PUT, DELETE संभालता है।
  • Response का status, content type और body सब हाथ से लिखना पड़ता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • @WebServlet("/users") = class-level URL
  • doGet / doPost / doPut / doDelete override
  • request.getParameter() se input
  • response.setStatus + getWriter().write se output
@WebServlet("/users")
public class UserServlet extends HttpServlet {

    @Override
    protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
            throws ServletException, IOException {
        String id = request.getParameter("id");
        String name = request.getParameter("name");

        response.setStatus(201);
        response.setContentType("application/json");
        response.getWriter().write("{\"message\": \"User Added Successfully\"}");
    }

    @Override
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
            throws ServletException, IOException {
        // GET /users handle karo
    }
}
Q10

What is the Servlet lifecycle (init, service, destroy)?

Main Definition

  • Tomcat creates the servlet object lazily, on the first request by default, by calling its constructor.
  • init(ServletConfig) runs once after creation for heavy setup, like @PostConstruct.
  • service(req, res) runs on every request, checks the HTTP verb and dispatches to doGet, doPost and so on.
  • destroy() runs once on shutdown or undeploy for cleanup, like @PreDestroy.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पहली request आने पर Tomcat servlet का object बनाता है और init() एक बार चलता है।
  • उसके बाद हर request पर service() चलता है जो देखता है GET है या POST और सही doXxx method बुला देता है।
  • Server बंद होने पर destroy() एक बार चलता है ताकि resources close हो जाएं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Constructor (lazy)→init() x1→service() har request→doGet/doPost→destroy() x1
MethodKab chaltaSpring mein jaisa
init(ServletConfig)Object banne ke baad ek baar@PostConstruct
service(req, res)Har incoming requestDispatcherServlet ka request handling
destroy()Shutdown / undeploy par ek baar@PreDestroy
  • Constructor: lazy, pehli request par
  • init(): ek baar (heavy resource load)
  • service(): har request, verb dekh kar dispatch
  • destroy(): ek baar, cleanup
Q11

What are the limitations of raw Servlets, and how does Spring MVC solve them?

Main Definition

  • Raw servlets cause tight coupling (new UserService() inside the servlet), manual JSON handling, manual response building in every method, and slow manual WAR deployment.
  • With many servlets, logging, validation, routing and response writing get repeated everywhere.
  • Spring MVC introduces one central servlet, the DispatcherServlet (Front Controller pattern), which handles the common work and forwards requests to light controller beans.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • हर servlet में service का object new से बनाना, JSON हाथ से बनाना और हर बार setStatus लिखना बहुत repetitive है।
  • ऊपर से हर change पर WAR बनाकर Tomcat में copy करके restart करना पड़ता था।
  • Spring MVC ने एक ही central DispatcherServlet दिया जो ये common काम संभालता है और request सही controller तक पहुंचाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Tight coupling: new UserService()
  • JSON string concatenation
  • Har method mein setStatus/setContentType/write
  • Har change par WAR copy + restart
  • Fix: DispatcherServlet + controllers + DI
Q12

What is the difference between Spring and Spring Boot? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Spring Framework provides the core programming model: IoC container, DI, Spring MVC, Spring Data, Spring Security and AOP.
  • Spring Boot is an opinionated, auto-configured layer on top of it that adds starters, auto-configuration and an embedded server, so you can run an application with almost no setup.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Spring Framework engine है: IoC container, DI, MVC।
  • Spring Boot उसी engine के ऊपर ready-made car है: starters, auto-configuration, embedded server।
  • Boot, Spring की जगह नहीं लेता, उसे use करना आसान बनाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Example se samjho

Plain Spring MVC app ke liye tumhe DispatcherServlet register karna, view resolver, Jackson converter, DataSource sab khud configure karna padta tha, aur WAR banakar alag Tomcat mein deploy karna padta tha. Boot mein spring-boot-starter-web add karo, main class chalao, app 8080 par ready.

Boot kya add karta hai
  • Starters: ek dependency mein related libraries ka set, versions tested.
  • Auto-configuration: classpath dekh kar beans khud banana.
  • Embedded server: Tomcat app ke andar, alag install nahi.
  • Externalized config: application.properties / yml, profiles.
  • Actuator: health, metrics jaise production endpoints.
Common mistakes
  • Sochna ki Boot ek alag framework hai. Nahi, andar Spring hi hai.
  • Sochna ki Boot mein config ho hi nahi sakti. Tum apna bean doge to auto-config peeche hat jaati hai.
  • Spring Core: IoC, DI aur beans, baaki sab modules ki neev.
  • Spring MVC: web aur REST. Spring Data: database access. Spring Security: auth. Spring AOP: logging, @Transactional jaise cross-cutting kaam.
  • Starter (spring-boot-starter-web) ek dependency mein zaroori libraries ka set de deta hai.
Yaad rakho'Spring Boot does not replace Spring. It automates the configuration of Spring modules.'

Q13

How does a Spring Boot application reach the database? Explain the stack.

Main Definition

  • A Boot app uses Spring Data JPA for repository interfaces, which uses Hibernate as the JPA implementation (ORM), which uses JDBC to send SQL to the relational database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Controller, Service को call करता है, Service, Repository को।
  • Spring Data JPA के पीछे Hibernate है, Hibernate के पीछे JDBC और फिर database driver।
  • हर layer नीचे वाली layer का काम छुपा देती है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Request ka safar step by step
  1. Controller userService.findById(5) call karta hai.
  2. Service userRepository.findById(5) call karti hai.
  3. Spring Data JPA ne runtime par repository ka proxy banaya hai, woh JPA EntityManager use karta hai.
  4. Hibernate (JPA implementation) SQL generate karta hai.
  5. JDBC, connection pool (HikariCP) se connection leta hai.
  6. Database driver (MySQL/PostgreSQL) SQL ko DB tak bhejta hai, result wapas aata hai aur Hibernate use entity object mein map karta hai.
Minimum config
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/shop
spring.datasource.username=app
spring.datasource.password=${DB_PASSWORD}
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate
Dhyan do
Dhyan doProduction mein ddl-auto=update/create mat rakho. Schema ke liye Flyway ya Liquibase use karo.
  1. Controller aur Service apne Repository interface ko call karte hain.
  2. Spring Data JPA us interface ki implementation runtime par banata hai.
  3. Hibernate entity ko SQL mein badalta hai.
  4. JDBC connection ke through SQL database ko bhejta hai.
Aage padhoIs stack ka detail (JDBC se Spring Data JPA tak) 'JDBC to JPA' notes mein hai.

3. Pehla Spring Boot app

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein humne dekha ki raw Servlets mein WAR banana, Tomcat alag chalana, JSON haath se likhna padta tha, aur Spring Boot ye sab automate karta hai. Ab sawaal ye hai ki asli mein ek Boot app banta kaise hai? Chalo pehla /hello API banate hain.
📖 Notes

Problem: setup mein hi din nikal jaata tha

Plain Spring MVC mein DispatcherServlet register karo, Jackson converter lagao, Tomcat install karo, WAR deploy karo. Naye bande ka pehla din setup mein jaata tha. Boot ka promise: project generate karo, main chalao, 8080 par app ready.

Spring Initializr (start.spring.io)

  1. start.spring.io kholo (ya IntelliJ ka New Project → Spring Boot).
  2. Build tool: Maven. Language: Java. Spring Boot version: stable 3.x lo.
  3. Group (com.example), Artifact (demo), Packaging: Jar, Java: 17 ya 21.
  4. Dependency add karo: Spring Web (spring-boot-starter-web).
  5. Generate → zip download → IDE mein open.
Yaad rakhoVersion ke saath SNAPSHOT = abhi kaam chal raha hai, RC/M = release candidate/milestone. Production ke liye hamesha stable release. Boot 3 ko minimum Java 17 chahiye.

spring-boot-starter-web kya laata hai

  • Spring MVC (DispatcherServlet ke saath) REST APIs ke liye.
  • Embedded Tomcat jo default port 8080 par chalta hai. Alag server install nahi.
  • Jackson jo Java objects ko JSON mein badalta hai.
  • Sab ke tested, compatible versions ek hi dependency mein. Yahi starter ka matlab hai.

Project structure

demo/
├── pom.xml                         <- Maven config (next topic)
└── src/
    ├── main/
    │   ├── java/com/example/demo/
    │   │   ├── DemoApplication.java      <- main class
    │   │   └── HelloController.java
    │   └── resources/
    │       └── application.properties    <- config
    └── test/java/...                     <- tests
Common galtiControllers/services ko main class ke package (com.example.demo) ya uske sub-package mein rakho. Bahar rakhoge to component scan unhe nahi dhoondhega aur 404 aayega.

Main class: sab yahin se shuru

package com.example.demo;

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;

@SpringBootApplication   // = @Configuration + @EnableAutoConfiguration + @ComponentScan
public class DemoApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // IoC container start + auto-config + embedded Tomcat start
        SpringApplication.run(DemoApplication.class, args);
    }
}

Kaise kaam karta hai (andar se)

  1. main() chalta hai, SpringApplication.run() call hota hai.
  2. Spring IoC container (ApplicationContext) banta hai.
  3. Component scan package mein @RestController jaisi classes dhoondhta hai aur beans banata hai.
  4. Auto-configuration classpath par Tomcat aur Spring MVC dekh kar embedded Tomcat + DispatcherServlet set kar deta hai.
  5. Tomcat 8080 par sunna shuru karta hai. App ready.

Pehla controller

Servlet se compare karo: na doGet, na setStatus, na getWriter().write. Mapping ab method-level hai. POST ke liye @PostMapping, PUT ke liye @PutMapping, DELETE ke liye @DeleteMapping. Agar method koi POJO return kare to Jackson use JSON bana deta hai.

package com.example.demo;

import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController   // = @Controller + @ResponseBody: return value seedha response body mein
public class HelloController {

    @GetMapping("/hello")          // GET /hello is method par aayega
    public String sayHello() {
        return "Hello World";
    }

    @GetMapping("/bye")
    public String sayBye() {
        return "Bye!";
    }
}

Hello World

@Controller vs @RestController

@Controller@RestController
Return valueView ka naam (HTML template)Seedha response body (String/JSON)
@ResponseBodyHar method par lagana padtaAlready included
UseServer-side pages (Thymeleaf)REST APIs

Port badalna: server.port

TareekaExample
application.propertiesserver.port=9090
application.ymlserver:\n port: 9090

Random portserver.port=0

Yaad rakhoCommand line argument properties file ko override karta hai. Isi externalized configuration ki wajah se ek hi JAR alag environments/ports par chal sakta hai.

JAR, WAR aur fat JAR

JAR (Java Archive) compiled .class files, resources aur package structure ka zip jaisa package hai. Classpath JVM ko batata hai ki .class aur .jar kahan dhoondhne hain.

TypeAndar kyaKaise chalta
Library JARSirf apni classes; needs pom.xml meinDoosre project ki dependency
WARClasses, servlets, WEB-INF/libExternal Tomcat ke webapps/ mein
Boot fat (executable) JARClasses + saari dependency JARs + embedded Tomcat + main()java -jar app.jar

Build aur run

./mvnw clean package          # target/demo-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar banta hai
java -jar target/demo-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar
Real exampleWahi ek JAR laptop, server ya Docker container mein chala do. Koi Tomcat install nahi, koi webapps/ copy nahi. Yahi pichle topic ke 'manual WAR deployment' dard ka ilaaj hai.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • start.spring.io se project; Spring Web starter = Spring MVC + embedded Tomcat (8080) + Jackson.
  • Code src/main/java mein, config src/main/resources/application.properties mein, tests src/test mein.
  • @SpringBootApplication + SpringApplication.run() = IoC container + auto-config + Tomcat start.
  • @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody; @GetMapping method-level mapping.
  • server.port se port badlo; command line override karta hai.
  • Boot fat JAR mein dependencies + embedded Tomcat, java -jar se chalta hai.

Q15

What is the structure of a Spring Boot project, and what does the main class do?

Main Definition

  • Maven's standard layout has pom.xml at the root, application code in src/main/java, configuration in src/main/resources (application.properties) and tests in src/test.
  • The main class is annotated with @SpringBootApplication, and SpringApplication.run() starts the Spring IoC container and the embedded Tomcat.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Code src/main/java में, config src/main/resources में और tests src/test/java में रहते हैं।
  • Main class पर @SpringBootApplication होता है और SpringApplication.run() पूरा context और server start करता है।

Q16

How do you build a REST endpoint with @RestController and @GetMapping?

Main Definition

  • @RestController combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, so method return values are written directly into the HTTP response body (String or JSON) instead of rendering a view.
  • @GetMapping("/path") maps an HTTP GET request for that path to the method.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @RestController का मतलब है हर method का return value सीधे response body बनेगा, ज़्यादातर JSON।
  • @GetMapping("/hello") बताता है कि GET /hello आने पर कौन सा method चलेगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@RestController
public class HelloController {

    @GetMapping("/hello")
    public String sayHello() {
        return "Hello World";
    }

    @GetMapping("/bye")
    public String sayBye() {
        return "Bye!";
    }
}
Extra (mera note)Class return type POJO ho to Jackson use JSON bana deta hai. Isi tarah POST ke liye @PostMapping, PUT ke liye @PutMapping aur DELETE ke liye @DeleteMapping hota hai.

Q18

What is a JAR file? What is the difference between an executable (fat) JAR and a library JAR? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A JAR (Java Archive) is a zip-like package of compiled .class files, resources and package structure.
  • A library JAR has only its own code and lists its needs in pom.xml.
  • An executable (fat) JAR has a main() method and embeds its dependency JARs, so it runs anywhere with java -jar.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • JAR एक zip file है जिसमें compiled .class files होती हैं।
  • Library JAR सिर्फ़ दूसरों के use के लिए होता है, जबकि Boot का fat JAR अपने अंदर सारी dependencies और Tomcat रखता है और java -jar से सीधे चल जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
TypeMain()DependenciesKaam
Library JARNahiAndar nahi, pom.xml mein likhi hoti hainDoosre projects use karte hain
Executable / Fat JARHaanAndar embeddedSeedha JVM par chalta hai
JAR vs WAR vs fat JAR
TypeAndar kyaKaise chalta
Library JARSirf tumhari classesDusre project ki dependency
WARClasses, servlets, WEB-INF/libExternal Tomcat ke webapps/ mein copy
Boot fat JARClasses + saari dependencies + embedded Tomcatjava -jar app.jar
Purana tareeka: WAR + external Tomcat
  1. Tomcat alag download karo aur start karo.
  2. pom.xml mein <packaging>war</packaging> rakho.
  3. mvn package se .war banao.
  4. WAR ko Tomcat ke webapps/ folder mein copy karo, Tomcat use unpack karke deploy karta hai.
  5. Har change par yahi dobara.
provided scope kyun

Servlet API sirf compile ke liye chahiye. Runtime par external Tomcat khud deta hai, isliye WAR mein bundle nahi hoti. Bundle karoge to Tomcat ki apni copy se class conflict ho sakta hai.

<dependency>
    <groupId>jakarta.servlet</groupId>

    <version>6.1.0</version>
    <scope>provided</scope>
</dependency>
Boot fat JAR

spring-boot-maven-plugin mvn package par fat JAR banata hai. Embedded Tomcat app ke andar hai, isliye koi alag server ya copy step nahi.

4. Maven

6 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein humne Initializr se project banaya aur ./mvnw clean package se fat JAR bana liya. Par pom.xml mein likhi ek line se saari libraries kahan se aa gayin? Folder structure aisa hi kyun hai? Ab sawaal ye hai ki Maven andar se kaam kaise karta hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: Maven ke bina zindagi

Socho tumhe Spring web app banana hai. Bina Maven ke tum har JAR (spring-webmvc, jackson, tomcat...) website se haath se download karoge, sahi version match karoge, aur un JARs ko jo aur JARs chahiye wo bhi dhoondhoge. Phir team ko list share karoge ki 'ye 40 JAR daal lo'. Ek version galat, aur build tut gaya.

  • Bahut saare JAR manually.
  • Version mismatch.
  • Transitive dependencies ka track (A ko B chahiye, B ko C).
  • Har developer ka setup alag.

Solution: Apache Maven

Maven Java ka project management aur build automation tool hai. Ye deta hai:

  • Standard directory structure (src/main/java, src/test...) jo IntelliJ, Eclipse sab samajhte hain.
  • Automatic dependency resolution, transitive dependencies ke saath.
  • Compile, test, package ka standard build lifecycle.
  • Ek file mein poora project description: pom.xml.

pom.xml aur GAV coordinates

POM = Project Object Model. Har project/library duniya mein GAV se unique pehchani jaati hai:

PartMatlabExample
groupIdOrganisation (reverse domain)in.codearmy
artifactIdProject ka naammaven-demo
versionVersion (SNAPSHOT = kaam chal raha)1.0.0-SNAPSHOT
<project>
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>      <!-- hamesha 4.0.0 -->

    <groupId>in.codearmy</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>              <!-- jar ya war -->

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.source>21</maven.compiler.source>
        <maven.compiler.target>21</maven.compiler.target>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
            <!-- version parent (spring-boot-starter-parent) se aata hai -->
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>             <!-- sirf tests mein -->
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</project>
Yaad rakhoProperties ko ${property.name} se poore POM mein reuse kar sakte ho, jaise ${java.version}.

Dependency scopes

ScopeCompileTestFinal package meinExample
compile (default)HaanHaanHaanspring-boot-starter-web
testNahi (main)HaanNahijunit, mockito
providedHaanHaanNahi (server deta hai)jakarta.servlet-api (external Tomcat)
runtimeNahiHaanHaanJDBC driver (mysql-connector-j)

Super POM aur Effective POM

  • Super POM = har POM ka chhupa hua top parent, bilkul jaise har Java class ka parent java.lang.Object. Default plugins, Maven Central ka address, default folders yahin se aate hain.
  • Spring Boot project mein beech mein ek aur parent hota hai: spring-boot-starter-parent, jo saari dependencies ke versions manage karta hai.
  • Effective POM = tumhara pom.xml + parent + Super POM, sab merge hokar jo final config banta hai. Maven asal mein isi par chalta hai.
mvn help:effective-pom     # final merged POM dekho

Repositories: dependency aati kahan se hai?

  • Local: cache; mvn install se tumhari apni JAR bhi yahin aati hai.
  • Central: Apache ki public repo, lakhon open-source JARs.
  • Private: company ke proprietary JARs ya security-audited copies, <repositories> ya settings.xml mein configure.
  1. pom.xml mein GAV likha: org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web.
  2. Maven pehle local repository ~/.m2/repository mein dekhta hai.
  3. Nahi mila to Maven Central (public) ya configured remote/private repo (Nexus, Artifactory) se download.
  4. Download local repo mein cache, agli baar internet nahi chahiye.
  5. Uski transitive dependencies bhi isi tarah resolve hoti hain.
Real exampleDependency ka GAV block mvnrepository.com par search karke copy karte hain.

Build lifecycle

Maven ke 3 lifecycles hain: clean (target/ saaf), default (build) aur site (docs). Default lifecycle ke phases order mein:

validate→compile→test→package→verify→install→deploy
Yaad rakhoKoi bhi phase chalao, uske pehle ke saare phases apne aap chalte hain. mvn install = validate + compile + test + package + verify + install.

Common commands

CommandKya karta
mvn cleantarget/ folder delete
mvn compilemain code compile
mvn testcompile + unit tests
mvn packagetest tak + JAR/WAR target/ mein
mvn installpackage + local ~/.m2 mein copy
mvn deployremote repository par upload
mvn clean install -DskipTeststests chhod kar build (sirf zaroorat par)
Dhyan dopackage JAR ko target/ mein rakhta hai, install use local repo ~/.m2 mein copy karta hai, deploy remote repo par bhejta hai. Spring Initializr projects mein ./mvnw (Maven Wrapper) hota hai, jo sahi Maven version khud download kar leta hai.

Archetype: project ka template

Archetype ek project template hai jo starter skeleton bana deta hai, taaki boilerplate haath se na likhna pade. Example: maven-archetype-quickstart ek Java console project JUnit ke saath bana deta hai. Spring Initializr bhi isi idea ka Boot version hai.

mvn archetype:generate \
  -DgroupId=in.codearmy -DartifactId=maven-demo \
  -DarchetypeArtifactId=maven-archetype-quickstart \
  -DinteractiveMode=false

Common galtiyan

  • Corrupt download ke baad build fail: ~/.m2/repository mein us library ka folder delete karke dobara build karo.
  • Company proxy ke peeche private repo/mirror settings.xml mein configure karna bhool jaana.
  • Boot parent ke hote hue bhi har dependency par version likh dena: version clash ho sakta hai, parent ko manage karne do.
  • Har baar -DskipTests use karna: tests hi to safety net hain.
Common galtiTest library (JUnit, Mockito) ko test scope ke bina daalna: wo production JAR mein chali jaati hai.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Maven = build automation + dependency management + standard structure.
  • Project ki pehchaan GAV: groupId, artifactId, version (SNAPSHOT = WIP).
  • Super POM sabka parent (jaise Object); Effective POM = sab merge hokar final.
  • Lookup order: ~/.m2 local → Maven Central / private repo → local mein cache.
  • Default lifecycle: validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, deploy; phase pichle sab chalata hai.
  • package → target/, install → ~/.m2, deploy → remote.
  • Archetype = project template (quickstart).

Why do we need Maven? What is Apache Maven?

Main Definition

  • Apache Maven is a project management and build automation tool for Java.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

Q21

What are the Super POM, Effective POM and dependency scope?

Main Definition

  • The Super POM is the implicit top-level parent of every POM, like java.lang.Object, supplying default plugins and the Maven Central mapping.
  • The Effective POM is the final merged result of your pom.xml, its parent (for example spring-boot-starter-parent) and the Super POM.
  • Scope controls where a dependency is used: compile (default) or test.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Super POM हर pom.xml का hidden parent है, जैसे Java में हर class का parent Object है।
  • Effective POM वो final merge किया हुआ POM है जो Maven असल में use करता है।
  • Scope बताता है dependency कब चाहिए: compile, test, provided या runtime।

Part 2: Spring Core

5. Coupling, DI aur IoC

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic (Maven) mein humne dekha ki Maven dependencies (jars) download karke project mein laata hai. Lekin jar aa jaane se kaam khatam nahi hota — ab sawaal ye hai ki hamari apni classes ek doosre ko kaise milti hain? Kaun kisko banata hai? Yahin se coupling, DI aur IoC ki kahani shuru hoti hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: class khud apni dependency banati hai

Socho tumhare paas ek OrderService hai. Order place hone par customer ko notification jaana chahiye. Sabse seedha tareeka: OrderService ke andar new EmailNotifier() likh do.

Kal business bolta hai: "Email nahi, SMS bhejo." Ab tumhe OrderService ka code kholna padega, badalna padega, phir se test aur deploy. Aur test chalate waqt bhi asli email chala jaata hai, kyunki fake lagane ka koi raasta hi nahi hai.

Isi ko kehte hain tight coupling — ek class ek concrete class se chipki hui hai aur usko khud new se banati hai. Q25

Real life analogy

Real exampleGhar mein bulb wire se solder kar diya (tight coupling) — bulb badalna hai to electrician bulao. Holder lagaya (interface) to koi bhi bulb — LED, CFL — ghuma ke laga do (loose coupling). Kaunsa bulb lagega ye ghar wale decide karte hain, holder nahi (DI).

Tight coupling kya-kya todta hai

  • Single Responsibility toot-ta hai: OrderService order bhi sambhal raha hai aur notifier banana bhi decide kar raha hai.
  • Open/Closed toot-ta hai: naya notifier (SMS, WhatsApp) laane ke liye purani class modify karni padti hai.
  • Unit testing mushkil: real dependency ki jagah fake/mock nahi daal sakte.
  • Har jagah jahan new EmailNotifier() likha hai, sab badalna padega.

Solution: interface + bahar se do (Dependency Injection)

Do kaam karo: (1) concrete class ki jagah interface par depend karo, (2) object khud mat banao — bahar se maango (constructor mein). Isi pattern ka naam hai Dependency Injection (DI). Q26

// TIGHT: khud new kar raha hai
class OrderService {
    private EmailNotifier notifier = new EmailNotifier();
}

// LOOSE: interface par depend, bahar se mil raha hai
interface Notifier { void send(String msg); }

class EmailNotifier implements Notifier { public void send(String m) { /* email */ } }
class SmsNotifier   implements Notifier { public void send(String m) { /* sms */ } }

class OrderService {
    private final Notifier notifier;
    OrderService(Notifier notifier) {   // jo bhi Notifier do, chalega
        this.notifier = notifier;
    }
    void placeOrder() { notifier.send("Order placed"); }
}

// Test mein: new OrderService(new FakeNotifier())  -> koi real email nahi

DI ke teen types

TypeKaiseKab use karo
Constructor injectionConstructor parameter seDefault choice, required dependencies, final fields
Setter injectionsetXxx() method par @AutowiredOptional dependency, baad mein badal sakte ho
Field injectionField par seedha @AutowiredAvoid — final nahi, test mein bina Spring ke set nahi kar sakte

Ab IoC kya hai?

Upar humne new OrderService(new EmailNotifier()) khud likha. Badi app mein 500 classes hon to ye wiring kaun karega? Yahin aata hai Inversion of Control (IoC).

Normal flow mein tumhara code control karta hai — kab object banana, kisko dena. IoC mein ye control ulta (invert) ho jaata hai: objects banana, unki lifecycle aur wiring ek bahar wala framework (Spring container) karta hai. Tum sirf batate ho "mujhe Notifier chahiye". Q27

Real exampleRestaurant mein tum khud kitchen mein jaake khana nahi banate (normal control). Tum order dete ho, kitchen banake deti hai (IoC). Waiter plate tumhari table par rakhta hai — ye DI hai.

IoC vs DI — confuse mat hona

IoCDI
Kya haiDesign principle (soch)Technique / pattern (tareeka)
Kehta haiControl framework ko de doDependencies bahar se pass karo
RishtaBada ideaIoC ko implement karne ka ek tareeka (doosre: Service Locator, events)

Purana tareeka: XML configuration

Annotations se pehle saare beans beans.xml mein likhe jaate the aur ClassPathXmlApplicationContext se load hote the. Aaj Boot mein ye kam dikhta hai, par legacy projects mein milega. Q28

<!-- beans.xml -->
<beans>
  <bean id="emailNotifier" class="com.shop.EmailNotifier"/>

  <!-- constructor injection -->
  <bean id="orderService" class="com.shop.OrderService"
        scope="singleton" init-method="init" destroy-method="cleanup">
      <constructor-arg ref="emailNotifier"/>
  </bean>

  <!-- setter injection: setNotifier() call hoga -->
  <bean id="reportService" class="com.shop.ReportService">
      <property name="notifier" ref="emailNotifier"/>
  </bean>
</beans>

// Java side
ApplicationContext ctx = new ClassPathXmlApplicationContext("beans.xml");
OrderService os = ctx.getBean(OrderService.class);

XML tags yaad karo

XMLMatlabAaj ka annotation equivalent
<bean id class>Ek bean define karo@Component / @Bean
<constructor-arg>Constructor injectionConstructor parameter
<property>Setter injection@Autowired setter
scope, init-method, destroy-methodScope aur lifecycle@Scope, @PostConstruct, @PreDestroy

Common galtiyan

Common galtiInterface bana diya par andar phir bhi new EmailNotifier() kar diya — coupling waisi ki waisi. DI ka matlab hai banana kisi aur ka kaam hai, sirf interface likhna kaafi nahi.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Tight coupling = concrete class + khud new karna; test aur change dono mushkil.
  • DI = dependency bahar se do, interface par depend karo.
  • Constructor injection default; field injection avoid.
  • IoC = principle (control framework ko), DI = technique (inject karna).
  • Purane Spring mein beans.xml: <constructor-arg> = constructor, <property> = setter injection.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q25

What is tight coupling, and why is it a problem?

Main Definition

  • Tight coupling is when a class depends on a concrete implementation and creates its own dependencies with new.
  • It breaks the Single Responsibility Principle and the Open/Closed Principle, and makes unit testing hard, because you cannot replace the real dependency with a fake.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Tight coupling में class खुद new करके concrete class बनाती है, तो implementation बदलने के लिए code बदलना पड़ता है।
  • जैसे phone में battery solder कर दी हो, बदलनी हो तो पूरा phone खोलो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PrincipleKaise tootta hai
SRPOrderService order ka kaam bhi karta hai aur objects banane ka bhi
OCPEmail se SMS badalne ke liye OrderService ko modify karna padta hai
TestabilityUnit test mein asli email server hit hota hai
Story

Ek OrderService hai jo andar new EmailNotifier() karta hai. Kal business bolta hai SMS bhejo. Ab OrderService ka code khol kar badalna padega, test mein real email jaayega, aur har jagah jahan new EmailNotifier() hai woh badlega.

Tight vs loose
// Tight
class OrderService {
    private EmailNotifier notifier = new EmailNotifier();
}

// Loose
class OrderService {
    private final Notifier notifier;
    OrderService(Notifier notifier) { this.notifier = notifier; }
}
Problems
  • Implementation badalne ke liye code badlo (OCP toot-ta hai).
  • Unit test mein fake inject nahi kar sakte.
  • Class ke do kaam ho gaye: logic aur object banana (SRP toot-ta hai).
public class OrderService {
    // khud bana raha hai: tight coupling
    private EmailService emailService = new EmailService();

    public void placeOrder() {
        System.out.println("Order Placed Successfully!");
        emailService.sendNotification();
    }
}
ReferenceThe IoC Container
Q26

What is Dependency Injection, and what are its types? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Dependency Injection (DI) is a design pattern where a class receives its dependencies from outside instead of creating them with new, and it should depend on an interface, not a concrete class.
  • The types are constructor injection (recommended), setter injection and field injection.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • DI में class अपनी dependencies खुद नहीं बनाती, बाहर से मिलती हैं।
  • Constructor, setter और field तीन तरीके हैं, और constructor injection सबसे अच्छा माना जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
TypeFayda
Constructorfinal field (immutable), object adhoora nahi banta. Recommended.
SetterRuntime par dependency badal sakte ho
Field (@Autowired)Chhota code, par dependency chhupti hai aur test mushkil
Teen types
TypeKaiseKab
ConstructorConstructor parameterDefault choice, required dependencies
SettersetXxx() par @AutowiredOptional dependency
FieldField par @AutowiredAvoid: final nahi, test mushkil
Sample
@Service
public class OrderService {
    private final Notifier notifier;

    public OrderService(Notifier notifier) { // single constructor: @Autowired optional
        this.notifier = notifier;
    }
}
Dhyan do
Dhyan doSpring 4.3 se, agar class mein ek hi constructor hai to @Autowired likhne ki zaroorat nahi.
public interface NotificationService { void sendNotification(); }

public class OrderService {
    private final NotificationService notificationService;

    // constructor injection
    public OrderService(NotificationService notificationService) {
        this.notificationService = notificationService;
    }

    public void placeOrder() {
        System.out.println("Order Placed!");
        notificationService.sendNotification();   // polymorphism
    }
}

// test mein
OrderService s = new OrderService(new FakeEmailService());
s.placeOrder();
Yaad rakho'A class should ask for what it needs, and not build everything itself.'

Q27

What is the difference between IoC and DI? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Inversion of Control (IoC) is the design principle of handing control over object creation, lifecycle and wiring to an external entity.
  • Dependency Injection (DI) is the technique that implements this principle by passing dependencies into an object.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • DI उस principle को implement करने का तरीका है।
  • IoC 'क्या' है, DI 'कैसे' है।

Q28

How was Spring configured with XML (beans.xml)?

Main Definition

  • Before annotations, beans were defined in beans.xml and loaded with ClassPathXmlApplicationContext.
  • A <bean> tag defines a bean, <constructor-arg> does constructor injection, <property> does setter injection, and attributes like scope, init-method and destroy-method configure the bean.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पहले beans को beans.xml में <bean> tag से define करते थे और ClassPathXmlApplicationContext से load करते थे।
  • आजकल annotations और Java config use होते हैं, XML सिर्फ़ पुराने projects में मिलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
<bean id="paymentService" class="in.codearmy.PaymentService" />

<!-- constructor injection -->
<bean id="orderService" class="in.codearmy.OrderService">
    <constructor-arg ref="paymentService" />
</bean>

<!-- setter injection -->
<bean id="userService" class="in.codearmy.UserService"
      scope="singleton" init-method="init" destroy-method="cleanUp">
    <property name="userName" value="Aditya" />
</bean>

6. IoC container aur beans

6 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein humne kaha ki IoC mein objects banana aur jodna 'framework' ka kaam hai. Ab dekhte hain wo framework andar se kya hai — Spring IoC container — aur jo objects wo sambhalta hai unhe beans kyun kehte hain.
📖 Notes

IoC container kya hai

Container ek badi factory + manager jaisa hai. Startup par ye tumhari classes padhta hai, unke objects banata hai, unki dependencies jodta hai (wiring), aur app band hone par unhe saaf bhi karta hai (lifecycle).

Jo object container banata aur manage karta hai usko Spring bean kehte hain. Yaad rakho: har bean ek object hai, par har object bean nahi. Method ke andar new ArrayList<>() kiya — wo sirf object hai, container ko uska pata hi nahi. Q29

Container ke do roop: BeanFactory aur ApplicationContext

BeanFactory basic container hai — beans banao aur do. ApplicationContext usko extend karta hai aur enterprise features add karta hai. Real apps (aur Spring Boot) hamesha ApplicationContext use karte hain. Q30

FeatureBeanFactoryApplicationContext
Bean banana / DIHaanHaan
Singleton kab bante hainLazy (maange tab)Eager (startup par)
Events publish (ApplicationEventPublisher)NahiHaan
i18n (MessageSource)NahiHaan
Annotation processing, BeanPostProcessor auto-registerManualAutomatic

ApplicationContext ke implementations

  • AnnotationConfigApplicationContext — Java config / annotations (@Configuration).
  • ClassPathXmlApplicationContext — purana XML wala (legacy).
  • Spring Boot mein SpringApplication.run() khud web-aware context bana deta hai (servlet app ke liye AnnotationConfigServletWebServerApplicationContext).
@Configuration
@ComponentScan("com.shop")
class AppConfig {}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var ctx = new AnnotationConfigApplicationContext(AppConfig.class);
        OrderService os = ctx.getBean(OrderService.class); // container se maango
        os.placeOrder();
        ctx.close(); // destroy callbacks chalenge
    }
}

Bean kaise declare karein: @Component vs @Bean

Container ko batana padta hai ki kaunsi class bean banegi. Do raaste hain. Q31

// 1) @Component: apni class par lagao, component scan khud dhoondh lega
@Component                 // @Service, @Repository, @Controller bhi isi ke roop hain
public class EmailNotifier implements Notifier { ... }

// 2) @Bean: @Configuration class ke method par. Third-party class ya custom setup ke liye
@Configuration
public class AppConfig {
    @Bean
    public ObjectMapper objectMapper() {          // Jackson ki class, uspe @Component nahi laga sakte
        return new ObjectMapper()
            .configure(SerializationFeature.INDENT_OUTPUT, true);
    }
}

@Component vs @Bean comparison

@Component@Bean
Kahan lagta haiClass parMethod par (@Configuration class mein)
Kiske liyeTumhari apni classesThird-party classes / custom ya conditional creation
Kaun detect karta hai@ComponentScanSpring method ko call karta hai
ControlSpring constructor se banata haiTum khud object banake return karte ho

@Autowired aur injection ka sahi tareeka

@Autowired Spring ko bolta hai: "yahan matching bean daal do". Best practice hai constructor injection. Class mein ek hi constructor hai to @Autowired likhna bhi zaroori nahi (Spring 4.3+). Q32

@Service
public class OrderService {
    private final Notifier notifier;           // final = immutable

    public OrderService(Notifier notifier) {   // single constructor -> @Autowired optional
        this.notifier = notifier;
    }
}

// Avoid:
@Service
class BadService {
    @Autowired private Notifier notifier;      // reflection se set, final nahi, test mein null
}

Constructor injection kyun best hai

  • Fields final — object bante hi complete aur immutable.
  • Koi dependency missing ho to startup par hi error, baad mein NullPointerException nahi.
  • Unit test mein bina Spring ke new OrderService(fakeNotifier) kar sakte ho.
  • Constructor mein 7-8 parameters dikhne lage to signal hai ki class zyada kaam kar rahi hai (field injection ye chhupa deta hai).

Autowiring andar se kaise resolve hoti hai

  1. Spring injection point ka type dekhta hai (jaise Notifier).
  2. Us type ka ek hi bean mila → inject.
  3. Zero mile → NoSuchBeanDefinitionException (Optional<> ya required=false ho to skip).
  4. Ek se zyada mile → pehle @Qualifier, phir @Primary, phir parameter/field ka naam bean name se match.
  5. Phir bhi decide nahi hua → NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.

Ek interface, kai beans: @Primary aur @Qualifier

Maan lo PaymentGateway ke do implementations hain — Razorpay aur Stripe. Spring confuse ho jaata hai kaunsa de. @Primary = default wala, @Qualifier("naam") = injection point par exact naam batao. Dono ho to @Qualifier jeetta hai. Q33

public interface PaymentGateway { void pay(int amt); }

@Component @Primary
class RazorpayGateway implements PaymentGateway { public void pay(int a) { } }

@Component("stripe")
class StripeGateway implements PaymentGateway { public void pay(int a) { } }

@Service
class CheckoutService {
    CheckoutService(PaymentGateway def,                        // Razorpay (@Primary)
                    @Qualifier("stripe") PaymentGateway s) {   // Stripe (explicit)
    }
}

Circular dependency

Jab A ko B chahiye aur B ko A — constructor injection mein koi bhi pehle nahi ban sakta. Spring BeanCurrentlyInCreationException deta hai. Spring Boot 2.6 se spring.main.allow-circular-references default false hai, isliye field/setter wala cycle bhi startup par fail hota hai. Q34

Circular dependency kaise todein

FixKab
Common logic teesri class mein nikaaloBest — design hi sahi ho jaata hai
Events (ApplicationEventPublisher)Ek side ko sirf 'batana' hai, result nahi chahiye
@Lazy ek constructor param parSpring asli bean ki jagah proxy deta hai, pehli call par asli banta hai
Setter/field injection + allow-circular-references=trueLast resort — design smell chhupata hai
Common galtiCircular dependency ko allow-circular-references=true se 'fix' karna. Error chala jaata hai par design ki problem waisi hi rehti hai.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Container = objects banata, jodta, aur lifecycle sambhalta hai; uske objects = beans.
  • ApplicationContext extends BeanFactory + events, i18n, eager singletons.
  • @Component = apni class par; @Bean = @Configuration method mein, third-party ke liye.
  • Constructor injection best; single constructor par @Autowired optional.
  • Kai beans ho to @Primary (default) ya @Qualifier (exact); @Qualifier jeetta hai.
  • Circular dependency: Boot 2.6+ default fail; best fix = redesign.

✅ Review questions (6): ab khud check karo

Q29

What is the Spring IoC container, and what is a Spring bean? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • The Spring IoC container creates application objects, manages their lifecycle (init and destroy) and wires dependencies automatically.
  • A Spring bean is an object that is instantiated, assembled and managed by the container.
  • Every bean is an object, but not every object is a bean.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Spring IoC container objects बनाता है, उन्हें आपस में जोड़ता है और उनका lifecycle संभालता है।
  • जो object container manage करता है उसे bean कहते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  1. Create: classes scan karke objects banata hai.
  2. Manage: kab init ho, kab destroy ho, ye dekhta hai.
  3. Wire: constructor ya setter dekh kar dependencies khud inject karta hai, code mein new nahi.
Yaad rakhoEntity classes (@Entity) database rows ko represent karti hain aur JPA unhe manage karta hai. Wo singleton beans nahi hoti.

  • It extends BeanFactory and adds enterprise features such as event publication, internationalization and annotation processing.
  • Implementations include AnnotationConfigApplicationContext and the legacy ClassPathXmlApplicationContext.

Q31

What is the difference between @Component and @Bean? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • @Component is a class-level annotation for classes you own, detected automatically by @ComponentScan.
  • @Bean is a method-level annotation inside a @Configuration class, used for third-party classes or custom instantiation, and Spring calls the method explicitly.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Component अपनी class पर लगता है और component scan उसे खुद ढूँढ लेता है।
  • @Bean एक method पर लगता है जो @Configuration class में होता है, ये third-party classes के लिए useful है जिनका code हम change नहीं कर सकते।

Q32

How does @Autowired work, and why is constructor injection preferred? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • @Autowired tells Spring to inject a matching bean.
  • Constructor injection is the best practice because it gives immutability with final fields, avoids NullPointerException from half-built objects, and allows unit testing without starting Spring.
  • Field injection is not recommended, because it uses reflection, hides dependencies and breaks immutability.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Autowired Spring को बोलता है कि matching bean inject करो।
  • Constructor injection best है क्योंकि fields final रहती हैं, dependency missing हो तो app start पर ही fail होता है और test लिखना आसान होता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Autowiring kaise resolve hoti hai
  1. Spring injection point ka type dekhta hai.
  2. Ek bean mila to inject.
  3. Zero mile to NoSuchBeanDefinitionException (ya required=false / Optional ho to skip).
  4. Ek se zyada mile to @Qualifier ya @Primary dekhta hai, phir parameter/field name ko bean name se match karta hai.
  5. Phir bhi decide nahi hua to NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.
Constructor injection ke fayde
  • Fields final, object immutable.
  • Dependency missing to startup par hi fail.
  • Test mein new OrderService(fakeNotifier), Spring ki zaroorat nahi.
  • Constructor mein bahut parameters ho gaye to signal hai ki class bahut kaam kar rahi hai.
Common mistakes
  • Field injection + constructor mein us field ko use karna: null milta hai.
  • Class par @Component lagana bhool jaana, phir 'no bean found'.
@Component
public class OrderService {
    private final PaymentService paymentService;

    // single constructor: @Autowired optional
    public OrderService(PaymentService paymentService) {
        this.paymentService = paymentService;
    }
}

// Setter injection
@Autowired
public void setPaymentService(PaymentService p) { this.paymentService = p; }

// Field injection (not recommended)
@Autowired
private PaymentService paymentService;

Q33

What do @Primary and @Qualifier do? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • If several beans implement the same interface, Spring throws NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException.
  • @Primary marks one bean as the default choice, and @Qualifier("beanName") explicitly names the bean to inject at that injection point.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • एक interface के दो beans हों तो Spring confuse हो जाता है।
  • @Primary default bean बना देता है, और @Qualifier("name") injection point पर exactly बताता है कौन सा चाहिए।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Example
public interface PaymentGateway { void pay(int amt); }

@Component @Primary
class RazorpayGateway implements PaymentGateway { ... }

@Component("stripe")
class StripeGateway implements PaymentGateway { ... }

@Service
class CheckoutService {
    CheckoutService(PaymentGateway def,                       // Razorpay (@Primary)
                    @Qualifier("stripe") PaymentGateway s) {} // Stripe
}
Yaad rakho
Yaad rakho@Qualifier, @Primary se zyada strong hai. @Primary default batata hai, @Qualifier exact choice.
@Component @Primary
public class CardPayment implements PaymentService { }

@Component
public class UpiPayment implements PaymentService { }

@Component
public class OrderService {
    public OrderService(@Qualifier("upiPayment") PaymentService payment) { }
}
Extra (mera note)Dono saath ho to @Qualifier jeet jaata hai, kyunki wo zyada specific hai. Default bean ka naam class ka naam hota hai, pehla akshar chhota (upiPayment).
