★ ← Pichhla important (Q32)★ Important listAgla important (Q34) → ★
Q34

What is a circular dependency, and how do you resolve it? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A circular dependency is when BeanA depends on BeanB and BeanB depends on BeanA.
  • With constructor injection Spring cannot create either and throws BeanCurrentlyInCreationException.
  • The best fix is to redesign and move shared logic to a third service.
  • Other options are setter or field injection or @Lazy, which injects a proxy.
  • Since Spring Boot 2.6 circular references are disabled by default.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • A को B चाहिए और B को A, ये circular dependency है।
  • Spring Boot 2.6 से ये default में error देता है।
  • Best fix design ठीक करना है, जैसे common logic किसी तीसरी class में निकाल देना।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Kya hota hai

Constructor injection mein A banane ke liye B chahiye, B banane ke liye A. Koi bhi pehle nahi ban sakta, Spring BeanCurrentlyInCreationException deta hai. Spring Boot 2.6+ mein spring.main.allow-circular-references default false hai, isliye field/setter wala cycle bhi error deta hai.

Fix karne ke options
FixKab
Common logic teesri class meinBest, design sahi hota hai
Events (ApplicationEventPublisher)Ek side ko sirf notify karna hai
@Lazy on one constructor paramTemporary fix, proxy inject hota hai
allow-circular-references=trueLast resort, avoid
@Lazy example
@Service
class A {
    private final B b;
    A(@Lazy B b) { this.b = b; } // B ka proxy milta hai, asli B baad mein
}
  1. Redesign (best): common logic teesri service mein.
  2. Setter ya field injection: Spring pehle adhoore objects banata hai, baad mein jodta hai.
  3. @Lazy: real bean ki jagah proxy inject hota hai, asli bean pehli use par banta hai.
  4. Boot 2.6+: spring.main.allow-circular-references=false default hai.
Dhyan doallow-circular-references=true karna sirf stop-gap hai. Pehla fix hamesha design theek karna hai.
ReferenceThe IoC Container
Important 12 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q33)★ Important listAgla important (Q35) → ★
➡️ Agle topic mein: container ek bean kitni baar banata hai (scopes) aur bean ki poori zindagi — constructor se @PreDestroy tak.Agla topic: Bean scopes aur lifecycle →

7. Bean scopes aur lifecycle

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein container ne beans banaye aur jode. Par do sawaal baaki hain: ek bean ke kitne objects bante hain? (scope) aur bean kab banta hai, kab ready hota hai, kab khatam hota hai? (lifecycle).
📖 Notes

Problem: ek object sabke liye, ya har baar naya?

OrderService jaisi stateless class ka ek hi object poori app ke liye kaafi hai — baar baar banana waste hai. Par ek ShoppingCart har user ka alag hona chahiye. Isliye Spring scope deta hai.

Analogy: office ka water cooler sab share karte hain (singleton), par paper cup har baar naya (prototype). Q35

Saare scopes

ScopeKitne objectsKahanDestroy Spring karta hai?
singleton (default)Ek per ApplicationContextHar appHaan
prototypeHar getBean() / injection par nayaHar appNahi — tumhari zimmedari
requestEk per HTTP requestWeb appHaan
sessionEk per HTTP sessionWeb appHaan
applicationEk per ServletContextWeb appHaan

Code

@Component                    // singleton by default
class OrderService { }

@Component
@Scope("prototype")           // ya ConfigurableBeanFactory.SCOPE_PROTOTYPE
class ReportBuilder { }

@Component
@RequestScope                 // web: har request ka naya
class RequestInfo { }

// check
var a = ctx.getBean(OrderService.class);
var b = ctx.getBean(OrderService.class);
System.out.println(a == b);   // true  (singleton)
var r1 = ctx.getBean(ReportBuilder.class);
var r2 = ctx.getBean(ReportBuilder.class);
System.out.println(r1 == r2); // false (prototype)

Common galti: singleton ke andar prototype

Common galtiSingleton ek hi baar banta hai, isliye usme inject hua prototype bhi ek hi baar inject hota hai — har call par naya nahi milega. Har baar naya chahiye to ObjectProvider<ReportBuilder> inject karke getObject() karo, ya @Lookup method, ya scoped proxy.

Singleton automatically thread-safe nahi hota

Ek singleton ko saari requests (threads) ek saath use karti hain. Isliye singleton mein mutable state (jaise int counter field) mat rakho — race condition hogi. Singleton beans stateless rakho.

Eager vs Lazy initialization

Default mein saare singleton beans startup par hi (eagerly) ban jaate hain. Fayda: config galti ho to app start hote hi fail ho jaati hai, pehli request par nahi.

@Lazy lagao to bean tab banega jab pehli baar getBean() ho ya kisi active bean mein inject ho. Poori app ke liye: spring.main.lazy-initialization=true. Q36

Eager (default)Lazy
Kab banta haiStartup parPehli zaroorat par
Startup timeZyadaKam
Config errorTurant dikhta haiBaad mein runtime par
Kab use karoProduction defaultHeavy, kabhi-kabhi use hone wale beans; dev mein fast startup

Bean lifecycle — andar se

Ab dekho ek bean ki poori zindagi. Q37

Lifecycle steps

  1. Config (annotations/XML) padh kar BeanDefinition (metadata) banti hai.
  2. BeanFactoryPostProcessor definitions badal sakte hain (jaise ${} placeholders resolve).
  3. Constructor se object bana — instantiation.
  4. Dependencies inject — populate (field/setter injection yahan).
  5. Aware callbacks: BeanNameAware.setBeanName(), ApplicationContextAware.setApplicationContext().
  6. BeanPostProcessor.postProcessBeforeInitialization — @PostConstruct yahin chalta hai.
  7. InitializingBean.afterPropertiesSet() → phir custom initMethod.
  8. BeanPostProcessor.postProcessAfterInitialization — yahan AOP proxy banta hai.
  9. Bean ready — app use karti hai.
  10. context.close() par: @PreDestroy → DisposableBean.destroy() → destroyMethod.

Code + console output

@Component
public class CacheLoader implements InitializingBean, DisposableBean {
    @Autowired private ProductRepository repo;

    public CacheLoader() {
        System.out.println("1. Constructor, repo = " + repo);   // null!
    }
    @PostConstruct                       // jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct
    void init() { System.out.println("2. @PostConstruct, repo ready"); }

    @Override
    public void afterPropertiesSet() { System.out.println("3. afterPropertiesSet"); }

    @PreDestroy
    void bye() { System.out.println("4. @PreDestroy"); }

    @Override
    public void destroy() { System.out.println("5. DisposableBean.destroy"); }
}
// Output:
// 1. Constructor, repo = null
// 2. @PostConstruct, repo ready
// 3. afterPropertiesSet
// ... app chal rahi hai ...
// 4. @PreDestroy
// 5. DisposableBean.destroy

Constructor vs @PostConstruct

Constructor injection se pehle chalta hai, isliye field/setter se inject hone wali cheezein wahan null hoti hain. @PostConstruct injection complete hone ke baad chalta hai — sab ready. Heavy kaam (cache preload, connection kholna) yahin karo, constructor halka rakho. Q38

Dhyan doSpring Boot 3 mein @PostConstruct / @PreDestroy jakarta.annotation package se aate hain (Boot 2 mein javax.annotation). Constructor injection use karo to dependencies constructor mein bhi available hoti hain.

Prototype aur destroy

Yaad rakhoPrototype bean par @PreDestroy nahi chalta — container bana ke de deta hai, phir bhool jaata hai. Cleanup tumhe khud karna hai.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • singleton (default) = ek per context; prototype = har baar naya, destroy Spring nahi karta.
  • request/session/application sirf web apps mein.
  • Singleton mein prototype inject = ek hi baar; ObjectProvider use karo.
  • Singletons eager bante hain; @Lazy / spring.main.lazy-initialization se deferred.
  • Order: constructor → injection → Aware → @PostConstruct → afterPropertiesSet → initMethod → ready → @PreDestroy → destroy.
  • Constructor mein field-injected cheezein null; heavy init @PostConstruct mein.

Q35

What are bean scopes: singleton vs prototype? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • singleton (the default) creates one shared instance per ApplicationContext, usually eagerly at startup.
  • prototype creates a new instance every time the bean is requested, and the container does not manage its destruction.
  • request and session scopes are web-only, one instance per HTTP request or session.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Singleton scope में पूरे context में एक ही object बनता है और सब उसे share करते हैं।
  • Prototype में हर बार माँगने पर नया object मिलता है।
  • Default singleton है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
ScopeInstanceCreation / lifecycle
singleton (default)Ek per containerStartup par eagerly. Poora lifecycle container ke haath mein.
prototypeHar request par nayaLazily. Container sirf banata hai, destroy nahi karta.
request / sessionHar HTTP request / session par ekWeb lifecycle ke saath
Saare scopes
ScopeKitne objectKahan
singletonEk per contextDefault
prototypeHar getBean / injection par nayaKoi bhi app
requestEk per HTTP requestWeb app
sessionEk per HTTP sessionWeb app
applicationEk per ServletContextWeb app
Common mistake: singleton ke andar prototype

Singleton ek hi baar banta hai, isliye usme inject hua prototype bhi ek hi baar inject hota hai. Har baar naya chahiye to ObjectProvider<T> use karo.

@Service
class ReportService {
    private final ObjectProvider<ReportBuilder> builders;
    ReportService(ObjectProvider<ReportBuilder> b) { this.builders = b; }
    void run() { ReportBuilder fresh = builders.getObject(); }
}
Dhyan do
Dhyan doSingleton bean shared hai aur multiple threads use karte hain. Usme mutable state (jaise counter field) mat rakho.
@Component
@Scope("prototype")   // ya ConfigurableBeanFactory.SCOPE_PROTOTYPE
public class TokenGenerator { }
Dhyan doSingleton bean mein mutable shared state mat rakho, kyunki ek hi object kai threads use karte hain.

Q36

What is the difference between eager and lazy initialization?

Main Definition

  • With eager initialization (the default for singletons) all beans are created at ApplicationContext startup.
  • With @Lazy creation is deferred until the bean is first requested through getBean() or injected into an active bean.
  • You can enable it globally with spring.main.lazy-initialization=true.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Eager में सारे singleton beans app start होते ही बन जाते हैं, तो गलती तुरंत पता चलती है।
  • Lazy (@Lazy) में bean तब बनता है जब पहली बार चाहिए, startup fast होता है पर error देर से दिखता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Component
@Lazy
public class HeavyReportService { }

# application.properties
spring.main.lazy-initialization=true
Extra (mera note)Eager ka fayda: missing bean ya wiring ki galti app start par hi dikh jaati hai. Lazy ka nuksaan: wahi galti pehli request par production mein dikh sakti hai.
ReferenceBean ScopesThe IoC Container
Q37

Explain the complete Spring bean lifecycle. ★ Important

Main Definition

  • The container reads configuration and creates BeanDefinitions (metadata), then instantiates the bean through its constructor, injects dependencies, runs Aware callbacks (BeanNameAware, ApplicationContextAware), runs initialization callbacks (@PostConstruct, InitializingBean.afterPropertiesSet(), initMethod), and the bean is ready.
  • On context.close() the destruction callbacks run (@PreDestroy, DisposableBean.destroy(), destroyMethod).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Container पहले BeanDefinition पढ़ता है, फिर object बनाता है, dependencies inject करता है, Aware callbacks और BeanPostProcessor चलाता है, फिर @PostConstruct।
  • App बंद होने पर @PreDestroy चलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PhasePreferredAlternatives
Init@PostConstructInitializingBean, @Bean(initMethod = "start")
Destroy@PreDestroyDisposableBean, @Bean(destroyMethod = "stop")
Step by step
  1. Config padh kar BeanDefinition banti hai.
  2. BeanFactoryPostProcessor definitions badal sakte hain (jaise placeholders resolve).
  3. Constructor se object bana (instantiation).
  4. Dependencies inject (populate).
  5. Aware callbacks: BeanNameAware, ApplicationContextAware.
  6. BeanPostProcessor postProcessBeforeInitialization (yahin @PostConstruct bhi chalta hai).
  7. afterPropertiesSet() → custom init-method.
  8. BeanPostProcessor postProcessAfterInitialization (yahin AOP proxy banta hai).
  9. Bean use mein.
  10. Shutdown: @PreDestroy → destroy() → custom destroy-method.
Sample
@Component
class CacheWarmer {
    @PostConstruct void load()  { System.out.println("cache load"); }
    @PreDestroy   void close() { System.out.println("cache clear"); }
}
Yaad rakho
Yaad rakho@PostConstruct / @PreDestroy ab jakarta.annotation package mein hain (Boot 3).
Extra (mera note)@PostConstruct aur @PreDestroy Spring ke nahi, Jakarta Annotations (jakarta.annotation) ke hain. Boot 3 mein import jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct hota hai.
ReferenceCustomizing Beans (lifecycle callbacks)
Important 14 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q35)★ Important listAgla important (Q39) → ★
Q38

Why use @PostConstruct instead of doing initialization in the constructor?

Main Definition

  • The constructor runs before field and setter injection, so injected fields are still null there.
  • @PostConstruct runs after dependency injection is complete, so all dependencies are ready.
  • It also keeps constructors lightweight by moving heavy tasks (preloading a cache, opening connections) to the init phase.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Constructor के time पर field और setter injection हुआ ही नहीं होता, इसलिए injected fields null मिल सकती हैं।
  • @PostConstruct सारी injection के बाद चलता है, इसलिए initialization का काम वहाँ safe है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Component
public class CacheLoader {

    @Autowired
    private DatabaseConfig dbConfig;

    public CacheLoader() {
        // WRONG: dbConfig abhi null hai
    }

    @PostConstruct
    public void initCache() {
        // CORRECT: dbConfig inject ho chuka hai
        System.out.println("Connecting to: " + dbConfig.getUrl());
    }
}
Extra (mera note)Constructor injection use karo to dependencies constructor mein hi mil jaati hain, par tab bhi heavy kaam @PostConstruct mein rakhna accha practice hai.

To Boot ye sab automatic kaise karta hai? Aur DB URL, port jaise values har environment mein alag kaise rakhein? Ye topic dono ka jawab hai.
📖 Notes

@SpringBootApplication — teen annotations ek mein

Main class par jo ek annotation lagta hai, wo asal mein meta-annotation hai jo teen kaam karta hai. Q39

Andar wala annotationKaam
@SpringBootConfigurationSpecial @Configuration — class mein @Bean methods likh sakte ho
@EnableAutoConfigurationClasspath dekh kar default beans khud register karo (Tomcat, Jackson, DataSource...)
@ComponentScanMain class ke package aur sub-packages mein @Component/@Service/@Repository/@RestController dhoondho
package com.shop;               // isi package aur iske neeche scan hoga

@SpringBootApplication
public class ShopApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(ShopApplication.class, args); // ApplicationContext ban gaya
    }
}
Common galtiController com.other package mein rakh diya aur main class com.shop mein — scan nahi hoga, 404 aayega. Main class hamesha root package mein rakho.

Auto-configuration andar se kaise kaam karta hai

Tumne spring-boot-starter-data-jpa + MySQL driver add kiya aur properties mein spring.datasource.url diya. Boot dekhta hai: DataSource class classpath par hai, tumne apna DataSource bean nahi banaya — to wo HikariCP DataSource, EntityManagerFactory aur TransactionManager khud bana deta hai. Kaunsa config laga, kaunsa nahi — dekhne ke liye debug=true chalao, Conditions Evaluation Report console mein aa jaayegi. Q40

  1. @EnableAutoConfiguration candidate classes padhta hai META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports file se (Boot 3; Boot 2 mein spring.factories tha).
  2. Har auto-config class par conditions check hoti hain.
  3. @ConditionalOnClass — kya ye class (jaise Tomcat, Jackson) classpath par hai?
  4. @ConditionalOnMissingBean — kya user ne khud apna bean nahi diya? (tumhara bean hamesha jeetta hai)
  5. @ConditionalOnProperty — kya koi property set hai?
  6. Jo pass ho, unke default beans ban jaate hain — jaise spring-boot-starter-web se embedded Tomcat + DispatcherServlet + Jackson.

Startup ke turant baad kaam: CommandLineRunner / ApplicationRunner

Context poora ready hone ke baad kuch chalana hai (seed data daalna, config log karna)? Ye interfaces implement karo, unka run() startup ke baad ek baar chalega. Q41

CommandLineRunnerApplicationRunner
ArgumentString... args (raw)ApplicationArguments (parsed: option vs non-option)
Kab chalta haiContext start hone ke baadSame
Order@Order se control@Order se control
@Component
class DataSeeder implements CommandLineRunner {
    public void run(String... args) {           // raw String[] args
        System.out.println("Seeding default products...");
    }
}

@Component
class ArgsLogger implements ApplicationRunner {
    public void run(ApplicationArguments args) { // parsed args
        System.out.println("profile option: " + args.getOptionValues("spring.profiles.active"));
    }
}

Problem: config har environment mein alag

Ab config ki baat. Har Boot app ke do hisse hain: code part (controller, service, repository) jo har jagah same rehta hai, aur configuration part (DB URL, username, password, server.port, third-party API keys) jo har environment mein badalta hai. Q42

  • Baar baar redeploy: environment badla to Java code badlo → Git commit, push → poori deployment pipeline phir se.
  • Security risk: DB username/password Java file mein → code GitHub par gaya to credentials leak.
  • Tight coupling: code aur config chipak jaate hain (t5 wali coupling problem, config ke level par).
EnvironmentKya hai
LocalDeveloper ki apni machine — localhost:8080, local MySQL
DevDevelopment testing environment
QA / Staging / Pre-ProdProd jaisa setup, live se pehle QA team ki final testing
ProductionAsli users; highly secure DB credentials, custom ports

Do formats: .properties vs .yml

Config src/main/resources mein do tarah likh sakte ho. Same data dono mein: Q43

# application.properties  (flat, dots se key-value)
spring.application.name=profile-demo
server.port=9090
app.welcome.message=Hello Welcome to My App
app.welcome.code=200
app.welcome.users=Aditya,Rohit,Rohan,Sohan

# application.yml  (tree, indentation se - Python jaisa)
spring:
  application:
    name: profile-demo
server:
  port: 9090
app:
  welcome:
    message: "Hello Welcome to My App"
    code: 200
    users:
      - Aditya

      - Rohan

.properties vs .yml comparison

.properties.yml / .yaml
StructureFlat key=value, dotsHierarchical tree, indentation
ListComma se: a,b,c- items
RepetitionPrefix baar baar likhnaPrefix ek baar
Galti ka riskKamGalat space = galat config (tabs allowed nahi)
Dono ek hi folder mein.properties jeetta hai (same key par)Haar jaata hai
Dhyan doSpring Boot andar se YAML ko bhi flat key-value pairs mein convert karta hai — app.welcome.message hi banta hai. Isliye code mein dono ke liye same @Value("${app.welcome.message}") chalega.

Config ko code mein laana: @Value

Properties ki values kisi bhi Spring bean mein @Value("${key}") se inject hoti hain — field, constructor parameter ya setter par. Spring type khud convert karta hai: "200" → Integer, "Aditya,Rohit" → List<String>. Key missing ho sakti hai to default do: ${key:default}, warna startup fail. Q44

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/demo")
public class DemoController {

    @Value("${app.welcome.message}")
    private String message;

    @Value("${app.welcome.code}")
    private Integer code;                 // "200" -> 200

    @Value("${app.welcome.users}")
    private List<String> users;           // comma-separated -> List

    @Value("${app.welcome.timeout:30}")  // key nahi hai to 30
    private int timeout;

    @GetMapping("/greet")
    public ResponseEntity<String> greet() {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(message + " " + code);
    }
}
// GET /api/demo/greet  ->  "Hello Welcome to My App 200"

Bahut saari properties? @ConfigurationProperties

10 @Value likhne ki jagah ek prefix ki saari properties ek type-safe POJO mein bind karo. Relaxed binding bhi milti hai: retry-count, retryCount, RETRY_COUNT sab retryCount field mein jaate hain. Q45

@Value@ConfigurationProperties
Kitni propertiesEk ekPoora group (prefix)
Type safety / validationKamHaan (@Validated bhi)
Relaxed bindingLimitedPoori
SpEL (#{...})HaanNahi
Kab use karo1-2 valuesRelated settings ka group
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "app.welcome")
public record WelcomeProps(String message, Integer code, List<String> users) {}

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableConfigurationProperties(WelcomeProps.class)   // ya @ConfigurationPropertiesScan
public class ShopApplication { ... }

@Service
class GreetService {
    GreetService(WelcomeProps props) { System.out.println(props.message()); }
}

Profiles: har environment ki apni file

Ab main jugaad: har environment ke liye alag property file — isko Profile management kehte hain. Naming convention: application-{profile}.properties (ya .yml). Q46

FileKiske liyeExample values (video demo)
application.propertiesCommon — har environment mein samespring.application.name=profile-demo
application-dev.propertiesSirf Devserver.port=9090, app.welcome.message=Dev Hello

Profile activate kaise karein

Teen tareeke hain — upar se neeche behtar hote jaate hain. Kuch set nahi kiya to default profile active hota hai. Q47

# 1) Andar se (application.properties) - theek nahi, file edit karni padti hai
spring.profiles.active=dev

# 2) Command line se (best practice, code/file kuch nahi badla)
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=prod
java -jar app.jar --spring.profiles.active=prod

# 3) Environment variable (CI/CD - Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes)
export SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod
docker run -e SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod my-app

@Profile: environment ke hisaab se alag BEAN

Property file sirf values badalti hai. Par kabhi poora implementation badalna hota hai. Video ka example: Notification service.

Production mein endpoint hit ho to asli SMS/Email jaana chahiye. Dev/testing mein real SMS ka kharcha bachane aur spam rokne ke liye sirf dummy notification. Solution: ek interface, do implementations, har ek par @Profile. Q48

NotificationService (interface)→NotificationServiceImpl — @Profile("prod") — real SMS/Email→DummyNotificationServiceImpl — @Profile({"dev","default","staging"}) — dummy

Notification service — code

public interface NotificationService { String sendNotification(); }

@Service
@Profile("prod")                       // sirf prod active ho tab ye bean banega
public class NotificationServiceImpl implements NotificationService {
    public String sendNotification() {
        // asli SMS / Email gateway call
        return "Real Notification Sent Successfully!";
    }
}

@Service
@Profile({"dev", "default", "staging"}) // dev, staging ya kuch set nahi (default)
public class DummyNotificationServiceImpl implements NotificationService {
    public String sendNotification() {
        return "Here is a Dummy Notification!";   // koi real message nahi
    }
}

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/notification")
public class NotificationController {
    private final NotificationService notificationService;

    public NotificationController(NotificationService notificationService) { // interface inject
        this.notificationService = notificationService;
    }

    @PostMapping
    public ResponseEntity<String> send() {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(notificationService.sendNotification());
    }
}

Kaunsa command → kaunsi file → kaunsa bean

CommandFiles loadedBean banaOutput (port)
mvn spring-boot:runapplication.propertiesDummyNotificationServiceImpl"Here is a Dummy Notification!" (8080)
... -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=devcommon + application-devDummyNotificationServiceImpl"Here is a Dummy Notification!" (9090)
... -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=prodcommon + application-prodNotificationServiceImpl"Real Notification Sent Successfully!" (8191)
Common galtiKisi profile ke liye koi implementation cover nahi kiya (jaise qa chalaya par kisi bean par qa nahi) → controller ko NotificationService milega hi nahi → NoSuchBeanDefinitionException, app start nahi hogi. Dono par same profile laga diya to NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException. Ye t6 wala autowiring rule hi hai.

Do chhote corrections

Dhyan do(1) Default run par port 8080 tab aata hai jab common file mein server.port set nahi hai (demo table isi maan kar hai); agar common file mein server.port=9090 hai to default run bhi 9090 par chalega. (2) spring.profiles.active ko application-{profile}.properties ke andar likhna Boot 2.4+ mein invalid hai — sirf common file, command line ya env var se set karo.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • @SpringBootApplication = @SpringBootConfiguration + @EnableAutoConfiguration + @ComponentScan (main package + neeche).
  • Auto-config = classpath + conditions (@ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean); tumhara bean hamesha jeetta hai.
  • Code same, config alag — hardcode karoge to redeploy, credential leak, tight coupling.
  • .properties flat, .yml tree; dono ho to .properties jeetta; YAML andar se flat ho jaata hai.
  • @Value("${key:default}") ek value; @ConfigurationProperties poora group, type-safe.
  • application-{profile}: common + profile dono load, profile override karta hai; activate CLI ya SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE se.
  • @Profile se bean hi badal do (real vs dummy notification).

Q39

What does @SpringBootApplication do? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • @SpringBootApplication is a meta-annotation that combines three: @SpringBootConfiguration (a specialised @Configuration), @EnableAutoConfiguration (auto-registers beans based on the classpath) and @ComponentScan (scans the main class package and its sub-packages for @Component, @Service, @Repository, @RestController).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @SpringBootApplication तीन annotations का combo है: @SpringBootConfiguration, @EnableAutoConfiguration और @ComponentScan।
  • Component scan main class के package और उसके sub-packages में ही चलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
AnnotationKaam
@SpringBootConfigurationIs class ko Spring config batata hai
@EnableAutoConfigurationClasspath dekh kar default beans lagata hai
@ComponentScanIs package aur sub-packages ki beans dhoondhta hai
Dhyan doAgar controller main class ke package ke bahar hai to ComponentScan use dekh nahi paayega aur endpoint 404 dega.

Important 15 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q37)★ Important listAgla important (Q40) → ★
Q40

How does Spring Boot auto-configuration work internally? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • When the context starts, @EnableAutoConfiguration loads auto-configuration classes and Boot inspects the classpath.
  • Each one is guarded by conditions: @ConditionalOnClass applies it only if a class (Tomcat, Jackson) is on the classpath, and @ConditionalOnMissingBean applies it only if you have not defined your own bean.
  • Matching ones register default beans, for example an embedded Tomcat.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Boot classpath देखकर अंदाज़ा लगाता है कि तुम्हें क्या चाहिए।
  • जैसे H2 और JPA classpath पर हों तो DataSource खुद बना देता है।
  • @ConditionalOnClass और @ConditionalOnMissingBean जैसी conditions decide करती हैं कौन सा config लगेगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
ConditionKab apply hota hai
@ConditionalOnClassJab target class classpath par ho
@ConditionalOnMissingBeanJab user ne apna bean na banaya ho
Andar kya hota hai
  1. @EnableAutoConfiguration candidate classes META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports se padhta hai (Boot 3).
  2. Har auto-config class par conditions check hoti hain.
  3. @ConditionalOnClass: class classpath par hai?
  4. @ConditionalOnMissingBean: user ne khud bean nahi diya?
  5. @ConditionalOnProperty: property set hai?
  6. Pass hone wali classes ke beans ban jaate hain.
Example

spring-boot-starter-data-jpa + H2 add kiya. DataSourceAutoConfiguration dekhta hai DataSource class hai aur tumne apna DataSource bean nahi diya, to woh ek embedded H2 DataSource bana deta hai. Tum apna @Bean DataSource doge to Boot ka wala skip ho jaayega.

Debug kaise karo
  • debug=true property ya --debug se condition evaluation report print hoti hai.
  • Kisi auto-config ko band karna: @SpringBootApplication(exclude = DataSourceAutoConfiguration.class).
Yaad rakho'Boot backs off when you define your own bean.' Isi se tumhara custom config default ko override karta hai.

Important 16 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q39)★ Important listAgla important (Q46) → ★
Q41

What are CommandLineRunner and ApplicationRunner?

Main Definition

  • CommandLineRunner and ApplicationRunner are interfaces whose run() method executes right after the ApplicationContext is fully started, useful for startup tasks such as seeding data or logging config.
  • ApplicationRunner receives parsed ApplicationArguments, while CommandLineRunner receives the raw String[] args.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • CommandLineRunner और ApplicationRunner का run() method app पूरा start होने के बाद एक बार चलता है।
  • Startup पर seed data डालने या कोई check करने के लिए useful है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Component
public class StartupTaskRunner implements ApplicationRunner {

    @Autowired
    private PaymentProperties paymentProps;

    @Override
    public void run(ApplicationArguments args) throws Exception {
        System.out.println("Application booted successfully!");
        System.out.println("Configured Gateway: " + paymentProps.getType());
    }
}
Extra (mera note)Kai runners ho to @Order se unka sequence tay kar sakte ho.
ReferenceSpring Boot Reference
Q42

Why must configuration be kept separate from code across environments?

Main Definition

  • An app has a code part (controller, service, repository) that stays the same everywhere and a configuration part (DB URL, credentials, port, API keys) that changes per environment: local, dev, QA/staging/pre-prod and production.
  • Hardcoding config in Java forces a code change and redeploy for every environment, risks leaking credentials to Git and tightly couples code with config.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Business logic हर environment में same रहता है, पर DB URL, password, port हर जगह बदलते हैं।
  • इन्हें Java code में hardcode करोगे तो हर बार code बदलकर दोबारा deploy करना पड़ेगा।
  • ऊपर से password GitHub पर चला गया तो data leak का खतरा है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Environments: local → dev → QA/staging/pre-prod → prod
  • Hardcode = frequent redeploy
  • Hardcode = credential leak risk
  • Hardcode = tight coupling
Q43

What is the difference between application.properties and application.yml?

Main Definition

  • application.properties uses a flat key-value format with dots, like server.port=9090.
  • application.yml uses a hierarchical tree with indentation, and lists are written with -.
  • If both exist in src/main/resources, .properties takes priority, and Spring Boot internally flattens YAML into the same key-value pairs anyway.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • properties file में dot लगाकर flat key=value लिखते हैं, yml में spaces वाली tree structure होती है जैसे Python।
  • दोनों files हों तो properties को priority मिलती है।
  • अंदर से Spring YAML को भी flat key-value में ही बदल देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
# application.properties
spring.application.name=profile-demo
server.port=9090
app.welcome.message=Hello Welcome to My App
app.welcome.code=200
app.welcome.users=Aditya,Rohit,Rohan,Sohan

# application.yml (same config)
spring:
  application:
    name: profile-demo
server:
  port: 9090
app:
  welcome:
    message: "Hello Welcome to My App"
    code: 200
    users:
      - Aditya
      - Rohit
      - Rohan
      - Sohan
Dhyan doYAML mein indentation hi structure hai. Tab mat use karo, sirf spaces; ek space ki galti se property galat parent ke neeche chali jaati hai.
Q44

How do you inject configuration values into a bean with @Value?

Main Definition

  • @Value("${key}") injects a property from application.properties or application.yml into a field, constructor parameter or setter of any Spring bean.
  • Spring converts types automatically, for example to Integer or to a List<String> from a comma-separated value.
  • A default can be given with ${key:default} so the app does not fail if the key is missing.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Value से properties file की value सीधे class के field में आ जाती है।
  • Spring type भी खुद बदल देता है, comma वाली value List बन जाती है।
  • Key न मिले तो ${key:default} से default value दे सकते हो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/demo")
public class DemoController {

    @Value("${app.welcome.message}")
    private String message;

    @Value("${app.welcome.code}")
    private Integer code;

    @Value("${app.welcome.users}")
    private List<String> users;

    @GetMapping("/greet")
    public ResponseEntity<String> greet() {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(message + " " + code);
    }
}
Q45

What is the difference between @Value and @ConfigurationProperties?

Main Definition

  • @Value("${key:default}") injects one property at a time, with an optional fallback default.
  • @ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "...") does bulk, type-safe binding of many related properties into a POJO, with relaxed binding (retry-count maps to retryCount).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Value एक-एक property inject करता है, छोटे cases के लिए ठीक है।
  • @ConfigurationProperties एक prefix की सारी properties को एक typed class में bind करता है, जो बड़ी config के लिए साफ़ और validate करने लायक है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Value@ConfigurationProperties
Kitni valuesEk ekPoora group
Type safetyKamZyada (POJO, validation)
Relaxed bindingLimitedHaan (retry-count to retryCount)
Problem: hardcoded config
  • Har environment (local, dev, staging, prod) ka DB URL, port, keys alag hote hain.
  • Code mein likha to har change par code edit, commit, redeploy.
  • Password Java file mein = security risk.
  • Code aur config tightly coupled.
properties vs yml

YAML indentation (spaces) se tree banata hai, andar Boot use flat keys mein hi convert karta hai. Dono file ho to same key par .properties jeet-ti hai.

# application.properties
app.welcome.message=Hello
app.welcome.code=200
app.welcome.users=Aditya,Rohit

# application.yml (same data)
app:
  welcome:
    message: "Hello"
    code: 200
    users:
      - Aditya
      - Rohit
@Value vs @ConfigurationProperties
@Value("${app.welcome.message:Hi}")   // default "Hi"
private String message;

@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "app.welcome")
public record WelcomeProps(String message, Integer code, List<String> users) {}
// main class par: @ConfigurationPropertiesScan
Profiles
  1. application.properties mein common config.
  2. application-dev.properties, application-prod.properties mein environment specific.
  3. Profile active hone par dono load hote hain, profile wali file same key override karti hai.
  4. Activate: java -jar app.jar --spring.profiles.active=prod, ya env var SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod, ya mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=prod.
  5. File ke andar spring.profiles.active likhna possible hai par best nahi.
@Profile se alag beans
CommandFilesBean
java -jar app.jarapplication.propertiesDummy (default profile)
--spring.profiles.active=dev+ application-devDummy
--spring.profiles.active=prod+ application-prodSmsNotificationService
@Service @Profile("prod")
class SmsNotificationService implements NotificationService { /* real SMS */ }

@Service @Profile({"dev", "default"})
class DummyNotificationService implements NotificationService { /* console log */ }
Common mistakes
  • YAML mein tab use karna (sirf spaces chalte hain).
  • @Value wali key missing aur default nahi: app start fail.
  • Prod profile mein bhi dummy bean active reh jaana kyunki @Profile galat likha.
# application.properties
payment.gateway.type=Paytm
payment.gateway.retry-count=5

@Component
public class PaymentGateway {
    @Value("${payment.gateway.type:Razorpay}")   // default Razorpay
    private String gatewayType;

    @Value("${payment.gateway.retry-count:3}")
    private int retryCount;
}

@Component
@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "payment.gateway")
public class PaymentProperties {
    private String type;        // payment.gateway.type
    private int retryCount;     // payment.gateway.retry-count
    // getters aur setters zaruri
}
Extra (mera note)Setters tab chahiye jab JavaBean binding use ho. Constructor binding (record ya final fields) mein setters ki zarurat nahi hoti.
ReferenceExternalized Configuration
Q46

What are Spring Boot profiles, and how are profile files loaded? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Profiles let you keep separate config per environment using the naming convention application-{profile}.properties (or .yml), for example application-dev, application-staging and application-prod.
  • The plain application.properties holds common settings.
  • When a profile is active, Spring loads both the common file and the profile file, and profile-specific values override the common ones.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • हर environment के लिए अलग file बनाओ: application-dev, application-staging, application-prod।
  • Common बातें main application.properties में रहती हैं।
  • dev active हो तो दोनों files पढ़ी जाती हैं और dev वाली values common वाली को override कर देती हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
FileExample values
application.propertiesCommon settings (har env mein same)
application-dev.propertiesserver.port=9090, app.welcome.message=Dev Hello
application-staging.propertiesserver.port=8080, app.welcome.message=Staging Hello
application-prod.propertiesserver.port=8191, app.welcome.message=Prod Hello

Q47

What are the ways to activate a Spring profile?

Main Definition

  • You can set spring.profiles.active=dev inside application.properties, but that still means editing a file.
  • The better way is external activation from the command line, for example java -jar app.jar --spring.profiles.active=prod or mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=prod.
  • In CI/CD, Docker or Kubernetes, use the environment variable SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE.
  • If nothing is set, the default profile is active.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Profile file के अंदर spring.profiles.active लिखकर भी चला सकते हो, पर इसके लिए भी file बदलनी पड़ती है।
  • Best तरीका है command line से profile pass करना, code को छुए बिना।
  • Docker या Kubernetes में SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE environment variable use करो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
# 1. File ke andar (avoid)
spring.profiles.active=dev

# 2. Command line (best)
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=prod
java -jar app.jar --spring.profiles.active=prod
java -Dspring.profiles.active=prod -jar app.jar

# 3. Environment variable (CI/CD, Docker, K8s)
export SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod
Q48

How do you create profile-dependent beans with @Profile?

Main Definition

  • @Profile on a bean class (or @Bean method) makes Spring create that bean only when the named profile is active.
  • A common case is a NotificationService interface with a real NotificationServiceImpl marked @Profile("prod") and a DummyNotificationServiceImpl marked @Profile({"dev", "default", "staging"}).
  • The controller just injects the interface, and the right implementation is chosen at startup.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Profile लगाने से वो bean सिर्फ़ उसी profile में बनता है।
  • Production में असली SMS/Email जाए, और dev में dummy ताकि पैसा और spam दोनों बचें।
  • Controller बस interface inject करता है, सही implementation Spring खुद चुनता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Kaunsa command, kaunsi file, kaunsa bean
CommandFiles loadedBeanOutput (port)
mvn spring-boot:runapplication.propertiesDummyNotificationServiceImplDummy (8080)
... -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=devcommon + application-devDummyNotificationServiceImplDummy (9090)
... -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=prodcommon + application-prodNotificationServiceImplReal (8191)
Common mistake

Agar kisi profile ke liye koi implementation match nahi karti (jaise 'qa' profile jo kisi @Profile mein nahi likha), to startup par NoSuchBeanDefinitionException aayegi. Har profile ke liye ek bean zaroor cover karo.

@Service
@Profile("prod")
public class NotificationServiceImpl implements NotificationService {
    public String sendNotification() { return "Real Notification Sent Successfully!"; }
}

@Service
@Profile({"dev", "default", "staging"})
public class DummyNotificationServiceImpl implements NotificationService {
    public String sendNotification() { return "Here is a Dummy Notification!"; }
}

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/notification")
public class NotificationController {
    private final NotificationService notificationService;
    public NotificationController(NotificationService ns) { this.notificationService = ns; }

    @PostMapping
    public ResponseEntity<String> send() {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(notificationService.sendNotification());
    }
}
➡️ Agle topic mein: beans aur config ready hain — inhe app mein kaise arrange karein? Controller → Service → Repository wali layered architecture.Agla topic: Layered architecture →

9. Layered architecture

2 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein Boot ne beans auto-configure kiye aur humne config ko profiles mein baanta. Ab sawaal hai: hamari apni classes (controller, service, repository) ko kis tarah arrange karein taaki app badi hone par bhi saaf rahe? Iska jawab hai layered architecture.
📖 Notes

Problem: sab kuch ek class mein

Socho ek controller method mein hi HTTP request padhna, discount calculate karna, aur SQL chalana — sab likh diya. Kal mobile app ke liye same logic chahiye, ya DB badalna hai — poora method todna padega, test karna mushkil. Ye bhi ek tarah ki tight coupling hai (t5 yaad karo).

Real exampleRestaurant: waiter order leta hai (Controller), chef khana banata hai (Service), store-room wala saman laata hai (Repository), godown mein saman rakha hai (Database). Waiter kabhi seedha godown nahi jaata.

Layers aur unka kaam

Har layer ka ek hi kaam, aur har layer sirf apne neeche wali layer se baat karti hai. Q49

LayerAnnotationKaam
Controller@RestControllerHTTP request/response, DTO validate, status code
Service@ServiceBusiness logic, @Transactional boundary
Repository@Repository / JpaRepositoryDatabase access
Database—Data store

Ek request ka safar

Client→Controller (DTO validate)→Service (@Transactional logic)→Repository→Database

Pura example: Student CRUD

Ab chaaron layers ek saath. POST /api/students aur GET /api/students. Q50

// 1) Entity - table ki ek row
@Entity
@Table(name = "students")
public class Student {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
    // getters/setters
}

// 2) Repository - koi code nahi, Spring Data JPA runtime par CRUD deta hai
public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> { }

// 3) Service - business logic
@Service
public class StudentService {
    private final StudentRepository repo;
    public StudentService(StudentRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }

    @Transactional
    public Student create(Student s) { return repo.save(s); }
    public List<Student> all() { return repo.findAll(); }
}

// 4) Controller - sirf HTTP
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/students")
public class StudentController {
    private final StudentService service;
    public StudentController(StudentService service) { this.service = service; }

    @PostMapping
    public ResponseEntity<Student> create(@RequestBody Student s) {
        return ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.CREATED).body(service.create(s)); // 201
    }
    @GetMapping
    public ResponseEntity<List<Student>> all() {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(service.all());                                  // 200
    }
}

Sample request / response

POST /api/students
{ "name": "Aditya", "email": "aditya@mail.com" }

-> 201 Created
{ "id": 1, "name": "Aditya", "email": "aditya@mail.com" }

-- Hibernate ki SQL
insert into students (email, name) values (?, ?)

GET /api/students
-> 200 OK
[ { "id": 1, "name": "Aditya", "email": "aditya@mail.com" } ]

Rules

  • Controller mein business logic nahi — sirf request/response.
  • Controller kabhi Repository ko direct call na kare (chhoti app mein bhi aadat achhi).
  • Transaction boundary (@Transactional) Service par.
  • Entity ko seedha API mein return karna production mein avoid karo — DTO use karo (upar example simple rakhne ke liye Entity diya hai).
  • Har layer neeche wali ko constructor injection se paati hai — yahi t5 ka DI hai.

Common galtiyan

Common galtiService mein HttpServletRequest ya ResponseEntity use karna — HTTP ki cheez service mein aa gayi, ab wo service kisi batch job ya message listener se reuse nahi ho sakti.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Controller (HTTP) → Service (logic + transaction) → Repository (DB) → Database.
  • Har layer sirf neeche wali se baat kare; controller → repository direct nahi.
  • Repository = JpaRepository<Entity, IdType> extend karo, CRUD free.
  • POST par 201 Created, GET par 200 OK — ResponseEntity se.
  • API mein Entity ki jagah DTO; @Transactional service par.

✅ Review questions (2): ab khud check karo

Q49

Explain the layered architecture of a Spring Boot application.

Main Definition

  • A Boot app separates concerns into layers: the Controller layer (@RestController) handles HTTP, the Service layer (@Service) holds business logic, the Repository layer (@Repository) does database access, and the database stores data.
  • Each layer talks only to the one below it.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Controller request लेता है, Service business logic चलाता है, Repository database से बात करता है।
  • हर layer का अपना काम है, जैसे restaurant में waiter, chef और store room।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Ek request ka safar
Client→Controller (DTO validate)→Service (@Transactional logic)→Repository→Database
Rules
  • Controller mein business logic nahi, sirf request/response.
  • Entity ko seedha API mein return mat karo, DTO use karo.
  • Transaction boundary Service par.
  • Controller kabhi Repository ko direct call na kare (chhote apps mein bhi aadat achhi).
Extra (mera note)Controller se seedha repository call karna aur entity ko hi API response mein bhej dena bad practice hai. Beech mein service aur DTO rakho.
ReferenceSpring Boot ReferenceSpring Web MVC
Q50

Show a complete layered CRUD example with Entity, Repository, Service and Controller.

Main Definition

  • The Entity (@Entity, @Table, @Id) maps a table row, the Repository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> so Spring Data JPA gives CRUD methods at runtime, the Service calls the repository, and the Controller exposes POST /api/students and GET /api/students returning ResponseEntity with the right status.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Entity table की row को represent करती है, Repository CRUD methods देता है, Service logic रखती है और Controller REST endpoints expose करता है।
  • Request ऊपर से नीचे जाती है और data वापस ऊपर आता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Entity
@Table(name = "students")
public class Student {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private String email;
    private int age;
}

@Repository
public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> { }

@Service
public class StudentService {
    @Autowired private StudentRepository studentRepository;

    public Student createStudent(Student s) { return studentRepository.save(s); }
    public List<Student> getAllStudents()   { return studentRepository.findAll(); }
}

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/students")
public class StudentController {
    @Autowired private StudentService studentService;

    @PostMapping
    public ResponseEntity<Student> create(@RequestBody Student s) {
        return new ResponseEntity<>(studentService.createStudent(s), HttpStatus.CREATED);
    }

    @GetMapping
    public ResponseEntity<List<Student>> getAll() {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(studentService.getAllStudents());
    }
}
Extra (mera note)Notes mein field injection (@Autowired) dikhaya gaya hai, par Q32 ke hisaab se constructor injection use karo. @Repository interface par optional hai, Spring Data khud detect kar leta hai.

➡️ Agle part mein: Controller tak request pahunchti kaise hai? Tomcat se DispatcherServlet, handler mapping aur response tak — Spring MVC request flow.Agla topic: Spring MVC request flow →

Part 3: Web layer (Spring MVC)

10. Spring MVC request flow

6 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic (Layered architecture) mein humne Controller → Service → Repository ki layers dekhi. Par sawaal ye hai: browser se aayi HTTP request Controller tak pahunchti kaise hai? Kaun decide karta hai ki GET /hello kis method pe jaayega? Yahi Spring MVC request flow hai.
📖 Notes

Pehle confusion clear karo: Spring MVC vs Spring Boot

Bahut log sochte hain Spring Boot ek web framework hai. Nahi! Asli web framework hai Spring Web MVC (spring-webmvc). @Controller, @RestController, @GetMapping, @RequestBody sab isi se aate hain.

Spring Boot sirf ek auto-configuration layer hai. Bina Boot ke Tomcat khud start karo, DispatcherServlet khud register karo, Jackson khud configure karo. spring-boot-starter-web ye sab apne aap kar deta hai. Q51

Problem: plain Servlets ka zamana

Socho tumhare paas User, Order, Payment teen module hain. Plain servlets mein har module ka apna servlet: UserServlet, OrderServlet, PaymentServlet. Har ek mein wahi kaam repeat: request parse karo, JSON banao, status code set karo, exception handle karo. Code duplicate, maintain karna mushkil.

Client→Tomcat Container→UserServlet / OrderServlet / PaymentServlet (har ek mein duplicate boilerplate)
Real exampleEk hotel socho jahan har room ka apna alag reception ho. Bekaar! Ek front desk hona chahiye jo har guest ko sahi room bheje. Wahi front desk hai DispatcherServlet.

Solution: Front Controller pattern = DispatcherServlet

DispatcherServlet khud controller call nahi karta; wo helpers (HandlerMapping, HandlerAdapter) se kaam karwata hai. Q52

  • Poori app mein sirf ek servlet: DispatcherServlet
  • Tomcat har request isi ko deta hai
  • Common kaam (JSON conversion, status, errors) ek jagah
  • Controllers sirf business logic likhte hain
Spring MVC Flow:
Client ---> Tomcat ---> DispatcherServlet (Front Controller)
                              |
               +--------------+--------------+
               |                             |
         HandlerMapping                HandlerAdapter
       (Controller dhoondo)          (Method chalao)
               |                             |
               +--------> Controller <-------+
                              |
                              v
                 JSON / ModelAndView return

Tomcat ka role (servlet level)

Tomcat port 8080 pe sunta hai. Raw HTTP text ko parse karke do Java objects banata hai: HttpServletRequest aur HttpServletResponse. Ye dono DispatcherServlet ko de diye jaate hain.

Kaise kaam karta hai andar se (GET /hello)

Q53

  1. Tomcat raw HTTP leta hai → HttpServletRequest / HttpServletResponse banata hai.
  2. Dono objects DispatcherServlet ko milte hain.
  3. DispatcherServlet HandlerMapping se poochta hai: is URL + HTTP method ke liye kaunsa controller method?
  4. Ye mapping table startup pe banti hai: IoC container ke saare @Controller/@RestController beans scan hote hain, @GetMapping/@PostMapping padhe jaate hain.
  5. HandlerAdapter us method ko invoke karta hai; argument resolvers @PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody bharte hain.
  6. JSON body ho to Jackson (HttpMessageConverter ke through) use Java object (POJO) mein badalta hai.
  7. @RestController: return object Jackson se JSON ban ke response body mein likha jaata hai.
  8. @Controller: return hua view name (jaise "home") ViewResolver ko jaata hai, jo prefix (/WEB-INF/views/) aur suffix (.jsp) jod ke page dhoondhta aur render karta hai.

Kaun kya resolve karta hai

Q54

CheezKahan seKaun bind karta hai
Path variable /students/{id}URL@PathVariable resolver
Query param ?name=RamTomcat parse karke request mein rakhta hai@RequestParam resolver (Spring)
Request body (JSON)POST/PUT payloadJackson via message converter
Dhyan doVideo notes mein query params ka resolver 'Tomcat' likha hai. Sahi tasveer: Tomcat sirf parse karta hai, method parameter mein Spring ka resolver bind karta hai.

Traditional MVC: Model, View, Controller

Spring MVC sirf REST ke liye nahi bana tha; pehle iska main use traditional web apps (HTML/JSP) tha. Flow: Browser request → Controller → Model mein data set → view name return → View engine (JSP/ViewResolver) → HTML wapas browser ko.

  • Model = data carrier (controller se view tak data le jaata hai)
  • View = JSP/HTML page
  • Controller = view ka naam return karta hai
  • ViewResolver = naam ko actual page file mein badalta hai
Browser (HTTP request)→@Controller→Model (addAttribute)→View name "home"→ViewResolver / JSP→HTML response
@Controller
public class HomeController {
    @GetMapping("/home")
    public String home(Model model) {
        model.addAttribute("message", "Enter Name"); // data model mein daala
        return "home";   // ViewResolver -> /WEB-INF/views/home.jsp
    }
}

@Controller vs @RestController

Q55

@Controller@RestController
Return valueView name ("home")Object → JSON
Kaun handle karta haiViewResolverJackson (HttpMessageConverter)
UseServer-rendered pagesREST APIs
Yaad rakho@RestController = @Controller + har method pe @ResponseBody.

Bina Boot ke Spring MVC (pure setup)

Dependencies khud: spring-webmvc, tomcat-embed-core, jackson-databind. Phir config class aur main method sab haath se:

@Configuration
@ComponentScan(basePackages = "in.codearmy")
@EnableWebMvc                 // @RequestBody, @GetMapping, @PostMapping wagairah ON
public class WebConfig {
    // ViewResolver beans / Interceptors bhi yahin manually
}

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        Tomcat tomcat = new Tomcat();          // 1. Tomcat banao
        tomcat.setPort(8080);
        tomcat.getConnector();
        Context ctx = tomcat.addContext("", new File("src/main/webapp").getAbsolutePath());

        // 2. Spring context
        AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext spring = new AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext();
        spring.register(WebConfig.class);

        // 3. DispatcherServlet register karo, "/" pe map
        Tomcat.addServlet(ctx, "dispatcherServlet", new DispatcherServlet(spring));
        ctx.addServletMappingDecoded("/", "dispatcherServlet");

        tomcat.start();                         // 4. Server start
        tomcat.getServer().await();
    }
}

Boot ke saath wahi cheez

Upar ka saara 25+ lines ka setup = @SpringBootApplication + spring-boot-starter-web. Boot embedded Tomcat, DispatcherServlet, Jackson sab auto-configure kar deta hai. Q56

Common galtiBoot app mein @EnableWebMvc mat lagao. Ye Boot ki MVC auto-configuration ko band kar deta hai (static resources, Jackson defaults wagairah chhoot jaate hain).
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Spring MVC = web framework; Boot = auto-config + embedded server
  • Front Controller: poori app ka ek hi servlet, DispatcherServlet
  • HandlerMapping = kaunsa method; HandlerAdapter = method call karna
  • Mapping table startup pe banti hai
  • Jackson JSON ↔ POJO karta hai
  • @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody

✅ Review questions (6): ab khud check karo

Q51

What is Spring MVC, and how is it different from Spring Boot?

Main Definition

  • Spring Web MVC (spring-webmvc) is the actual web framework; annotations like @Controller, @RestController, @GetMapping, @PostMapping and @RequestBody come from it.
  • Spring Boot is not a separate web framework but an auto-configuration layer on top of Spring MVC.
  • Without Boot you start Tomcat, declare the DispatcherServlet and configure Jackson yourself; spring-boot-starter-web does all of that automatically.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • असली web framework Spring MVC है, @RestController, @GetMapping जैसी annotations वहीं से आती हैं।
  • Spring Boot उसके ऊपर बस auto-configuration की layer है जो Tomcat start करना और DispatcherServlet register करना खुद कर देता है।
  • मतलब Boot गाड़ी नहीं, गाड़ी का automatic gear है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • spring-webmvc = framework
  • Boot = auto-configuration + embedded server
  • Plain MVC = manual Tomcat + DispatcherServlet + config
Q52

What is the DispatcherServlet (Front Controller pattern)?

Main Definition

  • In plain servlets every module needs its own servlet (UserServlet, OrderServlet, PaymentServlet), each repeating parsing, JSON conversion, status codes and exception handling.
  • Spring MVC follows the Front Controller pattern: there is only one central servlet, the DispatcherServlet, for the whole application.
  • Tomcat hands every request to it, and it delegates to the right controller method using helper components.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पहले हर module का अपना servlet होता था और सब में वही boilerplate code repeat होता था।
  • Spring MVC में पूरी app के लिए सिर्फ़ एक DispatcherServlet होता है, जैसे office का receptionist जो हर visitor को सही desk पर भेजता है।
  • Tomcat हर request उसी को देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Ek hi servlet poori app ke liye
  • Common kaam (JSON, status, errors) ek jagah
  • Controllers sirf business logic
Q53

Walk through the Spring MVC request flow step by step. ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Tomcat parses the raw request into HttpServletRequest/HttpServletResponse and hands them to the DispatcherServlet.
  • It asks HandlerMapping which controller method matches the URL and HTTP method, then uses a HandlerAdapter to invoke it, with argument resolvers filling path variables, query params and @RequestBody.
  • For @RestController the return value is written as JSON by Jackson; for @Controller the view name goes to a ViewResolver that renders a JSP/HTML page.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • DispatcherServlet खुद controller नहीं बुलाता, पहले HandlerMapping से पूछता है कि इस URL के लिए कौन सा method है।
  • फिर HandlerAdapter उस method को सही arguments के साथ चलाता है।
  • Result या तो Jackson से JSON बनकर जाता है या ViewResolver से JSP page बनता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Step by step (GET /hello)
  1. Tomcat (port 8080) raw HTTP leta hai, parse karke HttpServletRequest aur HttpServletResponse banata hai.
  2. Dono objects DispatcherServlet ko diye jaate hain.
  3. DispatcherServlet HandlerMapping (in-memory mapping table) se poochta hai: is URL + HTTP method ke liye kaunsa controller method?
  4. Ye table startup par banti hai: IoC container ke saare @Controller/@RestController beans scan hote hain aur @GetMapping/@PostMapping padhe jaate hain.
  5. HandlerAdapter method invoke karta hai; HandlerMethodArgumentResolver @PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody resolve karte hain.
  6. JSON body aayi ho to Jackson (HttpMessageConverter ke through) use Java POJO mein badalta hai.
  7. @RestController: return object Jackson se JSON banta hai aur response body mein likha jaata hai.
  8. @Controller: return view name (jaise "home") ViewResolver ko jaata hai jo prefix /WEB-INF/views/ aur suffix .jsp lagakar page render karta hai.
Important 18 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q46)★ Important listAgla important (Q57) → ★
Q54

How do HandlerMapping, HandlerAdapter and argument resolvers fill controller parameters?

Main Definition

  • HandlerMapping maps a URL pattern and HTTP method to a controller method; the table is built at startup.
  • HandlerAdapter actually calls that method and uses HandlerMethodArgumentResolver implementations to supply each parameter.
  • JSON bodies are converted to objects by Jackson through message converters, while query parameters are first parsed by Tomcat into the request and then bound by the resolver for @RequestParam.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • HandlerMapping एक map की तरह है जो बताता है कौन सा URL किस method पर जाएगा।
  • HandlerAdapter उस method को call करता है और argument resolvers हर parameter भर देते हैं।
  • JSON body को Jackson object में बदलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
DataKaise aata haiKaun resolve karta hai
Request body (JSON)POST / PUT payloadJackson (HttpMessageConverter) + @RequestBody resolver
Path variable/users/{id}HandlerMethodArgumentResolver (@PathVariable)
Query param/users?id=1Tomcat parse karta hai (request params), @RequestParam resolver bind karta hai
Yaad rakhoNotes mein query params ka resolver 'Tomcat' likha hai. Sahi tasveer: Tomcat params parse karke HttpServletRequest mein rakhta hai, aur Spring ka @RequestParam resolver unhe method parameter mein bind karta hai.
Q55

What are Model, View and Controller in traditional Spring MVC with JSP, and how does @RestController differ from @Controller?

Main Definition

  • In a traditional web app the Controller (@Controller) puts dynamic data into the Model (model.addAttribute(...)) and returns a view name.
  • The ViewResolver turns that name into a View (HTML/JSP page) and renders it with the model data.
  • @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody on every method, so return values are written as JSON instead of being treated as view names.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Model एक डिब्बा है जो controller से data उठाकर JSP page तक ले जाता है।
  • @Controller view का नाम return करता है और ViewResolver उससे page बनाता है।
  • @RestController में हर method पर @ResponseBody लगा होता है, इसलिए सीधा JSON जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Model = data carrier
  • View = JSP/HTML
  • Controller = view name return
  • @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody
@Controller
public class HomeController {
    @GetMapping("/home")
    public String home(Model model) {
        model.addAttribute("message", "Enter Name");
        return "home";   // ViewResolver -> /WEB-INF/views/home.jsp
    }
}
Q56

What does a pure Spring MVC setup look like without Spring Boot?

Main Definition

  • Without Boot you add spring-webmvc, tomcat-embed-core and jackson-databind yourself.
  • You write a @Configuration class with @EnableWebMvc and @ComponentScan, then a main method that creates Tomcat, creates an AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext, registers a DispatcherServlet mapped to / and starts the server.
  • Spring Boot replaces all of this with @SpringBootApplication plus spring-boot-starter-web.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Boot के बिना Tomcat खुद बनाना, Spring context बनाना और DispatcherServlet को '/' पर register करना पड़ता है।
  • ये 25+ lines का setup हर project में दोहराना पड़ता है।
  • Spring Boot में ये सब एक @SpringBootApplication से हो जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Dependencies: spring-webmvc, tomcat-embed-core, jackson-databind
  • @EnableWebMvc: MVC features on
  • DispatcherServlet ko '/' par map
@Configuration
@ComponentScan(basePackages = "in.codearmy")
@EnableWebMvc
public class WebConfig { }

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        Tomcat tomcat = new Tomcat();
        tomcat.setPort(8080);
        tomcat.getConnector();

        Context context = tomcat.addContext("", new File("src/main/webapp").getAbsolutePath());

        AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext springContext = new AnnotationConfigWebApplicationContext();
        springContext.register(WebConfig.class);

        DispatcherServlet dispatcherServlet = new DispatcherServlet(springContext);
        Tomcat.addServlet(context, "dispatcherServlet", dispatcherServlet);
        context.addServletMappingDecoded("/", "dispatcherServlet");

        tomcat.start();
        tomcat.getServer().await();
    }
}
