Common mistakes
  • 500 handler mein ex.getMessage() bhejna: internal details leak hoti hain.
  • @Valid lagana bhool jaana: tab MethodArgumentNotValidException aayegi hi nahi.
  • @ControllerAdvice use karke JSON expect karna: REST ke liye @RestControllerAdvice lo.
@RestControllerAdvice
public class GlobalExceptionHandler {

    @ExceptionHandler(ResourceNotFoundException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ExceptionResponseDTO> handleNotFound(
            ResourceNotFoundException ex, HttpServletRequest request) {
        ExceptionResponseDTO body = new ExceptionResponseDTO(LocalDateTime.now(),
            HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND.value(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND.getReasonPhrase(),
            ex.getMessage(), request.getRequestURI());
        return new ResponseEntity<>(body, HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND);           // 404
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(DuplicateResourceException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ExceptionResponseDTO> handleDuplicate(
            DuplicateResourceException ex, HttpServletRequest request) {
        ExceptionResponseDTO body = new ExceptionResponseDTO(LocalDateTime.now(),
            HttpStatus.CONFLICT.value(), HttpStatus.CONFLICT.getReasonPhrase(),
            ex.getMessage(), request.getRequestURI());
        return new ResponseEntity<>(body, HttpStatus.CONFLICT);            // 409
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ValidationExceptionResponseDTO> handleValidation(
            MethodArgumentNotValidException ex, HttpServletRequest request) {
        Map<String, String> errors = new HashMap<>();
        ex.getBindingResult().getFieldErrors()
          .forEach(e -> errors.put(e.getField(), e.getDefaultMessage()));
        ValidationExceptionResponseDTO body = new ValidationExceptionResponseDTO(LocalDateTime.now(),
            HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST.value(), HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST.getReasonPhrase(),
            "Validation Failed", request.getRequestURI(), errors);
        return new ResponseEntity<>(body, HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);         // 400
    }

    @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)
    public ResponseEntity<ExceptionResponseDTO> handleGeneric(
            Exception ex, HttpServletRequest request) {
        ExceptionResponseDTO body = new ExceptionResponseDTO(LocalDateTime.now(),
            HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.value(), HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.getReasonPhrase(),
            "Something went wrong. Please try again later.", request.getRequestURI());
        return new ResponseEntity<>(body, HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR); // 500
    }
}

Q82

What does a clean controller look like after adding a global exception handler?

Main Definition

  • With a global handler in place, the controller only receives requests, calls the service and returns the right success status.
  • It uses 201 Created for POST, 200 OK for GET/PUT and 204 No Content for DELETE.
  • @Valid @RequestBody triggers validation, and any thrown exception is handled centrally, so there are no if-else error checks in the controller.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Global handler लगने के बाद controller बिल्कुल साफ़ हो जाता है, बस service call करो और सही status लौटाओ।
  • POST पर 201, GET और PUT पर 200, DELETE पर 204।
  • Error का कोई if-else controller में नहीं रहता।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)

        return new ResponseEntity<>(studentService.createStudent(dto), HttpStatus.CREATED); // 201
    }

    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    public ResponseEntity<StudentResponseDTO> get(@PathVariable Long id) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(studentService.getStudentById(id));                    // 200
    }

    @PutMapping("/{id}")
    public ResponseEntity<StudentResponseDTO> update(@PathVariable Long id,
                                                     @Valid @RequestBody StudentRequestDTO dto) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok(studentService.updateStudent(id, dto));                 // 200
    }

    public ResponseEntity<Void> delete(@PathVariable Long id) {

        return ResponseEntity.noContent().build();                                      // 204
    }

14. Filters

10 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein errors ko ek jagah (global handler) le gaye. Ab wahi soch aage badhao: kuch kaam har request pe hone hain (logging, auth, timing). Unhe bhi ek common entry point chahiye. Wo hai Filter.
📖 Notes

Problem: cross-cutting concerns

Ye har controller mein likhoge to SRP tootega, code duplicate hoga, business logic infrastructure se chipak jaayega. Helper class banao to bhi har method se call karni padegi. Q83

  • Request logging (verb, URI, headers)
  • Authentication / API key check
  • Request ID (X-Request-ID) tracing ke liye
  • Response headers add karna
  • Turnaround time measure karna
Real exampleBuilding ka security guard socho. Wo gate pe sabko check karta hai; har office mein alag guard nahi hota. Filter wahi gate guard hai.

Filter kahan baithta hai

Filter Servlet container level (Tomcat) pe chalta hai, DispatcherServlet se pehle. Response ulte order mein wapas aata hai: Repository → Service → Controller → DispatcherServlet → Filter 3 → Filter 2 → Filter 1 → Client.

HandlerMapping abhi chala hi nahi, isliye filter ko raw request (ServletRequest/ServletResponse) milti hai aur use pata nahi kaunsa controller handle karega. Isliye global kaam ke liye perfect. Q84

Client→Tomcat→Filter 1→Filter 2→Filter 3→DispatcherServlet→Controller→Service→Repository

Filter kya kya kar sakta hai

  • Inspect: headers, cookies, query params, auth token, URI path
  • Security / short-circuit: unauthorized request ko DispatcherServlet tak jaane hi na do
  • Logging & tracing: incoming URI/payload, outgoing status code
  • Header add: jaise X-Request-ID
  • Turnaround time measure
  • Static resources (/static/*, logo.png, favicon.ico, /error) bhi filters se guzarte hain, controller tak kabhi nahi jaate
Yaad rakhoFilters Jakarta Servlet API se aate hain, Spring core se nahi. Tomcat (servlet container) unhe manage karta hai.

Filter interface (jakarta.servlet)

Q85

  • init(): filter instance bante waqt container startup pe ek baar
  • doFilter(): har request pe; pre + post processing yahin
  • destroy(): container shutdown/undeploy pe ek baar, cleanup ke liye
  • Params generic ServletRequest hain (non-HTTP protocols ke liye bhi), isliye HttpServletRequest mein cast karo tabhi getHeader(), getMethod(), getRequestURI(), setStatus() milenge
  • chain.doFilter(req, res) = agle filter ko do (last ho to DispatcherServlet)
  • Chain se pehle ka code = pre-processing, baad ka = post-processing
Filter 1→chain.doFilter()→Filter 2→chain.doFilter()→DispatcherServlet
public interface Filter {
    default void init(FilterConfig cfg) throws ServletException {}   // startup pe ek baar
    void doFilter(ServletRequest req, ServletResponse res, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException;                    // har request pe
    default void destroy() {}                                       // shutdown pe ek baar
}

Example 1: LoggingFilter (try-finally)

Q86

@Component
@Order(2)
public class LoggingFilter implements Filter {
    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        HttpServletRequest req = (HttpServletRequest) request;
        HttpServletResponse res = (HttpServletResponse) response;

        long start = System.currentTimeMillis();
        res.setHeader("X-Request-ID", UUID.randomUUID().toString()); // header PEHLE set
        System.out.println("Incoming: " + req.getMethod() + " " + req.getRequestURI());
        try {
            chain.doFilter(request, response);       // aage bhejo
        } finally {                                  // exception aaye tab bhi chalega
            long duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - start;
            System.out.println("Response Status: " + res.getStatus());
            System.out.println("API Turnaround Time: " + duration + " ms");
        }
    }
}

// Console:
// Incoming: GET /api/students
// Response Status: 200
// API Turnaround Time: 12 ms
Dhyan doHeader chain se pehle kyun? Controller ke likhne ke baad response committed ho jaata hai (read-only). Baad mein set kiya header chupchaap gum ho jaata hai.

Example 2: AuthenticationFilter (short-circuit)

Video #20 mein isi ka chhota version hai: sirf token header check, fail hone pe 401 + body {"message": "Authentication Is Required"} likh ke return. Matlab filter status code aur body dono khud bana ke wahin se lauta sakta hai. Q87

@Component
@Order(1)   // sabse pehle
public class AuthenticationFilter implements Filter {
    private static final String AUTH_TOKEN = "12345";
    private static final String API_KEY = "Secret123";

    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        HttpServletRequest req = (HttpServletRequest) request;
        HttpServletResponse res = (HttpServletResponse) response;

        String token = req.getHeader("Token");
        String apiKey = req.getHeader("X-API-Key");

        if (token == null || !AUTH_TOKEN.equals(token)) {
            res.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED);   // 401, sirf status
            return;   // chain.doFilter NAHI bulaya -> request yahin ruk gayi
        }
        if (apiKey == null || !API_KEY.equals(apiKey)) {
            res.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED);   // 401 + JSON body
            res.setContentType("application/json");
            res.getWriter().write("{\"message\": \"Invalid or missing API Key\"}");
            return;
        }
        chain.doFilter(request, response);   // dono sahi -> aage jaane do
    }
}

Ordering: @Order

Q88

  • Kam number = pehle chalega (request side)
  • Response side pe ulta order
  • Auth @Order(1), logging @Order(2): unauthorized request pe logging/business kaam waste na ho
  • Order na do to sequence guaranteed nahi, machine-to-machine badal sakta hai
  • FilterRegistrationBean.setOrder() bhi yahi karta hai
@Component
@Order(1) // PEHLE: security / authentication
public class AuthenticationFilter implements Filter { ... }

@Component
@Order(2) // BAAD MEIN: logging / turnaround metrics
public class LoggingFilter implements Filter { ... }

Filter summary (video #19)

FeatureFilter ka behaviour
LayerServlet container (DispatcherServlet se pehle)
SpecificationJakarta Servlet API (jakarta.servlet.Filter)
Handler contextRaw request/response, target controller ka pata nahi
Execution controlchain.doFilter() na bula ke return = short-circuit
Ordering@Order(n)
Use casesAuth, request/response logging, correlation ID (X-Request-ID), timing, encoding

Video #20: Response ko modify karna

Response ke 3 hisse: status code, headers, body. Teeno filter se badal sakte hain, par sab badalna achhi practice nahi. Pehle header, sirf header wala filter:

@Component
public class ResponseHeaderFilter implements Filter {
    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        HttpServletResponse httpResponse = (HttpServletResponse) response;  // 1. cast
        String requestId = UUID.randomUUID().toString();                   // 2. random ID
        httpResponse.setHeader("X-Request-ID", requestId);                 // 3. chain se PEHLE
        chain.doFilter(request, response);                                 // 4. aage bhejo
    }
}
Dhyan doStream commit state: chain.doFilter() ke andar controller chalne ke baad DispatcherServlet response ko output stream pe likh deta hai, response commit ho jaata hai aur non-editable ban jaata hai. Uske baad set kiya header client tak nahi pahunchega.

Response body badalna (possible, par bad practice)

Q89

@Component
public class ResponseBodyFilter implements Filter {
    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        var wrapped = new ContentCachingResponseWrapper((HttpServletResponse) response);
        chain.doFilter(request, wrapped);          // controller buffer mein likhega

        String original = new String(wrapped.getContentAsByteArray(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        String modified = """
            {
                "originalResponse": %s,
                "appName": "Student Management System"
            }
            """.formatted(original);                 // Java 15+ text block

        wrapped.resetBuffer();                     // warna body do baar jaayegi
        wrapped.getWriter().write(modified);
        wrapped.copyBodyToResponse();              // asli response mein copy
    }
}
Common galtiYe kaam karta hai (decorator pattern), par response ka contract controller/service ka hai. Filter mein body badalna bad practice hai.

Request body padhna: bada bug

Request ke 4 hisse: HTTP method, URI (/api/students), headers + query params, body (JSON).

HttpServletRequest read-only hai: getHeader("token"), getParameter("id"), getMethod(), getRequestURI() hain, par setHeader() / setParam() / setURI() jaise setters exist hi nahi karte. Kyun? Client ki bheji request hi final contract hai; filter ko use manmaane dhang se badalne ka haq nahi.

getBody() bhi nahi hai. Body sirf stream (getInputStream() = raw bytes, getReader() = BufferedReader) ke roop mein milti hai, kyunki Tomcat ko nahi pata wo JSON hai, image hai ya 2 GB video. Stream ek behti nadi jaisi hai: ek baar padh li to khatam. Q90

// BUG: filter ne body padh li
BufferedReader reader = httpRequest.getReader();
String line; StringBuilder body = new StringBuilder();
while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) body.append(line);
System.out.println("Body: " + body);
chain.doFilter(request, response);
// Postman: 500 Internal Server Error
// java.lang.IllegalStateException: getReader() has already been called for this request
// Kyun? Aage DispatcherServlet mein Jackson JSON ko StudentDTO banane aaya, stream khaali mili.
Yaad rakhoSafe tarika: ContentCachingRequestWrapper se wrap karo aur log chain ke baad getContentAsByteArray() se karo. Passwords/tokens mask karna mat bhoolo.

FilterRegistrationBean: sirf kuch URLs pe

Q91

@Configuration
public class FilterConfig {
    @Bean
    public FilterRegistrationBean<DummyFilter> dummyFilterBean() {
        var reg = new FilterRegistrationBean<DummyFilter>();
        reg.setFilter(new DummyFilter());          // filter instance (@Component NAHI)
        reg.setOrder(1);
        reg.addUrlPatterns("/api/*", "/admin/*");  // sirf inpe chalega
        return reg;
    }
}
Common galtiSame class pe @Component bhi aur FilterRegistrationBean bhi = filter do baar register. Ek hi tarika chuno.

OncePerRequestFilter (Spring ka better filter)

Q92

  • Servlet API ki jagah Spring ki abstract class
  • No manual typecasting: direct HttpServletRequest milta hai
  • Guaranteed single execution: forward/error dispatch mein bhi ek hi baar chalega
  • shouldNotFilter() se paths (jaise /public/*) clean tareeke se bypass
@Component
public class SpringDemoFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {
    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,
                                    FilterChain filterChain) throws ServletException, IOException {
        System.out.println("Executing OncePerRequestFilter");   // casting ki zarurat nahi
        filterChain.doFilter(request, response);
    }
    @Override
    protected boolean shouldNotFilter(HttpServletRequest request) {
        return !request.getRequestURI().startsWith("/api/");    // true = skip
    }
}

✅ Review questions (10): ab khud check karo

Q83

What cross-cutting problem do Filters solve, and why not put that logic in controllers?

Main Definition

  • Tasks like request logging, authentication, request ID generation, response header changes and turnaround time measurement are needed for every endpoint.
  • Writing them in each controller breaks SRP, duplicates code and couples business logic with infrastructure, and even a helper class must still be called from every method.
  • Filters (and Interceptors) put this logic at one common entry point.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Logging, token check, request ID, response time ये काम हर API में चाहिए।
  • हर controller में ये code लिखना duplicate और गंदा है, helper class बनाओ तब भी हर method में call करना पड़ता है।
  • Filter एक gate की तरह है जहाँ से हर request गुज़रती है, वहीं ये काम एक बार कर दो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Logging (verb, URI, headers)
  • Authentication / API key
  • X-Request-ID tracing
  • Response headers
  • Turnaround time
Q84

Where do Filters sit in the request flow, and what can they do? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Filters run at the Servlet container level, before the DispatcherServlet.
  • A request goes Filter 1 → Filter 2 → Filter 3 → DispatcherServlet → Controller → Service → Repository, and the response returns in reverse order.
  • Since HandlerMapping has not run yet, filters see only the raw request and do not know which controller will handle it, which makes them ideal for global tasks.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Filter Tomcat level पर DispatcherServlet से पहले चलते हैं।
  • Request 1-2-3 order में filters से जाती है और response उल्टे order 3-2-1 में वापस आता है।
  • Filter को नहीं पता कि आगे कौन सा controller चलेगा, इसलिए ये global कामों के लिए हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Headers, cookies, params, token, URI inspect
  • Unauthorized request ko wahin block (short-circuit)
  • Request/response logging, status log
  • X-Request-ID jaise headers add
  • Timing
  • Static resources (/static, favicon.ico, /error) bhi filters se guzarte hain
Important 31 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q81)★ Important listAgla important (Q86) → ★
Q85

What is the Filter interface, its lifecycle, and how does FilterChain.doFilter work?

Main Definition

  • jakarta.servlet.Filter comes from the Jakarta Servlet API and has init(FilterConfig) (once at startup), doFilter(request, response, chain) (every request) and destroy() (once at shutdown).
  • The parameters are generic ServletRequest/ServletResponse, so you cast them to HttpServletRequest/HttpServletResponse for HTTP methods.
  • Calling chain.doFilter(request, response) passes control to the next filter, or to the DispatcherServlet if it is the last one.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Filter Spring का नहीं, Jakarta Servlet API का interface है।
  • doFilter हर request पर चलता है, और chain.doFilter() बुलाने पर request अगले filter या आखिर में DispatcherServlet तक जाती है।
  • ServletRequest को HttpServletRequest में cast करना पड़ता है ताकि getHeader जैसे methods मिलें।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Filter 1→chain.doFilter()→Filter 2→chain.doFilter()→DispatcherServlet
package jakarta.servlet;

public interface Filter {
    default void init(FilterConfig filterConfig) throws ServletException {}
    void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException;
    default void destroy() {}
}

// doFilter ke andar
HttpServletRequest httpRequest = (HttpServletRequest) request;
HttpServletResponse httpResponse = (HttpServletResponse) response;
Yaad rakhochain.doFilter() se pehle ka code = pre-processing (request jaate waqt). Uske baad ka code = post-processing (response lautte waqt).
Q86

How do you write a logging filter that measures response time and adds a request ID? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Record the start time and set headers like X-Request-ID before calling chain.doFilter(...).
  • Put chain.doFilter(...) in a try block and log status and duration in finally, so metrics are recorded even if a controller throws.
  • Headers must be set before the chain because once the response is committed after downstream processing, it becomes read-only and later headers are lost.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Start time और X-Request-ID header chain.doFilter() से पहले set करो।
  • chain.doFilter() को try में और time का log finally में रखो ताकि exception में भी log हो।
  • बाद में header लगाओगे तो response commit हो चुका होगा और header client तक नहीं पहुंचेगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Component
@Order(2)
public class LoggingFilter implements Filter {

    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        HttpServletRequest httpRequest = (HttpServletRequest) request;
        HttpServletResponse httpResponse = (HttpServletResponse) response;

        long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis();
        httpResponse.setHeader("X-Request-ID", UUID.randomUUID().toString()); // pehle hi set
        System.out.println("Incoming: " + httpRequest.getMethod() + " " + httpRequest.getRequestURI());

        try {
            chain.doFilter(request, response);
        } finally {
            long duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime;
            System.out.println("Status: " + httpResponse.getStatus() + ", time: " + duration + " ms");
        }
    }
}
Important 32 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q84)★ Important listAgla important (Q87) → ★
Q87

How does an authentication filter short-circuit a request? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • The filter reads headers such as Token and X-API-Key and validates them.
  • If validation fails, it sets 401 Unauthorized (HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED), optionally writes a JSON body, and returns without calling chain.doFilter(...).
  • This short-circuit means the request never reaches the DispatcherServlet or any controller.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Token गलत या missing हो तो filter वहीं 401 set करके return कर देता है।
  • chain.doFilter() नहीं बुलाया तो request आगे controller तक जाती ही नहीं, इसे short-circuit कहते हैं।
  • जैसे building का guard बिना ID card वाले को gate पर ही रोक दे।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Component
@Order(1)
public class AuthenticationFilter implements Filter {
    private static final String AUTH_TOKEN = "12345";
    private static final String API_KEY = "Secret123";

    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        HttpServletRequest req = (HttpServletRequest) request;
        HttpServletResponse res = (HttpServletResponse) response;

        if (!AUTH_TOKEN.equals(req.getHeader("Token"))) {
            res.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED);   // 401
            res.setContentType("application/json");
            res.getWriter().write("{\"message\": \"Authentication Is Required\"}");
            return;                                               // short-circuit
        }
        if (!API_KEY.equals(req.getHeader("X-API-Key"))) {
            res.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED);
            res.setContentType("application/json");
            res.getWriter().write("{\"message\": \"Invalid or missing API Key\"}");
            return;
        }
        chain.doFilter(request, response);
    }
}
Dhyan doYe demo ke liye theek hai. Real production auth (JWT, roles) ke liye Spring Security use karo, jo khud ek filter chain hi hai.
Important 33 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q86)★ Important listAgla important (Q93) → ★
Q88

How are multiple filters ordered, and why does the order matter?

Main Definition

  • Filters registered as @Component beans can be ordered with @Order(n), and a lower number runs first on the way in.
  • The authentication filter should be @Order(1) so that unauthorized requests are rejected before logging or business work happens.
  • Without an explicit order, the sequence is not guaranteed and can differ between machines or deployments.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Order(1) वाला filter पहले चलता है, फिर @Order(2) वाला।
  • Auth filter सबसे पहले रखो ताकि गलत request logging या business logic तक पहुंचे ही नहीं।
  • Order न दो तो sequence fixed नहीं रहता, अलग machine पर अलग हो सकता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Kam number = pehle (request side)
  • Response side par ulta order
  • Auth pehle, logging baad mein
  • FilterRegistrationBean.setOrder() bhi same kaam
Q89

Can a filter modify the response body, and should it?

Main Definition

  • Once the controller has written the body, the original response is committed, so you cannot simply append to it.
  • Spring's ContentCachingResponseWrapper (decorator pattern) wraps the response so downstream code writes into a buffer.
  • The filter then reads it, calls resetBuffer(), writes the new body and finally calls copyBodyToResponse().
  • It works, but it is a bad practice, because the response contract should be owned by the controller and service layers.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Controller के बाद response commit हो जाता है, इसलिए सीधा body बदल नहीं सकते।
  • ContentCachingResponseWrapper response पर एक cover चढ़ा देता है जिसमें data buffer में रुकता है और हम उसे edit कर सकते हैं।
  • ये possible है पर bad practice है, response का format controller और service तय करें।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Component
public class ResponseBodyFilter implements Filter {
    @Override
    public void doFilter(ServletRequest request, ServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)
            throws IOException, ServletException {
        ContentCachingResponseWrapper wrapped =
                new ContentCachingResponseWrapper((HttpServletResponse) response);

        chain.doFilter(request, wrapped);                  // downstream wrapper mein likhega

        String originalBody = new String(wrapped.getContentAsByteArray(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        String modifiedBody = """
            {
                "originalResponse": %s,
                "appName": "Student Management System"
            }
            """.formatted(originalBody);

        wrapped.resetBuffer();                             // warna body do baar jaayegi
        wrapped.getWriter().write(modifiedBody);
        wrapped.copyBodyToResponse();                      // asli response mein copy (zaroori!)
    }
}
Dhyan doresetBuffer() bhoole to purana aur naya dono body chale jaate hain. copyBodyToResponse() bhoole to client ko khaali body milti hai.
Q90

Can a filter change or read the incoming request, and why does reading the body cause IllegalStateException?

Main Definition

  • HttpServletRequest is effectively read-only: there are getHeader, getParameter, getMethod and getRequestURI, but no setters, because the client's request is the contract.
  • The body is available only as a stream via getInputStream() or getReader(), since Tomcat does not know whether it is JSON, XML, an image or a 2 GB video.
  • If a filter reads that stream just to log it, the stream is consumed, and later Jackson finds it empty, failing with errors such as IllegalStateException: getReader() has already been called.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Request के headers, params या URI बदलने का कोई setter नहीं है, client ने जो भेजा वो final है।
  • Body एक stream है जो नदी के पानी की तरह एक बार बह गया तो वापस नहीं आता।
  • Filter में body पढ़ ली तो आगे Jackson को खाली stream मिलती है और 500 error आता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Safe tarika (Deep dive)
  • Spring ka ContentCachingRequestWrapper wrap karke chain.doFilter(wrapper, response) karo; jab Jackson body padhta hai to copy cache ho jaati hai. Log chain ke BAAD getContentAsByteArray() se karo.
  • Chain se PEHLE body chahiye to custom HttpServletRequestWrapper banao jo bytes ek baar padh kar getInputStream() har baar naya stream de.
  • Body logging mein passwords/tokens mask karo.
// BUG: body padh li, aage Jackson ke liye kuch nahi bacha
BufferedReader reader = httpRequest.getReader();
StringBuilder body = new StringBuilder();
String line;
while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) body.append(line);
System.out.println("Request Body: " + body);
chain.doFilter(request, response);   // -> 500 IllegalStateException
Q91

How do you register a filter with FilterRegistrationBean and limit it to URL patterns?

Main Definition

  • Instead of @Component, you can declare a FilterRegistrationBean<T> @Bean inside a @Configuration class.
  • It sets the filter instance, the order (setOrder(1)) and the URL patterns (addUrlPatterns("/api/*", "/admin/*")).
  • The filter then runs only for matching URLs, which is the cleanest way to scope a servlet filter.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Component की जगह config class में FilterRegistrationBean बनाकर filter register कर सकते हो।
  • इसमें order और URL patterns दोनों दे सकते हो।
  • addUrlPatterns("/api/*") देने पर filter सिर्फ़ /api वाले URLs पर चलेगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Configuration
public class FilterConfig {
    @Bean
    public FilterRegistrationBean<DummyFilter> dummyFilterBean() {
        FilterRegistrationBean<DummyFilter> reg = new FilterRegistrationBean<>();
        reg.setFilter(new DummyFilter());
        reg.setOrder(1);
        reg.addUrlPatterns("/api/*", "/admin/*");
        return reg;
    }
}
Dhyan doSame filter class par @Component bhi lagaya aur FilterRegistrationBean bhi banaya to wo do baar register ho sakta hai. Ek hi tarika chuno.
Q92

What is OncePerRequestFilter, and why is it preferred in Spring?

Main Definition

  • OncePerRequestFilter is a Spring abstract class implementing Filter.
  • You override doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse, FilterChain), so no casting is needed, and Spring guarantees a single execution per request even across internal forwards or error dispatches.
  • It also offers shouldNotFilter(request) to skip specific paths cleanly.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • OncePerRequestFilter Spring की class है जिसमें सीधा HttpServletRequest मिलता है, cast करने की ज़रूरत नहीं।
  • ये guarantee देता है कि एक request में filter सिर्फ़ एक बार चले।
  • shouldNotFilter() से बता सकते हो कि किन URLs पर filter skip करना है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)

public class SpringDemoFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {

    @Override

                                    HttpServletResponse response,

        System.out.println("Executing OncePerRequestFilter");

15. Interceptors

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein Filters dekhe, jo DispatcherServlet se pehle chalte hain aur raw request dekhte hain. Unki limitation: target controller ka pata nahi. Interceptor yahi gap bharta hai.
📖 Notes

Filters ke hote hue Interceptor kyun?

HandlerInterceptor Spring MVC level pe chalta hai: DispatcherServlet ne handler dhoondh liya, uske baad aur controller se pehle. Isliye use target HandlerMethod (controller class + method) milta hai. Q93

Filter vs Interceptor

Client / Postman→Tomcat→Filter chain (raw)→DispatcherServlet→Interceptor chain (HandlerMethod)→Controller→Service→Repository
FilterInterceptor
LevelServlet containerSpring MVC
TechnologyJakarta Servlet API (jakarta.servlet.Filter)Spring MVC (org.springframework.web.servlet.HandlerInterceptor)
KabDispatcherServlet se pehle (Tomcat aur Dispatcher ke beech)DispatcherServlet ke baad, controller se pehle
Controller ka pata?NahiHaan (HandlerMethod)
MethodsdoFilter(req, res, chain)preHandle, postHandle, afterCompletion

Kaise kaam karta hai

Q94

  1. DispatcherServlet HandlerMapping se handler leta hai
  2. Har interceptor ka preHandle() order mein; koi false de to wahin stop (short-circuit)
  3. HandlerAdapter controller chalata hai
  4. postHandle(): controller ke baad, view render/response likhne se pehle (ulta order)
  5. View render hota hai (MVC) ya Jackson JSON likhta hai (@RestController)
  6. afterCompletion(): poori request khatam hone ke baad (ulta order): cleanup, exception, metrics
Yaad rakhoController exception phenke to postHandle() nahi chalta, par afterCompletion() chalta hai (agar us interceptor ka preHandle true tha).

HandlerInterceptor interface

Teeno default hain, jo chahiye wahi override karo. Q95

MethodKabUse
preHandleController se pehle; true = aage, false = turant ruk jaoAuth/authorization check, params/URI nikalna, start timer
postHandleController ke baad, view render se pehleJSP/HTML apps mein ModelAndView ke model attributes badalna (REST mein ModelAndView = null)
afterCompletionPoori lifecycle khatam, response ban gayaTotal time, status log, ThreadLocal cleanup; ex = unhandled exception (agar global handler ne nahi pakdi)
public interface HandlerInterceptor {
    default boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res,
                              Object handler) throws Exception { return true; }
    default void postHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler,
                            @Nullable ModelAndView mav) throws Exception {}
    default void afterCompletion(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler,
                                 @Nullable Exception ex) throws Exception {}
}

// handler = Spring MVC ka chuna hua target; controllers ke liye HandlerMethod
if (handler instanceof HandlerMethod hm) {
    String controller = hm.getBeanType().getName();      // poora naam: com.x.StudentController
    // getSimpleName() -> sirf "StudentController"
    String method = hm.getMethod().getName();            // "getStudentById"
    System.out.println("Executing Controller: " + controller);
    System.out.println("Executing Method: " + method);
}

Register karna zaroori hai

Sirf @Component lagane se interceptor kuch nahi karta. WebMvcConfigurer mein register karo. Q96

PatternMatch karta hai
/api/students (exact)Sirf yahi path
/api/*/api/ ke baad ek level (/api/students)
/api/Saare nested paths (/api/students/5/marks)
@Configuration
public class WebConfig implements WebMvcConfigurer {
    private final LoggingInterceptor loggingInterceptor;
    private final AuthorizationInterceptor authInterceptor;

    public WebConfig(LoggingInterceptor l, AuthorizationInterceptor a) {
        this.loggingInterceptor = l; this.authInterceptor = a;
    }

    @Override
    public void addInterceptors(InterceptorRegistry registry) {
        registry.addInterceptor(authInterceptor)
                .addPathPatterns("/api/**")
                .excludePathPatterns("/api/auth/login", "/api/public/**")
                .order(1);
        registry.addInterceptor(loggingInterceptor)
                .addPathPatterns("/api/**")
                .order(2);
    }
}
Dhyan doVideo mein auth interceptor ka naam AuthenticationInterceptor hai, example mein AuthorizationInterceptor. Naam koi bhi ho, register wahi bean karo jo bana hai.

Example: Logging + Authorization interceptor

Q97

@Component
public class LoggingInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {
    @Override
    public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler) {
        req.setAttribute("startTime", System.currentTimeMillis());   // timer request mein rakho
        System.out.println("--- Incoming Request ---");
        System.out.println("HTTP Method: " + req.getMethod());
        System.out.println("Request URI: " + req.getRequestURI());
        System.out.println("Query Parameters: " + req.getQueryString());
        System.out.println("Client IP: " + req.getRemoteAddr());
        if (handler instanceof HandlerMethod hm) {
            System.out.println("Controller: " + hm.getBeanType().getSimpleName());
            System.out.println("Method: " + hm.getMethod().getName());
        }
        return true;   // chain aage chalne do
    }
    @Override
    public void afterCompletion(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res,
                                Object handler, Exception ex) {
        long duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - (Long) req.getAttribute("startTime");
        System.out.println("Response Status: " + res.getStatus());
        System.out.println("Total Execution Time: " + duration + " ms");
        if (ex != null) System.out.println("Exception Occurred: " + ex.getMessage());
    }
}

@Component
public class AuthorizationInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {
    @Override
    public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler)
            throws Exception {
        String role = req.getHeader("X-User-Role");
        if (role == null || !"ADMIN".equalsIgnoreCase(role)) {
            res.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_FORBIDDEN);          // 403
            res.setContentType("application/json");
            res.getWriter().write(
                "{\"error\": \"Forbidden: You are not authorized to perform this action\"}");
            return false;                                             // short-circuit
        }
        return true;
    }
}

Sample console output

--- Incoming Request ---
HTTP Method: GET
Request URI: /api/students/5
Query Parameters: null
Client IP: 127.0.0.1
Controller: StudentController
Method: getStudentById
Response Status: 200
Total Execution Time: 14 ms

Kab kya use karo

  • Filter: low-level global kaam: CORS, raw body wrapping, global logging, security
  • Interceptor: controller-aware kaam: kaunsa method chala, role check per path
  • Production authentication ke liye Spring Security use karo (wo khud filters pe bana hai); manual auth chhote projects ke liye theek
  • preHandle mein return false se pehle sahi status (401/403) aur body likh do, warna client ko khaali 200 milega
Common galtiInterceptor bana ke register karna bhool jaana; ya 401/403 set karke return true kar dena (request phir bhi controller tak chali jaayegi).
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Interceptor = Spring MVC level, DispatcherServlet ke baad
  • Use HandlerMethod milta hai (controller + method)
  • preHandle false = short-circuit
  • Exception pe postHandle skip, afterCompletion chalta hai
  • WebMvcConfigurer.addInterceptors mein register zaroori
  • /api/* ek level, /api/ sab nested

✅ Review questions (5): ab khud check karo

Q93

Why do we need Interceptors when Filters exist, and how do they differ? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Filters run before the DispatcherServlet and cannot know the target controller.
  • A HandlerInterceptor runs at the Spring MVC level, after the DispatcherServlet has resolved the handler and before the controller runs.
  • It therefore has access to the target HandlerMethod, meaning the controller class and method.
  • Use filters for global infrastructure and interceptors for controller-aware logic.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Filter को नहीं पता कौन सा controller चलेगा, पर Interceptor DispatcherServlet के बाद चलता है तो उसे controller class और method दोनों पता होते हैं।
  • Filter Tomcat level का है, Interceptor Spring MVC level का।
  • Global काम filter में, controller से जुड़ा काम interceptor में।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
FeatureServlet FilterHandlerInterceptor
SourceJakarta Servlet API (jakarta.servlet.Filter)Spring MVC (org.springframework.web.servlet)
Kab chaltaDispatcherServlet se pehleDispatcherServlet ke baad, controller se pehle
ContextRaw request/response, controller unknownHandlerMethod (class + method) pata
MethodsdoFilter(req, res, chain)preHandle, postHandle, afterCompletion
FocusRaw logging, CORS, security, encodingController-specific logic, fine metrics, model tweaks
Important 34 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q87)★ Important listAgla important (Q95) → ★
Q94

What is the request flow inside the DispatcherServlet with interceptors?

Main Definition

  • The DispatcherServlet first asks HandlerMapping for the handler and then calls each interceptor's preHandle() in order.
  • If any returns false, processing stops (short-circuit).
  • Otherwise the HandlerAdapter runs the controller, then postHandle() runs before view rendering or response writing.
  • Finally afterCompletion() runs after the whole request is complete.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पहले HandlerMapping controller ढूंढता है, फिर हर interceptor का preHandle चलता है।
  • कोई false लौटाए तो request वहीं रुक जाती है।
  • Controller के बाद postHandle और सब पूरा होने पर afterCompletion चलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
HandlerMapping→preHandle() (true/false)→Controller (HandlerAdapter)→postHandle()→View render / JSON→afterCompletion()
Yaad rakhoController exception phenke to postHandle() nahi chalta, lekin afterCompletion() chalta hai (agar us interceptor ka preHandle true laut chuka tha).
Q95

Explain preHandle, postHandle and afterCompletion, and how to get the controller details. ★ Important

Main Definition

  • All three methods of HandlerInterceptor are default methods, so you override only what you need.
  • preHandle returns a boolean (true to continue, false to stop) and suits auth checks and start timers.
  • postHandle gets a ModelAndView that is null for REST controllers.
  • afterCompletion gets the Exception (if unhandled) and suits total time, status logging and ThreadLocal cleanup.
  • Cast Object handler to HandlerMethod to read getBeanType() and getMethod().getName().

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • preHandle controller से पहले चलता है और true/false से तय करता है कि आगे जाना है या नहीं।
  • postHandle controller के बाद view render से पहले चलता है, REST में उसका ModelAndView null होता है।
  • afterCompletion सबसे आखिर में चलता है, total time और cleanup के लिए।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
MethodKabUse
preHandleController se pehleAuth/authorization, params padhna, start time
postHandleController ke baad, view se pehleModel attributes badalna (JSP apps); REST mein modelAndView null
afterCompletionPoori request ke baadTotal time, status log, exception log, ThreadLocal cleanup
public interface HandlerInterceptor {
    default boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res,
                              Object handler) throws Exception { return true; }
    default void postHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler,
                            @Nullable ModelAndView modelAndView) throws Exception {}
    default void afterCompletion(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler,
                                 @Nullable Exception ex) throws Exception {}
}

// handler se controller details
if (handler instanceof HandlerMethod hm) {
    String controller = hm.getBeanType().getSimpleName();
    String method = hm.getMethod().getName();
}

Q96

How do you register an interceptor with WebMvcConfigurer and path patterns?

Main Definition

  • An interceptor annotated with @Component does nothing until it is registered in a @Configuration class that implements WebMvcConfigurer and overrides addInterceptors(InterceptorRegistry).
  • There you set addPathPatterns, excludePathPatterns and order.
  • In patterns, /api/* matches one level and /api/ matches all nested paths.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • सिर्फ़ @Component लगाने से interceptor नहीं चलता, उसे WebMvcConfigurer की addInterceptors() में register करना पड़ता है।
  • वहीं बताओ किन paths पर चलना है, किन पर नहीं, और order क्या है।
  • /api/* एक level match करता है, /api/ अंदर के सारे paths।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PatternMatch
/api/studentsSirf exact path
/api/*/api/ ke baad ek level
/api//api/ ke neeche saare nested paths
@Configuration
public class WebConfig implements WebMvcConfigurer {
    private final LoggingInterceptor loggingInterceptor;
    private final AuthorizationInterceptor authInterceptor;

    public WebConfig(LoggingInterceptor l, AuthorizationInterceptor a) {
        this.loggingInterceptor = l;
        this.authInterceptor = a;
    }

    @Override
    public void addInterceptors(InterceptorRegistry registry) {
        registry.addInterceptor(authInterceptor)
                .addPathPatterns("/api/**")
                .excludePathPatterns("/api/auth/login", "/api/public/**")
                .order(1);
        registry.addInterceptor(loggingInterceptor)
                .addPathPatterns("/api/**")
                .order(2);
    }
}
Q97

Write a logging/metrics interceptor and a role-based authorization interceptor.

Main Definition

  • A logging interceptor stores the start time with request.setAttribute(...) in preHandle, logs method, URI, query string, client IP and controller details, and computes the duration and status in afterCompletion.
  • An authorization interceptor checks a header like X-User-Role.
  • If the role is not ADMIN, it writes 403 Forbidden with a JSON body and returns false to stop the chain.
  • For production auth, prefer Spring Security.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Logging interceptor preHandle में start time request attribute में रखता है और afterCompletion में total time निकालता है।
  • Authorization interceptor role check करता है और ADMIN न हो तो 403 लिखकर false लौटा देता है।
  • असली production auth के लिए Spring Security use करो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Best practices
  1. Global infrastructure (raw body wrapping, CORS, global logging, security headers) ke liye Filters.
  2. Controller/method metadata par depend karne wale logic aur fine-grained metrics ke liye Interceptors.
  3. Production auth/authorization ke liye Spring Security; manual filter/interceptor sirf basic projects ke liye.
  4. preHandle se false lautane se pehle sahi status (401 ya 403) aur body likh do, warna client ko khaali 200 milega.
@Component
public class LoggingInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {
    @Override
    public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler) {
        req.setAttribute("startTime", System.currentTimeMillis());
        System.out.println(req.getMethod() + " " + req.getRequestURI()
            + " ?" + req.getQueryString() + " from " + req.getRemoteAddr());
        if (handler instanceof HandlerMethod hm) {
            System.out.println("Controller: " + hm.getBeanType().getSimpleName()
                + ", method: " + hm.getMethod().getName());
        }
        return true;
    }

    @Override
    public void afterCompletion(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res,
                                Object handler, Exception ex) {
        long duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - (Long) req.getAttribute("startTime");
        System.out.println("Status: " + res.getStatus() + ", time: " + duration + " ms");
        if (ex != null) System.out.println("Exception: " + ex.getMessage());
    }
}

@Component
public class AuthorizationInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {
    @Override
    public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler)
            throws Exception {
        String role = req.getHeader("X-User-Role");
        if (!"ADMIN".equalsIgnoreCase(role)) {
            res.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_FORBIDDEN);   // 403
            res.setContentType("application/json");
            res.getWriter().write("{\"error\": \"Forbidden: You are not authorized\"}");
            return false;                                      // stop
        }
        return true;
    }
}

Part 4: Spring AOP

16. AOP basics

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic (Interceptors) mein humne dekha ki Interceptor sirf Controller calls ko wrap karta hai. Par agar logging/timing hume Service, Repository, Helper — kisi bhi bean ke method pe chahiye ho to? Yahin se AOP ki entry hoti hai.
📖 Notes

Teen layers: Filter vs Interceptor vs AOP

Request ka safar yaad karo. Har layer pe ek 'wrapper' laga sakte ho, bas level alag hai:

Request→Filter (Servlet level)→DispatcherServlet→Interceptor (MVC level)→Controller→AOP (Service / koi bhi bean)
CheezKahan kaam karti haiKya wrap karti hai
FilterServlet container, DispatcherServlet se pehleRaw HTTP request/response
InterceptorSpring MVC, DispatcherServlet aur Controller ke beechController (handler) calls
AOPPoori Spring applicationKisi bhi bean ka koi bhi method — web request ho ya na ho
Yaad rakhoFilter = HTTP level, Interceptor = Controller level, AOP = method level (har bean). Detail: Q98

Problem: Business logic vs Infrastructure logic

Socho tumhare paas createStudent() hai. Asli kaam sirf ek line ka hai: studentRepository.save(student). Ye business logic hai.

Par production mein usi method mein aur bhi bahut kuch chahiye: method ka naam aur params log karo, time measure karo, role/permission check karo, caching, auditing. Ye sab infrastructure (supporting) logic hai — aur ye Student, Payment, Order sab jagah same hota hai.

Result? 1 line ka method 20+ lines ka ho jata hai. Padhne wale ko asli business line dhoondhni padti hai.

public void createStudent(Student student) {
    long start = System.currentTimeMillis();          // infra: timing
    log.info("createStudent called with {}", student); // infra: logging
    if (!currentUser.hasRole("ADMIN")) throw new AccessDeniedException("..."); // infra: security

    studentRepository.save(student);                   // ASLI business logic (sirf ye 1 line!)

    log.info("createStudent took {} ms", System.currentTimeMillis() - start); // infra
}

Vertical vs Horizontal (Cross-cutting) concerns

  • Vertical concern = domain ka kaam — StudentService ke create/update, PaymentService ke pay/refund. Ye apni class ke andar 'khade' (vertically) rehte hain.
  • Horizontal / Cross-cutting concern = Logging, Security, Metrics, Auditing — ye har service ko 'aadha kaatte' hue horizontally guzarte hain.
  • Analogy: ek building ke har floor (Student, Payment, Order) alag hai, par bijli ki wiring aur CCTV har floor se guzarte hain. Wiring har floor ki deewar mein haath se mat banao — ek central system lagao.

Do bimaariyan: Code Scattering aur Code Tangling

ProblemMatlabExample
Code ScatteringSame infra code sau classes mein bikhra huaHar service mein same logStart/logEnd
Code TanglingEk hi method mein kai unrelated concerns uljhe hueauth + timing + logging + DB ek method mein
Dhyan doScattering = *bahut jagah*, Tangling = *ek jagah bahut kuch*. Dono cross-cutting concerns ki wajah se hote hain. Q99

Purane solutions aur kyon fail hote hain

  1. Helper/Utility class (LoggingServiceUtil.logStart(...)): code thoda chhota, par har method mein call likhna padta hai — bhool gaye to log gayab. Method abhi bhi bulky.
  2. Inheritance (extends BaseLoggingService): phir bhi super.logStart() khud call karna padta hai, aur class tightly coupled ho jati hai (Java mein ek hi parent!).
  3. Decorator pattern: ek wrapper class jo same interface implement kare (Is-A) aur andar asli object rakhe (Has-A), pehle/baad mein infra chalaye aur beech mein delegate kare. Business class ekdum clean! Par...

Decorator pattern — code (video wala example)

public interface StudentService {
    void createStudent(Student student);
}

@Service
public class StudentServiceIMPL implements StudentService {
    private final StudentRepository studentRepository;
    public StudentServiceIMPL(StudentRepository repo) { this.studentRepository = repo; }

    @Override
    public void createStudent(Student student) {
        studentRepository.save(student); // sirf business logic
    }
}

@Component
@Primary // Controller ko IMPL ki jagah ye wrapper inject hoga
public class LoggingDecorator implements StudentService {
    private final StudentServiceIMPL target;
    public LoggingDecorator(StudentServiceIMPL target) { this.target = target; }

    @Override
    public void createStudent(Student student) {
        LoggingServiceUtil.logStart("StudentServiceIMPL", "createStudent"); // pehle
        target.createStudent(student);                                       // asli kaam
        LoggingServiceUtil.logEnd("StudentServiceIMPL", "createStudent");   // baad mein
    }
}
Common galtiBade system mein har service ke liye haath se decorator likhna, phir ExecutionTimeDecorator → LoggingDecorator → IMPL ki chain aur @Primary manage karna — bahut error-prone. Isi ka automatic version AOP hai. Q100

Solution: Spring AOP = automatic decorator/proxy

Spring AOP wahi decorator runtime pe khud bana deta hai. Tum sirf infra logic ek jagah (Aspect) mein likho aur bata do kahan lagana hai. Spring target bean ke upar ek Proxy banata hai aur Controller ko wahi proxy de deta hai.

OOP domain entities (Student, Payment, Order) pe focus karta hai; AOP cross-cutting concerns (logging, security, timing) pe.

AOP ke 3 sawaal: WHAT, WHERE, WHEN

SawaalAOP termExample
WHAT — kya chalana hai?Advice ka body (Aspect method)Logging, timing, security check
WHERE — kahan lagana hai?PointcutService package ke saare methods
WHEN — kab chalana hai?Advice typeMethod se pehle, return ke baad, around

Terminology ek jagah

TermSimple matlab
TargetAsli bean jiska method intercept ho raha hai (StudentService)
ProxySpring ka banaya wrapper object jo target ko gherta hai
AspectCross-cutting logic wali class — @Aspect + @Component
PointcutExpression jo batata hai KAHAN apply karna hai
AdviceKAB aur KYA chalana hai (@Before, @Around ...)
Join PointIntercept hone wala method execution — uska naam, args, metadata
Yaad rakhoSpring AOP mein join point hamesha method execution hota hai (field access ya constructor nahi — wo full AspectJ karta hai). Q101
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Filter = HTTP, Interceptor = Controller, AOP = kisi bhi bean ka method.
  • Business logic = vertical concern; logging/security/timing = horizontal (cross-cutting).
  • Cross-cutting concerns se Code Scattering + Code Tangling hota hai.
  • Helper, inheritance, manual decorator — sab mein boilerplate ya wiring ka dard.
  • AOP = Spring ka automatic decorator: target ke upar Proxy.
  • Aspect (class), Pointcut (where), Advice (when + what), Join Point (method execution), Target (asli bean).

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q98

How do Filters, Interceptors and AOP compare as ways to wrap behaviour?

Main Definition

  • Filters wrap the raw HTTP request at the servlet container level before the DispatcherServlet.
  • Interceptors wrap controller calls at the Spring MVC level.
  • AOP can wrap any Spring bean method (services, repositories, helpers), before, after or around execution, and is not limited to web requests.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Filter raw HTTP request को लपेटता है, Interceptor controller को, और AOP किसी भी Spring bean के method को।
  • AOP web request से बंधा नहीं है, service या repository के method पर भी लग सकता है।
  • तीनों का मकसद एक है: common काम एक जगह रखना।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
FilterInterceptorAOP
LevelServlet containerSpring MVCSpring bean (proxy)
WrapsRaw HTTP requestController handlerKoi bhi bean method
Knows target?NahiHandlerMethodJoinPoint: method, args, target
Typical useAuth, CORS, request loggingController metrics, role checkService logging, timing, auditing, caching, @Transactional
Q99

What are cross-cutting concerns, and how do vertical and horizontal concerns differ?

Main Definition

  • A service method contains business logic (for example studentRepository.save(student)) and infrastructure logic such as logging, timing, permission checks, caching and auditing.
  • Business logic is a vertical concern that lives inside its own domain class (Student, Payment, Order).
  • Infrastructure is a horizontal or cross-cutting concern that spans all of them.
  • Mixing them causes code scattering (the same code repeated across classes) and code tangling (many concerns tangled inside one method).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Business logic हर domain का अपना होता है, ये vertical concern है।
  • Logging, security, timing हर class में चाहिए, ये horizontal यानी cross-cutting concern है।
  • इन्हें मिलाने से एक line का method बीस lines का बन जाता है, code बिखरता (scattering) भी है और उलझता (tangling) भी है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Vertical: StudentService.create(), PaymentService.pay()
  • Horizontal: logging, security, metrics sab classes mein
  • Scattering: same infra code 100 classes mein
  • Tangling: ek method mein auth + timing + log + DB
Q100

Why do helper classes, inheritance and manual decorators fail for cross-cutting concerns?

Main Definition

  • A helper/utility class still needs explicit logStart/logEnd calls in every method and is easy to forget.
  • Inheritance from a BaseLoggingService still requires super.logStart() calls and couples classes.
  • The Decorator pattern (a wrapper that implements the same interface and delegates to the real object, wired with @Primary) keeps the business class clean.
  • However, it needs a hand-written wrapper per service, and chaining several decorators becomes complex and error-prone.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Helper class में भी हर method के अंदर call लिखना पड़ता है और कोई भूल सकता है।
  • Inheritance में भी super.logStart() बुलाना पड़ता है।
  • Decorator pattern साफ़ है पर हर service के लिए हाथ से wrapper class लिखनी पड़ती है, और कई decorators जोड़ना मुश्किल हो जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
public interface StudentService { void createStudent(Student student); }

@Service
public class StudentServiceIMPL implements StudentService {
    private final StudentRepository repo;
    public StudentServiceIMPL(StudentRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }
    public void createStudent(Student s) { repo.save(s); }      // pure business logic
}

@Component
@Primary   // controller ko ye decorator inject hoga
public class LoggingDecorator implements StudentService {
    private final StudentServiceIMPL target;
    public LoggingDecorator(StudentServiceIMPL target) { this.target = target; }

    public void createStudent(Student s) {
        LoggingServiceUtil.logStart("StudentServiceIMPL", "createStudent");
        target.createStudent(s);                                   // delegate
        LoggingServiceUtil.logEnd("StudentServiceIMPL", "createStudent");
    }
}
SochoSpring AOP yahi decorator/wrapper khud runtime par bana deta hai. Isliye AOP ko 'automatic decorator' samjho.
Q101

What is Spring AOP, and what are aspect, advice, pointcut, join point, target and proxy? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Aspect-Oriented Programming separates cross-cutting concerns from business logic by automatically generating proxy wrappers around target beans.
  • An Aspect (@Aspect + @Component) holds the cross-cutting code.
  • A Pointcut says where it applies, an Advice says when and what to run, a Join Point is the method execution being intercepted (with its metadata and args), and the Target is the real bean being wrapped.
  • OOP focuses on domain entities, while AOP focuses on concerns like logging, security and timing.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • AOP वही decorator पैटर्न है जो Spring खुद runtime पर बना देता है।
  • Aspect वो class है जिसमें logging जैसा common code है, pointcut बताता है कहाँ लगाना है, advice बताती है कब और क्या चलाना है।
  • Join point वो method call है जिसे पकड़ा गया, और target असली bean है।

17. Advice types

6 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein AOP ke 3 sawaal dekhe — WHAT, WHERE, WHEN. Ab WHEN ka jawaab: Advice types. Ye decide karte hain ki aspect ka code target method ke pehle, baad, error pe, ya chaaron taraf chalega.
📖 Notes

Pehle setup: dependency

<!-- Spring Boot 3.x -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-aop</artifactId>
</dependency>
Dhyan doVideo mein spring-boot-starter-aspectj bataya gaya hai — wo naam Spring Boot 4 ka hai (rename hua). Boot 3 mein spring-boot-starter-aop hi use karo. Version parent POM manage karta hai. Andar dono AspectJ ke annotations (@Aspect, @Before...) use karte hain, par weaving Spring proxies se hoti hai.

Decorator ya Proxy — Spring AOP kaunsa pattern hai?

Class structure (UML) dono ka lagbhag same hai: wrapper same interface/type ka hai aur andar target rakhta hai. Fark intent ka hai:

Decorator = naya feature jodna (enhance). Proxy = access/lifecycle control karna. Spring internally isse Proxy kehta hai, par hum logging/security jod rahe hain isliye 'decorator jaisa' kehna bhi galat nahi.

Controller→Proxy 2→Proxy 1→Target (StudentService)

5 Advice types — try-catch-finally se samjho

Ye ek analogy poora topic yaad karwa degi. Socho proxy andar se aisa code chala raha hai:

// @Around poore block ko gherta hai
try {
    // 1. @Before  → target se pehle
    Object result = target.method();   // asli method
    // 2. @AfterReturning → sirf success pe
    return result;
} catch (Exception ex) {
    // 3. @AfterThrowing → sirf exception pe
    throw ex;
} finally {
    // 4. @After → HAMESHA (finally jaisa)
}
Yaad rakhoBefore = pehle, AfterReturning = try ka end, AfterThrowing = catch, After = finally, Around = sab kuch. Q102

@Before

  • Target se thik pehle chalta hai. Use: start log, precondition, basic validation/auth check.
  • return likhne se target nahi rukta — target chalega hi.
  • Par agar @Before se exception throw kar do, to target nahi chalega (indirect stop).
  • joinPoint.getArgs() se arguments padh sakte ho, badal nahi sakte (array mein naya object daalna target tak nahi jata).
@Aspect
@Component
public class LoggingAspect {

    @Before("execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.createStudent(..))")
    public void logBefore(JoinPoint jp) {
        System.out.println("A student is going to be saved...");
        Object[] args = jp.getArgs(); // read-only dekhne ke liye
        // throw new RuntimeException("blocked"); // ← aisa kiya to target nahi chalega
    }
}
Real exampleDetail: Q103

@AfterReturning

  • Sirf tab chalta hai jab target successfully return kare.
  • returning = "result" — ye naam advice ke parameter ke naam se match hona chahiye.
  • Result ko naye object se replace karna ya primitive/String badalna caller tak nahi pahunchta.
  • Mutable object (jaise StudentDTO) pe setter call karoge to change dikh jayega — par ye bad practice hai. Result badalna hai to @Around use karo.
@AfterReturning(
    pointcut = "execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))",
    returning = "result")
public void logAfterReturning(JoinPoint jp, Object result) {
    System.out.println(jp.getSignature().getName() + " returned: " + result);
}
Common galtiresult.setName("Rohit") jaisa hack mat karo — debugging nightmare ban jata hai. Q104

@AfterThrowing

  • Sirf tab chalta hai jab target exception throw kare.
  • throwing = "ex" se exception parameter mein milti hai. Parameter type filter bhi karta hai (IllegalArgumentException ex likha to sirf wahi type pe chalega).
  • Ye exception ko catch/consume nahi kar sakta — advice ke baad exception aage Controller aur @RestControllerAdvice tak jaati hi hai.
  • Use: error logging, monitoring, alert, audit.
@AfterThrowing(
    pointcut = "execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))",
    throwing = "ex")
public void logAfterThrowing(Exception ex) {
    System.out.println("Exception: " + ex.getMessage());
    System.out.println("Type: " + ex.getClass().getName());
}
Dhyan doException rokni hai? Wo kaam sirf @Around (try-catch) kar sakta hai. Q105

@After

Target khatam hone ke turant baad — success ho ya exception, hamesha. Bilkul finally jaisa. Ise return value ya exception nahi dikhti aur ye outcome badal nahi sakta. Use: lock release, connection close, 'method finished' log.

@After("execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))")
public void logAfter() {
    System.out.println("Method completed (success ya exception).");
}
Yaad rakhoQ106

@Around — sabse powerful

Ye poore method call ko gherta hai aur ProceedingJoinPoint milta hai (JoinPoint ka sub-type) jiske paas proceed() hai. Tum decide karte ho target chalega ya nahi, kab, kitni baar, kis args ke saath.

@Around ki superpowers

  1. Pehle aur baad dono jagah code chalao (timing!).
  2. Arguments badlo: pjp.proceed(newArgs).
  3. Return value badlo/replace karo — jo tum return karoge wahi caller ko milega.
  4. Exception consume karo: try-catch lagao aur fallback return karo.
  5. Target ko 0 baar (block/cache hit), 1 baar, ya loop mein kai baar (retry) chalao.
@Aspect
@Component
public class PerformanceAspect {

    @Around("execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))")
    public Object measure(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
        long start = System.currentTimeMillis();
        System.out.println("Starting: " + pjp.getSignature().getName());
        try {
            Object result = pjp.proceed();      // asli method chalao
            System.out.println("Time: " + (System.currentTimeMillis() - start) + " ms");
            return result;                       // ZAROORI: result wapas do
        } catch (Throwable ex) {
            System.out.println("Failed: " + ex.getMessage());
            throw ex;                            // ya consume karke fallback return karo
        } finally {
            System.out.println("Completed.");
        }
    }
}
Common galti(1) proceed() call karna bhool gaye → target kabhi nahi chalega. (2) Return type void rakha ya result return nahi kiya → caller ko null milega. (3) throws Throwable declare karna padta hai. Q107

Comparison matrix

AdviceSuccess pe?Exception pe?Args badle?Return badle?Exception roke?
@BeforeHaan (pehle)—NahiNahiNahi (throw karke target rok sakta hai)
@AfterReturningHaanNahiNahiNahiNahi
@AfterThrowingNahiHaanNahiNahiNahi
@AfterHaanHaanNahiNahiNahi
@AroundHaanHaanHaanHaanHaan

Kab kaunsa use karo

  • Sirf dekhna/log karna hai → sabse chhota advice chuno (@Before, @AfterReturning, @AfterThrowing, @After). Kam power = kam galti.
  • Timing, retry, caching, args/result badalna, exception suppress → @Around.
  • Rule of thumb: @Around tabhi jab simple advice se kaam na chale.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • 5 advice: Before, AfterReturning, AfterThrowing, After, Around.
  • Analogy: Before = try start, AfterReturning = try end, AfterThrowing = catch, After = finally, Around = sab.
  • @Before se target rokna hai to exception throw karo; return se nahi rukta.
  • @AfterThrowing exception consume nahi kar sakta — wo aage jaati hai.
  • @Around: ProceedingJoinPoint + proceed() + result return + throws Throwable.
  • Boot 3 starter = spring-boot-starter-aop (Boot 4 mein naam spring-boot-starter-aspectj).

✅ Review questions (6): ab khud check karo

Q102

What are the five advice types, explained with the try-catch-finally analogy? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Spring AOP has five advice types that decide when the aspect runs.
  • @Before runs before the method, @AfterReturning only after a successful return, @AfterThrowing only when an exception is thrown, and @After always runs, like finally.
  • @Around wraps the whole try-catch-finally block and controls the call itself.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • पांच advice types को try-catch-finally से समझो।
  • try के शुरू में @Before, सफल return के बाद @AfterReturning, catch में @AfterThrowing, finally में @After।
  • और @Around पूरे try-catch-finally block को ही घेर लेता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
AdviceSuccess par?Exception par?Args badle?Return badle?Exception dabaye?
@BeforeHaanN/ANahiNahiNahi (khud throw karke target rok sakta)
@AfterReturningHaanNahiNahiNahiNahi
@AfterThrowingNahiHaanNahiNahiNahi
@AfterHaanHaanNahiNahiNahi
@AroundHaanHaanHaan (proceed(args))HaanHaan
try {
    // @Before yahan
    Object result = targetMethod.proceed();   // target method
    // @AfterReturning yahan (sirf success)
    return result;
} catch (Exception ex) {
    // @AfterThrowing yahan (sirf exception)
    throw ex;
} finally {
    // @After yahan (hamesha)
}
// @Around = poora block wrap karta hai
Important 37 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q101)★ Important listAgla important (Q107) → ★
Q103

How does @Before advice work, and can it stop the target method?

Main Definition

  • @Before runs just before the target method and is used for start logs, precondition checks, basic validation or auth checks.
  • Writing return inside it does not stop the target method.
  • Throwing an exception from it does prevent the target from running.
  • JoinPoint.getArgs() gives read-only access to the arguments; you cannot replace them here.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Before target method से ठीक पहले चलता है।
  • उसके अंदर return लिखने से target नहीं रुकता, पर exception throw करो तो target नहीं चलेगा।
  • getArgs() से arguments पढ़ सकते हो, बदल नहीं सकते।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Aspect
@Component
public class LoggingAspect {
    @Before("execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.createStudent(..))")
    public void logBefore(JoinPoint joinPoint) {
        System.out.println("A student is going to be saved...");
        Object[] args = joinPoint.getArgs();   // read-only
    }
}
Q104

How does @AfterReturning work, and can it change the return value?

Main Definition

  • @AfterReturning runs only when the target returns normally, and returning = "result" binds the returned value to an advice parameter.
  • Replacing the value or a primitive/String in the advice does not change what the caller receives.
  • If the result is a mutable object, calling its setters does change it, but that is a bad practice; use @Around if you really need to change results.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @AfterReturning सिर्फ़ तब चलता है जब method बिना exception के return करे, और returning से result मिल जाता है।
  • यहाँ value बदलने से caller को नई value नहीं मिलती।
  • Object के setter से field बदल सकती है पर ये bad practice है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@AfterReturning(
    pointcut = "execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))",
    returning = "result")
public void logAfterReturning(JoinPoint joinPoint, Object result) {
    System.out.println("Target Method Returned: " + result);
}
Yaad rakhoreturning wala naam ("result") aur advice method ke parameter ka naam same hona chahiye.
Q105

How does @AfterThrowing work, and can it swallow the exception?

Main Definition

  • @AfterThrowing runs only when the target throws, and throwing = "ex" binds the exception to a parameter.
  • It is used for exception logging, error monitoring and auditing.
  • It cannot catch or consume the exception: after the advice, the exception still propagates to the caller (and on to your @RestControllerAdvice).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @AfterThrowing सिर्फ़ exception आने पर चलता है और throwing से exception मिल जाती है।
  • ये exception को रोक नहीं सकता, advice के बाद भी exception आगे caller तक जाती है।
  • इसका काम बस log करना और monitoring है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@AfterThrowing(
    pointcut = "execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))",
    throwing = "ex")
public void logAfterThrowing(Exception ex) {
    System.out.println("Exception: " + ex.getMessage() + " (" + ex.getClass().getName() + ")");
}
Q106

How does @After advice work, and when should you use it?

Main Definition

  • @After runs right after the target method finishes, whether it returned normally or threw an exception, exactly like a finally block.
  • It cannot see the return value or change the outcome.
  • Use it for cleanup such as releasing locks, closing connections or writing a 'method finished' log.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @After हर हाल में चलता है, method सफल हो या exception दे, बिल्कुल finally की तरह।
  • इसे return value नहीं मिलती।
  • Lock छोड़ना, connection बंद करना जैसे cleanup के लिए use करो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@After("execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))")
public void logAfter() {
    System.out.println("Method Execution Completed (Success or Exception).");
}
Q107

Why is @Around the most powerful advice, and how does ProceedingJoinPoint work? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • @Around wraps the entire method call and receives a ProceedingJoinPoint, a sub-type of JoinPoint with proceed().
  • You decide if, when and how often the target runs.
  • You can run code before and after, pass changed arguments with proceed(newArgs), replace the return value, catch and suppress exceptions, or call the target zero, one or many times (for example for retries).
  • The advice must return the result and declare throws Throwable.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Around पूरे method को घेर लेता है और proceed() बुलाने पर ही target चलता है।
  • इससे arguments बदल सकते हो, return value बदल सकते हो, exception दबा सकते हो, या target को retry में कई बार चला सकते हो।
  • Result return करना मत भूलो, वरना caller को null मिलेगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Common mistakes
  • proceed() bulana bhool gaye: target method chalega hi nahi.
  • Return type void rakh diya ya result return nahi kiya: caller ko null milega.
  • Exception chupchap nigal li: global exception handler tak error nahi pahunchegi, client ko galat 200 milega.
  • Jo kaam @Before/@After se ho jaaye uske liye @Around mat lo; sabse simple advice chuno.
@Aspect
@Component
public class PerformanceAspect {
    @Around("execution(* in.codearmy.service.StudentService.*(..))")
    public Object measureExecutionTime(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
        long start = System.currentTimeMillis();
        System.out.println("Starting: " + pjp.getSignature().getName());
        try {
            Object result = pjp.proceed();          // target call
            System.out.println("Time: " + (System.currentTimeMillis() - start) + " ms");
            return result;                          // ya modified result
        } catch (Throwable ex) {
            System.out.println("Failed: " + ex.getMessage());
            throw ex;                               // rethrow ya suppress
        } finally {
            System.out.println("Execution Completed.");
        }
    }
}
