23. Entity mapping

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Humne dekha ki ORM ko bas ek baar mapping batani hai. Ab wahi mapping kaise likhte hain: @Entity se shuru karke embedded objects, converters aur collections tak.
📖 Notes

Basic entity: @Entity, @Table, @Id, @Column

@Entity class ko table-backed entity banata hai. @Table(name) table ka naam set karta hai. @Id primary key hai aur @GeneratedValue(strategy = IDENTITY) DB ke auto-increment se id lata hai. @Column se naam, nullable, unique, length set karo. Bina annotation wala field bhi default column ban jaata hai.

import jakarta.persistence.*;

@Entity
@Table(name = "students")
public class Student {

    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)   // MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT
    private Long id;

    @Column(name = "student_name", nullable = false, length = 100)
    private String name;

    @Column(nullable = false, unique = true, length = 150)
    private String email;

    private int age;                // default mapping: column "age"

    protected Student() {}          // JPA ko no-arg constructor chahiye
}

Hibernate ne kya table banayi (ddl-auto=update)

create table students (
    id bigint not null auto_increment,
    student_name varchar(100) not null,
    email varchar(150) not null,
    age integer not null,
    primary key (id)
);
alter table students add constraint UK_email unique (email);
Dhyan doEntity ko no-arg constructor (public ya protected) chahiye, class final nahi honi chahiye (proxy ke liye), aur @Id zaroori hai.

Sahi Java types chuno

Java typeSQL type
LocalDateDATE
LocalTimeTIME
LocalDateTimeTIMESTAMP / DATETIME
BigDecimal(5,2)DECIMAL(5,2)
@Column(precision = 5, scale = 2)    // max 5 digits, 2 decimal (100.00)
private BigDecimal percentage;         // paise/percent: double nahi!

private LocalDate dateOfBirth;         // DATE
private LocalDateTime createdAt;       // DATETIME / TIMESTAMP

@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)           // 'ACTIVE' store hoga, 0 nahi
private StudentStatus status;

@Lob                                   // LONGTEXT / BLOB
private String profileDescription;

@Transient                             // koi column nahi banega
private String displayName;
Common galti@Enumerated ka default ORDINAL hai (0,1,2). Kal kisi ne enum ke beech mein naya value daal diya to purana saara data galat matlab dene lagega. Hamesha EnumType.STRING.

@Embeddable: value object bina apni identity ke

Address socho: house number, street, city, state, pin. Iski apni koi id nahi, ye hamesha kisi student ka hissa hai. Isliye alag table nahi chahiye. @Embeddable class banao, entity mein @Embedded lagao. Uske fields usi table ke columns ban jaate hain.

@Embeddable
public class Address {
    private String houseNumber;
    private String street;
    private String city;
    private String state;
    private String pinCode;
}

// Student ke andar
@Embedded
private Address permanentAddress;

Ek hi type do baar? @AttributeOverrides

Student ke paas permanentAddress aur currentAddress dono hain. Dono ka city column city hi banna chahega: clash! @AttributeOverrides se doosri copy ke column naam badlo.

students table ke columns
id, student_name, ..., city, pin_code, ..., current_city, current_pincode, ...
@Embedded
@AttributeOverrides({
    @AttributeOverride(name = "city",    column = @Column(name = "current_city")),
    @AttributeOverride(name = "pinCode", column = @Column(name = "current_pincode"))
    // ...baaki fields bhi isi tarah
})
private Address currentAddress;

@ElementCollection: values ki list, bina entity banaye

Student ke skills: Set<String>. Ek column mein list nahi aa sakti, aur Skill ko poori entity banana overkill hai. @ElementCollection Hibernate se ek alag collection table banwata hai jisme owner ki foreign key aur value hoti hai.

student_skills.student_idskill_name
1Java
1SQL
2Spring
@ElementCollection
@CollectionTable(name = "student_skills",
                 joinColumns = @JoinColumn(name = "student_id"))
@Column(name = "skill_name")
private Set<String> skills = new HashSet<>();
Yaad rakho@ElementCollection default LAZY hai, aur iski values ki apni id nahi hoti: list badalne par Hibernate aksar saari rows delete karke dobara insert karta hai. Bade/complex data ke liye proper @OneToMany entity behtar.

AttributeConverter: custom conversion

Maan lo DB mein isMonitor ko 'Yes'/'No' store karna hai, par Java mein Boolean. AttributeConverter<X, Y> implement karo: convertToDatabaseColumn() (Java → DB) aur convertToEntityAttribute() (DB → Java). Class par @Converter, field par @Convert.

@Converter
public class BooleanToStringConverter implements AttributeConverter<Boolean, String> {

    @Override
    public String convertToDatabaseColumn(Boolean attribute) {      // Java -> DB
        if (attribute == null) return null;
        return attribute ? "Yes" : "No";
    }

    @Override
    public Boolean convertToEntityAttribute(String dbData) {        // DB -> Java
        if (dbData == null) return null;
        return "Yes".equalsIgnoreCase(dbData);
    }
}

// entity field
@Convert(converter = BooleanToStringConverter.class)
private Boolean isMonitor;

Saare mapping annotations ek jagah

AnnotationKaam
@EntityClass ko JPA entity banata hai
@Table(name)Custom table naam
@Id / @GeneratedValuePrimary key / uski auto-generation
@Columnname, nullable, unique, length, precision, scale
@TransientField ko column banne se rokta hai
@EnumeratedEnum → STRING ya ORDINAL
@LobBada text ya binary
@Embeddable / @EmbeddedValue object ko parent table mein jodta hai
@AttributeOverridesEmbedded copy ke column naam badalta hai
@ElementCollection + @CollectionTableBasic / embeddable values ki collection, alag table
@Converter / @ConvertCustom Java ↔ DB conversion
Dhyan do@GeneratedValue(IDENTITY) simple hai par isse Hibernate ki JDBC insert batching band ho jaati hai (aage Q150 mein dekhenge). PostgreSQL / Oracle par SEQUENCE better option hai.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • @Entity + @Id zaroori; no-arg constructor chahiye.
  • Paisa = BigDecimal, date = LocalDate/LocalDateTime, enum = EnumType.STRING.
  • @Embedded = same table ke columns; ek type do baar ho to @AttributeOverrides.
  • @ElementCollection = values ki alag table, owner ki FK ke saath, entity nahi.
  • AttributeConverter = custom Java ↔ DB conversion (@Converter + @Convert).
  • @Transient field DB mein nahi jaata.

Q139

Which annotations do you use to map an entity to a table?

Main Definition

  • @Entity marks a class as a table-backed entity, @Table(name) sets the table name, @Id marks the primary key and @GeneratedValue(strategy = IDENTITY) lets the database auto-increment it.
  • @Column customises a column: name, nullable, unique, length.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Entity class को table से जोड़ता है, @Id primary key बताता है और @GeneratedValue उसे auto-increment करता है।
  • @Column से column का name, nullable और length set करते हैं।

  • @Lob बड़े text के लिए है और @Transient वाला field table में column नहीं बनता।

Q141

What are @Embeddable and @Embedded? What is @AttributeOverrides?

Main Definition

  • @Embeddable defines a value object (like Address) that has no identity of its own, and @Embedded places it inside an entity so its fields become columns of the same table.
  • If an entity embeds the same type twice, @AttributeOverrides gives each copy different column names to avoid a clash.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Embeddable एक value object है (जैसे Address) जिसकी अपनी id नहीं होती।
  • @Embedded करने पर उसके fields उसी table के columns बन जाते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Embeddable
public class Address {
    private String houseNumber;
    private String street;
    private String city;
    private String state;
    private String pinCode;
}

// inside Student
@Embedded
@AttributeOverrides({
    @AttributeOverride(name = "city",
        column = @Column(name = "current_city")),
    @AttributeOverride(name = "pinCode",
        column = @Column(name = "current_pincode"))
    // ...override every field the same way
})
private Address currentAddress;

Q142

What is an AttributeConverter?

Main Definition

  • An AttributeConverter<X, Y> converts a Java attribute to a database value and back, for example a Boolean to 'Yes' / 'No'.
  • I implement convertToDatabaseColumn() and convertToEntityAttribute(), mark the class with @Converter, and apply it on the field with @Convert.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • AttributeConverter Java value को DB value में और वापस बदलता है, जैसे Boolean को 'Yes'/'No'।
  • Class पर @Converter लगाओ और field पर @Convert से apply करो।

Q143

What is @ElementCollection?

Main Definition

  • @ElementCollection stores a collection of basic or embeddable values (like Set<String> skills) without making them entities.
  • Hibernate creates a separate collection table, named with @CollectionTable, that holds a foreign key to the owner and the value column.

  • Hibernate इसके लिए एक अलग table बनाता है जिसमें owner की foreign key होती है।

24. EntityManager, Persistence Context aur lifecycle

7 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Ab hamare paas mapped entity hai. Par Student object ko DB tak le kaun jaata hai, aur Hibernate ko kaise pata chalta hai ki kya badla? Iska jawab hai EntityManager aur uska Persistence Context — JPA ka dil.
📖 Notes

Do khiladi: EntityManagerFactory aur EntityManager

EntityManagerFactory: poori app ke liye ek, startup par banti hai, mehngi hai (mappings, metadata, pool). Factory ka kaam EntityManager banana.

EntityManager: chhota, short-lived object jisse tum persist, find, remove karte ho. Har transaction ke liye naya. Har EntityManager ke saath ek Persistence Context hota hai: memory ka workspace jisme uske loaded/saved entities track hote hain.

ComponentJPA (spec)Hibernate (impl)
FactoryEntityManagerFactorySessionFactory
API objectEntityManagerSession
Concrete class(sirf contract)SessionImpl

Thread-safety: @PersistenceContext proxy deta hai

Problem: EntityManager thread-safe nahi hai, par Spring ka repository bean singleton hai jise 100 threads saath use karte hain. Solution: @PersistenceContext asli EntityManager nahi, ek shared proxy inject karta hai. Jab @Transactional method chalta hai, proxy us thread ke transaction se bound asli EntityManager ko call forward karta hai.

@Repository
public class StudentDao {

    @PersistenceContext
    private EntityManager em;      // asli nahi, thread-bound proxy

    public void save(Student s) { em.persist(s); }
}
Yaad rakhoSpring Boot mein constructor injection se EntityManager lo tab bhi yahi shared proxy milta hai. Isliye singleton mein rakhna safe hai.

Persistence Context = L1 cache (transaction ka notebook)

Ek transaction shuru hua, Hibernate ne ek notebook khola. find(Student, 1) par notebook khaali hai, to SELECT chala aur student notebook mein likh liya. Dobara find(Student, 1): notebook mein mil gaya, koi SQL nahi, aur same Java object mila.

JavaSQL chala?
em.find(Student.class, 1L)Haan: select ... from students where id=?
em.find(Student.class, 1L) dobaraNahi (L1 cache)
em.find(Student.class, 2L)Haan: id=2 ke liye
Naye transaction mein find(1)Haan: naya notebook
@Transactional
public void demo() {
    Student a = em.find(Student.class, 1L); // SELECT chala
    Student b = em.find(Student.class, 1L); // L1 cache se, SQL nahi
    System.out.println(a == b);             // true: same object
}
Dhyan doL1 cache sirf ek transaction / EntityManager tak hai, users mein share nahi hota. Shared cache = second-level (L2) cache, wo alag setup hai aur default off.

Entity ki 4 states

StateMatlabDB se sync?
Transientnew se bana, Hibernate ko pata hi nahiNahi
Managed (Persistent)Persistence Context mein trackedHaan, changes apne aap
DetachedPehle managed tha, context band / detach() / clear()Nahi, changes ignore
RemovedDelete ke liye markFlush par DELETE

Ek student ki zindagi: code → state → SQL

CodeStateSQL
new Student("Ravi")TransientKuch nahi
em.persist(s)ManagedCommit/flush par INSERT
s.setName("Ravi Kumar") (transaction mein)ManagedCommit par UPDATE
transaction khatam / em.detach(s)DetachedKuch nahi (track nahi)
Student m = em.merge(s)m Managed (s abhi bhi detached)SELECT (agar cache mein nahi), commit par UPDATE
em.remove(m)RemovedCommit par DELETE

EntityManager ke methods

MethodTransitionKaam
persist(e)Transient → ManagedNaya entity save
find(Class, id)DB → ManagedPK se load, pehle L1 cache
merge(e)Detached → Managed copyManaged copy return karta hai
detach(e)Managed → DetachedEk entity tracking se bahar
clear()Sab → DetachedPoora L1 cache khaali
remove(e)Managed → RemovedDelete ke liye mark
contains(e)—Kya entity managed hai?
flush()—Pending SQL abhi DB bhejo (commit nahi)
refresh(e)—DB se dobara load, memory ki changes overwrite
Common galtiem.merge(s) ke baad s ko hi badalte rehna. merge() passed object ko managed nahi banata, nayi managed copy return karta hai. Hamesha s = em.merge(s);.

Dirty checking: save() ke bina UPDATE

Managed entity load hote hi Hibernate uski ek snapshot (photo) rakh leta hai. Commit ke time object ko photo se compare karta hai; kuch badla ho to UPDATE khud banata hai.

  1. findById(1) se student load hua, snapshot: name='Ravi'.
  2. setName("Ravi Kumar") kiya — abhi koi SQL nahi.
  3. Method khatam, @Transactional commit se pehle flush karta hai.
  4. Hibernate object vs snapshot compare karta hai: name badla.
  5. update students set student_name=? ... where id=? chal jaata hai.

Dirty checking code + generated SQL

@Transactional
public void updateStudent(Long id, StudentRequest req) {
    Student s = studentRepository.findById(id).orElseThrow();  // Managed
    s.setName(req.getName());
    s.setEmail(req.getEmail());
    // save() nahi likha! commit par UPDATE apne aap
}

-- console:
-- select s.id, s.age, s.email, s.student_name from students s where s.id=?
-- update students set age=?, email=?, student_name=? where id=?
Real exampleYe write-behind hai: Hibernate SQL turant nahi bhejta, flush tak jama karta hai. Isse ek field do baar badlo to bhi UPDATE ek hi baar, aur sab sahi order mein jaata hai.

Dirty checking ki common galtiyan

  • Method par @Transactional nahi: findById ke baad entity detached, setter ka koi asar nahi.
  • Detached entity (jaise request se aaya object) badalkar sochna ki update hoga: merge() / save() chahiye.
  • Galti se setter call kar diya (jaise mapping/formatting mein): wo bhi commit par DB mein chala jaayega!

Bulk insert: flush() + clear() in batches

1 lakh students ek loop mein persist kiye to har object notebook (Persistence Context) mein baitha rahega → OutOfMemoryError. Har N (jaise 100) records par flush() (SQL DB bhejo) aur clear() (notebook khaali karo).

@Transactional
public void saveAllInBatches(List<Student> list) {
    int batchSize = 100;
    for (int i = 0; i < list.size(); i++) {
        em.persist(list.get(i));
        if (i > 0 && i % batchSize == 0) {
            em.flush();   // pending INSERTs DB ko
            em.clear();   // L1 cache memory free
        }
    }
    em.flush();
    em.clear();
}

# asli JDBC batching (ek round-trip mein kai INSERT) ke liye:
spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.jdbc.batch_size=100
spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.order_inserts=true
Dhyan doGenerationType.IDENTITY par Hibernate JDBC insert batching band kar deta hai, kyunki id paane ke liye har INSERT turant chalana padta hai. flush/clear memory bachata hai; speed wali batching chahiye to SEQUENCE use karo.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • EntityManagerFactory = ek per app; EntityManager = ek per transaction, thread-safe nahi (Spring proxy deta hai).
  • Persistence Context = L1 cache: same id dobara find → SQL nahi, same object.
  • States: Transient → Managed → Detached / Removed.
  • merge() nayi managed copy return karta hai — returned object use karo.
  • Dirty checking: managed entity badlo, commit par UPDATE khud; save() ki zaroorat nahi.
  • Bulk insert: har N par flush() + clear(); IDENTITY par JDBC batching nahi hoti.

✅ Review questions (7): ab khud check karo

Q144

What is the difference between EntityManagerFactory, EntityManager and Persistence Context?

Main Definition

  • EntityManagerFactory is a long-lived, application-scoped factory (one per app) that creates EntityManagers.
  • EntityManager is the short-lived, thread-bound API I call (persist, find, remove).
  • Each EntityManager works with a Persistence Context: an in-memory workspace, also the first-level (L1) cache, that tracks the entities it loaded or saved.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • EntityManagerFactory पूरी app में एक होती है और factory की तरह EntityManager बनाती है।
  • EntityManager short-lived होता है और हर EntityManager के पास अपना Persistence Context (notebook) होता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
ComponentJPA (specification)Hibernate (implementation)
FactoryEntityManagerFactorySessionFactory
API objectEntityManagerSession
Concrete class(sirf contract)SessionImpl
Yaad rakhoHum hamesha JPA ke EntityManager se baat karte hain. Andar se wo Hibernate ke Session ko call karta hai.
ReferenceHibernate User GuideJakarta Persistence spec
Q145

Why do we use @PersistenceContext to inject the EntityManager?

Main Definition

  • EntityManager is not thread-safe, but Spring beans such as repositories are singletons.
  • @PersistenceContext injects a shared EntityManager proxy instead of a real EntityManager.
  • When a @Transactional method runs, the proxy hands out the EntityManager and Persistence Context bound to that thread's transaction.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • EntityManager thread-safe नहीं है पर repository singleton होती है।
  • @PersistenceContext एक proxy inject करता है जो हर transaction को उसका अपना असली EntityManager दे देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Repository
public class StudentRepository {

    @PersistenceContext
    private EntityManager entityManager;   // a thread-bound proxy

    public void save(Student s) { entityManager.persist(s); }
}
Extra (mera note)Spring Boot mein constructor ya @Autowired se EntityManager inject karne par bhi shared proxy hi milta hai. Interview ke liye safe answer: injected object real EntityManager nahi, thread-bound proxy hai.
ReferenceHibernate User GuideSpring Transaction Management
Q146

What is the Persistence Context, and how does the L1 cache work? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • The Persistence Context is Hibernate's first-level (L1) cache, scoped to one transaction.
  • On find(), Hibernate first checks this cache.
  • If the entity is there, it returns it without any SQL.
  • If not, it runs a SELECT, stores the entity in the cache and returns it.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Persistence Context एक transaction का notebook है, यही L1 cache है।
  • Same id दोबारा find() करो तो Hibernate DB पर नहीं जाता, notebook से ही object दे देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Story: transaction ka notebook

Ek transaction shuru hua, Hibernate ne ek notebook khola. find(Student, 1) par notebook khaali hai, to SELECT chala aur student notebook mein likh liya. Dobara find(Student, 1) par notebook mein mil gaya: koi SQL nahi, aur same Java object mila (s1 == s2 true).

Java code vs SQL
JavaSQL chala?
em.find(Student.class, 1L)Haan: SELECT ... WHERE id=1
em.find(Student.class, 1L) dobaraNahi (L1 cache)
em.find(Student.class, 2L)Haan: SELECT ... WHERE id=2
Transaction khatam, naye transaction mein find(1)Haan: naya notebook
Dhyan doL1 cache sirf ek transaction / EntityManager tak hai, sab users mein share nahi hota. Shared cache ke liye second-level (L2) cache alag cheez hai.
@Transactional
public void demo() {
    Student a = em.find(Student.class, 1L); // SELECT fired
    Student b = em.find(Student.class, 1L); // from L1 cache, no SQL
    System.out.println(a == b);             // true: same object
}
ReferenceHibernate User Guide

Q147

Which EntityManager methods should you know?

Main Definition

  • The key methods are persist() (Transient to Managed), find() (load by primary key into Managed), merge() (Detached to Managed, returns the managed copy), detach() and clear() (to Detached), remove() (Managed to Removed), plus contains(), flush() and refresh().

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • persist() नया object Managed बनाता है, find() id से load करता है, merge() detached को वापस Managed copy देता है।
  • remove() delete mark करता है और flush() pending SQL तुरंत DB भेजता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
MethodTransitionKaam
persist(e)Transient to ManagedNaya entity save karo
find(Class, id)DB to ManagedPK se load, pehle L1 cache dekhta hai
merge(e)Detached to ManagedDetached ki managed copy banata hai
detach(e)Managed to DetachedEk entity ko tracking se hatao
clear()All to DetachedPoora L1 cache khali
remove(e)Managed to RemovedDelete ke liye mark
contains(e)-Kya entity managed hai?
flush()-Pending changes ka SQL abhi DB ko bhejo
refresh(e)-DB se dobara load, entity ki state overwrite
Dhyan domerge() ka return value hi managed hota hai, wo object nahi jo tumne pass kiya.
ReferenceHibernate User Guide
Q148

What are the four entity lifecycle states in Hibernate? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Transient: a new object created with new, not tracked, no DB row.
  • Managed (Persistent): tracked in the Persistence Context, and changes are synced automatically.
  • Detached: was managed, but the context closed or detach() / clear() was called, so changes are ignored.
  • Removed: marked for deletion, and the DELETE runs at flush.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Entity की चार states हैं: Transient (नया, track नहीं), Managed (track हो रहा), Detached (पहले track था, अब नहीं) और Removed (delete के लिए marked)।
  • सिर्फ़ Managed entity के changes अपने आप DB में जाते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Ek student ki zindagi
CodeStateDB mein?
new Student("Ravi")TransientNahi
em.persist(s)ManagedCommit par INSERT
s.setName("X") (transaction mein)ManagedCommit par UPDATE
transaction khatam / em.detach(s)DetachedHaan, par track nahi
em.merge(s)Managed copy milti haiCommit par UPDATE
em.remove(managed)RemovedCommit par DELETE
Yaad rakhomerge() wahi object Managed nahi banata, ek nayi managed copy return karta hai. Uske baad returned object use karo.

Q149

How does automatic update work? What are dirty checking and write-behind? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Dirty checking is how Hibernate updates without an explicit update call.
  • A managed entity is loaded together with a snapshot.
  • When I change it with setters and the transaction commits (flush), Hibernate compares the entity with the snapshot and, if it changed, generates an UPDATE.
  • Changes are sent together at flush time, which is the write-behind pattern.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Managed entity load होते ही Hibernate उसकी एक photo (snapshot) रख लेता है।
  • Commit पर object को photo से compare करता है और जो बदला उसका UPDATE खुद चला देता है, save() की ज़रूरत नहीं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Step by step: update bina save()
  1. find() se student load hua, Hibernate ne uski snapshot (photo) rakh li: name='Ravi'.
  2. Tumne setName('Ravi Kumar') kiya, abhi koi SQL nahi.
  3. Method khatam, @Transactional commit se pehle flush karta hai.
  4. Hibernate object ko snapshot se compare karta hai: name badla hai.
  5. UPDATE students SET name='Ravi Kumar' WHERE id=1 chal jaata hai.
Code
@Transactional
public void rename(Long id, String name) {
    Student s = repo.findById(id).orElseThrow();
    s.setName(name);   // bas itna. save() ki zaroorat nahi
}
Write-behind

Hibernate SQL turant nahi bhejta, flush tak jama karta hai (write-behind). Isse kai changes ek saath aur sahi order mein jaate hain, aur ek field do baar badlo to bhi UPDATE ek hi baar.

Common mistakes
  • Method par @Transactional nahi: entity detached ho jaati hai, change DB mein nahi jaata.
  • Detached entity badalkar sochna ki update ho jayega: merge() ya save() chahiye.
  • Galti se setter call kar diya: wo bhi commit par save ho jaayega.
@Transactional
public void updateStudent(StudentRequest request, Long id) {
    Student student = studentRepository.findById(id);   // Managed
    student.setName(request.getName());                // heap change
    student.setEmail(request.getEmail());
    student.setAge(request.getAge());
    // no save() / update() needed: UPDATE runs at commit
}
Dhyan doEntity Managed state mein honi chahiye. Detached entity ko badalne se UPDATE nahi chalta.
ReferenceHibernate User Guide
Important 49 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q148)★ Important listAgla important (Q152) → ★
Q150

How do you insert a huge number of records without OutOfMemoryError?

Main Definition

  • Persisting a huge list in one loop fills the Persistence Context with every entity and can cause OutOfMemoryError.
  • I process in batches: after every N records (for example 100) I call flush() to send the SQL to the database and clear() to empty the L1 cache.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • लाखों records एक loop में persist करोगे तो Persistence Context भर जाएगा और OutOfMemoryError आएगा।
  • हर 100 records पर flush() और clear() करो ताकि memory खाली होती रहे।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Batch insert code
@Transactional
public void importAll(List<Student> list) {
    for (int i = 0; i < list.size(); i++) {
        em.persist(list.get(i));
        if (i > 0 && i % 100 == 0) {
            em.flush();   // SQL DB bhejo
            em.clear();   // notebook khaali karo
        }
    }
}
// application.properties
// spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.jdbc.batch_size=100
// spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.order_inserts=true
Dhyan doGenerationType.IDENTITY par Hibernate JDBC insert batching band kar deta hai, kyunki id paane ke liye har INSERT turant chalana padta hai. Batching chahiye to SEQUENCE use karo.
@Transactional
public void saveAllInBatches(List<Student> studentList) {
    int batchSize = 100;

    for (int i = 0; i < studentList.size(); i++) {
        entityManager.persist(studentList.get(i));

        if (i > 0 && i % batchSize == 0) {
            entityManager.flush();   // send INSERTs to DB
            entityManager.clear();   // free L1 cache memory
        }
    }
    entityManager.flush();
    entityManager.clear();
}
Extra (mera note)GenerationType.IDENTITY ke saath Hibernate har INSERT turant chalata hai (ID chahiye), isliye JDBC insert batching disable ho jaati hai. flush() aur clear() memory bachate hain, speed ke liye batching ka alag setup chahiye.
ReferenceHibernate User Guide
➡️ Agle topic mein: ek entity doosri se kaise judti hai — @ManyToOne, @OneToMany, @OneToOne, @ManyToMany aur cascade.Agla topic: Relationships aur cascade →

25. Relationships aur cascade

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Ab tak ek akeli Student entity thi. Real app mein student kisi department mein hota hai, courses leta hai, uska profile hota hai. Database mein ye rishte foreign keys se bante hain. Ab dekhte hain JPA mein inhe kaise map karte hain.
📖 Notes

Chaar relationships

  • Unidirectional: sirf ek side ke paas reference (Student ke paas Department, Department ke paas list nahi).
  • Bidirectional: dono ke paas ek doosre ka reference.
TypeExample
@ManyToOneKai students → ek department
@OneToManyEk department → kai students
@OneToOneEk user → ek profile
@ManyToManyKai students ↔ kai courses

Owning side vs inverse side

Bidirectional mein FK sirf ek table mein hoti hai. Jis entity ke paas FK hai wo owning side hai: wahi SQL chalati hai. Doosri inverse side hai, mappedBy lagati hai, aur FK ko manage nahi karti — bas ek mirror hai.

Yaad rakhomappedBy = "FK main nahi rakhta, doosri side ke is field ko dekho".

@ManyToOne / @OneToMany: FK hamesha 'many' side

Ek department ke kai students hain. Department table ke ek column mein student ids ki list rakhna possible hi nahi. Isliye FK students table mein: students.department_id.

students.idnamedepartment_id (FK)
1Ravi10
2Anu10
3Karan20

Mapping code

@Entity
public class Student {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;

    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY, optional = false)
    @JoinColumn(name = "department_id", nullable = false)   // owning side: FK yahin
    private Department department;
}

@Entity
public class Department {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;

    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "department")                     // inverse side
    private List<Student> students = new ArrayList<>();

    // helper: dono sides memory mein sync
    public void addStudent(Student s) {
        students.add(s);
        s.setDepartment(this);
    }
}

-- generated DDL:
-- create table students (id bigint not null auto_increment, name varchar(255),
--     department_id bigint not null, primary key (id))
-- alter table students add constraint FK_dept foreign key (department_id)
--     references departments (id)

Relationship ki common galtiyan

  • Sirf department.getStudents().add(s) kiya: inverse side ignore hoti hai, FK set nahi hogi. s.setDepartment(d) zaroori — isliye helper method.
  • @OneToMany par mappedBy bhool gaye: Hibernate ek faltu join table department_students bana deta hai.
  • Bidirectional entities ke toString() / equals() / hashCode() (Lombok @Data) mein dono taraf ke fields: infinite recursion → StackOverflowError. Jackson JSON mein bhi wahi loop — DTO return karo.

@OneToOne: FK + UNIQUE

One-to-one mein FK kisi bhi table mein ho sakti hai, par us par UNIQUE constraint hona chahiye. Warna do profiles same user ko point kar sakti hain aur ye asal mein many-to-one ban jaata hai.

@Entity
public class Profile {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String bio;

    @OneToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "user_id", unique = true)   // owning side
    private User user;
}

@Entity
@Table(name = "users")       // 'user' kai DBs mein reserved word hai
public class User {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @OneToOne(mappedBy = "user")                    // inverse side
    private Profile profile;
}

@ManyToMany: beech mein join table

Ek student kai courses, ek course kai students. Kisi bhi side FK rakho to rows repeat hongi. Isliye ek join table student_course banti hai jisme do FK hoti hain, aur dono milke composite primary key.

@Entity
public class Student {
    @ManyToMany
    @JoinTable(name = "student_course",
        joinColumns = @JoinColumn(name = "student_id"),
        inverseJoinColumns = @JoinColumn(name = "course_id"))
    private Set<Course> courses = new HashSet<>();     // owning side
}

@Entity
public class Course {
    @ManyToMany(mappedBy = "courses")
    private Set<Student> students = new HashSet<>();   // inverse side
}

-- student.getCourses().add(java); commit par:
-- insert into student_course (student_id, course_id) values (?, ?)
Real exampleAgar join table mein extra data chahiye (enrolled_on, grade) to @ManyToMany chhodo: Enrollment entity banao aur do @ManyToOne se jodo.

FK kahan rehti hai — summary

MappingForeign key kahanConfig
@ManyToOne'Many' table mein@JoinColumn
@OneToManyInverse side, FK nahimappedBy
@OneToOneOwning table mein + UNIQUE@JoinColumn(unique = true)
@ManyToManyAlag join table mein@JoinTable + mappedBy

Cascade: parent ka operation children tak

Department save kiya, uske 3 naye students bhi save hone chahiye. Bina cascade ke har student ka alag save() likhna padega. Cascade parent par hua operation children tak pass karta hai.

TypeEffect
PERSISTParent save → naye children bhi save
MERGEParent merge → children bhi merge
REMOVEParent delete → children bhi delete
ALLPERSIST + MERGE + REMOVE + REFRESH + DETACH
orphanRemoval = trueList se hataya child DB se bhi delete
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
private List<OrderItem> items = new ArrayList<>();

order.addItem(new OrderItem("Pen", 2));
order.addItem(new OrderItem("Book", 1));
orderRepository.save(order);

-- insert into orders (...) values (...)
-- insert into order_item (order_id, name, qty) values (?, ?, ?)
-- insert into order_item (order_id, name, qty) values (?, ?, ?)

Cascade kab, kab nahi

Bina REMOVE ke, students wala department delete karoge to DB bolega: Cannot delete or update a parent row: a foreign key constraint fails.

Common galtiCascade REMOVE / ALL sirf asli parent-child (composition) par: Order → OrderItem. @ManyToOne ya @ManyToMany par REMOVE kabhi nahi — ek student delete kiya aur poora department ya shared courses ud gaye!
📌 Yaad rakho
  • FK hamesha 'many' side; owning side = jiske paas FK, inverse side = mappedBy.
  • Inverse side badalne se DB mein kuch nahi hota — owning side set karo, helper method banao.
  • OneToOne = FK + UNIQUE; ManyToMany = join table + do FK.
  • Join table mein extra column chahiye to beech ki entity banao.
  • Cascade parent → child; REMOVE/ALL sirf composition par, ManyToOne/ManyToMany par kabhi nahi.
  • orphanRemoval = list se hataya child DB se delete.

Q151

What are relationship cardinality, directionality, and the owning vs inverse side?

Main Definition

  • JPA relationships are @ManyToOne, @OneToMany, @OneToOne and @ManyToMany.
  • They can be unidirectional (one entity references the other) or bidirectional (both do).
  • In a bidirectional mapping one side is the owning side, which holds the foreign key and drives the SQL.
  • The other is the inverse side, marked with mappedBy, and it does not manage the foreign key.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Relationship one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one या many-to-many हो सकती है, और एक तरफ़ा या दोनों तरफ़ा।
  • Bidirectional में जिस side की table में foreign key है वो owning side है, दूसरी तरफ़ mappedBy लगता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
TypeExample
@ManyToOneKai students, ek department
@OneToManyEk department, kai students
@OneToOneEk user, ek profile
@ManyToManyKai students, kai courses
  • Unidirectional: Student ke paas Department hai, Department ke paas students ki list nahi.
  • Bidirectional: dono ke paas ek dusre ka reference hai.

Q152

How do @ManyToOne and @OneToMany work, and where does the foreign key go? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • In @ManyToOne / @OneToMany, the 'many' side always holds the foreign key (students.department_id).
  • Student is the owning side with @ManyToOne + @JoinColumn.
  • Department is the inverse side with @OneToMany(mappedBy = 'department'), and JPA creates no join table for it.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Foreign key हमेशा 'many' वाली table में जाती है, जैसे students.department_id।
  • Student owning side है (@ManyToOne + @JoinColumn) और Department inverse side है (@OneToMany(mappedBy))।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Sample tables
students.idstudents.namestudents.department_id (FK)
1Ravi10
2Anu10
3Karan20

departments table mein sirf id aur name hai (10 = CSE, 20 = ECE). Ek department ke kai students hain, isliye FK 'many' side (students) mein hai. Department table ke ek column mein student ids ki list rakhna possible hi nahi.

Mapping
@Entity class Student {
    @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
    @JoinColumn(name = "department_id")   // owning side: FK yahin
    private Department department;
}
@Entity class Department {
    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "department")  // inverse side: sirf mirror
    private List<Student> students = new ArrayList<>();
}
Common mistakes
  • Sirf department.getStudents().add(s) kiya: FK update nahi hota, kyunki inverse side ignore hoti hai. student.setDepartment(d) zaroori hai.
  • OneToMany par mappedBy na lagana: Hibernate ek extra join table bana deta hai.
  • Bidirectional toString()/JSON mein infinite loop.
@Entity
public class Student {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;

    @ManyToOne(optional = false)
    @JoinColumn(name = "department_id", nullable = false)
    private Department department;          // owning side
}

@Entity
public class Department {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;

    @OneToMany(mappedBy = "department")
    private List<Student> students = new ArrayList<>();   // inverse side
}
Dhyan doBidirectional mein dono sides memory mein khud sync karni padti hain, warna object graph stale rehta hai. Entity ke andar helper method banao.

Q153

How does @OneToOne work?

Main Definition

  • In @OneToOne the foreign key can sit in either table, but it must have a UNIQUE constraint.
  • Without it, many rows could point to the same parent and the mapping is really many-to-one.
  • The owning side uses @OneToOne + @JoinColumn(name, unique = true); the inverse side uses @OneToOne(mappedBy = ...).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @OneToOne में foreign key किसी भी table में हो सकती है पर उस पर UNIQUE constraint ज़रूरी है।
  • वरना कई rows एक ही parent को point करेंगी और वो असल में many-to-one बन जाएगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Entity
public class Profile {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String bio;

    @OneToOne
    @JoinColumn(name = "user_id", unique = true)   // owning side
    private User user;
}

@Entity
public class User {
    @Id @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;
    private String name;

    @OneToOne(mappedBy = "user")                  // inverse side
    private Profile profile;
}

Q154

How does @ManyToMany work, and why is a join table needed?

Main Definition

  • @ManyToMany needs a join table, because a foreign key on either side would repeat rows.
  • The owning side declares @JoinTable(name, joinColumns, inverseJoinColumns).
  • The join table holds two foreign keys that together form a composite primary key.
  • The other side uses mappedBy.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Many-to-many में किसी भी table में foreign key नहीं रख सकते, इसलिए बीच में join table बनती है।
  • उसमें दोनों तरफ़ की foreign keys होती हैं, जैसे student_course table।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
MappingForeign key kahanConfig
@ManyToOne'Many' table mein@JoinColumn
@OneToManyInverse side, FK nahimappedBy
@OneToOneOwning table mein + UNIQUE@JoinColumn(unique = true)
@ManyToManyAlag join table mein@JoinTable + mappedBy

public class Student2 {

    @JoinTable(
        name = "student_course",
        joinColumns = @JoinColumn(name = "student_id"),
        inverseJoinColumns = @JoinColumn(name = "course_id"))

Q155

What is cascading in JPA? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Cascading passes an operation from a parent entity to its children.
  • CascadeType.PERSIST: saving the parent also saves new children.
  • CascadeType.REMOVE: deleting the parent deletes its children.
  • CascadeType.ALL applies PERSIST, MERGE, REMOVE, REFRESH and DETACH.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Cascade parent पर किया गया operation children पर भी चला देता है।
  • PERSIST से parent save करते ही children save, REMOVE से parent delete करते ही children भी delete।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Example
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "order", cascade = CascadeType.ALL, orphanRemoval = true)
private List<OrderItem> items = new ArrayList<>();

order.addItem(new OrderItem(...));
em.persist(order);   // order + saare items INSERT
Kab kya
TypeEffect
PERSISTParent save, naye children bhi save
MERGEParent merge, children bhi merge
REMOVEParent delete, children bhi delete
ALLSab upar wale + REFRESH, DETACH
orphanRemoval=trueList se hata diya child DB se bhi delete
Dhyan doCascade REMOVE / ALL sirf parent-child (composition) par lagao, jaise Order-OrderItem. @ManyToOne ya @ManyToMany par REMOVE kabhi nahi: ek student delete karte hi poora department ya shared courses ud jaayenge.
  • Parent-child (master-detail) rishte mein use karo, jaise Department to Student ya Order to OrderItems.
  • CascadeType.ALL sochkar lagao: delete bhi child tak pahunchta hai.
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "department", cascade = CascadeType.PERSIST)
private List<Student> students;

// With cascade, one call saves the department and its students
departmentRepository.save(department);
Error jo REMOVE ke bina aata haiCannot delete or update a parent row: a foreign key constraint fails

26. Lazy, eager aur N+1

3 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Relationships map ho gaye. Ab sawaal ye hai ki findById(student) par Hibernate department, courses, profile sab ek saath laaye ya tab jab maange? Yahi fetch type ka faisla hai, aur galat faisla seedha N+1 problem deta hai.
📖 Notes

LAZY vs EAGER

EAGER: main entity ke saath related entity bhi turant aati hai (aksar JOIN se).

LAZY: pehle sirf main entity. Related entity ki jagah ek proxy (nakli object jisme sirf id) baith jaata hai. Jab tum us par koi getter call karte ho, tab SELECT chalta hai.

Socho ek department ke 5000 students hain aur tumhe sirf department ka naam chahiye. EAGER mein 5000 students bhi memory mein aa jaate. Lazy isi se bachata hai.

JPA ke default fetch types

AnnotationDefault fetch
@ManyToOneEAGER
@OneToOneEAGER
@OneToManyLAZY
@ManyToManyLAZY
@ElementCollectionLAZY
Yaad rakhoTrick: '...ToOne' = EAGER, '...ToMany' = LAZY. Best practice: sab relations LAZY rakho, @ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY) explicitly likho.

Lazy andar se + SQL

@Transactional
public void show(Long id) {
    Student s = studentRepository.findById(id).orElseThrow();
    // select s.* from students s where s.id=?      (department nahi aaya)

    Department d = s.getDepartment();   // proxy, abhi bhi SQL nahi
    System.out.println(d.getName());    // ab SQL:
    // select d.* from departments d where d.id=?
}

LazyInitializationException

Lazy proxy ko data laane ke liye open Persistence Context chahiye. Agar transaction khatam ho chuka (jaise controller mein, ya JSON banate waqt) aur tab getName() call hua, to proxy DB tak nahi ja sakta:

org.hibernate.LazyInitializationException:
  could not initialize proxy [Department#10] - no Session
Common galtiIsse chhupane ke liye relation ko EAGER kar dena ya spring.jpa.open-in-view par bharosa karna galat fix hai. Sahi fix: service ke andar (transaction mein) zaroori data JOIN FETCH / @EntityGraph se lo aur DTO return karo. Note: Boot mein open-in-view default true hai aur startup par warning deta hai; production mein false karna better.

N+1 problem: kahani

100 students ki list chahiye aur har ek ka department naam print karna hai. findAll() ne 1 query chalayi. Phir loop mein har student ka lazy department alag query se aaya: 100 aur. Total 1 + N = 101 queries. Data thoda, round-trips bahut.

List<Student> students = studentRepository.findAll();   // 1 query
for (Student s : students) {
    System.out.println(s.getDepartment().getName());      // har student par +1
}

-- select * from students;                       (1)
-- select * from departments where id=10;        (2)
-- select * from departments where id=20;        (3)
-- ... total 1 + N
Dhyan doN+1 ki wajah lazy loading khud nahi, loop ke andar lazy relation access karna hai. EAGER karne se bhi N+1 nahi jaata (findAll ke baad Hibernate phir bhi alag queries chala sakta hai).

Pehchaan kaise karo

spring.jpa.show-sql=true karo. Logs mein same SELECT baar-baar alag id ke saath dikhe to N+1 hai. spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.generate_statistics=true se query count bhi dikh jaata hai.

Fixes

FixKaiseQueries
JOIN FETCH@Query("SELECT s FROM Student s JOIN FETCH s.department")1
@EntityGraph@EntityGraph(attributePaths = "department")1
Batch fetchinghibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=501 + N/50
DTO projectionSELECT new com.x.StudentDto(s.name, d.name) FROM Student s JOIN s.department d1

@EntityGraph: mapping LAZY, is query ke liye JOIN

@EntityGraph(attributePaths = {...}) repository method par lagao. Mapping LAZY hi rehti hai, bas is ek query ke liye Hibernate listed relations ko JOIN se saath le aata hai. 101 queries → 1.

public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> {

    @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"department", "profile"})
    List<Student> findAll();

    @Query("SELECT s FROM Student s JOIN FETCH s.department WHERE s.age > :age")
    List<Student> findOlderWithDept(@Param("age") int age);
}

-- ab sirf ek query:
-- select s.*, d.*, p.* from students s
--   left join departments d on d.id = s.department_id
--   left join profile p on p.user_id = s.id
Dhyan doDo alag List (bag) collections ek saath JOIN FETCH karoge to MultipleBagFetchException. Aur collection fetch ke saath pagination memory mein hoti hai (warning aati hai). Ek collection ek query, ya Set / batch fetching use karo.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • LAZY = jab maango tab (proxy), EAGER = turant.
  • Defaults: ...ToOne EAGER, ...ToMany LAZY; best practice sab LAZY.
  • Transaction band hone ke baad lazy access = LazyInitializationException.
  • N+1 = 1 list query + har row ke liye 1 query; wajah loop mein lazy access.
  • Fix: JOIN FETCH, @EntityGraph, batch fetch size, DTO projection.
  • show-sql mein same SELECT alag id ke saath repeat = N+1.

✅ Review questions (3): ab khud check karo

Q156

What is the difference between lazy and eager loading? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • LAZY loading fetches the main entity first and loads related entities only when they are accessed, using proxies.
  • EAGER loading fetches related entities immediately, usually with a join.
  • Lazy avoids loading a huge object graph into memory when it is not needed.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • LAZY में related data तभी load होता है जब उसे access करो, EAGER में तुरंत साथ में।
  • Default में @ManyToOne/@OneToOne EAGER और @OneToMany/@ManyToMany LAZY होते हैं, best practice सबको LAZY रखना है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Defaults
AnnotationDefault fetch
@ManyToOneEAGER
@OneToOneEAGER
@OneToManyLAZY
@ManyToManyLAZY
@ElementCollectionLAZY
Lazy kaise kaam karta hai

student.getDepartment() par Hibernate ek proxy object deta hai jisme sirf id hai. Jab tum getName() call karte ho tab SELECT chalta hai. Agar tab tak transaction / session band ho chuka hai to LazyInitializationException aata hai.

Best practice
  • Sab relations LAZY rakho (@ManyToOne(fetch = LAZY) explicitly likho).
  • Jis query mein data chahiye wahan JOIN FETCH ya @EntityGraph lagao (Q158).
  • LazyInitializationException ko EAGER karke ya open-in-view se mat chhupao; DTO ya fetch join use karo.
  • Lazy khud kharab nahi hai: ye bade object graph se memory bachata hai.
  • Lazy field ko persistence context band hone ke baad access karoge to LazyInitializationException aata hai.
@ManyToOne(fetch = FetchType.LAZY)
@JoinColumn(name = "department_id")
private Department department;
Yaad rakhoJPA defaults: @ManyToOne aur @OneToOne = EAGER. @OneToMany aur @ManyToMany = LAZY.
ReferenceHibernate User Guide
Important 52 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q155)★ Important listAgla important (Q157) → ★
Q157

What is the N+1 query problem, and how do you fix it? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • The N+1 problem: one query loads N parent rows, then each parent's lazy association fires one extra query, giving 1 + N queries.
  • For 100 students that is 101 SQL calls.
  • It is caused by accessing lazy relations inside a loop, not by lazy loading itself.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • एक query से 100 students आए, फिर loop में हर student का department लिया तो 100 extra queries, कुल 101।
  • इसे JOIN FETCH, @EntityGraph या batch fetching से एक-दो queries में ठीक करते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
SQL jo actually chalti hai
List<Student> list = repo.findAll();                 // 1 query
for (Student s : list)
    System.out.println(s.getDepartment().getName()); // har student par 1 query

-- SELECT * FROM students;                    (1)
-- SELECT * FROM departments WHERE id=10;     (2)
-- SELECT * FROM departments WHERE id=20;     (3)
-- ... total 1 + N
Fixes
FixKaiseQueries
JOIN FETCH@Query("SELECT s FROM Student s JOIN FETCH s.department")1
@EntityGraph@EntityGraph(attributePaths = "department")1
Batch fetchinghibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=501 + N/50
DTO projectionSELECT new StudentDto(s.name, d.name) ...1
SochoPehchaan kaise karo? show-sql on karo aur logs mein same SELECT baar-baar alag id ke saath dikhe to N+1 hai.
List<Student> students = studentRepository.findAll();   // 1 query

for (Student s : students) {
    // each call fires 1 more SELECT (lazy department)
    System.out.println(s.getDepartment().getName());
}
Fix@EntityGraph (agla concept), JOIN FETCH in JPQL, ya batch fetching.
ReferenceN+1 query problem (Vlad Mihalcea)Hibernate User Guide
Important 53 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q156)★ Important listAgla important (Q162) → ★
Q158

What is @EntityGraph?

Main Definition

  • @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {...}) on a repository method tells Hibernate to fetch the listed associations eagerly with a JOIN for that query only, while the mapping itself stays LAZY.
  • It turns 1 + N queries into 1 query.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @EntityGraph repository method पर बताता है कि इस query में कौन सी relation JOIN से साथ लानी है।
  • Mapping LAZY ही रहती है, बस इस query के लिए data एक बार में आ जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> {

    @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"department", "profile"})
    List<Student> findAll();
}
ReferenceJPA Query MethodsN+1 query problem (Vlad Mihalcea)

27. Spring Data JPA

7 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: EntityManager se humne persist, find, merge, JPQL sab khud likha. Par har entity ke liye wahi save, findById, findAll, delete dobara likhna boring hai. Pichle topic ka @EntityGraph bhi ek repository interface par laga tha. Ab dekhte hain wo interface kaam kaise karta hai: Spring Data JPA.
📖 Notes

Problem aur solution

Har entity ke DAO mein 80% code same: save, find by id, find all, delete, count. Sirf entity ka type badalta hai.

Spring Data JPA: tum bas ek interface declare karo, Spring runtime par implementation bana deta hai. Spring Data umbrella project hai jo JPA, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra sab ke liye ek jaisa Repository model deta hai; Spring Data JPA uska SQL wala hissa hai, JPA + Hibernate ke upar.

public interface StudentRepository extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> {
    // save, findById, findAll, deleteById, count ... sab pehle se ready
}

@Service
public class StudentService {
    private final StudentRepository repo;
    public StudentService(StudentRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }

    public Student get(Long id) { return repo.findById(id).orElseThrow(); }
}

Repository hierarchy

InterfaceKya deta hai
Repository<T, ID>Marker, kuch nahi
CrudRepositorysave, findById, existsById, findAll, deleteById, count (Iterable)
ListCrudRepositoryWahi, par List return
PagingAndSortingRepositoryfindAll(Sort), findAll(Pageable)
ListPagingAndSortingRepositorySorting wala, List return
JpaRepositoryUpar ke dono List variants + flush, saveAndFlush, deleteAllInBatch, getReferenceById
Dhyan doSpring Data 3 (Boot 3) se PagingAndSortingRepository ab CrudRepository ko extend nahi karta, aur List variants naye hain. Isliye zyadatar log seedha JpaRepository lete hain.

Andar kya hota hai: dynamic proxy

Startup par Spring tumhare interface ka JDK dynamic proxy banata hai (wahi proxy idea jo AOP mein dekha). Standard methods SimpleJpaRepository ko jaate hain jo EntityManager call karta hai. Custom naam wale methods query parser ko.

StudentRepository (interface)→JDK dynamic proxy→save/findById → SimpleJpaRepository | findByEmail → method-name parser→EntityManager→Hibernate → JDBC → DB

save() andar se: persist ya merge

  • Data pehle Persistence Context mein, DB tak flush / commit par.
  • Id khud set ki (jaise UUID / natural key) to isNew() false → merge() → pehle SELECT, phir INSERT. Fix: Persistable implement karo ya @Version field.
  • Hamesha returned object use karo: student = repo.save(student);
  • saveAll() ek bulk INSERT nahi, loop mein save() hai. Asli batching ke liye hibernate.jdbc.batch_size + SEQUENCE ids.
// SimpleJpaRepository.save() (simplified)
@Transactional
public <S extends T> S save(S entity) {
    if (entityInformation.isNew(entity)) {   // id null (ya primitive 0)?
        em.persist(entity);
        return entity;
    } else {
        return em.merge(entity);             // nayi managed copy
    }
}

Derived query methods: naam se query

Method naam = [Subject] + By + [Predicate]. Subject action hai (find, exists, count, delete, findTop3, findDistinct), predicate conditions. Spring naam padhke JPQL bana deta hai.

KeywordSQL
And / OrAND / OR
StartingWith / EndingWith / Containing / LikeLIKE 'x%' / '%x' / '%x%' / apna pattern
GreaterThan / LessThan / Between> / < / BETWEEN
In(Collection)IN (...)
IsNull / IsNotNullIS NULL / IS NOT NULL
OrderBy...DescORDER BY ... DESC
Optional<Student> findByEmail(String email);
List<Student> findByAgeBetween(int min, int max);
List<Student> findByNameContainingOrderByNameAsc(String part);
boolean existsByEmail(String email);
List<Student> findTop3ByOrderByAgeDesc();

-- findByAgeBetween(18, 25) se:
-- select s.* from students s where s.age between ? and ?
-- findByNameContaining("av") se:
-- select s.* from students s where s.student_name like ? escape '\'   (value '%av%')
Yaad rakhoGalat property naam (typo) startup par hi fail karta hai — achhi baat. Par naam bahut lamba ho jaaye to @Query use karo.

@Query: JPQL ya native SQL

JPQL (default) entity class aur field naam par chalta hai (Student s, s.email). Native SQL (nativeQuery = true) table aur column naam par. Parameters :name + @Param.

// JPQL: entity naam
@Query("SELECT s FROM Student s WHERE s.email = :email")
Optional<Student> findByEmailCustom(@Param("email") String email);

// Native: table naam
@Query(value = "SELECT * FROM students WHERE email = :email", nativeQuery = true)
Optional<Student> findByEmailNative(@Param("email") String email);

// Explicit join
@Query("SELECT s FROM Student s JOIN s.department d WHERE d.active = true")
List<Student> findInActiveDepartments();

// Implicit join (path se)
@Query("SELECT s FROM Student s WHERE s.department.active = true")
List<Student> findInActiveDepartmentsImplicit();

// UPDATE/DELETE query ke liye @Modifying + transaction chahiye
@Modifying
@Query("UPDATE Student s SET s.age = s.age + 1")
int incrementAges();
Dhyan do@Modifying query seedha DB par chalti hai, Persistence Context ko bypass karke. Uske baad memory mein pade entities purane ho sakte hain — @Modifying(clearAutomatically = true) use karo.

Sorting aur pagination

Sort ORDER BY lagata hai. PageRequest.of(page, size, sort) pagination — page index 0 se shuru.

FeaturePage<T>Slice<T>
SQL queries2 (SELECT + COUNT)1 (size + 1 rows laata hai)
Total countPata haiNahi pata
hasNext()HaanHaan
KabPage numbers wala UIInfinite scroll, bada data
Sort sort = Sort.by("name").ascending().and(Sort.by("age").descending());

Pageable pageable = PageRequest.of(0, 10, Sort.by("name"));
Page<Student> page = studentRepository.findAll(pageable);

page.getContent();        // is page ke 10 students
page.getTotalPages();
page.getTotalElements();
page.hasNext();

-- Page<T> do queries chalata hai:
-- select s.* from students s order by s.student_name asc limit ?, ?
-- select count(s.id) from students s
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Interface likho (extends JpaRepository<Entity, Id>), implementation Spring runtime par proxy se banata hai.
  • Standard methods → SimpleJpaRepository → EntityManager; custom naam → query parser.
  • save() = isNew ? persist : merge; DB tak flush/commit par; returned object use karo.
  • Derived query: find/exists/count/delete + By + conditions.
  • @Query: JPQL = entity naam, native = table naam; :param + @Param; update ke liye @Modifying.
  • Page = 2 queries (count ke saath), Slice = 1 query (sirf hasNext); page index 0 se.

Q159

Why Spring Data JPA, and what is the difference between Spring Data and Spring Data JPA?

Main Definition

  • Spring Data JPA removes the repository boilerplate: I declare an interface and Spring generates the implementation at runtime.
  • Spring Data is the umbrella module that gives a uniform Repository model for many stores (JPA, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra).
  • Spring Data JPA is its implementation for SQL databases, built on JPA and Hibernate.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Spring Data JPA में सिर्फ़ interface लिखो, implementation Spring runtime पर खुद बना देता है।
  • Spring Data बड़ा umbrella है (MongoDB, Redis भी), Spring Data JPA उसका relational database वाला हिस्सा है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)

        extends JpaRepository<Student, Long> {
    // save, findById, findAll, deleteById ... already available
}

Q160

What is the Spring Data repository interface hierarchy?

Main Definition

  • Repository is a marker interface.
  • CrudRepository adds CRUD (save, findById, existsById, deleteById, count).
  • PagingAndSortingRepository adds sorting and pagination.
  • The List variants return List instead of Iterable.
  • JpaRepository extends both List variants and adds JPA extras like flush, saveAndFlush, deleteAllInBatch.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Repository marker है, CrudRepository basic CRUD देता है, PagingAndSortingRepository sorting और paging जोड़ता है।
  • JpaRepository सब कुछ plus flush और batch delete जैसे JPA features देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
ReferenceRepository core concepts
Q161

How does Spring Data JPA work internally?

Main Definition

  • At startup Spring creates a dynamic proxy for my repository interface.
  • Standard methods (save, findById, delete) are forwarded to SimpleJpaRepository, which calls the EntityManager (persist, merge, find, remove).
  • Custom method names like findByEmail go to the query method parser, which builds the JPQL or SQL from the name.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Startup पर Spring तुम्हारे interface का proxy बनाता है।
  • save(), findById() जैसे methods SimpleJpaRepository को जाते हैं और findByName() जैसे names से query बनाकर EntityManager से चलती है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Call ka safar
StudentRepository (tumhara interface)→JDK dynamic proxy→save/findById → SimpleJpaRepository→findByName → method name se query→EntityManager→Hibernate → JDBC → DB

Q162

What does save() do internally, and is saveAll() a bulk insert? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • save() calls EntityManager.persist() for a new entity and merge() for an existing or detached one.
  • The data goes to the Persistence Context and reaches the database at flush / commit.
  • saveAll() is not a single bulk INSERT: it loops and calls save() for each entity.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • save() नई entity पर persist() और पुरानी पर merge() call करता है, और SQL commit/flush पर जाता है।
  • saveAll() एक bulk INSERT नहीं है, अंदर loop में हर entity के लिए save() ही चलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
save() ka andar ka code (simplified)
@Transactional
public <S extends T> S save(S entity) {
    if (entityInformation.isNew(entity)) {   // id null hai?
        em.persist(entity);
        return entity;
    } else {
        return em.merge(entity);             // nayi managed copy
    }
}
Dhyan dene wali baatein
  • isNew() default mein id null (ya primitive 0) check karta hai. Agar tum id khud set karte ho to save() merge() chalayega: pehle SELECT, phir INSERT.
  • merge() ka returned object use karo: entity = repo.save(entity).
  • saveAll() loop mein save() hai. Asli batch ke liye hibernate.jdbc.batch_size + SEQUENCE ids chahiye.
Dhyan doInterview mein bolo: save() = persist ya merge, aur DB tak data flush par pahunchta hai.

What are derived query methods?

Main Definition

  • A derived query method is parsed from its name as [Subject] + By + [Predicate].
  • The subject (find, exists, count, delete, findTop3, findDistinct) is the action and the predicate holds the conditions.
  • Spring generates the query for me, so I write no JPQL.

Q164

What is @Query, and how do JPQL and native SQL differ?

Main Definition

  • @Query lets me write a custom query.
  • JPQL (the default) works on entity classes and fields (SELECT s FROM Student s).
  • Native SQL (nativeQuery = true) works on table and column names.
  • I bind parameters with :name and @Param.
  • In JPQL a join can be explicit (JOIN s.department d) or implicit (s.department.active).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Query से अपनी query लिखते हैं।
  • JPQL entity class और fields पर चलता है, native SQL (nativeQuery = true) असली table और column names पर।

Q165

How do Sort, Pageable, Page and Slice work? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Sort adds an ORDER BY.
  • Pageable / PageRequest.of(pageIndex, size, sort) adds pagination, and the page index starts at 0.
  • Page<T> runs 2 queries (the data plus COUNT(*)) and knows total pages and total elements.
  • Slice<T> runs 1 query (it fetches limit + 1 rows) and only knows hasNext(), so it is faster for infinite scroll.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Sort से ORDER BY लगता है और PageRequest.of(page, size) से pagination, page 0 से शुरू होता है।
  • Page दो queries चलाता है (data + COUNT), Slice एक ही चलाता है और बस बताता है कि आगे data है या नहीं।

➡️ Agle (aakhri) topic mein: in sab ko transaction mein kaun baandhta hai? @Transactional, rollback ke rules, aur JDBC vs JPA kab kya chunna.Agla topic: @Transactional aur sahi tool chunna →

28. @Transactional aur sahi tool chunna

3 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pure part mein @Transactional baar-baar aaya: dirty checking, lazy loading, flush — sab transaction ke andar hi chalte hain. Raw JDBC mein humne setAutoCommit(false) / commit / rollback khud likha tha, aur Part 4 mein AOP proxy dekha tha. Ab dono milte hain: @Transactional = AOP proxy jo transaction sambhalta hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: teen levels par same kaam

Har service method mein try-commit-catch-rollback likhna wahi boilerplate hai jo JDBC mein tha. Ye ek cross-cutting concern hai, aur cross-cutting = AOP.

SQLPlain HibernateSpring
BEGIN;tx = session.beginTransaction();@Transactional laga do
UPDATE ...; UPDATE ...;session.persist(...)repo.save(...)
COMMIT; / ROLLBACK;tx.commit(); / tx.rollback();Proxy khud commit / rollback

Andar kya hota hai

  1. Spring tumhari service ka proxy banata hai (around advice).
  2. Call aayi: proxy TransactionManager (JPA mein JpaTransactionManager) se transaction shuru karta hai — pool se connection, autoCommit=false, naya EntityManager / Persistence Context thread se bind.
  3. Asli method chalta hai (repository calls, setters, sab).
  4. Normal return: flush (dirty checking ki SQL) + commit. RuntimeException: rollback.
  5. Connection pool ko wapas, Persistence Context band.
Yaad rakhoTransaction ki boundary = Persistence Context ki lifetime. Isiliye transaction ke bahar entity detached hoti hai aur lazy access fail hota hai.

Code: service layer par lagao

@Service
public class TransferService {

    private final AccountRepository repo;
    public TransferService(AccountRepository repo) { this.repo = repo; }

    @Transactional                       // org.springframework.transaction.annotation
    public void transfer(Long from, Long to, BigDecimal amount) {
        Account a = repo.findById(from).orElseThrow();
        Account b = repo.findById(to).orElseThrow();
        a.setBalance(a.getBalance().subtract(amount));   // dirty checking
        b.setBalance(b.getBalance().add(amount));
        // koi exception nahi → dono UPDATE ek saath commit
    }
}

-- select ... from account where id=?
-- select ... from account where id=?
-- update account set balance=? where id=?
-- update account set balance=? where id=?
-- (commit)
Real exampleRepository par nahi, service method par lagao: ek business operation = ek transaction. @Transactional(readOnly = true) read-only methods par lagao — Hibernate dirty checking skip karta hai.

Rollback rule: unchecked haan, checked nahi

Default: Spring RuntimeException aur Error par rollback karta hai, par checked exception (IOException, SQLException, tumhara custom checked) par commit kar deta hai!

ExceptionDefaultFix
RuntimeException / Error (unchecked)Rollback—
Checked (IOException, custom Exception)Commit!rollbackFor = Exception.class
Koi exception jis par rollback nahi chahiye—noRollbackFor = X.class

Kahani: checked exception par adha data save

placeOrder() mein order INSERT hua, phir payment client ne IOException phenka. Method fail hua, par Spring ne rollback nahi kiya kyunki default rule sirf unchecked par hai. Order DB mein reh gaya bina payment ke.

@Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class)   // checked par bhi rollback
public void placeOrder(Order o) throws IOException {
    orderRepo.save(o);
    paymentClient.charge(o);   // IOException aaye to bhi order undo
}

@Transactional(rollbackFor = IOException.class)  // sirf specific checked
public void createOrder(Order o) throws IOException { ... }

Common galtiyan (jinse @Transactional chupchaap fail hota hai)

  • Exception ko catch karke log kiya aur throw nahi kiya: proxy ko pata hi nahi chala, commit ho gaya.
  • Self-invocation: same class ke andar se this.save() call kiya — proxy bypass, transaction laga hi nahi (Part 4 ka AOP rule).
  • private method par @Transactional: proxy use intercept nahi kar sakta.
  • Checked exception par rollback expect kiya bina rollbackFor ke.
  • Transaction ke andar lamba HTTP call: DB connection der tak pakda rehta hai, pool khatam.
Dhyan dojakarta.transaction.Transactional bhi kaam karta hai, par rollbackFor, readOnly, propagation jaise options Spring wale org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional mein hain. Wahi import karo.

Spring JDBC vs JPA: sahi tool chuno

MetricSpring JDBC (JdbcTemplate)JPA / Hibernate
ControlSQL par 100% tumhara controlORM SQL khud banata hai
Best forReports, complex joins, bulk, tuned performanceStandard CRUD, object-oriented domain
SQL likhnaHar query khudZyadatar nahi
MappingRowMapper haath seAnnotations se automatic
Extra featuresKam magic, kam surpriseDirty checking, L1 cache, cascade, lazy
RiskBoilerplate zyadaN+1, lazy exceptions, hidden SQL
Real exampleDono ek hi project mein saath chal sakte hain aur same DataSource + same @Transactional share karte hain: normal CRUD JPA se, bhaari reports ya bulk updates JdbcTemplate se.

Poore Part 5 ka safar ek line mein

Raw JDBC (sab khud)→JdbcTemplate + HikariCP (boilerplate gaya)→JPA / Hibernate (SQL aur mapping gaye)→Spring Data JPA (repository code gaya)→@Transactional (commit/rollback gaya)
📌 Yaad rakho
  • @Transactional = AOP around advice: begin → method → flush + commit / rollback.
  • Service layer par lagao; readOnly = true read methods par.
  • Default rollback sirf RuntimeException / Error par; checked ke liye rollbackFor = Exception.class.
  • Catch karke nigal liya, self-invocation, private method = transaction fail ya laga hi nahi.
  • Transaction boundary = Persistence Context ki lifetime.
  • Control aur complex SQL → JdbcTemplate; CRUD domain → JPA; dono saath bhi chal sakte hain.

✅ Review questions (3): ab khud check karo

Q166

How does @Transactional work compared to SQL and plain Hibernate transactions?

Main Definition

  • @Transactional wraps a method in a database transaction using Spring AOP: an around advice begins the transaction before the method, commits if it finishes normally and rolls back on failure.
  • It replaces hand-written BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK in SQL and session.beginTransaction() / tx.commit() in raw Hibernate.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Transactional method के आसपास Spring AOP से BEGIN, COMMIT और ROLLBACK लगा देता है।
  • Method ठीक चला तो commit, exception आया तो rollback, बिलकुल bank transfer की तरह।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
LevelKaise
SQLBEGIN; UPDATE ...; COMMIT; (error par ROLLBACK;)
Raw Hibernatesession.beginTransaction(); ... tx.commit(); catch: tx.rollback();
Spring@Transactional + Spring AOP (around advice)
Teen tareeke, same kaam
SQLPlain HibernateSpring
BEGIN;tx = session.beginTransaction();@Transactional laga do
UPDATE ...; UPDATE ...;session.persist(...)repo.save(...)
COMMIT; / ROLLBACK;tx.commit(); / tx.rollback();Proxy khud commit / rollback karta hai
Andar kya hota hai
  1. Spring tumhari service ka proxy banata hai.
  2. Call aane par proxy TransactionManager se transaction shuru karta hai (connection autoCommit=false).
  3. Asli method chalta hai.
  4. Normal return: flush + commit. RuntimeException: rollback.
  5. Connection pool ko wapas.
  • Transaction ki boundary hi Persistence Context ki lifetime hoti hai.
  • Service layer ke method par lagao, repository par nahi.
ReferenceSpring Transaction Management
Q167

What does rollbackFor do in @Transactional? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • By default Spring rolls back for unchecked exceptions (RuntimeException and Error) and does not roll back for checked exceptions such as IOException or SQLException, so the transaction commits.
  • To roll back for checked exceptions I set @Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class) or a specific exception class.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Default में rollback सिर्फ़ RuntimeException और Error पर होता है, checked exception पर data commit हो जाता है।
  • Checked exception पर भी rollback चाहिए तो rollbackFor = Exception.class लगाओ।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Exception typeDefault behaviour
RuntimeException, Error (unchecked)Rollback
Checked (IOException, SQLException, custom)Commit, rollback nahi
Story: checked exception par data save ho gaya

placeOrder() mein order INSERT hua, phir payment client ne IOException (checked) phenka. Method fail hua, par Spring ne rollback nahi kiya kyunki default rule sirf unchecked par rollback hai. Order DB mein reh gaya bina payment ke.

Rules ek table mein
ExceptionDefaultFix
RuntimeException / ErrorRollback-
Checked (IOException, SQLException)CommitrollbackFor = Exception.class
Koi exception jo rollback na kare-noRollbackFor = X.class
Code
@Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class)
public void placeOrder(Order o) throws IOException {
    orderRepo.save(o);
    paymentClient.charge(o);   // IOException aaye to bhi rollback
}
Common mistakes
  • Exception ko catch karke log kar diya aur throw nahi kiya: Spring ko pata hi nahi chala, commit ho gaya.
  • Same class ke andar se @Transactional method call (self-invocation): proxy bypass, transaction laga hi nahi.
  • private method par @Transactional: kaam nahi karta.
// Roll back for a specific checked exception
@Transactional(rollbackFor = IOException.class)
public void createOrder(Order order) throws IOException {
    // if IOException is thrown, the transaction rolls back
}

// Roll back for all checked and unchecked exceptions
@Transactional(rollbackFor = Exception.class)
public void processPayment(Payment payment) throws Exception {
    // ...
}
ReferenceRolling back a declarative transactionSpring Transaction Management

Q168

When would you choose Spring JDBC over JPA/Hibernate?

Main Definition

  • Choose Spring JDBC when you need 100% control over the SQL, complex joins and tuned performance in data-intensive code: Spring manages the connection, but you write the SQL yourself.
  • Choose JPA/Hibernate for standard CRUD applications where object-oriented mapping matters, because the ORM generates the SQL for you.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • SQL पर पूरा control, complex joins या heavy reporting चाहिए तो Spring JDBC लो।
  • Normal CRUD app जहाँ objects और relationships हैं, वहाँ JPA/Hibernate ज़्यादा productive है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)

ControlSQL par 100% developer ka controlORM SQL khud generate karta hai
Best forData-intensive kaam, complex joins, tuned performanceStandard CRUD apps, object-oriented mapping
SQL likhnaKhud likhni padti haiZyadatar nahi likhni padti
Connection managementSpring sambhalta haiHibernate aur Spring milke sambhalte hain

Part 6: Production-ready Spring Boot

29. Testing

7 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Part 5 ke last topic (@Transactional aur sahi tool chunna) tak humari Product/Student REST API poori ban chuki hai: controller, service, JPA repository, transactions. Lekin abhi tak hum use Postman se haath se check kar rahe hain. Kal koi naya field add hoga ya query badlegi, to kaise pata chalega ki purana kuch toota nahi? Production-ready app ka pehla kadam: automated tests.
📖 Notes

Problem: Postman se testing kab tak?

Socho tumne ProductService mein discount ka logic badla. Ab tumhe 15 endpoints Postman se dobara chalane padenge, har case (valid, invalid, not found) ke saath. Ek bhi bhool gaye to bug production mein.

Automated test ek robot tester hai: mvn test chalao, 30 second mein 200 checks ho jaate hain, har PR pe CI mein bhi. Isi confidence se hum refactor aur release fearlessly karte hain.

Real examplePrice field Double se BigDecimal kiya. Unit tests ne turant bata diya ki 3 jagah rounding galat ho gaya. Bina tests ke ye customer ke bill mein dikhta.

Test pyramid: kitne tests, kis level pe

Teen level hain. Neeche unit tests: ek class, baaki sab mock, milliseconds mein. Beech mein slice tests: sirf web layer (@WebMvcTest) ya sirf JPA layer (@DataJpaTest). Upar thode integration tests: poori app + real DB (@SpringBootTest + Testcontainers). Neeche jitna zyada, upar jitna kam, utna fast aur stable build.

LevelKya pakadta haiKya nahi pakadta
UnitBusiness logic bugsWiring, JSON, SQL
SliceURL mapping, validation, JSON, queriesLayers ka aapas mein judna
IntegrationPoora flow, config, real DBKaunsi line galat hai (slow, vague)

JUnit 5: basic building blocks

spring-boot-starter-test (test scope) mein JUnit 5, AssertJ, Mockito, MockMvc, JSONPath sab aa jaate hain. Har test ka shape Arrange → Act → Assert (given / when / then) rakho: pehle data ready, phir method call, phir result check.

  • @Test = test method (public hona zaroori nahi)
  • @BeforeEach = har test se pehle fresh setup
  • @ParameterizedTest + @CsvSource = ek test, bahut inputs
  • assertThrows / assertThatThrownBy = exception check
  • Detail aur sample output: Q170, AssertJ: Q171
@Test
void discountIsApplied() {
    // Arrange
    var calc = new PriceCalculator();
    // Act
    double result = calc.withDiscount(1000.0, 10);
    // Assert
    assertThat(result).isEqualTo(900.0);
}

Mockito: service ko DB ke bina test karo

ProductService ko ProductRepository chahiye. Unit test mein real DB nahi chahiye, to hum ek mock repository dete hain jo wahi return kare jo hum bolein. Jaise film mein stunt double: dikhne mein same, control humare haath.

@Mock fake banata hai, @InjectMocks real service banake mock constructor mein daal deta hai. when().thenReturn() se script likho, verify() se check karo ki save hua, aur ArgumentCaptor se dekho ki kya save hua.

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class ProductServiceTest {
    @Mock ProductRepository repo;
    @InjectMocks ProductService service;

    @Test
    void getById_throws_whenMissing() {
        when(repo.findById(99L)).thenReturn(Optional.empty());
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> service.getById(99L))
            .isInstanceOf(ProductNotFoundException.class)
            .hasMessageContaining("99");
    }
}
Dhyan doPura example (captor, verifyNoMoreInteractions) Q172 mein. Constructor injection use karo (field @Autowired nahi) to @InjectMocks ke bina bhi new ProductService(repo) likh sakte ho.

Slice tests: @WebMvcTest aur @DataJpaTest

Controller test karna hai: URL sahi map hua? @Valid ne 400 diya? JSON mein name aaya? Iske liye poori app start karna wasteful hai. @WebMvcTest(ProductController.class) sirf web layer laata hai, aur MockMvc se bina server ke HTTP request simulate karte hain. Service ko @MockitoBean se mock karo (Boot 3.4+; purane projects mein @MockBean, jo ab deprecated hai).

Repository ke custom queries (findByNameContainingIgnoreCase, @Query) ke liye @DataJpaTest: sirf JPA layer, har test ke baad rollback.

mvc.perform(post("/api/v1/products")
        .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
        .content("""
            {"name":"","price":-5}"""))
   .andExpect(status().isBadRequest())
   .andExpect(jsonPath("$.errors.name").exists());
Yaad rakhoProduct CRUD API (Q67), ResponseEntity + 201 (Q69) aur validation (Q71) wale features ko yahi slice tests cover karte hain. Pura code Q173 mein.

@SpringBootTest + Testcontainers: real DB ke saath

Kuch bugs sirf tab dikhte hain jab sab judta hai: galat property, missing bean, PostgreSQL-specific SQL jo H2 mein chal jaata tha. Iske liye @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT) poori app real port pe start karta hai aur TestRestTemplate se asli HTTP call hoti hai.

Testcontainers test ke time Docker mein asli PostgreSQL chala deta hai. Boot 3.1+ mein container pe @ServiceConnection lagao, spring.datasource.url waghera khud set ho jaate hain.

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@Testcontainers
class ProductApiIT {
    @Container @ServiceConnection
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired TestRestTemplate rest;

    @Test
    void createThenGet() {
        var res = rest.postForEntity("/api/v1/products",
                new ProductRequest("Pen", new BigDecimal("10")), ProductResponse.class);
        assertThat(res.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.CREATED);
    }
}
Dhyan doRANDOM_PORT mein test ka @Transactional server ka data rollback nahi karta. @BeforeEach mein repo.deleteAll() karo. Details: Q174.

Test config aur profiles

Tests kabhi real payment gateway ya prod DB ko touch na karein. src/test/resources/application-test.yml + @ActiveProfiles("test"), ya ek class ke liye @SpringBootTest(properties = "..."). Testcontainers ke saath @ServiceConnection ya @DynamicPropertySource se dynamic URL.

Common galtiyan

  • Implementation detail test karna: har internal call verify karna. Behaviour (output, status, DB state) check karo.
  • Har test @SpringBootTest: build 10 minute ka ho jaata hai. Har class mein alag @MockitoBean se naya context banta hai.
  • State reset nahi karna: test A ka data test B ko fail karta hai, aur order badalne pe random failure (flaky test).
  • Sirf happy path: 400/404/409/401 cases bhi test karo.
  • Sirf H2: PostgreSQL ka JSONB, sequence, case-sensitivity H2 mein alag hai. Important queries Testcontainers pe chalao.
  • Thread.sleep se async wait karna: flaky. Awaitility use karo.
Common galtiimport org.junit.Test (JUnit 4) galti se aa gaya to test discover hi nahi hota aur build green dikhta hai. Hamesha org.junit.jupiter.api.Test.

REST API: kya test karna hai (checklist)
