📌 Yaad rakho
  • Pyramid: bahut unit, kuch slice, thode integration tests
  • Unit = JUnit 5 + Mockito, Spring context nahi
  • @WebMvcTest + MockMvc + @MockitoBean (Boot 3.4+) = controller slice
  • @DataJpaTest = JPA slice, har test ke baad rollback
  • @SpringBootTest + Testcontainers + @ServiceConnection = real DB integration
  • Behaviour test karo, implementation nahi; har test independent rakho

✅ Review questions (7): ab khud check karo

Q169

Why do we write automated tests, and what is the test pyramid? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Automated tests prove that code works now and keep proving it after every change, so you can refactor and release without fear.
  • The test pyramid says: write many fast unit tests (one class, dependencies mocked), fewer slice tests (one layer with a small Spring context, e.g.
  • @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest) and few full integration tests (@SpringBootTest, real DB).
  • Lower levels are fast and precise; higher levels are slow but catch wiring problems.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Test एक safety net है: code बदलो और 2 second में पता चल जाए कि कुछ टूटा या नहीं।
  • Pyramid कहता है नीचे बहुत सारे fast unit tests, बीच में कुछ slice tests, और ऊपर थोड़े से full integration tests।
  • जैसे building की नींव चौड़ी होती है और ऊपर की मंज़िल छोटी।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
LevelKya test hota haiSpring toolSpeed
UnitEk class (service, mapper, validator)JUnit 5 + Mockito, no Springms
SliceEk layer: web ya JPA@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest1-3 s
IntegrationPoori app + real DB@SpringBootTest + Testcontainers5-20 s
Ice-cream cone anti-pattern

Agar zyada tests @SpringBootTest ya manual Postman pe hain aur unit tests kam, to pyramid ulta ho jaata hai (ice-cream cone). Build slow, failures vague. Logic ko unit test karo, wiring ko thode integration tests se.

  • Regression pakadna: purana feature naye change se na toote
  • Refactoring ka confidence
  • Tests = living documentation
  • CI mein har PR pe automatically chalein

★ ← Pichhla important (Q167)★ Important listAgla important (Q172) → ★
Q170

What are the JUnit 5 basics: @Test, assertions, @BeforeEach and @ParameterizedTest?

Main Definition

  • JUnit 5 (Jupiter) marks a test method with @Test; @BeforeEach/@AfterEach run around every test and @BeforeAll/@AfterAll once per class (static).
  • Assertions like assertEquals, assertTrue, assertThrows fail the test when the expectation is wrong.
  • @ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource, @CsvSource or @MethodSource runs the same test with many inputs; @DisplayName gives readable names.
  • spring-boot-starter-test already includes JUnit 5, AssertJ, Mockito and MockMvc.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Test बताता है कि ये method एक test है, और assertEquals check करता है कि expected और actual same हैं।
  • @BeforeEach हर test से पहले fresh setup करता है ताकि tests एक दूसरे को affect न करें।
  • @ParameterizedTest से एक ही test अलग-अलग inputs के साथ कई बार चलता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Sample output
PriceCalculatorTest
  ✔ 10% discount on 1000 gives 900
  ✔ negativeDiscountIsRejected()
  ✔ manyCases
     ✔ 1000.0 with 0% -> 1000.0
     ✔ 1000.0 with 50% -> 500.0
     ✔ 200.0 with 100% -> 0.0
Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
JUnit 4 vs 5

JUnit 4: @Before, @RunWith(SpringRunner.class), org.junit.Test. JUnit 5: @BeforeEach, @ExtendWith(...) (Spring Boot test annotations already include SpringExtension), org.junit.jupiter.api.Test. Boot 3 mein JUnit 5 hi use karo; galat import (org.junit.Test) se test chalega hi nahi.

import org.junit.jupiter.api.*;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.CsvSource;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.*;

class PriceCalculatorTest {

    PriceCalculator calc;

    @BeforeEach                       // har test se pehle naya object
    void setUp() { calc = new PriceCalculator(); }

    @Test
    @DisplayName("10% discount on 1000 gives 900")
    void appliesDiscount() {
        assertEquals(900.0, calc.withDiscount(1000.0, 10), 0.001);
    }

    @Test
    void negativeDiscountIsRejected() {
        var ex = assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class,
                () -> calc.withDiscount(1000.0, -5));
        assertEquals("discount must be 0-100", ex.getMessage());
    }

    @ParameterizedTest(name = "{0} with {1}% -> {2}")
    @CsvSource({ "1000, 0, 1000", "1000, 50, 500", "200, 100, 0" })
    void manyCases(double price, int pct, double expected) {
        assertEquals(expected, calc.withDiscount(price, pct), 0.001);
    }
}
Q171

Why prefer AssertJ assertions over plain JUnit assertions?

Main Definition

  • AssertJ (assertThat(actual)...) gives fluent, readable assertions with rich checks for collections, strings, exceptions and objects, and much clearer failure messages.
  • It is included in spring-boot-starter-test.
  • Examples: assertThat(list).hasSize(2).extracting(Product::name).containsExactly("Pen", "Book") and assertThatThrownBy(() -> ...).isInstanceOf(...).hasMessageContaining(...).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • AssertJ में assertion English sentence जैसा पढ़ा जाता है: assertThat(price).isPositive()।
  • Lists, strings और exceptions के लिए बहुत सारे ready methods हैं और fail होने पर message भी साफ़ आता है।

Q172

How do you unit test a service with Mockito (@Mock, @InjectMocks, when/thenReturn, verify, ArgumentCaptor)? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A service depends on a repository; in a unit test we replace it with a mock so no DB or Spring context is needed.
  • @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) enables @Mock (fake dependency) and @InjectMocks (real class under test with mocks injected via constructor).
  • when(...).thenReturn(...) / thenThrow(...) stubs behaviour, verify(mock).method(...) checks an interaction happened, and ArgumentCaptor captures the argument passed to a mock so you can assert on it.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Mock एक नकली dependency है जो वही return करती है जो हम बोलें, जैसे film shooting में stunt double।
  • when().thenReturn() से behaviour set करते हैं, verify() से check करते हैं कि method call हुआ, और ArgumentCaptor से देखते हैं कि कौन सा data pass हुआ।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
APIKaam
when(x).thenReturn(v)Stub: call pe ye value do
thenThrow(ex)Stub: exception phenko
verify(m).call() / times(2) / never()Interaction hua ya nahi
any(), eq()Argument matchers (mix karo to sab matchers hon)
ArgumentCaptorPass hua argument pakdo aur check karo
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class ProductServiceTest {

    @Mock ProductRepository repo;              // fake
    @InjectMocks ProductService service;       // real, repo inject ho gaya

    @Test
    void getById_returnsDto_whenFound() {
        when(repo.findById(1L)).thenReturn(Optional.of(new Product(1L, "Pen", new BigDecimal("10"))));

        ProductResponse res = service.getById(1L);

        assertThat(res.name()).isEqualTo("Pen");
        verify(repo).findById(1L);
    }

    @Test
    void getById_throws_whenMissing() {
        when(repo.findById(99L)).thenReturn(Optional.empty());
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> service.getById(99L))
            .isInstanceOf(ProductNotFoundException.class);
    }

    @Test
    void create_savesTrimmedName() {
        when(repo.save(any(Product.class))).thenAnswer(inv -> {
            Product p = inv.getArgument(0); p.setId(5L); return p; });

        service.create(new ProductRequest("  Pen  ", new BigDecimal("10")));

        ArgumentCaptor<Product> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(Product.class);
        verify(repo).save(captor.capture());
        assertThat(captor.getValue().getName()).isEqualTo("Pen");   // trim hua?
        verifyNoMoreInteractions(repo);
    }
}
Dhyan doMockito strict stubs (MockitoExtension default) unused when(...) pe UnnecessaryStubbingException deta hai. Ye achhi baat hai: test mein faltu setup nahi rehta.
Important 58 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q169)★ Important listAgla important (Q173) → ★
Q173

What are slice tests: @WebMvcTest with MockMvc and @MockitoBean, and @DataJpaTest? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A slice test starts only one layer of the Spring context.
  • @WebMvcTest(ProductController.class) loads controllers, @ControllerAdvice, Jackson, validation and filters, but no services or repositories; you call endpoints with MockMvc and supply the service as a mock with @MockitoBean (Spring Framework 6.2 / Boot 3.4+; @MockBean before, now deprecated).
  • @DataJpaTest loads only JPA (entities, repositories, an embedded DB by default) and wraps each test in a transaction that is rolled back.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Slice test में पूरी app नहीं, सिर्फ़ एक layer start होती है, इसलिए fast है।
  • @WebMvcTest controller, JSON और validation check करता है और service को @MockitoBean से fake बना देते हैं।
  • @DataJpaTest सिर्फ़ repository और DB layer test करता है और हर test के बाद data rollback हो जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@WebMvcTest@DataJpaTest
Load hota haiControllers, advice, Jackson, validation, filtersEntities, repositories, DataSource, Flyway/Liquibase
Nahi hota@Service, @RepositoryControllers, services
ToolMockMvcRepository + TestEntityManager
DBKoi nahiEmbedded (H2) by default, ya real DB with Testcontainers
Security ke saath

Agar Spring Security classpath pe hai to @WebMvcTest security filters bhi load karta hai aur bina user ke 401/403 aata hai. spring-security-test ka @WithMockUser ya .with(jwt()) use karo (Part 7 mein dekhenge).

Already dekha

Controller test ka basic version Q73 mein hai; yahan hum use pyramid ke andar rakh rahe hain.

@WebMvcTest(ProductController.class)
class ProductControllerTest {

    @Autowired MockMvc mvc;
    @MockitoBean ProductService service;   // Boot 3.4+ (pehle @MockBean)

    @Test
    void get_returns200AndJson() throws Exception {
        when(service.getById(1L)).thenReturn(new ProductResponse(1L, "Pen", new BigDecimal("10")));

        mvc.perform(get("/api/v1/products/1"))
           .andExpect(status().isOk())
           .andExpect(jsonPath("$.name").value("Pen"));
    }

    @Test
    void create_withBlankName_returns400() throws Exception {
        mvc.perform(post("/api/v1/products")
                .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                .content("""
                    {"name":"","price":10}"""))
           .andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        verifyNoInteractions(service);     // validation ne pehle hi rok diya
    }
}

@DataJpaTest
class ProductRepositoryTest {
    @Autowired ProductRepository repo;
    @Autowired TestEntityManager em;

    @Test
    void findByNameContaining_works() {
        em.persist(new Product(null, "Blue Pen", new BigDecimal("10")));
        em.persist(new Product(null, "Notebook", new BigDecimal("50")));

        assertThat(repo.findByNameContainingIgnoreCase("pen")).hasSize(1);
    }   // test khatam -> rollback
}

Q174

How do you write a full integration test with @SpringBootTest and Testcontainers (@ServiceConnection)? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • @SpringBootTest starts the whole application context.
  • With webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT a real server starts and you call it with TestRestTemplate (or WebTestClient / RestClient); with the default MOCK environment you add @AutoConfigureMockMvc and use MockMvc.
  • Testcontainers runs a real database in Docker (e.g.
  • PostgreSQL) for the test, so you test against the same DB as production instead of H2.
  • Since Boot 3.1, @ServiceConnection on the container field auto-configures the datasource URL, user and password.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @SpringBootTest पूरी app start करता है, बिल्कुल production जैसी।
  • Testcontainers Docker में असली PostgreSQL चला देता है, ताकि H2 और असली DB के फ़र्क से bug छूट न जाए।
  • @ServiceConnection लगाने से DB का URL, username, password अपने आप set हो जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Sample log
Creating container for image: postgres:16-alpine
Container postgres:16-alpine started in PT2.1S
Tomcat started on port 54321 (http) with context path '/'
Started ProductApiIT in 6.8 seconds
Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0
Dhyan do

RANDOM_PORT mein test aur server alag threads pe chalte hain, isliye test pe @Transactional rollback server ke data ko rollback nahi karta. Isliye @BeforeEach mein cleanup karo. Docker machine pe chalna zaroori hai (CI mein bhi).

Context caching

Spring same configuration wale test classes ke liye context cache karta hai. Har class mein alag @MockitoBean / properties lagane se naya context banta hai aur build slow ho jaata hai. Common base class banao.

// pom.xml (test scope): spring-boot-testcontainers, org.testcontainers:postgresql, org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter

@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = SpringBootTest.WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@Testcontainers
class ProductApiIT {

    @Container
    @ServiceConnection                       // spring.datasource.* auto set
    static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:16-alpine");

    @Autowired TestRestTemplate rest;
    @Autowired ProductRepository repo;

    @BeforeEach
    void clean() { repo.deleteAll(); }       // har test fresh state

    @Test
    void createThenGet() {
        var req = new ProductRequest("Pen", new BigDecimal("10"));
        ResponseEntity<ProductResponse> created =
            rest.postForEntity("/api/v1/products", req, ProductResponse.class);

        assertThat(created.getStatusCode()).isEqualTo(HttpStatus.CREATED);
        Long id = created.getBody().id();

        ProductResponse fetched = rest.getForObject("/api/v1/products/" + id, ProductResponse.class);
        assertThat(fetched.name()).isEqualTo("Pen");
    }
}

Q175

How do you manage test configuration, what are common testing mistakes, and what should you test in a REST API?

Main Definition

  • Test-only settings go in src/test/resources/application-test.yml activated with @ActiveProfiles("test"), or per class with @SpringBootTest(properties = ...) / @TestPropertySource, and dynamic values via @DynamicPropertySource.
  • Common mistakes: testing implementation details (verifying every internal call) instead of behaviour, using @SpringBootTest for everything, shared state between tests, H2-only testing that hides DB differences, and only testing the happy path.
  • For a REST API test: status codes, response body, validation errors (400), not found (404), conflicts (409), security (401/403) and the business rules in the service.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Test की settings अलग profile या test properties में रखो ताकि असली DB या असली API से न टकराएँ।
  • Common गलती है हर test को @SpringBootTest बनाना, या tests के बीच data share करना।
  • REST API में सिर्फ़ 200 नहीं, 400, 404, 409 और 401 वाले cases भी test करो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
REST API checklistKis level pe
Business rules (price > 0, stock check)Unit (service + Mockito)
200/201 + JSON shape, Location header@WebMvcTest
400 validation errors ka body@WebMvcTest
404 / 409 via @RestControllerAdvice@WebMvcTest
Custom queries, constraints@DataJpaTest (Testcontainers)
401 / 403 security rules@WebMvcTest + spring-security-test
Pura flow create → get → delete1-2 @SpringBootTest
# src/test/resources/application-test.yml
spring:
  jpa:
    show-sql: true
app:
  payment-gateway:
    url: http://localhost:9999     # real gateway ko kabhi hit mat karo

// test class
@SpringBootTest
@ActiveProfiles("test")
class OrderFlowIT { ... }

@SpringBootTest(properties = "app.feature.discount=false")
class DiscountOffIT { ... }
Common galtiverify(repo, times(1)).findById(...) har test mein likhna implementation detail test karna hai. Kal service cache use kare to test toot jaayega, jabki behaviour sahi hai. Result (output) check karo; verify sirf side-effects (save, send email) ke liye.
➡️ Agle topic mein: tests pass, app deploy ho gayi. Ab production mein kaise pata chalega ki app healthy hai, slow kyun hai, aur error kahan aaya? Actuator, logging aur monitoring.Agla topic: Actuator, logging aur monitoring →

30. Actuator, logging aur monitoring

6 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein tests ne confidence diya ki code deploy se pehle sahi hai. Lekin production mein cheezein phir bhi bigadti hain: DB down, memory full, koi endpoint achanak slow. Wahan debugger nahi laga sakte. App ko khud batana padega ki andar kya ho raha hai: yahi observability hai (health + logs + metrics).
📖 Notes

Problem: production ek black box

Raat 2 baje call aata hai: 'app slow hai'. Tum server pe jaate ho, aur kya dekhoge? App zinda hai? DB connection pool full hai? Kaunsa endpoint slow hai? Kaunsi request fail hui aur kyun?

Car ka dashboard socho: speed, fuel, engine temperature, warning lights. Bina dashboard ke gaadi chalana andhere mein chalana hai. Spring Boot app ke liye dashboard teen cheezon se banta hai.

PillarSawaalTool
HealthApp zinda aur ready hai?Actuator /health
LogsKya hua, kis request mein?SLF4J + Logback, MDC
MetricsKitna, kitni der, kitni baar?Micrometer → Prometheus → Grafana

Spring Boot Actuator

Ek dependency spring-boot-starter-actuator add karo aur /actuator/* endpoints mil jaate hain. Load balancer aur Kubernetes /actuator/health dekh ke decide karte hain ki is instance ko traffic bhejna hai ya nahi.

  • health, info, metrics, loggers, prometheus, env, configprops, mappings, threaddump, heapdump
  • Web pe default sirf health exposed
  • DB, Redis, disk ke health checks auto-configure hote hain
  • Endpoint list aur kaam: Q176
# GET /actuator/health
{
  "status": "UP",
  "components": {
    "db":        { "status": "UP", "details": { "database": "PostgreSQL" } },
    "diskSpace": { "status": "UP" },
    "ping":      { "status": "UP" }
  }
}

Endpoints safely expose karo

env aur heapdump jaise endpoints config aur memory dump dikha sakte hain, jisme passwords tak ho sakte hain. Isliye include: "*" production mein kabhi nahi. Sirf zaroori endpoints, alag management port, aur security.

management:
  server:
    port: 8081                         # public 8080 se alag
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info,prometheus,loggers
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: when-authorized
Common galtiTutorial se management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* copy karke prod mein daal diya, aur public internet pe /actuator/heapdump khula reh gaya. Ye real security incident hota hai.

Custom HealthIndicator aur info

Agar app ek payment gateway pe depend karti hai to uska status bhi health mein dikhna chahiye. HealthIndicator implement karo, Health.up() ya Health.down() return karo. Info endpoint mein version aur build time info.* properties ya build-info se aata hai. Pura code aur output: Q177.

@Component
public class PaymentGatewayHealthIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    @Override
    public Health health() {
        return gatewayIsUp()
            ? Health.up().withDetail("gateway", "reachable").build()
            : Health.down().withDetail("gateway", "unreachable").build();
    }
}

Logging: SLF4J + Logback

Code SLF4J API se log karta hai, andar Logback kaam karta hai (Boot default). Har class ka apna logger: LoggerFactory.getLogger(ProductService.class), isliye log line mein class ka naam aata hai.

Levels: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR. Default INFO, matlab DEBUG/TRACE chhupe rehte hain. Package-wise level logging.level.com.example=DEBUG.

LevelKab
ERRORKuch fail hua, action chahiye (payment fail)
WARNGadbad lekin app chal rahi (retry hua, fallback)
INFOImportant business events (order placed, app started)
DEBUGDeveloper detail (method input, SQL)
TRACEBahut detail (har loop step)
log.info("Product created id={} name={}", saved.getId(), saved.getName());   // ✅ placeholder
log.info("Product created id=" + saved.getId());                              // ❌ concat
log.error("Stock sync failed for product {}", id, e);   // exception LAST argument = stack trace

Log file, rotation, profiles aur JSON logs

Production mein logging.file.name se file mein likho, aur rolling policy se 10MB pe nayi file, 14 din purani delete. Dev mein DEBUG, prod mein INFO: logback-spring.xml ke <springProfile> se (ya application-prod.yml mein logging.level).

Boot 3.4+ mein logging.structured.format.console=ecs lagao aur har line JSON ban jaati hai. ELK / Grafana Loki mein requestId ya level se filter karna aasaan. Config aur output: Q179.

{"@timestamp":"2026-10-14T04:45:02.118Z","log":{"level":"INFO","logger":"c.e.product.service.ProductService"},"message":"Product created id=42 name=Pen","requestId":"a1b2c3d4"}
Dhyan dologback.xml nahi, logback-spring.xml naam rakho. Tabhi <springProfile> aur <springProperty> kaam karte hain.

MDC: har log line mein request id

100 requests ek saath aa rahi hain, logs mix ho gaye. Ek customer ki failed request ki saari lines kaise nikaalein? MDC ek per-thread map hai: filter mein MDC.put("requestId", id) karo, aur us thread ki har log line mein wo id aa jaayegi.

Filters ka concept humne pehle dekha tha: request-id aur timing wala logging filter Q86, aur OncePerRequestFilter Q92. Yahan wahi filter MDC bharta hai.

MDC.put("requestId", id);
try { chain.doFilter(req, res); }
finally { MDC.remove("requestId"); }   // thread pool: hatana zaroori

# log
 INFO [a1b2c3d4] ProductController : GET /api/v1/products/42
 WARN [a1b2c3d4] GlobalHandler     : Product 42 not found
Common galtifinally mein MDC.remove bhool gaye to Tomcat ka wahi thread agli request mein purani requestId ke saath log karega. Galat debugging ka sabse confusing source.

Micrometer metrics: numbers naapo

Logs batate hain kya hua, metrics batate hain kitna aur kitni der. Micrometer metrics ka SLF4J hai: code ek API use karta hai, backend Prometheus, Datadog, CloudWatch kuch bhi.

Boot khud hi http.server.requests (har endpoint ka count + latency), JVM memory, GC, Hikari pool metrics deta hai. Business metrics khud banao: Counter (sirf badhta: orders placed), Timer (count + time: payment call), Gauge (abhi ki value: queue size).

Counter orders = Counter.builder("orders.placed").tag("channel", "web").register(registry);
orders.increment();

Timer.builder("payment.call").register(registry)
     .record(() -> paymentClient.charge(req));

# GET /actuator/metrics/http.server.requests?tag=uri:/api/v1/products/{id}
{ "name": "http.server.requests", "baseUnit": "seconds",
  "measurements": [ {"statistic":"COUNT","value":5321.0},
                    {"statistic":"TOTAL_TIME","value":96.4},
                    {"statistic":"MAX","value":0.84} ] }
Dhyan do@Timed annotation ke liye TimedAspect bean (aur AOP starter) chahiye; warna annotation chupchaap ignore hoti hai. Details Q181.

Prometheus + Grafana

micrometer-registry-prometheus add karo → /actuator/prometheus text format mein saare metrics deta hai. Prometheus server har 15 second mein ise pull (scrape) karta hai aur time-series DB mein rakhta hai. Grafana Prometheus se query (PromQL) karke dashboard banata hai (requests/sec, p95 latency, error rate) aur alert bhejta hai (Slack/email) jab error rate 5% se upar jaaye.

# Grafana panel query (PromQL): p95 latency per endpoint
histogram_quantile(0.95,
  sum by (le, uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_bucket[5m])))
# (histogram buckets ke liye: management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.http.server.requests=true)

Kya kabhi log mat karo

  • Passwords, JWT/refresh tokens, API keys, OTP
  • Card number, CVV, bank details, Aadhaar/PAN
  • Poora request/response body jo in fields ko le jaata ho
  • Metric tags mein userId, email (PII + high cardinality se Prometheus phat jaata hai)
Real exampleLogin request DTO ka Lombok @Data wala toString() password ke saath log ho gaya: LoginRequest(username=ram, password=Ram@123). Logs bahut logon ke paas jaate hain; ye leak hai. Sensitive fields toString se bahar rakho.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Actuator = /actuator/health, info, metrics, loggers, prometheus; web pe default sirf health
  • Sirf zaroori endpoints expose karo, alag management port + security
  • SLF4J API + Logback engine; {} placeholder; exception last argument
  • logback-spring.xml + <springProfile>; Boot 3.4+ logging.structured.format.console=ecs
  • MDC + filter = har line mein requestId; finally mein remove
  • Micrometer (Counter/Timer/Gauge) → Prometheus scrape → Grafana dashboard + alerts
  • Passwords/tokens/card numbers kabhi log nahi

✅ Review questions (6): ab khud check karo

Q176

What is Spring Boot Actuator and which endpoints does it provide?

Main Definition

  • Spring Boot Actuator (spring-boot-starter-actuator) adds production-ready endpoints under /actuator to observe and manage a running app: health (UP/DOWN incl.
  • DB, disk), info (build/git/app info), metrics (JVM, HTTP, DB pool), env and configprops (resolved configuration, values masked), loggers (view and change log levels at runtime), prometheus (metrics in Prometheus format, needs micrometer-registry-prometheus), plus beans, mappings, threaddump, heapdump.
  • Over HTTP only health is exposed by default.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Actuator app का health check-up machine है: app ज़िंदा है या नहीं, DB connected है या नहीं, memory कितनी use हो रही है, ये सब /actuator URLs पर दिखता है।
  • By default web पर सिर्फ़ health खुला होता है, बाकी हमें खुद expose करने पड़ते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
EndpointKaam
/actuator/healthUP/DOWN, load balancer aur Kubernetes probes isse dekhte hain
/actuator/infoApp version, git commit, build time
/actuator/metrics/{name}Ek metric, e.g. http.server.requests, jvm.memory.used
/actuator/loggers/{name}GET level dekho, POST se runtime pe badlo
/actuator/prometheusSaare metrics Prometheus text format mein
/actuator/env, /configpropsConfig kahan se aaya (sensitive values )
Kubernetes probes

Kubernetes pe Boot /actuator/health/liveness aur /actuator/health/readiness groups automatically enable karta hai (management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true se kahin bhi). Liveness DOWN = pod restart; readiness DOWN = traffic band.

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
  <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
</dependency>

# GET /actuator/health   (show-details: always ke saath)
{
  "status": "UP",
  "components": {
    "db":        { "status": "UP", "details": { "database": "PostgreSQL", "validationQuery": "isValid()" } },
    "diskSpace": { "status": "UP", "details": { "total": 499963174912, "free": 91234567890, "threshold": 10485760 } },
    "ping":      { "status": "UP" }
  }
}
Q177

How do you expose Actuator endpoints safely and add a custom HealthIndicator and info? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Use management.endpoints.web.exposure.include to expose only what you need (e.g.
  • health,info,prometheus), never * on a public port.
  • Put actuator on a separate management port (management.server.port) reachable only inside the network, and/or protect /actuator/ with Spring Security, allowing only health publicly.
  • Control health details with management.endpoint.health.show-details (never, when-authorized, always).
  • A custom check is a bean implementing HealthIndicator; info comes from info.* properties (with management.info.env.enabled=true), build-info and git.properties, or an InfoContributor bean.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Actuator में env, heapdump जैसे endpoints secrets और memory dump तक दिखा सकते हैं, इसलिए सब कुछ public मत करो।
  • सिर्फ़ health, info, prometheus expose करो, अलग management port रखो या security लगाओ।
  • अपनी custom health check के लिए HealthIndicator bean बनाओ।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Output
GET /actuator/health
{ "status": "DOWN",
  "components": {
    "db": { "status": "UP" },
    "paymentGateway": { "status": "DOWN",
       "details": { "gateway": "unreachable", "error": "ResourceAccessException: Connect timed out" } } } }

GET /actuator/info
{ "app": { "name": "product-service", "version": "1.4.2" },
  "build": { "artifact": "product-service", "time": "2026-10-10T08:12:00Z" } }
Naam kaise bana

Bean PaymentGatewayHealthIndicator ka component naam suffix HealthIndicator hata ke paymentGateway banta hai. Build info ke liye spring-boot-maven-plugin mein build-info goal add karo.

Dhyan do

Agar ek optional dependency down hone se poori app DOWN dikhti hai to load balancer saara traffic hata dega. Optional cheezon ko readiness/liveness groups se bahar rakho.

# application.yml
management:
  server:
    port: 8081                       # actuator alag port pe (sirf internal network)
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,info,prometheus,loggers
  endpoint:
    health:
      show-details: when-authorized
  info:
    env:
      enabled: true
info:
  app:
    name: product-service
    version: 1.4.2

// Custom health: payment gateway reachable hai?
@Component
public class PaymentGatewayHealthIndicator implements HealthIndicator {
    private final RestClient client;
    public PaymentGatewayHealthIndicator(RestClient.Builder b) {
        this.client = b.baseUrl("https://pay.example.com").build();
    }
    @Override
    public Health health() {
        try {
            client.get().uri("/ping").retrieve().toBodilessEntity();
            return Health.up().withDetail("gateway", "reachable").build();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return Health.down(e).withDetail("gateway", "unreachable").build();
        }
    }
}

Q178

How does logging work in Spring Boot with SLF4J and Logback? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Code logs through the SLF4J API (LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyClass.class), or Lombok @Slf4j); Spring Boot's default implementation behind it is Logback.
  • Levels from most to least detailed: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR; the default root level is INFO.
  • Use parameterised logging (log.info("Order {} created", id)) instead of string concatenation, and pass the exception as the last argument to get the stack trace.
  • Levels are set per package with logging.level.<package>=DEBUG and can be changed at runtime via the loggers actuator endpoint.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • SLF4J एक common interface है और Logback असली काम करने वाला engine है, Spring Boot में ये default आता है।
  • हर class का अपना logger होता है और levels होते हैं: TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR।
  • {} placeholder वाला logging use करो, string जोड़कर नहीं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Console output (default pattern)
2026-10-14T10:15:02.118+05:30  INFO 18244 --- [product-service] [nio-8080-exec-3] c.e.product.service.ProductService : Product created id=42 name=Pen
2026-10-14T10:15:07.530+05:30 ERROR 18244 --- [product-service] [nio-8080-exec-5] c.e.product.service.ProductService : Stock sync failed for product 42
org.springframework.web.client.ResourceAccessException: I/O error on POST request ...
Runtime pe level badlo
curl -X POST localhost:8081/actuator/loggers/com.example.product \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"configuredLevel":"DEBUG"}'
# restart ki zaroorat nahi; wapas INFO karna mat bhoolna
Kyun {} placeholder

log.debug("x " + bigObject) mein string hamesha banti hai, chahe DEBUG off ho. log.debug("x {}", bigObject) mein message tabhi format hota hai jab level enabled ho.

@Service
public class ProductService {
    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(ProductService.class);

    public ProductResponse create(ProductRequest req) {
        log.debug("Creating product {}", req.name());           // sirf debug mode mein
        Product saved = repo.save(mapper.toEntity(req));
        log.info("Product created id={} name={}", saved.getId(), saved.getName());
        return mapper.toResponse(saved);
    }

    public void syncStock(Long id) {
        try { stockClient.sync(id); }
        catch (RestClientException e) {
            log.error("Stock sync failed for product {}", id, e);  // exception LAST -> stack trace
        }
    }
}

# application.yml
logging:
  level:
    root: INFO
    com.example.product: DEBUG
    org.hibernate.SQL: DEBUG          # generated SQL dekhna ho to
Important 62 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q177)★ Important listAgla important (Q180) → ★
Q179

How do you configure log files, rotation, profile-specific logging and JSON (structured) logging?

Main Definition

  • Set logging.file.name (or logging.file.path) to also write to a file; Logback rotates it using logging.logback.rollingpolicy.max-file-size, max-history and total-size-cap.
  • For full control create logback-spring.xml (not logback.xml) so you can use <springProfile name="prod"> and <springProperty>.
  • Since Spring Boot 3.4, structured logging is built in: logging.structured.format.console=ecs (or logstash, gelf) prints each log line as JSON, which tools like ELK, Loki or Datadog can index.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Production में logs file में जाते हैं और rotation से पुरानी files अपने आप delete होती हैं ताकि disk न भरे।
  • logback-spring.xml से dev और prod के लिए अलग logging set कर सकते हो।
  • Boot 3.4 से एक property से JSON logs मिल जाते हैं जिन्हें ELK या Grafana Loki आसानी से search कर सकते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
JSON output (ecs)
{"@timestamp":"2026-10-14T04:45:02.118Z","log":{"level":"INFO","logger":"com.example.product.service.ProductService"},"process":{"pid":18244,"thread":{"name":"http-nio-8080-exec-3"}},"service":{"name":"product-service"},"message":"Product created id=42 name=Pen","requestId":"a1b2c3d4","ecs":{"version":"8.11"}}
Kyun JSON

Plain text ko grep karna padta hai. JSON mein requestId, level, logger alag fields hain, to log tool mein requestId:a1b2c3d4 filter karke ek request ki poori kahani mil jaati hai. Boot 3.4 se pehle logstash-logback-encoder library use hoti thi.

# application-prod.yml
logging:
  file:
    name: /var/log/product-service/app.log

Q180

What is MDC and how do you add a request id to every log line? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context) is a per-thread map in SLF4J; values put in it (e.g.
  • requestId, userId) are automatically added to every log line on that thread.
  • A servlet filter (OncePerRequestFilter) reads an incoming X-Request-Id header or generates a UUID, puts it in MDC, returns it as a response header and removes it in finally because threads are reused from a pool.
  • The log pattern prints it with %X{requestId}; structured JSON logging includes MDC keys automatically.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • MDC हर thread का एक छोटा सा bag है जिसमें requestId जैसी value रखो तो उस request की हर log line में वो अपने आप आ जाती है।
  • Filter में requestId डालो और finally में हटाओ, क्योंकि thread pool वाले threads दूसरी request में reuse होते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Output
 INFO [a1b2c3d4] ... ProductController : GET /api/v1/products/42
DEBUG [a1b2c3d4] ... ProductService    : Loading product 42
 WARN [a1b2c3d4] ... GlobalHandler     : ProductNotFoundException: Product 42 not found
 INFO [9f8e7d6c] ... ProductController : GET /api/v1/products
Filter ka basic

Filters kaise kaam karte hain aur request-id/timing wala logging filter Q86 mein detail mein hai; OncePerRequestFilter kyun: Q92.

Microservices mein

Multiple services mein Micrometer Tracing (Brave/OpenTelemetry bridge) automatically traceId aur spanId MDC mein daalta hai aur HTTP calls pe aage bhejta hai. Tab manual request id ki zaroorat kam ho jaati hai.

Async ka dhyan

MDC ThreadLocal hai. @Async ya CompletableFuture ke naye thread pe ye khaali hoga jab tak TaskDecorator se copy na karo.

@Component
public class RequestIdFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {
    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, FilterChain chain)
            throws ServletException, IOException {
        String id = Optional.ofNullable(req.getHeader("X-Request-Id"))
                            .orElse(UUID.randomUUID().toString().substring(0, 8));
        MDC.put("requestId", id);
        res.setHeader("X-Request-Id", id);
        try {
            chain.doFilter(req, res);
        } finally {
            MDC.remove("requestId");      // ZAROORI: thread reuse hota hai
        }
    }
}

# application.yml (plain text logs ke liye)
logging:
  pattern:
    level: "%5p [%X{requestId:-}]"

Q181

How do you add custom metrics with Micrometer, and how do Prometheus and Grafana fit in? What must never be logged?

Main Definition

  • Micrometer is the metrics facade in Spring Boot (like SLF4J for metrics).
  • Inject MeterRegistry and create a Counter (only goes up: orders placed), Timer (count + duration: payment call latency) or Gauge (current value: queue size); @Timed on a method also works when a TimedAspect bean is registered.
  • With micrometer-registry-prometheus, /actuator/prometheus exposes all metrics; Prometheus scrapes it every few seconds and stores time series, Grafana draws dashboards and alerts on them.
  • Never log or tag metrics with passwords, tokens, OTPs, card numbers or full personal data.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Micrometer से app के अंदर के numbers गिनते हैं: कितने orders बने, payment call में कितना time लगा।
  • Prometheus हर कुछ second में /actuator/prometheus से ये numbers खींचता है और Grafana उनसे graphs और alerts बनाता है।
  • Logs में password, token या card number कभी नहीं लिखना।

Kya log NAHI karna
  • Passwords, JWT/refresh tokens, API keys, OTP
  • Card number, CVV, Aadhaar/PAN jaisi IDs
  • Poora request body jisme ye ho sakte hain (log.info("{}", request) with toString)
  • Metric tags mein userId/email (high cardinality, aur PII bhi)
Dhyan doDTO ka toString() override karke sensitive fields mask karo, ya record mein password field ho to use alag rakho.
@Service
public class OrderService {
    private final Counter ordersPlaced;
    private final Timer paymentTimer;

    public OrderService(MeterRegistry registry) {
        this.ordersPlaced = Counter.builder("orders.placed")
                .description("Orders successfully placed")
                .tag("channel", "web")
                .register(registry);
        this.paymentTimer = Timer.builder("payment.call").register(registry);
    }

    public Order place(OrderRequest req) {
        Order o = paymentTimer.record(() -> paymentClient.charge(req));   // time naapo
        ordersPlaced.increment();
        return o;
    }
}

// @Timed ke liye (needs spring-boot-starter-aop)
@Bean TimedAspect timedAspect(MeterRegistry r) { return new TimedAspect(r); }

@Timed(value = "product.search", histogram = true)
public List<ProductResponse> search(String q) { ... }

31. Caching

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein Grafana dashboard ne dikhaya ki product details endpoint sabse zyada hit hota hai aur har baar same row DB se padhta hai, jabki product ka price din mein ek baar badalta hai. DB pe faltu load, response 40 ms. Agar result ko memory mein rakh lein to? Yahi caching hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: same sawaal, baar baar DB se

Socho ek kirana dukaan. Har customer 'Parle-G' maangta hai aur dukaandar har baar peeche godown mein jaata hai. Smart dukaandar popular cheezein counter pe rakh leta hai. Counter = cache, godown = database.

Cache se do fayde: latency kam (DB 20-50 ms vs memory <1 ms) aur DB load kam (1000 same reads = 1 query). Kimat: data stale (purana) ho sakta hai, aur memory lagti hai.

Cache-aside: kaise kaam karta hai

Spring ka @Cacheable yahi pattern method ke around proxy se lagata hai. Detail: Q182.

  1. Request aayi: product 42 chahiye
  2. Pehle cache mein key products::42 dekho
  3. Hit: mil gaya → seedha return, DB ko chhua nahi
  4. Miss: DB se padho → cache mein rakho → return
  5. Update/delete pe: DB badlo aur cache entry evict karo

Setup: @EnableCaching

Main class (ya config class) pe @EnableCaching lagao. Koi cache library nahi hai to Boot ConcurrentMapCacheManager use karta hai (simple map). Bas annotations lagao aur caching chalu.

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableCaching
public class ProductApp {
    public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(ProductApp.class, args); }
}

@Cacheable, @CachePut, @CacheEvict, @Caching

Humari Product CRUD API (Q67) ki service pe caching lagaate hain:

AnnotationMethod chalta hai?Cache pe asar
@CacheableSirf miss peResult store
@CachePutHameshaResult se overwrite
@CacheEvictHameshaEntry (ya allEntries) delete
@Caching-Upar wale ka combination
@Service
public class ProductService {

    @Cacheable(value = "products", key = "#id")
    public ProductResponse getById(Long id) {
        log.info("DB hit for product {}", id);
        return repo.findById(id).map(mapper::toResponse)
                   .orElseThrow(() -> new ProductNotFoundException(id));
    }

    @CachePut(value = "products", key = "#id")        // hamesha chalo + cache update
    @CacheEvict(value = "productLists", allEntries = true)
    public ProductResponse update(Long id, ProductRequest req) { ... }

    @Caching(evict = {
        @CacheEvict(value = "products", key = "#id"),
        @CacheEvict(value = "productLists", allEntries = true) })
    public void delete(Long id) { repo.deleteById(id); }
}

Sample output: hit vs miss

Key aur conditions: key = "#id", condition = "#page < 5" (call se pehle check), unless = "#result == null" (result pe check). Detail: Q183.

# 1st GET /api/v1/products/42   (miss)
INFO  ProductService : DB hit for product 42
Hibernate: select p1_0.id,p1_0.name,p1_0.price from product p1_0 where p1_0.id=?
-> 38 ms

# 2nd GET /api/v1/products/42   (hit)
(koi log nahi, koi SQL nahi)
-> 2 ms

# PUT /api/v1/products/42 -> cache update, list cache evict
# DELETE /api/v1/products/42 -> entry evict, agla GET phir DB se

Cache provider chuno: ConcurrentMap vs Caffeine vs Redis

Default map mein na TTL na size limit: memory badhti rahegi aur data kabhi refresh nahi hoga. Production mein mat chhodo.

Caffeine: same JVM mein, fast, size limit + TTL. Single instance ya reference data ke liye best. Redis: alag server, saare instances share karte hain, restart pe bhi bacha rehta hai.

# Caffeine
spring.cache.type=caffeine
spring.cache.caffeine.spec=maximumSize=1000,expireAfterWrite=10m

# Redis (spring-boot-starter-data-redis)
spring.cache.type=redis
spring.cache.redis.time-to-live=10m
spring.data.redis.host=localhost
Dhyan doRedis default JDK serialization use karta hai (class Serializable honi chahiye, data binary). GenericJackson2JsonRedisSerializer se JSON mein rakho. Code aur comparison table: Q184.

Kya cache karo, kya nahi

Rule: padha zyada, badla kam, laana mehenga → cache. Galat data ka nuksaan bada ho → cache mat karo.

Cache karoMat karo
Product details, categoriesCheckout ke time stock count
Config, country listWallet balance, payment status
External API (rates) 5 minHar user ka unique random search
Heavy report (TTL 1h)JPA entities (lazy relations) — DTO cache karo

Invalidation, stale data aur multiple instances

Har cache entry pe TTL lagao, chahe evict bhi kar rahe ho; koi bhool gaya evict to bhi TTL data ko theek kar dega.

Problem tab aati hai jab app ke 3 instances load balancer ke peeche hain aur har ek ka apna Caffeine cache hai. Update instance A pe gaya, A ka cache evict hua, lekin B aur C purana price dikhate rahenge jab tak TTL khatam na ho. Isliye multi-instance mein Redis (distributed cache) use karo. Detail: Q185.

Common galtiProduct update pe products::42 evict kiya lekin productLists (category page) evict nahi kiya. Detail page pe naya price, list page pe purana. Related caches bhi evict karo.

Self-invocation: cache kaam kyun nahi kar raha?

Caching bhi @Transactional ki tarah AOP proxy se chalti hai. Controller → proxy → service: proxy cache check karta hai. Lekin service ke andar this.getById(id) call proxy ko bypass karta hai, to cache lagta hi nahi. Ye wahi problem hai jo Q114 mein dekhi thi.

Fix: cached method ko alag bean mein rakho. Aur annotation sirf public method pe, Spring bean pe hi kaam karti hai. Code: Q186.

Common galtiyan

  • Default ConcurrentMap production mein: no TTL, memory leak jaisa
  • Write pe evict bhool jaana → stale data
  • Self-invocation → cache silently bypass
  • @CachePut aur @Cacheable same method pe
  • Mutable cached object ko modify karna (local cache mein sab ko badla hua dikhega)
  • Multi-instance mein local cache aur 'kabhi kabhi purana data' wale bug
  • Cache ko source of truth samajhna: DB hi truth hai, cache sirf copy
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Cache-aside: hit → return; miss → DB → cache mein put → return; write → evict
  • @EnableCaching + @Cacheable / @CachePut / @CacheEvict / @Caching
  • key, condition (pehle), unless (result pe)
  • Default map = no TTL; Caffeine = local + TTL; Redis = distributed + shared
  • Hamesha TTL + write pe evict (related list caches bhi)
  • Self-invocation se cache bypass hota hai (AOP proxy), alag bean mein rakho

✅ Review questions (5): ab khud check karo

Q182

Why cache, and what is the cache-aside pattern?

Main Definition

  • A cache keeps the result of an expensive operation (DB query, remote API call) in fast memory so repeated reads skip the slow work, reducing latency and DB load.
  • In the cache-aside pattern the application checks the cache first: on a hit it returns the cached value; on a miss it loads from the DB, stores the result in the cache and returns it; on a write it updates the DB and evicts or updates the cache entry.
  • Spring's @Cacheable implements exactly this around a method.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Cache एक छोटी fast memory है जिसमें बार-बार माँगा जाने वाला data रख लेते हैं, जैसे दुकानदार popular चीज़ें counter पर रखता है, godown में नहीं।
  • पहले cache देखो, मिला तो वहीं से दो (hit), नहीं मिला तो DB से लाकर cache में रखो (miss)।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Bina cacheCache ke saath (hit)
Latency~20-50 ms (DB)<1 ms (local) / ~1 ms (Redis)
DB queries 1000 same reads10001
RiskDB overloadStale data
  1. Request: GET /products/42
  2. Cache mein key 42 dekho
  3. Hit → seedha return (DB ko chhua bhi nahi)
  4. Miss → DB query → result cache mein put → return
  5. Update/delete → DB change + cache evict
Q183

How do @EnableCaching, @Cacheable, @CachePut, @CacheEvict and @Caching work, with keys and conditions? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • @EnableCaching turns on Spring's cache abstraction (via an AOP proxy).
  • @Cacheable("products") returns the cached value if the key exists, otherwise runs the method and caches the result.
  • @CachePut always runs the method and updates the cache (for updates).
  • @CacheEvict removes an entry (key) or all entries (allEntries = true).
  • @Caching groups several of these.
  • The default key is built from the method arguments; customise with SpEL key = "#id", and control caching with condition (checked before the call) and unless (checked on the result, e.g.
  • unless = "#result == null").

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Cacheable पहले cache देखता है, मिले तो method चलता ही नहीं।
  • @CachePut हमेशा method चलाकर cache update करता है, और @CacheEvict cache से entry हटाता है।
  • key, condition और unless से तय करते हो कि क्या और कब cache होगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Output (2 baar GET /products/42)
INFO [a1b2] ProductService : DB hit for product 42
Hibernate: select p1_0.id,p1_0.name,p1_0.price from product p1_0 where p1_0.id=?
-- doosri request: koi log nahi, koi SQL nahi (cache hit)
Dhyan do
  • Cached object return hota hai, copy nahi (local cache mein). Use modify mat karo.
  • @CachePut aur @Cacheable ek hi method pe mat lagao.
  • Update ke baad list wale caches (productLists) bhi evict karna mat bhoolna, warna list mein purana price dikhega.
  • Exception throw hone pe kuch cache nahi hota.
@SpringBootApplication
@EnableCaching
public class ProductApp { ... }

@Service
public class ProductService {

    @Cacheable(value = "products", key = "#id", unless = "#result == null")
    public ProductResponse getById(Long id) {
        log.info("DB hit for product {}", id);
        return repo.findById(id).map(mapper::toResponse)
                   .orElseThrow(() -> new ProductNotFoundException(id));   // exception cache nahi hota
    }

    @CachePut(value = "products", key = "#result.id")
    public ProductResponse update(Long id, ProductRequest req) { ... }

    @Caching(evict = {
        @CacheEvict(value = "products", key = "#id"),
        @CacheEvict(value = "productLists", allEntries = true)
    })
    public void delete(Long id) { repo.deleteById(id); }

    @Cacheable(value = "productLists", key = "#category + ':' + #page",
               condition = "#page < 5")              // sirf pehle 5 pages cache
    public List<ProductResponse> byCategory(String category, int page) { ... }
}

Q184

What is the difference between the default ConcurrentMapCache, Caffeine and Redis caches?

Main Definition

  • Without a cache library Boot uses ConcurrentMapCacheManager: a plain in-memory map with no TTL and no size limit (fine for demos, risky in production).
  • Caffeine is a high-performance local (in-JVM) cache with size limits, expireAfterWrite TTL and statistics; add com.github.ben-manes.caffeine:caffeine and configure spring.cache.caffeine.spec.
  • Redis (spring-boot-starter-data-redis) is a distributed cache in a separate server shared by all app instances; configure TTL with spring.cache.redis.time-to-live and use JSON serialization instead of the default JDK serialization.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Default cache एक simple map है जिसमें न expiry है न size limit, memory भरती रहती है।
  • Caffeine उसी app की memory में fast cache है TTL और size limit के साथ।
  • Redis अलग server है जिसे सारी app instances share करती हैं, इसलिए multiple servers में यही सही है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
ConcurrentMap (default)CaffeineRedis
KahanJVM heapJVM heapAlag server (network)
TTL / size limitNahi / NahiHaan / HaanHaan (TTL) / server memory policy
SpeedBahut fastBahut fastFast (~1 ms network)
Multiple instancesHar instance ka alagHar instance ka alagSab share karte hain
Restart peGayaGayaBacha rehta hai
KabDemo/testsSingle instance, reference dataMulti-instance, shared/session data
Redis mein kya dikhta hai
127.0.0.1:6379> KEYS product-service::*
1) "product-service::products::42"
127.0.0.1:6379> TTL "product-service::products::42"
(integer) 583
127.0.0.1:6379> GET "product-service::products::42"
"{\"@class\":\"com.example.product.dto.ProductResponse\",\"id\":42,\"name\":\"Pen\",\"price\":10.00}"
Serialization galti

Default JdkSerializationRedisSerializer ke liye class ko Serializable hona padta hai, aur Redis mein binary data dikhta hai. Class rename/package change pe purani entries deserialize nahi hoti. JSON serializer readable hai; deploy pe cache key prefix/version badal dena safe hai.

# Caffeine
spring:
  cache:
    type: caffeine
    cache-names: products,productLists
    caffeine:
      spec: maximumSize=1000,expireAfterWrite=10m

# Redis
spring:
  cache:
    type: redis
    redis:
      time-to-live: 10m
      key-prefix: "product-service::"
  data:
    redis:
      host: localhost
      port: 6379

// Redis: values JSON mein (JDK serialization ki jagah), per-cache TTL
@Bean
RedisCacheManagerBuilderCustomizer redisCustomizer() {
    var json = RedisCacheConfiguration.defaultCacheConfig()
        .entryTtl(Duration.ofMinutes(10))
        .serializeValuesWith(RedisSerializationContext.SerializationPair
            .fromSerializer(new GenericJackson2JsonRedisSerializer()));
    return b -> b.cacheDefaults(json)
                 .withCacheConfiguration("productLists", json.entryTtl(Duration.ofMinutes(2)));
}
Q185

What should and shouldn't you cache, and how do you handle invalidation and stale data, including with multiple instances? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Cache data that is read often, changes rarely and is expensive to load (product catalog, categories, config, exchange rates).
  • Avoid caching rapidly changing or must-be-exact data (stock count during checkout, account balance), per-user sensitive data in a shared cache without care, and huge result sets.
  • Every cache risks stale data, so always set a TTL, evict/update on writes, and evict related list caches too.
  • With multiple instances, local caches (Caffeine) diverge because an evict on instance A doesn't reach instance B; use a distributed cache (Redis) or accept short TTLs.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • वही data cache करो जो बार-बार पढ़ा जाता है और कम बदलता है, जैसे product catalog।
  • Stock या balance जैसा हर second बदलने वाला data cache मत करो।
  • हर cache पर TTL लगाओ, और अगर app के 3 instances हैं तो local cache की जगह Redis use करो वरना हर server अलग पुराना data दिखाएगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Cache karoCache mat karo
Product details, categoriesLive stock / seat availability at checkout
Country/state list, configWallet balance, payment status
External rate API (5 min OK)Per-request unique data (search with random filters)
Expensive report (TTL 1 hour)Bahut bade lists (memory khaa jaayenge)
Multi-instance problem
  1. Instance A aur B dono ke Caffeine mein product 42 = Rs 10
  2. Admin ka PUT instance A pe gaya: DB = Rs 12, A ka cache evict
  3. Agla GET instance B pe: B ke cache se Rs 10 (stale!)
  4. Fix: Redis (ek hi shared cache) ya short TTL ya pub/sub se evict broadcast
Other pitfalls
  • Cache stampede: popular key expire hui aur 1000 requests ek saath DB pe. Caffeine/@Cacheable(sync = true) ek hi thread ko load karne deta hai.
  • DB transaction rollback hua lekin @CachePut ho chuka: cache mein galat data. Write ke baad evict karna zyada safe hai.
  • Entities (lazy relations ke saath) cache mat karo; DTO cache karo.
Yaad rakho"There are only two hard things in computer science: cache invalidation and naming things." Shuru mein TTL + evict-on-write se kaam chalao.
Important 65 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q183)★ Important listAgla important (Q188) → ★
Q186

Why doesn't @Cacheable work when a method is called from the same class (self-invocation)?

Main Definition

  • Spring caching is implemented with an AOP proxy around the bean, just like @Transactional.
  • When a controller calls service.getById(), the call goes through the proxy which checks the cache.
  • But when a method inside the same class calls this.getById(), it bypasses the proxy, so no caching happens.
  • Fixes: move the cached method to another bean (best), or inject the bean's own proxy (@Lazy self-reference).
  • Also, caching annotations only work on public methods of Spring-managed beans.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • @Cacheable proxy के through काम करता है, जैसे receptionist हर visitor को check करता है।
  • लेकिन class के अंदर से this.getById() call करो तो receptionist बीच में आता ही नहीं, इसलिए cache नहीं लगता।
  • Cached method को अलग bean में रखो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Same problem pehle bhi

Ye wahi AOP self-invocation problem hai jo @Transactional mein dekha: Q114. Proxy kab banta hai: Q119.

@Service
public class ProductService {
    @Cacheable("products")
    public ProductResponse getById(Long id) { ... }

    public List<ProductResponse> getMany(List<Long> ids) {
        return ids.stream().map(this::getById).toList();   // ❌ cache bypass: har baar DB
    }
}

// ✅ Fix: cached lookup alag bean mein
@Service
class ProductLookup {
    @Cacheable("products")
    public ProductResponse getById(Long id) { ... }
}
@Service
class ProductService {
    private final ProductLookup lookup;
    ProductService(ProductLookup lookup) { this.lookup = lookup; }
    public List<ProductResponse> getMany(List<Long> ids) {
        return ids.stream().map(lookup::getById).toList();  // proxy se jaata hai
    }
}
➡️ App ab tested, observable aur fast hai. Lekin abhi koi bhi DELETE /products/42 call kar sakta hai aur /actuator bhi khula hai. App ready aur fast hai, ab use secure karo: Part 7 Spring Security.Agla topic: Spring Security basics aur filter chain →

Part 7: Spring Security

32. Spring Security basics aur filter chain

11 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Part 6 mein humne app ko production-ready banaya: Actuator, logging, aur aakhir mein Caching se fast bhi kar diya. App ready hai, ab use secure karo. Abhi koi bhi DELETE /api/users/5 maar sakta hai, bina login ke. Ab sawaal ye hai: request ko controller tak pahunchne se pehle kaun rokega aur poochega "tum kaun ho"? Yahin se Spring Security shuru hota hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: bina security ka app

Socho tumhari Student/Order API live hai. Koi bhi browser ya Postman se GET /api/orders/102 maar ke kisi ka bhi order dekh sakta hai, DELETE /api/users/5 se user uda sakta hai. Har controller method mein if (user == null) ... likhna? Har jagah repeat, aur ek jagah bhoole to poora app khula.

Hume ek security guard chahiye jo darwaze pe khada ho, har aane wale ko check kare, aur controller ko sirf business logic likhne de. Wahi guard hai Spring Security. Q187

Real exampleOffice building socho. Gate pe guard ID card dekhta hai (authentication: tum kaun ho). Andar har room ke darwaze pe card reader hai jo decide karta hai tumhara card ye room kholega ya nahi (authorization: tum kya kar sakte ho).

Do sawaal: Authentication vs Authorization

Pehle pehchaan, phir permission. Ye do shabd poore Part 7 ki reedh ki haddi hain. Q188

AuthenticationAuthorization
SawaalTum kaun ho?Tum kya kar sakte ho?
KaiseUsername/password, tokenRoles, authorities
OrderPehleBaad mein
Fail401 Unauthorized403 Forbidden

Shuruaat: ek dependency aur poora app lock

Ye default sirf dev ke liye hai. Real app mein hum apna SecurityFilterChain bean likhte hain aur Boot ka default hat jaata hai. Q189 Q190

  • Har endpoint ab login maangta hai (browser mein /login form, Postman mein 401)
  • Default user: user, password: upar wala (har restart pe naya)
  • Form login + HTTP Basic dono on
  • CSRF protection on, security headers on
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
</dependency>

// App start karo, console mein:
Using generated security password: 8e557245-73e2-4286-969a-ff57fe326336
This generated password is for development use only.

Kaise kaam karta hai andar se: filter chain

Part 3 mein humne Filters padhe the: wo DispatcherServlet se pehle chalte hain. Spring Security bilkul yahi use karta hai. Har request controller tak pahunchne se pehle security filters ki ek line se guzarti hai, airport ki security line jaisi. Kahin fail hui to aage nahi jaati. Q191

  1. SecurityContextHolderFilter: pichli request/session se context load karta hai.
  2. CsrfFilter: state badalne wali requests (POST/PUT/DELETE) mein CSRF token check.
  3. Authentication filters (UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter, BasicAuthenticationFilter, BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter ya tumhara JWT filter): credentials nikaal ke user pehchaante hain.
  4. ExceptionTranslationFilter: aage se aayi security exceptions pakad ke 401 / 403 mein badalta hai.
  5. AuthorizationFilter (aakhri): rule check (hasRole, authenticated). Pass to DispatcherServlet → Controller.
Dhyan doExact filters aur order tumhare configure kiye mechanism pe depend karte hain. Dekhna ho to logging.level.org.springframework.security=TRACE lagao; startup aur har request pe filters ka naam log mein aata hai.

Container se Spring tak: DelegatingFilterProxy aur FilterChainProxy

Problem: Tomcat (servlet container) Spring beans ko nahi jaanta, aur Spring Security ke filters to beans hain. Bridge chahiye.

DelegatingFilterProxy ek normal servlet filter hai jo Tomcat mein register hota hai aur kaam ek Spring bean ko de deta hai. Wo bean hai FilterChainProxy (naam springSecurityFilterChain). FilterChainProxy request ka URL dekh ke pehli matching SecurityFilterChain chalata hai. Q192

Request→Tomcat→DelegatingFilterProxy→FilterChainProxy→Matching SecurityFilterChain ke filters→DispatcherServlet→Controller

Rules likhna: SecurityFilterChain bean

Purana WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter (extend karke override) Security 6 mein hat gaya. Ab ek simple @Bean likhte hain jo HttpSecurity lekar rules banata hai. Q193

@Configuration
@EnableMethodSecurity              // Topic 3 mein kaam aayega
public class SecurityConfig {

    @Bean
    SecurityFilterChain securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        http
            .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable())                       // sirf Bearer-token API ke liye (Topic 6)
            .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                .requestMatchers("/auth/**", "/public/**").permitAll()   // sabke liye open
                .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")           // sirf ROLE_ADMIN
                .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/api/products/**").hasAuthority("PRODUCT_READ")
                .anyRequest().authenticated()                            // baaki sab: login chahiye
            )
            .httpBasic(Customizer.withDefaults());
        return http.build();
    }
}
Common galtiRules upar se neeche match hote hain, pehla match jeetta hai. anyRequest().authenticated() upar likh diya to neeche ke rules kabhi nahi chalenge (Spring error bhi deta hai). Specific pehle, generic last.

Ek se zyada chains: API alag, website alag

Ek hi app mein /api/ stateless JWT wala ho aur baaki website form-login wali, to do SecurityFilterChain beans banao. Har ek pe securityMatcher() aur @Order.

@Bean @Order(1)
SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    http.securityMatcher("/api/**")
        .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.anyRequest().authenticated())
        .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()));
    return http.build();
}

@Bean @Order(2)   // catch-all hamesha last
SecurityFilterChain web(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.anyRequest().authenticated())
        .formLogin(Customizer.withDefaults());
    return http.build();
}

Fail hua to kya: 401 vs 403

Naam confusing hai: 401 ka naam 'Unauthorized' hai par matlab unauthenticated. Q194

StatusMatlabKaun bhejtaExample
401 UnauthorizedPehchaan nahi (no / invalid / expired token)AuthenticationEntryPointToken bheja hi nahi
403 ForbiddenPehchaan liya, permission nahiAccessDeniedHandlerUSER ne /admin/ maara
http.exceptionHandling(ex -> ex
    .authenticationEntryPoint((req, res, e) -> {          // 401
        res.setStatus(401);
        res.setContentType("application/json");
        res.getWriter().write("{\"error\":\"Login required\"}");
    })
    .accessDeniedHandler((req, res, e) -> {               // 403
        res.setStatus(403);
        res.setContentType("application/json");
        res.getWriter().write("{\"error\":\"Access denied\"}");
    })
);
Dhyan doYe exceptions filter mein hoti hain, DispatcherServlet se pehle, isliye Part 3 wala @RestControllerAdvice inhe nahi pakadta. ExceptionTranslationFilter inhe in do handlers tak le jaata hai. Error body mein stack trace ya internal detail mat daalo. Q195

Current user kahan rehta hai: SecurityContextHolder

Login pass hone ke baad user ki details (Authentication: principal, authorities) SecurityContextHolder mein rakh di jaati hain, ek pocket jaisi jahan se code mein kahin bhi nikaal lo. Default strategy ThreadLocal hai: har request-thread ki apni pocket. Q196

Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
String username = auth.getName();                 // "rahul"
auth.getAuthorities();                            // [ROLE_ADMIN, USER_READ]

// Controller mein aasan tareeka
@GetMapping("/me")
public String me(@AuthenticationPrincipal UserDetails user) { return user.getUsername(); }
Common galti@Async method ya naye thread mein context khaali milta hai (ThreadLocal hai na). DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor / DelegatingSecurityContextRunnable se propagate karo.

Rules test karna

Security rules bhi code hain, aur galti hone par data leak hota hai. spring-security-test + MockMvc se har endpoint ke teen case test karo. Q197

CaseSetupExpect
Bina loginkuch nahi401
Galat role@WithMockUser(roles="USER")403
Sahi role@WithMockUser(roles="ADMIN") / .with(jwt())200
POST/PUT/DELETE (CSRF on).with(csrf())warna 403
@Test
@WithMockUser(roles = "USER")
void userCannotDelete() throws Exception {
    mockMvc.perform(delete("/admin/users/1").with(csrf()))
           .andExpect(status().isForbidden());
}
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Authentication = tum kaun ho (fail 401); Authorization = kya kar sakte ho (fail 403).
  • Starter add karte hi sab lock; default user user + console password sirf dev ke liye.
  • Request → DelegatingFilterProxy → FilterChainProxy → SecurityFilterChain filters → DispatcherServlet → Controller.
  • Rules SecurityFilterChain @Bean mein; specific upar, anyRequest() last.
  • 401 = AuthenticationEntryPoint, 403 = AccessDeniedHandler; @RestControllerAdvice inhe nahi pakadta.
  • SecurityContextHolder = current user ki ThreadLocal pocket.
  • Har endpoint ke 401/403/200 tests @WithMockUser se.

✅ Review questions (11): ab khud check karo

Q187

What is Spring Security?

Main Definition

  • Spring Security is a framework that provides authentication (who are you), authorization (what can you access) and protection against common attacks like CSRF and session fixation.
  • It works through a chain of servlet filters and integrates with Spring Boot, JWT, OAuth 2.0 and method-level security.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • मान लो आपका app एक building है और Spring Security उसका security guard है।
  • Guard पहले पूछता है "आप कौन हो?" (Authentication), फिर check करता है "आप किस room में जा सकते हो?" (Authorization), और hackers के attacks से भी बचाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Authentication: Who are you?
  • Authorization: What are you allowed to access?
  • Attack protection: CSRF, session fixation, security headers
  • Kaam karta hai servlet filters ke through, controller se pehle
  • Works with Spring Boot, REST APIs, JWT, OAuth 2.0 aur method-level security
Q188

What is the difference between authentication and authorization? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Authentication verifies identity (who you are), for example with username and password.
  • Authorization decides access (what you can do) using roles and authorities.
  • Failed authentication gives 401 Unauthorized; failed authorization gives 403 Forbidden.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Authentication = अपना ID card दिखाना (आप कौन हो)।
  • Authorization = check करना कि आपके card से कौन-सा door खुलेगा (आप क्या कर सकते हो)।
  • पहले login, फिर permission; login fail तो 401, permission नहीं तो 403।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
AuthenticationAuthorization
Verifies identityChecks permissions
Happens before access is grantedDecides what the identity can access
Example: username and passwordExample: only ADMIN can delete users
Fail = 401Fail = 403
Real exampleUser login kar leta hai, to authentication pass. Phir wo admin-only API try karta hai bina role ke, to authorization fail aur 403 Forbidden.

Q189

How do you enable Spring Security in Spring Boot?

Main Definition

  • Add the spring-boot-starter-security dependency.
  • Spring Boot auto-configuration then secures every endpoint with a default SecurityFilterChain, form login / HTTP Basic, and a generated password for the default user.
  • In real projects you override it with your own SecurityFilterChain bean.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • बस एक dependency (spring-boot-starter-security) add करो, Spring Boot automatically पूरे app को lock कर देता है।
  • बाद में हम अपने rules (SecurityFilterChain) खुद लिखते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
</dependency>
Yaad rakhoJaise hi tum apna SecurityFilterChain bean banate ho, Boot ka default chain hat jaata hai (back off).
Q190

What is the default security configuration?

Main Definition

  • With the starter added, all endpoints require authentication by default.
  • Boot auto-configures form login and HTTP Basic, creates an in-memory user named user with a generated password printed in the logs, and keeps CSRF protection on.
  • This is for development only, never production.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Dependency add करते ही हर URL lock हो जाता है।
  • एक default user "user" बनता है और उसका password console में print होता है।
  • ये सिर्फ़ testing के लिए है, production app में नहीं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Saare endpoints login maangte hain
  • Form login (/login page) aur HTTP Basic
  • Default user user + random password (har restart pe naya)
  • CSRF on, security headers on
  • Fixed password chahiye to spring.security.user.name / spring.security.user.password (sirf dev ke liye)
