Q191

What is the Spring Security filter chain? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • The filter chain is an ordered set of servlet filters (SecurityContext, authentication, CSRF, ExceptionTranslationFilter, AuthorizationFilter) that every request passes through before the DispatcherServlet and controller.
  • Spring plugs it in through DelegatingFilterProxy and FilterChainProxy.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Filter chain airport की security line जैसी है।
  • हर request को controller तक पहुँचने से पहले कई checkpoints से गुज़रना पड़ता है।
  • कहीं fail हुई तो आगे नहीं जाती।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Exact filters aur unka order tumhare configure kiye mechanism (form login, Basic, JWT) pe depend karta hai
  • Request controller invoke hone se pehle hi reject ho sakti hai
  • Login nahi = 401, permission nahi = 403
  • Debug: logging.level.org.springframework.security=TRACE se har filter ka naam log mein dikhta hai
Important 67 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q188)★ Important listAgla important (Q193) → ★
Q192

What are DelegatingFilterProxy and FilterChainProxy? Can we have multiple SecurityFilterChains?

Main Definition

  • DelegatingFilterProxy is a plain servlet filter registered with the container that delegates to a Spring bean.
  • That bean is FilterChainProxy (springSecurityFilterChain), which picks the first matching SecurityFilterChain for the request.
  • Yes, you can define multiple SecurityFilterChain beans, each with a securityMatcher() and an @Order, for example one for /api/ (JWT, stateless) and one for the web UI (form login).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • DelegatingFilterProxy एक bridge है जो servlet container की request Spring तक पहुँचाता है।
  • FilterChainProxy फिर decide करता है कि इस URL पर कौन-सी security chain लगेगी।
  • अलग URLs के लिए अलग chains बना सकते हो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Bean @Order(1)
SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    http.securityMatcher("/api/**")
        .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.anyRequest().authenticated())
        .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()));
    return http.build();
}

@Bean @Order(2)
SecurityFilterChain web(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.anyRequest().authenticated())
        .formLogin(Customizer.withDefaults());
    return http.build();
}
Dhyan doPehli matching chain hi chalti hai. Bina securityMatcher wali (catch-all) chain ko sabse aakhri @Order do, warna wo sab kuch pakad legi.
Q193

What is SecurityFilterChain? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • SecurityFilterChain is the bean that defines the HttpSecurity rules: which requests are public (permitAll), which need login (authenticated), which need a role or authority, and which mechanisms (form login, Basic, JWT, CSRF, CORS, session policy) are enabled.
  • It replaced the deprecated (and in Security 6 removed) WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • SecurityFilterChain rules की एक list है: कौन-सा URL सबके लिए open है, कौन-सा login माँगता है, और कौन-सा सिर्फ़ ADMIN के लिए है।
  • ये एक @Bean के रूप में लिखी जाती है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • permitAll(): koi bhi access kar sakta hai
  • authenticated(): login zaroori
  • hasRole("ADMIN"): ROLE_ADMIN authority chahiye
  • hasAuthority("USER_READ"): exact wahi authority chahiye
  • Rules upar se neeche match hote hain: specific pehle, anyRequest() last mein
@Configuration
@EnableMethodSecurity
public class SecurityConfig {
    @Bean
    SecurityFilterChain securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        http
            .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable())
            .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
                .requestMatchers("/auth/**").permitAll()
                .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")
                .anyRequest().authenticated()
            )
            .httpBasic(Customizer.withDefaults());
        return http.build();
    }
}
Dhyan doYe Spring Boot 3 / Security 6+ ka simplified example hai. CSRF disable karna aur HTTP Basic production ke universal defaults nahi hain. Mechanism apne architecture ke hisaab se choose karo.
Important 68 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q191)★ Important listAgla important (Q194) → ★
Q194

What is the difference between 401 and 403? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • 401 Unauthorized means authentication failed or is missing (no token, or an invalid or expired one).
  • 403 Forbidden means the user is authenticated but not authorized for that resource.
  • In Spring, 401 comes from the AuthenticationEntryPoint and 403 from the AccessDeniedHandler.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • 401 = "आप कौन हो, पता नहीं" (login नहीं या token invalid)।
  • 403 = "आपको पहचान लिया, पर ये काम करने की permission नहीं है"।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
HTTP statusMeaningExample
401 UnauthorizedAuthentication missing ya invalidMissing ya expired access token
403 ForbiddenRequest samjhi, access deniedLogged-in user ke paas ADMIN role nahi
Yaad rakhoNaam confusing hai: 401 ka naam 'Unauthorized' hai par matlab unauthenticated hai.
Important 69 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q193)★ Important listAgla important (Q198) → ★
Q195

How do you handle security exceptions?

Main Definition

  • With an AuthenticationEntryPoint (unauthenticated, returns 401) and an AccessDeniedHandler (authenticated but not allowed, returns 403), configured through http.exceptionHandling().
  • The ExceptionTranslationFilter catches the security exceptions and calls them.
  • Return a consistent JSON error body and do not leak internal details.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Login नहीं है तो AuthenticationEntryPoint response देता है (401)।
  • Login है पर permission नहीं तो AccessDeniedHandler (403)।
  • दोनों में clean JSON error भेजो, internal details नहीं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
http.exceptionHandling(ex -> ex
    .authenticationEntryPoint((request, response, exception) ->
        response.sendError(401))
    .accessDeniedHandler((request, response, exception) ->
        response.sendError(403))
);
Dhyan doFilter mein aayi security exceptions @RestControllerAdvice tak nahi pahunchti, kyunki wo DispatcherServlet se pehle hoti hain. Isliye inke liye ye do handlers hi sahi jagah hain. Consistent error format, koi stack trace nahi, aur security events ko log karo.
Q196

What is SecurityContextHolder?

Main Definition

  • SecurityContextHolder holds the SecurityContext, which contains the current Authentication (principal, credentials, authorities).
  • By default it uses a ThreadLocal strategy, so the context must be propagated explicitly to async threads.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • SecurityContextHolder एक pocket की तरह है जिसमें current logged-in user की details रखी होती हैं।
  • Code में कहीं भी निकालकर देख सकते हो कि user कौन है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Authentication auth = SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication();
String username = auth.getName();

// Controller mein seedha bhi le sakte ho
@GetMapping("/me")
public String me(@AuthenticationPrincipal UserDetails user) {
    return user.getUsername();
}
Dhyan doServlet apps mein context current thread se juda hota hai. @Async ya naye thread mein wo khaali milega; DelegatingSecurityContextExecutor / DelegatingSecurityContextRunnable jaise wrappers se propagate karo.
Q197

How do you test Spring Security?

Main Definition

  • Use spring-security-test with MockMvc.
  • @WithMockUser(roles = "ADMIN") runs a test as a fake logged-in user, and the jwt() and csrf() request post-processors add a token or a CSRF token.
  • Assert 401, 403 and 200 for each role.
  • Method security is tested with @WithMockUser on service tests.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Testing में fake user बनाकर check करो: बिना login 401, wrong role 403, सही role 200।
  • @WithMockUser ये काम आसान कर देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Test
@WithMockUser(roles = "USER")
void userCannotDelete() throws Exception {
    mockMvc.perform(delete("/admin/users/1").with(csrf()))
           .andExpect(status().isForbidden());          // 403
}

@Test
void anonymousGets401() throws Exception {
    mockMvc.perform(get("/api/orders"))
           .andExpect(status().isUnauthorized());       // 401
}

@Test
void jwtUserCanRead() throws Exception {
    mockMvc.perform(get("/api/orders")
            .with(jwt().authorities(new SimpleGrantedAuthority("ORDER_READ"))))
           .andExpect(status().isOk());                 // 200
}
Yaad rakhoHar secured endpoint ke liye teen test: anonymous (401), galat role (403), sahi role (200). Ye security rules ka regression net hai.
➡️ Agle topic mein: filter ne "tum kaun ho" check kaise kiya? Login andar se: UserDetailsService, AuthenticationProvider aur BCrypt passwords.Agla topic: Login andar se aur passwords →

33. Login andar se aur passwords

7 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichhle topic mein dekha ki authentication filter request se credentials nikaalta hai aur kaamyaab hone par user ko SecurityContextHolder mein rakhta hai. Par beech mein hua kya? Username se user DB se kaun laaya, password kisne match kiya, aur password DB mein kaise save hai? Ye login ka andar ka safar hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: default user se kaam nahi chalega

Real app mein users DB ki users table mein hain, apne password aur role ke saath. Spring Security ko batana hai ki user kahan se laaye aur password kaise match kare. Iske liye teen khiladi hain: AuthenticationManager, AuthenticationProvider, UserDetailsService (+ PasswordEncoder).

Login ka flow (andar se)

  1. Filter (ya tumhara /auth/login controller) username + password se UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken (unauthenticated) banata hai.
  2. AuthenticationManager (implementation: ProviderManager) ko deta hai. Manager khud check nahi karta, sahi provider ko de deta hai.
  3. DaoAuthenticationProvider UserDetailsService.loadUserByUsername() se user (hash + roles) laata hai.
  4. Provider passwordEncoder.matches(typed, storedHash) chalata hai.
  5. Match: authenticated Authentication (authorities ke saath) wapas; SecurityContextHolder mein set. Galat: BadCredentialsException → 401.
Real exampleBank branch: manager (AuthenticationManager) form leta hai aur clerk (Provider) ko de deta hai. Clerk register (UserDetailsService) se tumhara record nikaalta hai aur signature match karta hai (PasswordEncoder).

UserDetailsService: sirf user laana

Ek hi method: loadUserByUsername(). Kaam sirf DB se user nikaal ke UserDetails mein lapetna. Password match karna iska kaam nahi. Q198

@Service
public class CustomUserDetailsService implements UserDetailsService {
    private final UserRepository repository;
    public CustomUserDetailsService(UserRepository repository) { this.repository = repository; }

    @Override
    public UserDetails loadUserByUsername(String username) {
        AppUser user = repository.findByUsername(username)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new UsernameNotFoundException("User not found"));
        return User.withUsername(user.getUsername())
            .password(user.getPassword())      // DB ka BCrypt hash
            .authorities(user.getRole())       // "ROLE_ADMIN"
            .build();
    }
}
Yaad rakhoSpring Boot ko ek UserDetailsService bean aur ek PasswordEncoder bean mil jaaye to wo khud DaoAuthenticationProvider bana deta hai. Alag provider likhne ki zarurat tab hai jab login ka tareeka alag ho (OTP, LDAP).

Manager vs Provider vs UserDetailsService

Q199

ComponentKaamAnalogy
AuthenticationManager (ProviderManager)Request leta hai, providers ko try karta haiBranch manager
AuthenticationProvider (DaoAuthenticationProvider)Asli authenticationClerk
UserDetailsServiceUser loadRegister
PasswordEncoderHash banana / match karnaSignature verify
// JWT login endpoint mein manager ko khud use karte hain (Topic 4)
@Bean
AuthenticationManager authenticationManager(AuthenticationConfiguration cfg) throws Exception {
    return cfg.getAuthenticationManager();
}

Passwords: plain text kabhi nahi

Maan lo DB leak ho gaya. Plain text passwords hain to attacker ko sab mil gaye, aur log wahi password Gmail aur bank pe bhi use karte hain. Isliye hash store karte hain: one-way machine, password andar, fixed string bahar, wapas password nahi nikalta. Login pe typed password ko phir hash karke compare karte hain. Q200

Hashing encryption nahi hai. Encryption ko key se wapas khol sakte ho; hash ko nahi.

MD5 / SHA-256 kyun nahi? BCrypt kyun?

Q201

  • Salt: random string jud ke hash; 1000 users ka '123456' bhi 1000 alag hash. Salt hash string ke andar hi store hota hai.
  • Slow + adaptive: cost factor 10 = 2^10 = 1024 rounds. User ko milliseconds, attacker ko saal. Hardware tez ho to cost badha do.
  • Format: $2a$ version, 10 cost, phir 22 char salt, phir hash.
MD5 / SHA-256BCrypt
SpeedBahut tez (GPU pe billions/sec)Jaan-boojh ke slow
SaltNahiHar password ka random salt
Same password, same hash?HaanNahi
Rainbow tableKaam karti haiBekaar
Passwords ke liyeNahiHaan (Argon2, PBKDF2 bhi)

Spring mein: encode() aur matches()

@Bean
PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
    return new BCryptPasswordEncoder();          // default strength 10
}

// Register
user.setPassword(passwordEncoder.encode("Secret@123"));
// DB: $2a$10$N9qo8uLOickgx2ZMRZoMyeIjZAgcfl7p92ldGxad68LJZdL17lhWy

passwordEncoder.encode("Secret@123");   // har baar ALAG output (salt random)
passwordEncoder.matches("Secret@123", storedHash);   // true
Common galtiencode(raw).equals(storedHash) se compare karna. Ye hamesha false aayega kyunki salt har baar naya hai. Hamesha matches().

Algorithm badalna ho to: DelegatingPasswordEncoder

Purane app mein SHA hashes pade hain aur ab BCrypt pe jaana hai, bina sab users ka password reset kiye? DelegatingPasswordEncoder har hash ke aage {id} prefix lagata hai, isliye ek saath kai algorithms chal sakte hain, aur login pe purana hash naye mein upgrade ho sakta hai. Q202

@Bean
PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
    return PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder();  // naye hash: {bcrypt}
}
// {bcrypt}$2a$10$N9qo8uLOickgx2ZMRZoMye...
// {pbkdf2}5d923b44a6d129f3ddf3e3c8...
// {noop}password      <- sirf demo
Dhyan doPrefix-less purana hash + DelegatingPasswordEncoder = error There is no PasswordEncoder mapped for the id "null".

Session wale app mein: session fixation

Form-login app login ke baad user ko HTTP session (JSESSIONID cookie) se yaad rakhta hai. Attack: attacker pehle se ek session ID victim ke browser mein fit kar deta hai, victim login karta hai, aur attacker usi ID se andar. Spring ka bachav: login hote hi session ID badal do (changeSessionId, default). Q203

SessionCreationPolicyMatlab
ALWAYSHamesha session banao
IF_REQUIRED (default)Zarurat ho to
NEVERKhud mat banao, ho to use karo
STATELESSKabhi nahi (JWT APIs, Topic 4)
http.sessionManagement(session -> session
    .sessionFixation(fix -> fix.changeSessionId())   // default
    .maximumSessions(1)                              // ek user, ek session
    .maxSessionsPreventsLogin(false)                 // naya login purana hata de
);

"Mujhe yaad rakho": Remember-Me

Browser band hone pe session cookie chali jaati hai. Remember-Me ek long-lived cookie deta hai. Do tareeke: hash-based (cookie mein signed hash; simple) aur persistent token (series + token DB mein; revoke aur chori detect ho sakti hai, isliye safer). Q204

http.rememberMe(rm -> rm
    .tokenRepository(persistentTokenRepository())
    .tokenValiditySeconds(14 * 24 * 60 * 60));     // 14 din
Dhyan doRemember-me se aaya user password change ya payment jaise kaam ke liye dobara password de. Ye rotation wala idea (series + token) Topic 5 ke refresh tokens mein phir milega.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Manager (ProviderManager) → DaoAuthenticationProvider → UserDetailsService + PasswordEncoder → SecurityContextHolder.
  • UserDetailsService sirf user laata hai; password provider match karta hai.
  • Password: BCrypt/Argon2/PBKDF2 (slow + salt + adaptive); MD5/SHA-256 kabhi nahi.
  • Compare matches() se, equals() se kabhi nahi.
  • DelegatingPasswordEncoder: {bcrypt} prefix, algorithm migration.
  • Session fixation: login pe session ID change (default).
  • Remember-Me: persistent token approach safer.

✅ Review questions (7): ab khud check karo

Q198

What is UserDetailsService? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • UserDetailsService is a core interface with one method, loadUserByUsername(), that loads a user as a UserDetails object from a data source like a database.
  • It only loads the user.
  • Password verification is done by the AuthenticationProvider with a PasswordEncoder.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • UserDetailsService एक register की तरह है।
  • आप username दो, ये database से उस user की details (password hash, role) निकाल देता है।
  • Password match करना इसका काम नहीं है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Service
public class CustomUserDetailsService implements UserDetailsService {
    private final UserRepository repository;

    public CustomUserDetailsService(UserRepository repository) {
        this.repository = repository;
    }

    @Override
    public UserDetails loadUserByUsername(String username) {
        AppUser user = repository.findByUsername(username)
            .orElseThrow(() -> new UsernameNotFoundException("User not found"));
        return User.withUsername(user.getUsername())
            .password(user.getPassword())     // already encoded (BCrypt hash)
            .authorities(user.getRole())      // e.g. "ROLE_ADMIN"
            .build();
    }
}
Dhyan doYahan user.getPassword() already encoded hash return karta hai, aur getRole() kuch aisa deta hai: ROLE_ADMIN. Apni entity ka naam User mat rakho warna Spring ke User builder se naam takrayega.
Important 70 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q194)★ Important listAgla important (Q199) → ★
Q199

What is the difference between UserDetailsService and AuthenticationProvider? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • UserDetailsService only loads user data.
  • AuthenticationProvider performs the actual authentication: it takes the credentials, uses the loaded user and the PasswordEncoder, and returns an authenticated Authentication object.
  • DaoAuthenticationProvider is the standard one for username/password, and it is called by the AuthenticationManager (ProviderManager).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • AuthenticationManager manager है, AuthenticationProvider असली checking करता है।
  • Provider, UserDetailsService से user लेता है और PasswordEncoder से password match करता है।
  • Match हो गया तो login successful।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
ComponentKaam
AuthenticationManager (ProviderManager)Request leta hai, sahi provider ko deta hai
AuthenticationProvider (DaoAuthenticationProvider)Asli check: user lao + password match
UserDetailsServiceSirf user DB se load karna
PasswordEncodermatches(raw, hash)
// Login endpoint mein manager ko use karna
@Bean
AuthenticationManager authenticationManager(AuthenticationConfiguration cfg) throws Exception {
    return cfg.getAuthenticationManager();
}

Authentication auth = authenticationManager.authenticate(
    new UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(req.username(), req.password()));
// galat password -> BadCredentialsException
Yaad rakhoKai providers ho sakte hain (DB, LDAP, OTP). ProviderManager unhe ek-ek karke try karta hai jab tak koi supports() karke authenticate na kar de.
Important 71 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q198)★ Important listAgla important (Q200) → ★
Q200

How do you store passwords securely? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Never store plain-text passwords.
  • Store a one-way, salted, adaptive hash using BCryptPasswordEncoder (or Argon2 / PBKDF2).
  • On login, Spring compares the submitted password with the stored hash through PasswordEncoder.matches().
  • Hashing is not encryption.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Password को कभी plain text में save नहीं करते।
  • BCrypt उसे hash में बदल देता है, जिसे वापस password में convert नहीं किया जा सकता।
  • Login पर typed password को उसी तरह hash करके match करते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Kyun hash, aur BCrypt hi kyun?

Hash one-way hota hai: password se hash ban sakta hai, par hash se password wapas nahi nikalta. BCrypt isme salt (har password ke liye random string) aur slow rounds (cost factor, Spring default 10) jodta hai, isliye same password ke hash alag aate hain aur brute-force bahut mehnga ho jaata hai. Poori detail Q201 mein.

Register vs login

Register par encode() se hash banake DB mein save karo. Login par Spring matches(raw, storedHash) chalata hai, jo stored hash ke andar se salt aur cost nikaal leta hai. Compare hamesha matches() se karo, equals() se nahi, kyunki encode() har baar alag output deta hai.

@Bean
PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
    return new BCryptPasswordEncoder();
}

// Register ke time
String encoded = passwordEncoder.encode(request.getPassword());
user.setPassword(encoded);

// Login par Spring khud chalata hai:
passwordEncoder.matches(rawPassword, storedHash);  // true / false
Important 72 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q199)★ Important listAgla important (Q208) → ★
Q201

What is password encoding, and why not use MD5 or SHA-256 directly?

Main Definition

  • Passwords need a slow, salted, adaptive hash such as BCrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2.
  • MD5 and plain SHA-256 are fast general-purpose hashes, so attackers can test billions of guesses per second using GPUs and rainbow tables.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • MD5/SHA बहुत fast हैं, इसलिए attacker एक second में करोड़ों passwords try कर सकता है।
  • BCrypt जानबूझकर slow है और हर password में random salt add करता है, जिससे crack करना बहुत मुश्किल हो जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
MD5 / SHA-256BCrypt
SpeedVery fastDeliberately slow
SaltBuilt-in nahiBuilt-in, har password ka random
Same password, same hash?HaanNahi
Rainbow tableKaam karti haiBekaar
Passwords ke liye?NahiHaan
Problem kya hai?

Maan lo database leak ho gaya. Passwords plain text mein hain to attacker ko sab mil gaye, aur log wahi password dusri sites pe bhi use karte hain. Isliye hash store karte hain, par hash kaisa hai ye bahut matter karta hai.

Dikkat 1: MD5 / SHA-256 bahut tez hain

Ye files check karne jaise kaamon ke liye bane the. Ek modern GPU second mein billions hashes nikaal sakta hai. Attacker common passwords (123456, password, qwerty) ka hash nikaal ke chori hui DB se match karta hai (dictionary / brute-force attack).

Dikkat 2: salt nahi

Same password ka same hash aata hai, to attacker pehle se badi lookup table (rainbow table) bana leta hai. 1000 users ka password 123456 hai to DB mein 1000 jagah same hash. Ek crack, sab crack.

BCrypt kya add karta hai
  • Salt: har password ke saath random string; same password ke hash alag; rainbow table bekaar. Salt chhupana nahi padta, hash string ke andar hi hota hai.
  • Slow (adaptive): cost factor 10 = 2^10 rounds. User ko kuch milliseconds ka fark, attacker ke liye saalon ka kaam. Computers tez hon to cost badha do.
Good vs bad
  • Good: BCrypt, Argon2, PBKDF2
  • Bad for passwords: MD5, SHA-1, plain SHA-256
$2a$10$N9qo8uLOickgx2ZMRZoMyeIjZAgcfl7p92ldGxad68LJZdL17lhWy
 |   |  |<------- 22 char salt ---->|<------- 31 char hash ------->|
 |   +-- cost factor 10 (2^10 = 1024 rounds)
 +------ BCrypt version
Q202

What is DelegatingPasswordEncoder?

Main Definition

  • DelegatingPasswordEncoder is the default encoder from PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder().
  • It stores a prefix with each hash, like {bcrypt}$2a$10$..., so the app can support multiple algorithms at once.
  • It can also migrate old hashes to a stronger algorithm (upgrade on login) without breaking existing users.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Hash के आगे {bcrypt} जैसा prefix लगता है ताकि Spring को पता चले कौन-सा algorithm use हुआ।
  • इससे पुराने weak hashes को धीरे-धीरे नए strong hash में migrate कर सकते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Bean
PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder() {
    return PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder();
}
// DB mein stored values:
// {bcrypt}$2a$10$N9qo8uLOickgx2ZMRZoMye...
// {pbkdf2}5d923b44a6d129f3ddf3e3c8d29412723dcbde72...
// {noop}password   <- sirf demo, kabhi production mein nahi
Dhyan doPrefix ke bina hash DB mein ho aur DelegatingPasswordEncoder use karo to error aata hai: There is no PasswordEncoder mapped for the id "null". Upgrade on login ke liye UserDetailsPasswordService implement karo.
Q203

What is session fixation, and how does Spring handle session management?

Main Definition

  • Session fixation is an attack where the attacker plants a known session ID in the victim's browser before login and reuses it after the victim logs in.
  • Spring prevents it by changing the session ID on login (changeSessionId, the default).
  • With sessionManagement() you can also limit concurrent sessions per user and choose a SessionCreationPolicy (ALWAYS, IF_REQUIRED, NEVER, STATELESS).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Session fixation में attacker पहले से एक session ID आपके browser में set कर देता है।
  • Spring login होते ही session ID change कर देता है, तो attacker वाली ID बेकार हो जाती है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Default protection: successful login par changeSessionId()
  • maximumSessions(n): ek user ke concurrent logins limit
  • IF_REQUIRED (default): zarurat ho to session banao
  • STATELESS: koi HttpSession nahi (JWT APIs)
http.sessionManagement(session -> session
    .sessionFixation(fix -> fix.changeSessionId())
    .maximumSessions(1)                 // ek user, ek session
    .maxSessionsPreventsLogin(false)    // naya login purana session hata deta hai
);
Q204

What is Remember-Me authentication?

Main Definition

  • Remember-Me keeps a user logged in across browser restarts using a long-lived cookie.
  • Spring offers a hash-based token (simple, the cookie holds a signed hash) and a persistent token approach (series + token stored in a database, safer because tokens can be revoked and theft can be detected).
  • It is enabled with http.rememberMe().

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Remember-Me मतलब "मुझे याद रखो" checkbox।
  • एक long-lived cookie save होती है, जिससे browser दोबारा खोलने पर भी आप logged-in रहते हो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
http.rememberMe(rm -> rm
    .tokenRepository(persistentTokenRepository())   // JdbcTokenRepositoryImpl
    .tokenValiditySeconds(14 * 24 * 60 * 60)         // 14 days
);
Dhyan doRemember-me cookie se login hua user sensitive kaam (password change, payment) ke liye dobara password se verify karwao.
➡️ Agle topic mein: login ho gaya, user pehchaan liya. Ab ye user kya-kya kar sakta hai? Roles, authorities, method security aur ownership check.Agla topic: Authorization: roles, method security aur ownership →

34. Authorization: roles, method security aur ownership

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichhle topic mein login ho gaya aur UserDetailsService ne user ke saath uski authorities (ROLE_ADMIN, USER_READ) bhi SecurityContext mein rakh di. Ab inhi authorities se decide hoga ki user kya kar sakta hai: yahi authorization hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: login hona kaafi nahi

Login karke har user har cheez kar sake? Nahi. Office mein manager leave approve karta hai, employee nahi. App mein ADMIN user delete karta hai, normal USER nahi. Aur ek level aur: Rahul sirf apna order dekhe, Priya ka nahi. Yahi teen layers hain: role, permission, ownership.

RBAC: role aur authority

Q205

  • Role = bada group: ADMIN, MANAGER, USER. Spring mein ROLE_ prefix ke saath: ROLE_ADMIN.
  • Authority = chhoti exact permission: USER_READ, USER_DELETE, ORDER_APPROVE. Koi prefix nahi.
  • Spring ke liye role bhi ek authority hi hai, bas ROLE_ se shuru.
User (DB)→ROLE_ADMIN, USER_DELETE→SecurityContext→hasRole / hasAuthority→200 ya 403
// UserDetailsService ke andar
return User.withUsername("rahul")
    .password(encodedPassword)
    .authorities("ROLE_ADMIN", "USER_READ", "USER_DELETE")
    .build();
// ya sirf roles: .roles("ADMIN")  -> Spring khud ROLE_ADMIN bana deta hai

Example 1: hasRole() (role ke basis pe)

hasRole('ADMIN') likhoge to Spring andar se ROLE_ADMIN dhoondhta hai. Prefix khud lagata hai, isliye hasRole('ROLE_ADMIN') mat likhna.

// URL level (SecurityFilterChain)
http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers("/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")                    // sirf ADMIN
    .requestMatchers("/reports/**").hasAnyRole("ADMIN", "MANAGER")    // dono mein se koi
    .anyRequest().authenticated()
);

// Method level
@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
@DeleteMapping("/users/{id}")
public void deleteUser(@PathVariable Long id) { userService.deleteUser(id); }

Example 2: hasAuthority() (exact permission)

hasAuthority('USER_DELETE') bilkul wahi string match karta hai. Isse fine-grained control milta hai: MANAGER ko sirf USER_READ do, USER_DELETE nahi.

hasRole()hasAuthority()
Kya checkRole (group)Exact permission string
PrefixROLE_ khud lagataKoi nahi
ExamplehasRole('ADMIN') = ROLE_ADMINhasAuthority('USER_DELETE')
KabBade groupsChhoti permissions: read, delete, approve
Fail403403
http.authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.GET, "/users/**").hasAuthority("USER_READ")
    .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.DELETE, "/users/**").hasAuthority("USER_DELETE")
);

@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('USER_DELETE')")
public void deleteUser(Long id) { ... }

// Ye dono same kaam karte hain:
@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")             // ROLE_ADMIN check
@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN')")   // ROLE_ADMIN check
Real exampleOffice app: ADMIN ke paas USER_READ + USER_DELETE, MANAGER ke paas sirf USER_READ, USER ke paas kuch nahi. MANAGER GET /users → 200, DELETE /users/5 → 403. Q206

Method-level security: kyun, jab URL rules hain?

URL rule darwaze pe guard jaisa hai; method security kamre ke andar locker pe taala. Method kisi bhi raaste se call ho (controller, doosri service, scheduler), check hamesha chalega. Q207

  • Ek service method kai controllers se call hota hai: rule ek baar method pe
  • URL se 'ye order isi user ka hai?' check nahi hota; method pe SpEL se ho sakta hai
  • Rule business logic ke paas, bhoolna mushkil
@Configuration
@EnableMethodSecurity      // @PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize chalu (bina iske chupchaap ignore)
// @EnableMethodSecurity(securedEnabled = true, jsr250Enabled = true)  -> @Secured, @RolesAllowed
public class MethodSecurityConfig { }

@PreAuthorize: method se PEHLE (sabse zyada use)

Condition false to method chalega hi nahi, seedha 403. SpEL se parameters aur logged-in user dono mil jaate hain.

@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
public void approvePayment(Long paymentId) { ... }          // sirf ADMIN

@PreAuthorize("#username == authentication.name")           // sirf apni profile
public void updateProfile(String username, ProfileDto dto) { ... }

@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN') or #userId == authentication.principal.id")
public UserDto getUser(Long userId) { ... }                 // role YA owner
Yaad rakho#username = method ka parameter, authentication.name = logged-in user. authentication.principal.id tabhi chalega jab tumhara principal class getId() deta ho. Isi language ko SpEL kehte hain.

@PostAuthorize: method ke BAAD, result dekh kar

Story: shopping app, API GET /orders/{id}. Rahul ka order 101, Priya ka 102. Rahul login karke /orders/101 kholta hai, theek. Ab URL mein 101 ko 102 kar deta hai aur use Priya ka address, phone, items dikh jaate hain! Ise IDOR / BOLA bug kehte hain.

@PreAuthorize se kyun nahi rukta? Method se pehle sirf id = 102 hai; order kiska hai ye DB mein hai. Isliye: method chalne do, phir return hue order ko check karo.

  • returnObject = Spring ka built-in naam (sirf @PostAuthorize mein): method ne jo return kiya, yaani Order
  • returnObject.ownerUsername = order kiska hai (getter se padha jaata hai)
  • authentication.name = abhi kaun login hai
  • Same to data milta hai, alag to 403
@PostAuthorize("returnObject.ownerUsername == authentication.name")
public Order getOrder(Long id) {
    return orderRepository.findById(id).orElseThrow();
}

public class Order {
    private Long id;
    private String ownerUsername;     // "priya": order kisne kiya
    private BigDecimal amount;
    public String getOwnerUsername() { return ownerUsername; }
}

Sample data se samjho

Rahul: GET /orders/102→getOrder(102) chala→DB se Priya ka order→"priya" == "rahul"? Nahi→403, data nahi diya
idownerUsernameitemamount
101rahulMobile cover299
102priyaHeadphones1999
Case 1: Rahul -> GET /orders/101
returnObject = { "id": 101, "ownerUsername": "rahul", "item": "Mobile cover", "amount": 299 }
authentication.name = "rahul"
"rahul" == "rahul" -> true  -> 200 OK, order mil gaya

Case 2: Rahul -> GET /orders/102   (URL badla)
returnObject = { "id": 102, "ownerUsername": "priya", "item": "Headphones", "amount": 1999 }
authentication.name = "rahul"
"priya" == "rahul" -> false -> 403 Forbidden, data nahi bheja
Common galti@PostAuthorize sirf read methods ke liye. Delete, update, payment mein method pehle hi chal chuka hota hai: order delete ho gaya, paisa kat gaya, 403 baad mein aaye to koi fayda nahi. Wahan @PreAuthorize ya service mein pehle check.

@Secured aur @RolesAllowed (purane / simple)

Controller call→Spring proxy→@PreAuthorize check→Method chalta hai→@PostAuthorize check→Result ya 403
AnnotationKab checkSpEL?Use kab
@PreAuthorizeMethod se pehleHaanDefault choice
@PostAuthorizeMethod ke baadHaan (returnObject)Sirf read methods
@SecuredPehleNahiPurana code
@RolesAllowedPehleNahiJava standard chahiye to
@Secured("ROLE_ADMIN")       // Spring ka purana, ROLE_ khud likhna padta hai
public void deleteAll() { ... }

@RolesAllowed("ADMIN")       // Java standard (JSR-250, jakarta.annotation.security)
public void deleteAll() { ... }
Common galtiYe sab proxy se kaam karta hai (Part 4 AOP yaad karo). Isliye: (1) @EnableMethodSecurity bhoole to annotations ignore; (2) same class mein this.method() call proxy bypass karta hai; (3) private method pe annotation kaam nahi karta.

Asli bachav: ownership check (BOLA / IDOR)

Sirf ORDER_READ hona sabke private orders ka access nahi deta. OWASP API Security list mein BOLA number 1 risk hai. Real projects mein sabse behtar tareeka: query mein hi owner daal do, taaki doosre ka data DB se aaye hi nahi. Q208

@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ORDER_READ')")
@GetMapping("/orders/{id}")
public Order getOrder(@PathVariable Long id, Authentication auth) {
    return orderService.getOrderForCurrentUser(id, auth.getName());
}

public Order getOrderForCurrentUser(Long id, String currentUser) {
    return orderRepository.findByIdAndOwnerUsername(id, currentUser)
        .orElseThrow(() -> new AccessDeniedException("Not your order"));
}
Dhyan doKuch teams yahan 403 ki jagah 404 return karti hain taaki attacker ko ye bhi pata na chale ki order 102 exist karta hai. Dono theek hain, consistent raho.
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Role = group (ROLE_ADMIN), authority = exact permission (USER_DELETE).
  • hasRole('ADMIN') = hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN'); hasRole('ROLE_ADMIN') mat likho.
  • @EnableMethodSecurity ke bina method annotations ignore.
  • @PreAuthorize = pehle (default); @PostAuthorize = baad mein, returnObject ke saath, sirf read methods.
  • Proxy: self-call aur private method pe check nahi chalta.
  • Role kaafi nahi: har record pe ownership check (BOLA / IDOR); best: findByIdAndOwnerUsername.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q205

What is Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)?

Main Definition

  • RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) grants access based on the role assigned to a user, such as ADMIN or USER.
  • In Spring you enforce it with hasRole() in the filter chain or @PreAuthorize on methods, with @EnableMethodSecurity turned on.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • RBAC मतलब role के हिसाब से access।
  • जैसे office में manager leave approve कर सकता है, employee नहीं।
  • वैसे ही ADMIN delete कर सकता है, USER नहीं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Role vs authority
  • Role = bada group: ADMIN, MANAGER, USER. Spring mein ROLE_ prefix ke saath store: ROLE_ADMIN.
  • Authority = chhoti specific permission: USER_READ, USER_DELETE, ORDER_APPROVE. Koi prefix nahi.
  • Spring ke liye role bhi andar se ek authority hi hai, bas ROLE_ se shuru hoti hai.
RBAC kaise kaam karta hai
User (DB)→ROLE_ADMIN, USER_DELETE→SecurityContext→hasRole / hasAuthority→200 ya 403
Real example

Office app: ADMIN ke paas USER_READ + USER_DELETE, MANAGER ke paas sirf USER_READ, USER ke paas kuch nahi. MANAGER GET /users kar sakta hai (200), par DELETE /users/5 par 403.

@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
@DeleteMapping("/users/{id}")
public void deleteUser(@PathVariable Long id) {
    userService.deleteUser(id);
}
Q206

What is the difference between hasRole() and hasAuthority()?

Main Definition

  • hasRole('ADMIN') checks for the authority ROLE_ADMIN, because Spring adds the ROLE_ prefix.
  • hasAuthority('USER_READ') checks the exact string.
  • Use roles for coarse groups and authorities (permissions) for fine-grained access.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • hasRole('ADMIN') automatically आगे ROLE_ लगाकर ROLE_ADMIN check करता है।
  • hasAuthority('X') exact वही string check करता है।
  • Role बड़ा group है, authority छोटी permission।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
hasRole()hasAuthority()
Kya check karta haiRole (group)Exact permission string
PrefixROLE_ khud lagata haiKoi prefix nahi
ExamplehasRole('ADMIN') = ROLE_ADMINhasAuthority('USER_DELETE')
Kab useBade groups: ADMIN, USERChhoti permissions: read, delete, approve
Fail hone par403403
@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")             // checks ROLE_ADMIN
@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN')")   // same: checks ROLE_ADMIN
@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('USER_READ')")    // checks exact USER_READ
@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ROLE_ADMIN')")        // galat aadat: prefix khud mat lagao
Q207

What is method-level security?

Main Definition

  • Method-level security applies authorization rules on methods with annotations like @PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize, @Secured and @RolesAllowed, enabled with @EnableMethodSecurity.
  • It supports SpEL expressions, so you can also check things like ownership of the resource.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • URL की जगह सीधे method पर security लगाना।
  • @PreAuthorize method चलने से पहले check करता है, @PostAuthorize चलने के बाद result देखकर।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
AnnotationKab checkSpEL?Use kab
@PreAuthorizeMethod se pehleHaanDefault choice
@PostAuthorizeMethod ke baadHaan (returnObject)Sirf read methods
@SecuredMethod se pehleNahiPurana code (securedEnabled = true)
@RolesAllowedMethod se pehleNahiJSR-250 standard (jsr250Enabled = true)
@EnableMethodSecurity      // bina iske annotations chupchaap ignore
@Configuration
class MethodSecurityConfig { }

@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")
public void approvePayment(Long paymentId) { ... }

@PreAuthorize("#username == authentication.name")            // ownership
public void updateProfile(String username, ProfileDto dto) { ... }

@PostAuthorize("returnObject.ownerUsername == authentication.name")
public Order getOrder(Long id) { return orderRepository.findById(id).orElseThrow(); }
Common galti@PostAuthorize se side effects nahi rukte: delete/update/payment method pehle hi chal chuka hota hai. Wahan @PreAuthorize ya service mein pehle check karo. Same class ka this.method() call proxy bypass karta hai, aur private method par annotation kaam nahi karta.
Q208

Ek API ko sirf specific users access kar sakte hain. Kaise implement karoge? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Enforce authorization on the server with roles / authorities plus an object-level ownership check on every resource.
  • Without it the API is vulnerable to BOLA / IDOR (Broken Object Level Authorization), OWASP API Security risk #1.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • सिर्फ़ role check करना काफ़ी नहीं।
  • हर record के लिए check करो कि "क्या ये इसी user का है?" वरना user A, user B का order देख लेगा (BOLA/IDOR)।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('ORDER_READ')")
@GetMapping("/orders/{id}")
public Order getOrder(@PathVariable Long id, Authentication auth) {
    return orderService.getOrderForCurrentUser(id, auth.getName());
}

// Service: owner query mein hi daal do
public Order getOrderForCurrentUser(Long id, String currentUser) {
    return orderRepository.findByIdAndOwnerUsername(id, currentUser)
        .orElseThrow(() -> new AccessDeniedException("Not your order"));
}
Dhyan doSirf ORDER_READ hona sabke private data ka access nahi deta. Service ko verify karna hi chahiye ki current user ko is specific order ka access hai.

35. Session vs JWT aur JWT andar se

6 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Ab tak user login karta hai aur hum roles se authorization karte hain. Par HTTP stateless hai: agli request pe server ko kaise pata ki ye wahi Rahul hai? Har request pe password bhejna to pagalpan hai. Do raaste hain: server session yaad rakhe, ya user ek signed token (JWT) lekar aaye.
📖 Notes

Problem: har request pe 'tum kaun ho?'

Login ek baar hota hai, requests hazaar. Server ko pehchaan yaad rakhni hai. Socho cinema: ya to gate pe register mein naam likha jaaye aur har baar register check ho (session), ya tumhe ek stamp laga ticket mile jo guard dekh ke maan le (JWT).

Session vs JWT

Session-basedJWT-based
StateServer session store meinServer kuch yaad nahi rakhta (stateless)
Client bhejtaJSESSIONID cookieAuthorization: Bearer <jwt>
LogoutSession invalidate, turant khatamToken expiry tak valid (jab tak revocation na ho)
Kai serversShared session store (Redis / Spring Session)Sabke paas same verify key
Achha kahanServer-rendered web appAPIs, mobile, microservices
Dhyan doJWT apne aap zyada secure ya scalable nahi. Revocation, refresh, storage, expiry, key rotation sab design karna padta hai (Topic 5). Q209

Stateless authentication

Stateless = server koi HTTP session nahi banata. Har request apna credential (Bearer JWT) saath laati hai aur har baar verify hoti hai. Load balancer ke peeche koi bhi instance request le sakta hai. Q210

http.sessionManagement(session ->
    session.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS));

JWT kya hai: teen hisse

Teeno Base64URL encode hokar dot se jude: header.payload.signature. Signed hai, encrypted nahi: payload koi bhi jwt.io pe decode kar ke padh sakta hai, isliye password ya secret kabhi nahi. Q211

  • Header: alg (HS256 / RS256) aur typ
  • Payload: claims: sub (kaun), exp (kab tak), iss (kisne banaya), aud (kiske liye), roles
  • Signature: server ki key se bana stamp; integrity aur authenticity

Part A: token kaise BANTA hai (login par)

Header + Payload→Base64URL encode→dot se jodo→secret key se sign→header.payload.signature
Step 1: header  = { "alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT" }
Step 2: payload = { "sub": "rahul", "role": "ADMIN", "iss": "myapp", "exp": 1767225600 }

Step 3: Base64URL (encryption nahi, sirf URL-safe text)
header  -> eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9
payload -> eyJzdWIiOiJyYWh1bCIsInJvbGUiOiJBRE1JTiIsImlzcyI6Im15YXBwIiwiZXhwIjoxNzY3MjI1NjAwfQ

Step 4: sign
data      = <header> + "." + <payload>
signature = HMAC-SHA256(data, "my-secret-key")
          = K3jbjHzBeI2ok9dXt4B4unZD8oWHFncRWEww4w4jE50

Step 5: final JWT
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9
.eyJzdWIiOiJyYWh1bCIsInJvbGUiOiJBRE1JTiIsImlzcyI6Im15YXBwIiwiZXhwIjoxNzY3MjI1NjAwfQ
.K3jbjHzBeI2ok9dXt4B4unZD8oWHFncRWEww4w4jE50

Client har request mein: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Yaad rakhosub = user kaun, role = permission, iss = token kisne banaya, exp = kab expire (Unix seconds).

Part B: token kaise VERIFY hota hai (har request par)

Part A ka ulta. Server signature ko 'decrypt' nahi karta, dobara banata hai aur compare karta hai. Q212

  1. Token ko dot par 3 hisson mein todo.
  2. Header ka alg dekho: sirf server ka configured algorithm (HS256) allow. none kabhi nahi.
  3. header.payload pe same secret se dobara HMAC-SHA256 chalao.
  4. Bana hua signature vs token ka signature: match = asli aur unchanged; nahi = 401.
  5. Payload ke claims: exp nikal to nahi gaya? iss humara? aud humare liye?
  6. Sab theek: sub aur role se Authentication banao, SecurityContextHolder mein rakho.
Token aaya→3 parts→same key se dobara sign→signature match?→exp, iss, aud→User set ya 401

Hacker ne payload badla to?

Rahul payload mein "role": "ADMIN" ko "SUPER_ADMIN" kar deta hai. Encoded payload badal gaya, par uske paas secret key nahi, to purana signature hi bhejta hai.

naya payload    -> eyJzdWIiOiJyYWh1bCIsInJvbGUiOiJTVVBFUl9BRE1JTiIsImlzcyI6Im15YXBwIiwiZXhwIjoxNzY3MjI1NjAwfQ
server ne banaya : UKo1c6DoYs815FG5YM8PXrh_WcQRaG6JoCFpRw9JvIk
token mein aaya  : K3jbjHzBeI2ok9dXt4B4unZD8oWHFncRWEww4w4jE50
match?           : NAHI -> 401 Unauthorized
Yaad rakhoPayload padh koi bhi sakta hai, badal koi nahi sakta. Sirf decode karke bharosa karna verification nahi hai.

HS256 vs RS256

HS256RS256
KeyEk shared secretPrivate + public key pair
SignSecret sePrivate key se (sirf auth server)
VerifySame secret se dobara signPublic key se
KabEk hi app banata aur check kartaAlag auth server (Keycloak, Auth0); kai services verify karti hain
Dhyan doHS256 mein jis bhi service ke paas secret hai wo token bana bhi sakti hai. Microservices (Part 8) mein isliye RS256 + JWKS endpoint common hai: services sirf public key se verify karti hain.

Spring mein JWT: poora flow

Q213

  • /auth/login endpoint: AuthenticationManager se credentials check, JWT issue
  • Token service: banana + validate
  • Har request: OncePerRequestFilter (ya OAuth2 Resource Server) token verify karke SecurityContext set kare
  • Chain STATELESS + filter sahi jagah
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/auth")
class AuthController {
    private final AuthenticationManager authManager;
    private final JwtService jwtService;
    AuthController(AuthenticationManager m, JwtService j) { authManager = m; jwtService = j; }

    @PostMapping("/login")
    TokenResponse login(@RequestBody LoginRequest req) {
        Authentication auth = authManager.authenticate(
            new UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(req.username(), req.password()));  // galat -> 401
        return new TokenResponse(jwtService.generate(auth));
    }
}

@Service
class JwtService {
    private final SecretKey key = Keys.hmacShaKeyFor(Decoders.BASE64.decode(System.getenv("JWT_SECRET")));

    String generate(Authentication auth) {
        Instant now = Instant.now();
        return Jwts.builder()
            .subject(auth.getName())
            .issuer("myapp")
            .claim("roles", auth.getAuthorities().stream().map(GrantedAuthority::getAuthority).toList())
            .issuedAt(Date.from(now))
            .expiration(Date.from(now.plus(15, ChronoUnit.MINUTES)))
            .signWith(key)                                   // HS256
            .compact();
    }

    Claims parse(String token) {                             // signature + exp + iss
        return Jwts.parser().verifyWith(key).requireIssuer("myapp")
            .build().parseSignedClaims(token).getPayload();
    }
}

JWT filter aur chain

@Component
public class JwtAuthFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {
    private final JwtService jwtService;
    public JwtAuthFilter(JwtService jwtService) { this.jwtService = jwtService; }

    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,
                                    FilterChain chain) throws ServletException, IOException {
        String header = request.getHeader("Authorization");
        if (header != null && header.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
            try {
                Claims c = jwtService.parse(header.substring(7));
                List<SimpleGrantedAuthority> auths = c.get("roles", List.class).stream()
                    .map(r -> new SimpleGrantedAuthority((String) r)).toList();
                var auth = new UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken(c.getSubject(), null, auths);
                SecurityContextHolder.getContext().setAuthentication(auth);
            } catch (JwtException e) {
                SecurityContextHolder.clearContext();   // invalid -> anonymous -> baad mein 401
            }
        }
        chain.doFilter(request, response);
    }
}

// SecurityConfig
http.csrf(c -> c.disable())
    .sessionManagement(s -> s.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))
    .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.requestMatchers("/auth/**").permitAll().anyRequest().authenticated())
    .addFilterBefore(jwtAuthFilter, UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter.class);
Common galtiFilter ko @Component banaya to Boot use servlet container mein bhi register kar deta hai (do baar chalega). Ya @Component hata ke bean khud banao, ya FilterRegistrationBean se setEnabled(false) karo. OncePerRequestFilter kyun: Q92.

Shortcut: OAuth2 Resource Server (recommended)

Khud ka filter likhne ki jagah Spring ka built-in support use karo (spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server). Ye signature, alg, exp, nbf aur iss khud check karta hai aur BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter lagata hai.

# application.yml: alag auth server (RS256)
spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri: https://auth.myapp.com

// SecurityConfig
http.oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()));

// Apni secret key (HS256) ho to decoder bean
@Bean
JwtDecoder jwtDecoder() {
    SecretKey key = new SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(), "HmacSHA256");
    return NimbusJwtDecoder.withSecretKey(key).macAlgorithm(MacAlgorithm.HS256).build();
}
Dhyan doDefault mein scopes SCOPE_ authorities bante hain. Custom roles claim ke liye JwtAuthenticationConverter configure karo. aud check ke liye Boot 3.2+ mein spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.audiences.

OAuth 2.0 vs JWT

OAuth courier service hai, JWT envelope. OAuth ke access tokens JWT bhi ho sakte hain ya opaque bhi. Tumhari API Resource Server hai: token issuer (Keycloak, Auth0, Okta) deta hai, API sirf verify karti hai. Q214

OAuth 2.0JWT
KyaAuthorization framework (RFC 6749)Token format (RFC 7519)
BatataToken kaise milega, kaun deta hai (grant flows)Token ke andar kya likha aur kaise sign
PlayersClient, Authorization Server, Resource Server, UserHeader, Payload, Signature
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Session = server yaad rakhta (JSESSIONID); JWT = stateless, signed token har request mein.
  • STATELESS policy: koi HttpSession nahi.
  • JWT = Header.Payload.Signature; signed, encrypted nahi; payload mein secret nahi.
  • Verify = same key se dobara sign + compare + exp/iss/aud; alg: none kabhi nahi.
  • Decode karna validate karna nahi hai.
  • Spring: login endpoint + OncePerRequestFilter, ya better OAuth2 Resource Server.
  • OAuth 2.0 = framework, JWT = format; API = Resource Server.

✅ Review questions (6): ab khud check karo

Q209

What is the difference between session-based authentication and JWT? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • In session-based auth the server keeps server-side state and the client sends a session ID cookie (JSESSIONID).
  • In JWT-based auth the server is stateless and the client sends a self-contained signed token.
  • JWT is easy to scale but needs extra design for revocation, refresh tokens and key rotation.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Session में server हर user को याद रखता है (session store में entry होती है)।
  • JWT में server कुछ याद नहीं रखता, user खुद signed token लेकर आता है।
  • Token expire होने तक valid रहता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Session-basedJWT-based
Server session state rakhta haiHar token ke liye session lookup nahi
Session ID aksar cookie meinToken aksar Authorization: Bearer header mein
Logout = server session invalidateValid JWT expiry tak chalta hai jab tak revocation na ho
Kai instances: shared session store (Redis)Kai instances: same validation keys / policy
Dhyan doJWT apne aap mein zyada secure ya zyada scalable nahi hai. Revocation, refresh tokens, storage, expiry aur key rotation phir bhi matter karte hain.
Important 74 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q208)★ Important listAgla important (Q211) → ★
Q210

What is stateless authentication?

Main Definition

  • Stateless authentication means the server creates no HTTP session and stores no per-user state.
  • Every request carries its own credential, usually a Bearer JWT, which is verified each time.
  • In Spring this is SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Stateless मतलब server कुछ store नहीं करता।
  • हर request अपना token साथ लाती है और server हर बार उसे verify करता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Koi JSESSIONID cookie nahi
  • Load balancer ke peeche koi bhi instance request handle kar sakta hai
  • Har request pe signature + claims check
http.sessionManagement(session ->
    session.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS));
Q211

What is JWT, and how does it work? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, signed token in the form Header.Payload.Signature.
  • The header holds the algorithm, the payload holds claims (sub, exp, iss, aud, roles), and the signature proves integrity and authenticity.
  • It is signed, not encrypted, and is sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • JWT एक signed token है, तीन parts में: Header (कौन-सा algorithm), Payload (user की details), Signature (stamp)।
  • Signature से server check करता है कि token असली है।
  • Payload कोई भी decode करके पढ़ सकता है, इसलिए उसमें password मत डालो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
HS256RS256
KeyEk hi secret keyPrivate + public key
SignSecret key sePrivate key (sirf auth server)
VerifySame key se dobara sign + comparePublic key se
KabEk hi app banata aur check karta haiAlag auth server (Keycloak, Auth0), kai services verify
  1. User logs in.
  2. Server credentials verify karta hai.
  3. Server access token issue karta hai.
  4. Client use Authorization: Bearer <token> header mein bhejta hai.
  5. Server token validate karke request authorize karta hai.
{ "alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT" }                                        // header
{ "sub": "rahul", "role": "ADMIN", "iss": "myapp", "exp": 1767225600 }  // payload

eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9
.eyJzdWIiOiJyYWh1bCIsInJvbGUiOiJBRE1JTiIsImlzcyI6Im15YXBwIiwiZXhwIjoxNzY3MjI1NjAwfQ
.K3jbjHzBeI2ok9dXt4B4unZD8oWHFncRWEww4w4jE50
Dhyan doSigned JWT apne aap encrypted nahi hota. Payload mein password ya confidential data kabhi mat daalo. Poora build + verify step by step notes mein hai.
Important 75 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q209)★ Important listAgla important (Q213) → ★
Q212

JWT ki signature kaise validate karoge?

Main Definition

  • Verify the signature with the trusted key (JWK / public key or the shared secret) and an explicitly allowed algorithm (never trust the header's alg, never accept none).
  • Then validate exp, iss, aud and required claims.
  • Decoding alone is not validation.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • सिर्फ़ token decode करके पढ़ लेना trust नहीं है।
  • Signature को सही key से verify करो, फिर expiry, issuer और audience check करो।
  • तभी token valid माना जाएगा।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  1. Token ke 3 parts alag karo.
  2. alg allowed hai? (HS256 / RS256, none nahi)
  3. header.payload ko same key se dobara sign karo (RS256 mein public key se check).
  4. Signature match? Nahi to 401.
  5. exp, iss, aud check. Fail to 401.
  6. Pass to user SecurityContext mein set.
// Tareeka 1 (recommended): OAuth2 Resource Server
// application.yml (RS256, auth server ki public keys)
spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri: https://auth.myapp.com

// HS256 (apni secret key) ke liye decoder bean
@Bean
JwtDecoder jwtDecoder() {
    SecretKey key = new SecretKeySpec(secret.getBytes(), "HmacSHA256");
    return NimbusJwtDecoder.withSecretKey(key)
        .macAlgorithm(MacAlgorithm.HS256)   // sirf HS256 allowed
        .build();
}

// Tareeka 2: khud ka filter (jjwt 0.12)
Claims claims = Jwts.parser()
    .verifyWith(secretKey)         // signature check
    .requireIssuer("myapp")        // iss check
    .build()
    .parseSignedClaims(token)      // galat signature / expired -> exception
    .getPayload();
Dhyan doKya sirf decode karke payload pe bharosa kar sakte hain? Nahi. Pehle signature aur claims verify karo.
Q213

How do you implement JWT authentication in Spring Security? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Add a login endpoint that validates credentials with the AuthenticationManager and issues a signed access token.
  • For each request, a OncePerRequestFilter (or the OAuth2 Resource Server support) validates the signature, exp, iss and aud, builds an Authentication and puts it in the SecurityContextHolder.
  • The chain is configured as STATELESS.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Login पर server JWT देता है।
  • फिर हर request के साथ client वो token भेजता है।
  • एक filter हर बार token verify करता है और valid हो तो user को SecurityContext में set कर देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Authentication endpoint (/auth/login)
  • AuthenticationManager (credentials check)
  • Token service (JWT banana + validate karna)
  • Custom OncePerRequestFilter ya built-in resource-server setup
  • Stateless SecurityFilterChain
@Component
public class JwtAuthFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {
    private final JwtService jwtService;
    public JwtAuthFilter(JwtService jwtService) { this.jwtService = jwtService; }

    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,
                                    FilterChain chain) throws ServletException, IOException {
        String header = request.getHeader("Authorization");
        if (header != null && header.startsWith("Bearer ")) {
            String token = header.substring(7);
            // 1. signature, exp, iss, aud validate karo (jwtService)
            // 2. valid ho to Authentication banao aur
            //    SecurityContextHolder mein set karo
        }
        chain.doFilter(request, response);
    }
}
Dhyan doYe sirf skeleton hai; validation aur context setup zaroori hai (poora code notes mein). Unverified token se role ya identity kabhi trust mat karo. OncePerRequestFilter kyun: Q92.

Q214

What is OAuth 2.0, and how is it different from JWT?

Main Definition

  • OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework that defines how a client obtains and uses access tokens from an authorization server.
  • JWT is only a token format, and OAuth access tokens can be JWTs or opaque tokens.
  • Your API acts as an OAuth2 Resource Server and validates tokens from the issuer.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • OAuth 2.0 एक process (rules) है कि token कैसे मिलेगा और कैसे use होगा।
  • JWT सिर्फ़ token का format है।
  • जैसे OAuth courier service है और JWT envelope।

Kya haiFramework / protocol (RFC 6749)Token format (RFC 7519)
Batata haiToken kaise milega (grant flows), kaun issue karegaToken ke andar claims kaise likhe aur sign ho
RolesClient, Authorization Server, Resource Server, Resource OwnerHeader, Payload, Signature
http.oauth2ResourceServer(oauth2 -> oauth2.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()));
// + spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri (ya jwk-set-uri / JwtDecoder bean)
Yaad rakhoResource server ko issuer/JWK ya decoder configuration chahiye. API token ko apni trust configuration ke hisaab se validate karti hai.
