Part 8: Microservices

38. Monolith se Microservices tak

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichhle Parts mein humne ek app ko test, monitor, cache aur secure (Spring Security, JWT) karna seekha, aur Part 5 mein @Transactional se ek database ka transaction. Sab ek hi app ke andar tha. Ab tak tum REST APIs bana rahe ho jo ek hi Spring Boot jar mein chalti hain. Sawaal ye hai: jab app aur team dono bahut bade ho jaayein tab kya? Yahin se microservices ki kahani shuru hoti hai.
📖 Notes

Problem: monolith jo bahut bada ho gaya

Socho tumne ek e-commerce app banayi: users, products, orders, payment, emails. Sab ek hi project, ek jar, ek MySQL. Shuru mein ye best hai: ek mvn package, ek deploy, ek @Transactional.

Do saal baad 40 developers, 3 lakh lines. Ab dekho kya hota hai: email template mein ek line badli to poora app redeploy. Sale ke din sirf product search par load hai, par scale poore app ko karna padta hai. Payment module mein ek memory leak aur poori site down. Har team ek doosre ke code se takra rahi hai.

  • Chhota change = poora redeploy, release slow
  • Scaling sab ka saath, mehenga
  • Ek bug poora system gira deta hai
  • Tech stack badalna lagbhag impossible
  • Naye developer ke liye codebase samajhna mushkil

Solution: microservices

Microservice ek chhoti, independently deployable service hai jo ek business capability sambhalti hai aur uska apna database hota hai. Services network par REST ya events se baat karti hain. Analogy: ek bada dhaba jahan ek hi aadmi sab karta tha, ab ek food court ban gaya, har counter apna kaam khud karta hai.

Hamara running example: ShopKart

ServiceKaamApna DB
user-serviceSignup, profile, addressPostgreSQL users
product-serviceCatalog, price, searchPostgreSQL / Elasticsearch
order-serviceCart se order, order statusPostgreSQL orders
payment-serviceCharge, refundPostgreSQL payments
notification-serviceEmail / SMSKoi DB nahi ya chhota Mongo
Yaad rakhoPoore Part 6 mein yahi example chalega. Har service ek alag Spring Boot app hai, jaisi tum ab tak banate aaye ho.

Microservice ki pehchaan (characteristics)

  • Single responsibility: ek business capability (orders), na ki ek technical layer.
  • Independent deploy: order-service ka naya version bina payment ko chhuye.
  • Own database: koi doosri service iski tables directly nahi padhti.
  • Decentralised: har team apna stack, apna release, apna data chun sakti hai.
  • Failure isolation: notification down hai to bhi order place ho jaana chahiye.
  • Automation: CI/CD, containers, monitoring ke bina microservices chal hi nahi sakte.

Monolith vs microservices

Detail: Q236

PointMonolithMicroservices
DeployEk unitHar service alag
CallMethod call, nanosecondsNetwork call, milliseconds, fail ho sakti hai
TransactionEk @TransactionalSaga + eventual consistency
DebuggingEk log fileCentral logs + tracing
TeamSab ek codebase parHar team ki apni service

Kaise todein: business capability / bounded context

Galat tareeka: controller-service, dao-service. Layers se todoge to har feature ke liye saari services badalni padengi.

Sahi tareeka: business capability se, ya DDD ka bounded context. 'Product' ka matlab catalog mein naam/price/image hai, par order ke andar sirf productId + price at that time. Har context ka apna model, apni service.

  1. Business ke kaam list karo (catalog, ordering, payment, shipping).
  2. Dekho kaunsa data kaun sa kaam own karta hai.
  3. Ek table do services likh rahi hain? Boundary galat hai.
  4. Monolith ke aage gateway lagao, ek-ek capability nikaal kar nayi service mein le jao (strangler fig).

Kab use karo, kab nahi

Use karo jabMat use karo jab
Kai teams ek product par, release takrate hain2-5 log ki team
Kuch hisson ko alag scale karna haiMVP / naya product, domain abhi clear nahi
Domain boundaries clear hainCI/CD, monitoring, containers ka setup nahi
High availability zarooriLoad chhota, ek server kaafi
Common galtiFashion ke liye microservices. Pehle modular monolith banao (package-by-feature, saaf boundaries), dard ho tab todo. Galat todne se distributed monolith banta hai: sab services ek saath deploy karni padti hain, aur network ki problems free mein.

Microservices ke saath kya-kya naya aata hai

Ek app ke 5 app bante hi naye sawaal: services baat kaise karein? Ek doosre ka address kaise jaanein? Config kahan rakhein? Ek service down to baaki ka kya? Transaction kaise? Logs kahan dekhein? Agle 5 topics yahi ek-ek karke solve karte hain.

Communication→Discovery + Gateway→Config + Resilience→Data + Saga→Observability + Security + Deploy
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Microservice = ek business capability + apna DB + independent deploy.
  • Monolith bura nahi; chhoti team aur naye product ke liye best start.
  • Business capability / bounded context se todo, layer se nahi.
  • Strangler fig: monolith se dheere-dheere ek-ek hissa nikaalo.
  • Microservices = flexibility ke badle network, data aur ops ki complexity.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q235

What is a microservice? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A microservice is a small, independently deployable service that owns one business capability and its own data, and talks to other services over the network (HTTP or messaging).
  • A system built this way is a set of loosely coupled services instead of one big deployable.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Microservice एक छोटी, अलग से deploy होने वाली service है जो सिर्फ़ एक business काम संभालती है, जैसे order या payment।
  • उसका अपना database होता है और वो दूसरी services से network पर बात करती है।
  • जैसे एक बड़े restaurant में अलग-अलग counter: हर counter अपना काम खुद संभालता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
Example

E-commerce: user-service, product-service, order-service, payment-service, notification-service. Har ek alag Spring Boot app, alag port, alag DB.

  • Single responsibility: ek business capability
  • Independent deploy aur scale
  • Database per service
  • Network par REST ya events se baat
  • Chhoti team ownership (you build it, you run it)
Important 80 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q229)★ Important listAgla important (Q236) → ★
Q236

Monolith vs microservices: what is the difference? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A monolith is one codebase built and deployed as a single unit with one shared database.
  • Microservices split the system into many small services that are built, deployed and scaled independently, each with its own data, at the cost of network calls and operational complexity.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Monolith में पूरा app एक ही jar में होता है, एक ही database के साथ; एक छोटा change भी पूरा app redeploy करवाता है।
  • Microservices में हर हिस्सा अलग app है जो अलग deploy और scale होता है।
  • फ़ायदा flexibility का है, लेकिन network, monitoring और debugging मुश्किल हो जाते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PointMonolithMicroservices
DeployEk unit, sab saathHar service alag
ScalingPoora app scaleSirf busy service scale
DatabaseEk shared DBDatabase per service
CallIn-process method call (fast)Network call (slow, fail ho sakti hai)
TransactionSimple @TransactionalSaga, eventual consistency
DebuggingEk log, ek stack traceDistributed tracing chahiye
ShuruaatAasan, chhoti team ke liye bestZyada infra aur DevOps
Important 81 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q235)★ Important listAgla important (Q239) → ★
Q237

What are the advantages and disadvantages of microservices, and when should you not use them?

Main Definition

  • Advantages: independent deployment, independent scaling, fault isolation, technology freedom and team autonomy.
  • Disadvantages: network latency and failures, distributed data and transactions, complex testing, monitoring and DevOps.
  • Avoid them for small teams, early products with unclear domains, or apps without real scaling needs; a modular monolith is often the better start.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Microservices से हर team अपनी service अलग deploy और scale कर सकती है, और एक service गिरने से पूरा system नहीं गिरता।
  • लेकिन network failures, distributed data और monitoring का खर्च बढ़ जाता है।
  • छोटी team या नए product के लिए पहले modular monolith बनाओ, ज़रूरत पड़े तब तोड़ो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Pros: independent deploy, selective scaling, fault isolation, polyglot, team autonomy
  • Cons: latency, partial failure, data consistency, ops cost, harder testing
  • Mat use karo: chhoti team, MVP, domain clear nahi, koi scaling problem nahi
Yaad rakhoGalat tareeke se tode gaye services 'distributed monolith' ban jaate hain: sab ek saath deploy karne padte hain, aur network ki problem bonus mein.
Q238

How do you decompose a monolith into microservices?

Main Definition

  • Split by business capability or by bounded context (Domain-Driven Design), not by technical layer.
  • Each service owns a cohesive set of data and rules.
  • Migrate gradually with the strangler fig pattern: put a gateway in front, move one capability at a time to a new service, and route its traffic there.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Services को business काम के हिसाब से तोड़ो, जैसे Orders, Payments, Catalog; layers (controller, service, dao) के हिसाब से नहीं।
  • हर service का अपना data और rules होते हैं।
  • पुराने monolith से एक-एक हिस्सा धीरे-धीरे बाहर निकालो, इसे strangler fig pattern कहते हैं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Business capability / bounded context se todo
  • High cohesion andar, loose coupling bahar
  • Ek table do services likhein to boundary galat hai
  • Strangler fig: gateway ke peeche ek-ek feature nikaalo
➡️ Agle topic mein: ab order-service ko product ki price chahiye. Do services aapas mein baat kaise karti hain: REST ya events?Agla topic: Services aapas mein baat kaise karti hain →

39. Services aapas mein baat kaise karti hain

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein humne monolith ko ShopKart ki 5 services mein toda. Monolith mein productService.getPrice(id) ek method call tha. Ab product-service doosri JVM, doosri machine par hai. To order-service usse baat kaise kare?
📖 Notes

Problem: method call ab network call hai

Monolith mein call fail nahi hoti thi, bas exception aata tha. Network call slow ho sakti hai, timeout ho sakti hai, doosri service down ho sakti hai, ya response aadha aaye. Isliye communication ka style soch kar chuno.

StyleAnalogyTools
SynchronousPhone call: jawab ka waitREST (RestClient, WebClient, OpenFeign), gRPC
AsynchronousWhatsApp message: bhejo aur aage badhoKafka, RabbitMQ

Sync option 1: RestClient (Spring 6.1+, Boot 3.2+)

RestTemplate ka modern replacement. Fluent API, blocking, normal Spring MVC app ke liye perfect. Boot ek RestClient.Builder bean deta hai (jisme message converters aur tracing pehle se lage hote hain), use inject karke banao.

@Configuration
class ClientConfig {
    @Bean
    RestClient productRestClient(RestClient.Builder builder) {
        return builder.baseUrl("http://localhost:8082").build();
    }
}

@Service
class OrderService {
    private final RestClient productClient;
    OrderService(RestClient productRestClient) { this.productClient = productRestClient; }

    BigDecimal priceOf(Long productId) {
        ProductDto p = productClient.get()
                .uri("/products/{id}", productId)
                .retrieve()
                .onStatus(HttpStatusCode::is4xxClientError,
                        (req, res) -> { throw new ProductNotFoundException(productId); })
                .body(ProductDto.class);
        return p.price();
    }
}
record ProductDto(Long id, String name, BigDecimal price) {}

Sync option 2: WebClient (reactive)

WebFlux ka non-blocking client. Thread wait nahi karta, result Mono/Flux mein aata hai. Reactive app ho ya ek saath kai services ko parallel call karna ho tab use karo. MVC app mein .block() karke chalana possible hai par fir RestClient hi simple hai.

Mono<ProductDto> product = webClient.get()
        .uri("/products/{id}", id)
        .retrieve()
        .bodyToMono(ProductDto.class)
        .timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3));

// parallel: product + stock ek saath
Mono.zip(productMono, stockMono)
    .map(t -> new CartLine(t.getT1(), t.getT2()));

Sync option 3: OpenFeign (declarative)

Bas interface likho, Spring Cloud implementation bana deta hai. Spring Data repository jaisa feel. Bahut saare endpoints ho to code sabse saaf.

<!-- pom.xml (Spring Cloud BOM ke saath) -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-openfeign</artifactId>
</dependency>

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableFeignClients
public class OrderServiceApplication { ... }

@FeignClient(name = "product-service", url = "${product.url:}")  // Eureka ho to url hata do
public interface ProductClient {
    @GetMapping("/products/{id}")
    ProductDto getProduct(@PathVariable("id") Long id);
}
Yaad rakhoSpring Cloud OpenFeign ab feature-complete (maintenance) mode mein hai. Spring 6 ka apna declarative option @HttpExchange interface hai jo RestClient/WebClient par chalta hai. Naye projects mein dono dikhenge. Comparison: Q240

Spring Cloud BOM: versions ek jagah

Spring Cloud ke saare starters ka version BOM se aata hai. Boot 3.2/3.3 ke saath 2023.0.x (Leyton), Boot 3.4 ke saath 2024.0.x (Moorgate), Boot 3.5 ke saath 2025.0.x.

<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
      <artifactId>spring-cloud-dependencies</artifactId>
      <version>2024.0.1</version>
      <type>pom</type>
      <scope>import</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>

Async: events aur message broker

Order place hua. Notification ko email bhejna hai, analytics ko count badhana hai, loyalty ko points dene hain. Kya order-service teeno ko REST call kare aur wait kare? Nahi. Agar email service down hai to order kyun ruke?

Order-service sirf ek event publish karti hai: OrderPlaced. Jisko zaroorat hai woh subscribe karta hai. Producer ko pata bhi nahi kaun sun raha hai: loose coupling.

# application.yml
spring.kafka:
  bootstrap-servers: localhost:9092
  producer.value-serializer: org.springframework.kafka.support.serializer.JsonSerializer
  consumer.value-deserializer: org.springframework.kafka.support.serializer.JsonDeserializer
  consumer.properties.spring.json.trusted.packages: "com.shopkart.events"

// order-service: producer
record OrderPlaced(Long orderId, Long userId, BigDecimal amount) {}
kafkaTemplate.send("order-events", orderId.toString(), new OrderPlaced(orderId, userId, amount));

// notification-service: consumer
@KafkaListener(topics = "order-events", groupId = "notification-service")
public void onOrderPlaced(OrderPlaced event) {
    emailService.sendOrderConfirmation(event.userId(), event.orderId());
}

Kafka vs RabbitMQ (basic)

Spring mein: spring-kafka (KafkaTemplate, @KafkaListener) aur spring-boot-starter-amqp (RabbitTemplate, @RabbitListener). Detail: Q242

PointRabbitMQKafka
ModelQueue: consume hua to hataLog: event retention tak rehta hai
ReplayNahi (normal queues)Haan, offset peeche le jao
ThroughputAchhaBahut zyada (partitions)
RoutingExchanges se flexible routingTopic + partition key
Best forTask queues, commandsEvent streaming, audit, analytics

Kab sync, kab async

SituationChoice
Checkout se pehle stock/price abhi chahiyeSync REST
User ko turant result dikhana hai (profile fetch)Sync REST
Order ke baad email, analytics, pointsAsync event
Lamba kaam (invoice PDF, video encode)Async message
Kai services ko same khabarAsync event (pub-sub)

Timeouts: sabse zaroori setting

Product-service slow ho gayi aur tumne timeout nahi lagaya. Order-service ke Tomcat threads (default 200) ek-ek karke wahan latak gaye. Ab order-service bhi kisi ko jawab nahi de rahi. Gateway ke threads bhi latke. Ek slow service ne poora system gira diya: cascading failure.

# Boot 3.4+: sab auto-configured HTTP clients ke liye
spring.http.client:
  connect-timeout: 2s
  read-timeout: 3s

# OpenFeign
spring.cloud.openfeign.client.config.default:
  connect-timeout: 2000
  read-timeout: 3000
Common galtiDefault timeouts ke bharose rehna (kai clients mein read timeout infinite hota hai). Har remote call par timeout + (agle topics mein) circuit breaker. Detail: Q243
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Sync = REST (RestClient / WebClient / OpenFeign); async = events (Kafka / RabbitMQ).
  • RestClient = naya default sync client; RestTemplate maintenance mode mein.
  • Builder bean inject karke client banao (converters + tracing milte hain).
  • Jawab abhi chahiye → sync; sirf batana hai → event.
  • Har remote call par connect + read timeout.

✅ Review questions (5): ab khud check karo

Q239

How do microservices communicate with each other? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Two styles: synchronous request/response, usually REST over HTTP (RestClient, WebClient, OpenFeign) or gRPC, where the caller waits for an answer; and asynchronous messaging via a broker like Kafka or RabbitMQ, where a service publishes an event and others consume it later.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Sync में एक service दूसरी को HTTP call करती है और जवाब का wait करती है, जैसे phone call।
  • Async में service एक message या event broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ) पर डाल देती है और आगे बढ़ जाती है, जैसे WhatsApp message।
  • जिसे जवाब तुरंत चाहिए वहाँ sync, बाकी जगह async।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Sync: REST (RestClient / WebClient / OpenFeign), gRPC
  • Async: Kafka, RabbitMQ (events / commands)
  • Har remote call par timeout zaroor
Important 82 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q236)★ Important listAgla important (Q240) → ★
Q240

RestClient vs WebClient vs OpenFeign: which one should you use? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • RestClient (Spring 6.1+) is the modern synchronous fluent HTTP client and the replacement for RestTemplate in new code.
  • WebClient is the reactive, non-blocking client from WebFlux, best for reactive apps or many parallel calls.
  • OpenFeign (Spring Cloud) is declarative: you write an interface with @FeignClient and Spring generates the client.
  • Spring 6 also offers @HttpExchange interfaces backed by RestClient/WebClient.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • RestClient सीधा और blocking है, normal Spring MVC app के लिए सबसे आसान।
  • WebClient reactive है, जब non-blocking या बहुत सारे parallel calls चाहिए।
  • OpenFeign में बस एक interface लिखो, implementation Spring खुद बना देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
RestClientWebClientOpenFeign
StyleFluent, syncFluent, reactive (Mono/Flux)Declarative interface
Blocking?HaanNahiHaan (default)
Dependencyspring-web (Boot 3.2+)spring-boot-starter-webfluxspring-cloud-starter-openfeign
KabNormal MVC servicesReactive stack, fan-out callsBahut saare endpoints, clean code
// RestClient
Product p = restClient.get().uri("/products/{id}", id)
        .retrieve().body(Product.class);

// OpenFeign
@FeignClient(name = "product-service")
interface ProductClient {
    @GetMapping("/products/{id}") Product get(@PathVariable Long id);
}
Dhyan doRestTemplate abhi bhi kaam karta hai par maintenance mode mein hai. Naye code mein RestClient lo.
Important 83 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q239)★ Important listAgla important (Q241) → ★
Q241

Synchronous vs asynchronous communication: when to choose which? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Use synchronous calls when the caller needs the answer right now to continue (e.g. checking stock before confirming a cart).
  • Use asynchronous events when other services only need to react to something that happened (order placed → send email, update analytics).
  • Async gives loose coupling and resilience (the consumer can be down) but brings eventual consistency.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • अगर आगे बढ़ने के लिए जवाब अभी चाहिए तो sync call करो।
  • अगर बस दूसरों को बताना है कि कुछ हुआ, जैसे order place हुआ, तो event publish करो।
  • Async में दूसरी service down हो तब भी काम नहीं रुकता, बस data थोड़ी देर में consistent होता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PointSync (REST)Async (Kafka/RabbitMQ)
CouplingTemporal coupling: dono up hone chahiyeLoose: consumer baad mein padh lega
LatencyChain lambi to slowProducer turant free
FailureCascade ho sakta haiBroker message rakh leta hai
ConsistencyTurantEventual
DebugAasanMushkil (tracing chahiye)
Important 84 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q240)★ Important listAgla important (Q244) → ★
Q242

What is Kafka vs RabbitMQ in microservices?

Main Definition

  • RabbitMQ is a traditional message broker: messages go to queues via exchanges and are removed once acknowledged; great for task queues and routing.
  • Kafka is a distributed, durable event log: events are appended to partitioned topics, kept for a retention period, and consumer groups track their own offsets, so events can be replayed; great for high-throughput event streaming.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • RabbitMQ एक post office की तरह है: message queue में आता है, consumer ने लिया और message हट गया।
  • Kafka एक register की तरह है: हर event लिखा रहता है और कोई भी consumer अपनी जगह से फिर पढ़ सकता है।
  • High volume event streaming के लिए Kafka, simple task queue और routing के लिए RabbitMQ।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
// Spring Kafka: event bhejna
kafkaTemplate.send("order-events", order.id().toString(), new OrderPlaced(order.id()));

// event padhna
@KafkaListener(topics = "order-events", groupId = "notification-service")
void on(OrderPlaced e) { emailService.sendConfirmation(e.orderId()); }
Q243

Why are timeouts important in service-to-service calls?

Main Definition

  • Without timeouts, a slow downstream service makes callers wait forever, holding threads and connections until the caller itself runs out and fails: a cascading failure.
  • Always set a connect timeout and a read/response timeout on every HTTP client, and combine them with retry and circuit breaker.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • अगर downstream service slow है और timeout नहीं लगाया तो caller के threads वहीं अटक जाते हैं।
  • धीरे-धीरे caller भी hang हो जाता है और failure पूरे system में फैल जाता है।
  • इसलिए हर HTTP client पर connect और read timeout ज़रूर लगाओ।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Bean
RestClient productRestClient(RestClient.Builder builder) {
    var settings = ClientHttpRequestFactorySettings.defaults()
            .withConnectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
            .withReadTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3));
    return builder.baseUrl("http://product-service")
            .requestFactory(ClientHttpRequestFactories.get(settings))   // Boot 3.2/3.3 API
            .build();
}
Dhyan doBoot 3.4+ mein ClientHttpRequestFactoryBuilder aur spring.http.client.connect-timeout / read-timeout properties bhi hain. Version ke hisaab se API check karo.
➡️ Agle topic mein: abhi humne http://localhost:8082 hardcode kiya. Product-service ke 3 instances ho aur IP badalte rahein to? Service discovery aur API Gateway.Agla topic: Service discovery aur API Gateway →

40. Service discovery aur API Gateway

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein order-service ne RestClient se product-service ko call kiya, par URL http://localhost:8082 hardcode tha. Production mein ye chal nahi sakta. Kyun? Aur mobile app 5 alag services ke URL kaise yaad rakhe? Do naye components chahiye: service registry aur API Gateway.
📖 Notes

Problem: hardcoded URLs

Analogy: dost ka phone number yaad rakhne ki jagah contact list mein naam se dhundho. Number badla to contact list update ho jaati hai, tumhe naam hi yaad rakhna hai.

  • Product-service ke 3 instances hain: kis IP par bhejun?
  • Cloud / Kubernetes mein container restart hote hi IP badal jaata hai.
  • Load badha, 2 naye instance aaye: config file kaun update karega?
  • Ek instance mar gaya: usko traffic bhejna band kaun karega?

Solution: service registry (Eureka)

  1. Eureka Server chalta hai (registry, port 8761).
  2. Har service start hote hi apna naam + host + port register karti hai.
  3. Har ~30 sec heartbeat bhejti hai; heartbeat band to registry se hata di jaati hai.
  4. Caller registry ki copy cache karta hai aur product-service naam ko live instances ki list mein badalta hai.
  5. LoadBalancer list mein se ek instance chunta hai (round-robin).

Eureka Server banana

<!-- discovery-server/pom.xml -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-netflix-eureka-server</artifactId>
</dependency>

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableEurekaServer
public class DiscoveryServerApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(DiscoveryServerApplication.class, args); }
}

# application.yml
server.port: 8761
eureka:
  client:
    register-with-eureka: false   # server khud ko register na kare
    fetch-registry: false

Eureka Client: har service mein

Sirf dependency aur naam. @EnableEurekaClient / @EnableDiscoveryClient ab zaroori nahi, classpath par starter hai to auto-register.

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-netflix-eureka-client</artifactId>
</dependency>

spring.application.name: product-service      # yahi naam registry mein dikhega
server.port: 0                                 # random port, kai instances ek machine par
eureka.client.service-url.defaultZone: http://localhost:8761/eureka/
eureka.instance.instance-id: ${spring.application.name}:${random.value}

Client-side load balancing: @LoadBalanced

Spring Cloud LoadBalancer (purane Netflix Ribbon ki jagah) caller ke andar hi instance chunta hai. Builder par @LoadBalanced lagao aur URL mein host ki jagah service ka naam likho. Feign client (@FeignClient(name=...)) aur gateway ke lb:// routes ise apne aap use karte hain.

@Bean
@LoadBalanced
RestClient.Builder loadBalancedBuilder() { return RestClient.builder(); }

ProductDto p = loadBalancedBuilder.build().get()
        .uri("http://product-service/products/{id}", id)   // naam! IP nahi
        .retrieve().body(ProductDto.class);
Dhyan doKubernetes par Eureka aksar nahi lagate: K8s Service ka DNS naam (http://product-service:8080) aur kube-proxy hi discovery + load balancing kar dete hain (server-side). Eureka tab kaam ka hai jab VM / bare-metal / Docker Compose par ho.

Problem 2: client ko 5 URL kyun pata hon?

Mobile app ko user-service:8081, order-service:8083... sab pata hon? Har service mein alag JWT check, alag CORS, alag rate limit? Internal services bahar expose? Galat. Chahiye ek main gate: API Gateway.

SochoUpar ShopKart architecture figure mein dekho: client sirf gateway ko jaanta hai.

Spring Cloud Gateway

Gateway khud ek Spring Boot app hai (reactive, Netty par; ab ek Server MVC variant bhi hai). Teen shabd yaad karo: Route (kahan bhejna), Predicate (kis request ke liye), Filter (raste mein kya badalna).

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-gateway</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-netflix-eureka-client</artifactId>
</dependency>

# api-gateway application.yml
server.port: 8080
spring:
  application.name: api-gateway
  cloud:
    gateway:
      routes:
        - id: product-service
          uri: lb://product-service          # lb = Eureka + LoadBalancer
          predicates:
            - Path=/api/products/**
          filters:
            - StripPrefix=1                  # /api/products/7 -> /products/7
        - id: order-service
          uri: lb://order-service
          predicates:
            - Path=/api/orders/**
            - Method=GET,POST
          filters:
            - StripPrefix=1
            - AddRequestHeader=X-Source, gateway
Dhyan doSpring Cloud 2025.0+ mein properties spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.routes ke neeche shift hui hain aur starter ka naam spring-cloud-starter-gateway-server-webflux hai. 2023.x/2024.x mein upar wala syntax hi sahi hai.

Java DSL se route

@Bean
RouteLocator routes(RouteLocatorBuilder rb) {
    return rb.routes()
        .route("user-service", r -> r.path("/api/users/**")
                .filters(f -> f.stripPrefix(1)
                               .circuitBreaker(c -> c.setName("userCB").setFallbackUri("forward:/fallback/users")))
                .uri("lb://user-service"))
        .build();
}

Gateway ki zimmedariyan

KaamKaise
RoutingPath / Host / Header / Method predicates
AuthJWT validate (oauth2-resource-server) + TokenRelay filter
Rate limitingRequestRateLimiter filter + Redis (token bucket)
CORSspring.cloud.gateway.globalcors ek jagah
ResilienceCircuitBreaker, Retry filters
ObservabilityTracing yahin se shuru, access logs
Common galtiGateway mein business logic daal dena (order total calculate karna). Gateway sirf traffic cop hai. Aur gateway ko single point of failure mat banao: uske bhi 2+ instances chalao.

History: Netflix stack ka kya hua

Purana (Netflix OSS)Aaj (Spring Cloud 2023+)
Zuul 1 (gateway)Spring Cloud Gateway
Ribbon (client LB)Spring Cloud LoadBalancer
Hystrix (circuit breaker)Resilience4j
Sleuth (tracing)Micrometer Tracing
EurekaAbhi bhi supported
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Hardcoded URL fail: IP badalte hain, instances aate-jaate hain.
  • Eureka = phone book; service register + heartbeat; caller naam se dhundta hai.
  • @LoadBalanced + http://service-name ya gateway mein lb://service-name.
  • Gateway = single entry: routing, JWT, rate limit, CORS, circuit breaker.
  • Route = predicates + filters + uri.
  • Kubernetes par K8s Service DNS aksar Eureka ki jagah le leta hai.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q244

What is service discovery and what is Eureka? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Service discovery lets services find each other by logical name instead of hardcoded host:port, because instances start, stop and move dynamically.
  • Netflix Eureka (Spring Cloud Netflix) is a service registry: each service registers itself and sends heartbeats; clients fetch the registry and resolve product-service to a live instance.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Service discovery एक phone book की तरह है: service का नाम दो, उसका current address मिल जाता है।
  • Eureka server वो registry है जहाँ हर service start होते ही अपना नाम और address register करती है और heartbeat भेजती रहती है।
  • Instance बंद हुआ तो registry से हट जाता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Eureka Server: @EnableEurekaServer
  • Client: bas spring-cloud-starter-netflix-eureka-client + spring.application.name
  • Heartbeat ~30s; heartbeat band to instance evict
  • Kubernetes mein aksar K8s Service DNS hi discovery ka kaam karta hai
Important 85 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q241)★ Important listAgla important (Q246) → ★
Q245

What is client-side load balancing and how does @LoadBalanced work?

Main Definition

  • In client-side load balancing the caller itself picks one instance from the registry list (default round-robin) for each request.
  • Spring Cloud LoadBalancer (replacement of Netflix Ribbon) does this: annotate a RestClient.Builder / WebClient.Builder / RestTemplate bean with @LoadBalanced and use http://service-name URLs; Feign clients and gateway lb:// routes use it automatically.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Client-side load balancing में caller खुद तय करता है कि किस instance पर request भेजे, बारी-बारी से (round-robin)।
  • @LoadBalanced लगाने से URL में service का नाम लिखो, Spring Cloud LoadBalancer उसे असली instance address में बदल देता है।
  • Ribbon पुराना था, अब Spring Cloud LoadBalancer है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Bean @LoadBalanced
RestClient.Builder lbRestClientBuilder() { return RestClient.builder(); }

// use
restClientBuilder.build().get()
    .uri("http://product-service/products/{id}", id)   // naam, host:port nahi
    .retrieve().body(Product.class);
Q246

What is an API Gateway and what does it do? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • An API Gateway is the single entry point for all clients.
  • It routes each request to the right service and handles cross-cutting concerns in one place: authentication/JWT validation, rate limiting, CORS, request/response rewriting, retries, circuit breaking, logging/tracing.
  • In Spring the standard choice is Spring Cloud Gateway (Zuul 1 is retired).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • API Gateway building का main gate है: हर client यहीं से अंदर आता है और gateway उसे सही service तक भेजता है।
  • Login check, rate limit, CORS जैसे common काम एक ही जगह हो जाते हैं, हर service में दोहराने नहीं पड़ते।
  • Spring में इसके लिए Spring Cloud Gateway use होता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Routing (path / host / header predicates)
  • Auth: JWT token check
  • Rate limiting (Redis RequestRateLimiter)
  • CORS, header add/remove, path rewrite
  • Circuit breaker + fallback, retry
  • Client ko internal services ka pata nahi chalta
Important 86 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q244)★ Important listAgla important (Q249) → ★
Q247

How do you configure routes, predicates and filters in Spring Cloud Gateway?

Main Definition

  • A route has an id, a destination uri (often lb://service-name), predicates that decide whether a request matches (Path, Method, Header, Host...) and filters that modify the request/response (StripPrefix, AddRequestHeader, RequestRateLimiter, CircuitBreaker, Retry).
  • Routes can be defined in application.yml or with a RouteLocator bean.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Route बताता है कि कौन सी request कहाँ जाएगी।
  • Predicate एक condition है, जैसे path /api/orders/ से शुरू हो।
  • Filter request या response में बदलाव करता है, जैसे prefix हटाना या header जोड़ना।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
spring:
  cloud:
    gateway:
      routes:
        - id: order-service
          uri: lb://order-service
          predicates:
            - Path=/api/orders/**
          filters:
            - StripPrefix=1          # /api/orders/5 -> /orders/5
Dhyan doNaye releases (2025.0+) mein property prefix spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.* ho gaya hai; purana spring.cloud.gateway.* deprecated warning ke saath chalta hai.
➡️ Agle topic mein: 20 services ka config kahan rakhein, aur jab product-service down ho to order-service gire nahi: Config Server aur Resilience4j.Agla topic: Config aur resilience →

41. Config aur resilience

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein gateway aur Eureka lagaye, ab services ek doosre ko naam se dhundh leti hain. Do nayi pareshaniyan bachi: (1) har service ka application.yml alag-alag jar mein bikhra hai, aur (2) jab koi service slow ya down ho to calling service bhi gir jaati hai. Pehle config, fir resilience.
📖 Notes

Problem: config bikhra hua

5 services x 3 environments (dev, test, prod) = 15 config files, jar ke andar. DB password badla to 5 jar rebuild + redeploy? Feature flag on karna hai to deploy? Galat. Config ko jar se bahar aur ek jagah rakho.

Spring Cloud Config Server

  1. Ek Git repo mein files: application.yml (common), order-service.yml, order-service-prod.yml.
  2. Config Server (port 8888) us repo ko padhta hai.
  3. Har service startup par GET /order-service/prod se apna config leti hai.
  4. Git = history, review, rollback free mein.
<!-- config-server -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-config-server</artifactId>
</dependency>

@SpringBootApplication
@EnableConfigServer
public class ConfigServerApplication { ... }

server.port: 8888
spring.cloud.config.server.git:
  uri: https://github.com/shopkart/config-repo
  default-label: main

<!-- har client service -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-config</artifactId>
</dependency>

spring:
  application.name: order-service
  profiles.active: prod
  config.import: "optional:configserver:http://localhost:8888"
Yaad rakhoBoot 2.4+ se bootstrap.yml ki zaroorat nahi, spring.config.import use karo. Kubernetes par aksar Config Server ki jagah ConfigMap (normal config) + Secret (passwords) env vars ya mounted files ke roop mein dete hain.

Runtime par config refresh

Ek-ek instance ko refresh bhejna mushkil hai: Spring Cloud Bus (Kafka/RabbitMQ) se /actuator/busrefresh ek baar call karo, sab instances refresh. @ConfigurationProperties beans bhi refresh par rebind hote hain.

@RestController
@RefreshScope                         // refresh par ye bean naye values ke saath dobara banega
class FeatureController {
    @Value("${feature.new-checkout:false}") boolean newCheckout;
    @GetMapping("/feature") boolean flag() { return newCheckout; }
}

# actuator endpoint expose karo, fir:
# POST http://order-service/actuator/refresh

Problem: ek slow service, poora system down

Payment gateway slow ho gaya (har call 30 sec). Order-service ke threads wahan latke, order-service ruki, gateway ruka, ab product browse karna bhi band. Jabki product ka payment se koi lena dena nahi tha. Ise cascading failure kehte hain.

Solution: fault tolerance patterns. Spring mein library: Resilience4j (Hystrix ka replacement).

Circuit breaker: ghar ka MCB

Ghar mein short circuit hua to MCB trip ho jaata hai, taaki aag na lage. Circuit breaker bhi failing service ko call karna kuch der ke liye band kar deta hai aur turant fallback deta hai. Thodi der baad dheere se check karta hai ki service theek hui ya nahi.

Teen states

StateBehaviourTransition
CLOSEDSab calls jaati hain; sliding window mein result gina jaata haiFailure rate >= 50% (ya slow call rate) → OPEN
OPENCalls bina bheje reject; fallback chalta haiwaitDurationInOpenState (e.g. 10s) baad → HALF_OPEN
HALF_OPENSirf N trial callsTrial pass → CLOSED; fail → wapas OPEN

Resilience4j setup + fallback code

<!-- Spring Cloud wala starter (andar resilience4j + AOP) -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.cloud</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-cloud-starter-circuitbreaker-resilience4j</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-aop</artifactId>
</dependency>

resilience4j:
  circuitbreaker:
    instances:
      product:
        sliding-window-size: 10
        minimum-number-of-calls: 5
        failure-rate-threshold: 50
        wait-duration-in-open-state: 10s
        permitted-number-of-calls-in-half-open-state: 3
  retry:
    instances:
      product:
        max-attempts: 3
        wait-duration: 500ms
  timelimiter:
    instances:
      product:
        timeout-duration: 2s

@Service
class CatalogFacade {
    private final ProductClient productClient;
    CatalogFacade(ProductClient productClient) { this.productClient = productClient; }

    @CircuitBreaker(name = "product", fallbackMethod = "fallback")
    @Retry(name = "product")
    public ProductDto getProduct(Long id) {
        return productClient.getProduct(id);          // remote call
    }

    // same return type + same params + last param Throwable
    private ProductDto fallback(Long id, Throwable ex) {
        log.warn("product-service unavailable: {}", ex.toString());
        return new ProductDto(id, "Temporarily unavailable", null);
    }
}
Common galtiYe annotations AOP proxy par chalte hain (Part 4 yaad karo): same class ke andar se call kiya to kuch nahi lagega. Aur fallback ka signature galat hua to NoSuchMethodException jaisa error milta hai.

Baaki resilience patterns

Default order (bahar se andar): Retry → CircuitBreaker → RateLimiter → TimeLimiter → Bulkhead → method. Matlab har retry attempt circuit breaker se guzarta hai. Detail: Q251

PatternKya karta haiExample
RetryTemporary failure par dobara try (backoff ke saath)Network glitch par 3 attempts
TimeLimiter / timeoutItne time se zyada wait nahi2s ke baad cancel
RateLimiterTime period mein max calls10 calls/second
BulkheadMax concurrent calls ek dependency koPayment ko max 20 threads
FallbackFail par default / cached jawabRecommendations nahi to 'Top sellers'

Monitor karo

Actuator ke saath /actuator/circuitbreakers aur /actuator/health (agar management.health.circuitbreakers.enabled=true) state dikhate hain, aur Micrometer metrics (resilience4j_circuitbreaker_state) Grafana tak jaate hain.

Dhyan doRetry sirf idempotent operations par. Payment POST par blind retry = customer ka paisa do baar kat sakta hai. Wahan idempotency key use karo (agla topic).
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Config jar se bahar: Config Server (Git) ya K8s ConfigMap/Secret.
  • spring.config.import=configserver:; refresh = @RefreshScope + /actuator/refresh (ya Bus).
  • Circuit breaker: CLOSED → OPEN → HALF_OPEN → CLOSED/OPEN.
  • Resilience4j: CircuitBreaker, Retry, TimeLimiter, RateLimiter, Bulkhead + fallback.
  • Fallback = same signature + Throwable; self-invocation par kaam nahi karta.
  • Retry sirf idempotent calls par.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q248

How do you manage configuration in microservices?

Main Definition

  • Externalize config out of the jar and keep it central and per-environment.
  • Options: Spring Cloud Config Server (serves properties from a Git repo; clients import it with spring.config.import=configserver:), Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets, or a vault for secrets.
  • Changes can be applied at runtime with @RefreshScope + /actuator/refresh or Spring Cloud Bus.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • 20 services के 3-3 environment का config हर jar में रखोगे तो change करना नामुमकिन है।
  • Config Server एक Git repo से सबको config देता है, या Kubernetes में ConfigMap और Secret use होते हैं।
  • Passwords हमेशा Secret या Vault में रखो, Git में plain text नहीं।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Config Server: @EnableConfigServer + Git repo
  • File naming: order-service-prod.yml
  • Refresh: @RefreshScope bean + POST /actuator/refresh
  • Sab instances ek saath: Spring Cloud Bus (/actuator/busrefresh)
# order-service application.yml
spring:
  application:
    name: order-service
  config:
    import: "optional:configserver:http://localhost:8888"
Q249

What is a circuit breaker and what are its states? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A circuit breaker wraps remote calls and stops calling a failing service for a while, failing fast (or returning a fallback) instead of waiting on timeouts.
  • States: CLOSED (calls pass, failures counted), OPEN (failure rate crossed the threshold; calls are rejected immediately for a wait duration), HALF_OPEN (a few trial calls allowed; success → CLOSED, failure → OPEN).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Circuit breaker घर के MCB जैसा है: बार-बार fault आए तो trip हो जाता है ताकि नुकसान न फैले।
  • CLOSED में calls जाती हैं, failure rate ज़्यादा हुआ तो OPEN होकर calls तुरंत reject होती हैं।
  • कुछ देर बाद HALF_OPEN में थोड़ी test calls जाती हैं; ठीक रहीं तो वापस CLOSED।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
StateKya hota haiKab badalta hai
CLOSEDCalls normal jaati hain, result countFailure rate >= threshold → OPEN
OPENCalls turant reject (CallNotPermittedException) / fallbackwaitDurationInOpenState ke baad → HALF_OPEN
HALF_OPENKuch trial calls allowedSuccess → CLOSED, fail → OPEN
Important 87 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q246)★ Important listAgla important (Q250) → ★
Q250

How do you implement a circuit breaker with fallback using Resilience4j? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Add spring-cloud-starter-circuitbreaker-resilience4j (or resilience4j-spring-boot3 + AOP), annotate the calling method with @CircuitBreaker(name = "product", fallbackMethod = "..."), and configure thresholds in application.yml.
  • The fallback method has the same return type and parameters plus a trailing Throwable.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Method पर @CircuitBreaker लगाओ और एक fallback method दो जो failure पर default जवाब लौटाए।
  • Threshold, window size और wait time application.yml में set होते हैं।
  • Fallback का signature same होना चाहिए, बस आख़िर में एक Throwable parameter।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@CircuitBreaker(name = "product", fallbackMethod = "productFallback")
public Product getProduct(Long id) {
    return productClient.get(id);
}
private Product productFallback(Long id, Throwable ex) {
    return new Product(id, "Unavailable", BigDecimal.ZERO);   // cached / default
}
Common galtiAnnotations Spring AOP proxy se chalte hain: same class ke andar se call kiya (self-invocation) to circuit breaker lagega hi nahi. Netflix Hystrix 2018 se maintenance mode mein hai, naya code Resilience4j mein.
Important 88 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q249)★ Important listAgla important (Q253) → ★
Q251

What are retry, rate limiter, bulkhead and time limiter in Resilience4j?

Main Definition

  • Retry re-attempts a failed call a few times with a wait/backoff (only for idempotent, transient failures).
  • RateLimiter limits how many calls are allowed per time period.
  • Bulkhead limits concurrent calls so one slow dependency cannot use up all threads.
  • TimeLimiter puts a time limit on async (CompletableFuture) calls.
  • They are combined with CircuitBreaker.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Retry: छोटी गड़बड़ी पर दोबारा कोशिश।
  • Rate limiter: एक समय में कितनी calls जाएँ, उसकी limit।
  • Bulkhead: जहाज़ के अलग-अलग compartment की तरह, एक slow service सारे threads न खा जाए।
  • TimeLimiter: async call पर time limit।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PatternProblemAnnotation
RetryTemporary network glitch@Retry
CircuitBreakerService baar baar fail@CircuitBreaker
RateLimiterZyada calls se overload@RateLimiter
BulkheadEk dependency saare threads kha jaaye@Bulkhead
TimeLimiterAsync call der tak latki@TimeLimiter
Dhyan doRetry sirf idempotent calls par (GET, ya idempotency key wala POST). Warna payment do baar kat sakta hai.
➡️ Agle topic mein: order + payment + stock teen alag databases mein hain. Ek @Transactional se kaam nahi chalega. To consistency kaise? Saga pattern.Agla topic: Data, transactions aur Saga →

42. Data, transactions aur Saga

4 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Part 5 mein ek @Transactional ne order save aur stock update dono ko ek saath commit ya rollback kar diya tha. Pichle topic mein humne seekha ki service fail ho to system kaise bache. Ab sabse mushkil sawaal: jab order, payment aur inventory teen alag services aur teen alag databases mein hain, to 'sab ya kuch nahi' kaise ho?
📖 Notes

Database per service

Microservices ka rule: har service ka apna database, aur koi doosri service uski tables directly nahi chhuti. Kyun? Agar order-service seedha payments table padhe, to payment team column rename kare aur order toot jaaye. Ye hidden coupling hai.

Data chahiye to API se maango ya events se apni copy rakho (jaise order-service product ka naam + price order line mein save kar leti hai).

Shared DBDatabase per service
Join aasanJoin nahi, API composition
Ek ACID transactionSaga + eventual consistency
Schema change sabko todta haiService apna schema khud badle
Ek DB technologyPolyglot: Postgres, Mongo, Redis

Problem: distributed transaction

Place order = order save (orders DB) + payment charge (payments DB) + stock kam (inventory DB). Payment ho gaya par stock nahi bacha. Ab? Ek @Transactional sirf ek database connection par kaam karta hai. Teen services ke teen DB par nahi.

2PC (two-phase commit) kyun nahi?

  • 2PC/XA: coordinator sabse 'prepare?' poochta hai, sab haan bolein to 'commit'.
  • Prepare se commit tak sab participants ke locks pakde rehte hain: slow aur throughput kam.
  • Coordinator ya ek participant down = sab latke (blocking).
  • Kafka, RabbitMQ, MongoDB, kai cloud DB XA support hi nahi karte.
  • Sab services ek saath up honi chahiye: microservices ka 'independent' hona khatam.

Solution: Saga pattern

Saga = local transactions ki ek chain. Har service apna local @Transactional karti hai aur event/reply bhejti hai jo agla step chalata hai. Koi step fail hua to pichhle steps ke compensating transactions chalte hain (undo nahi, ulta business action: refund, stock wapas, order cancel). Analogy: travel booking: flight book, hotel book, cab fail hua to hotel aur flight cancel karke refund.

ShopKart order saga (step by step)

  1. order-service: order PENDING save → OrderCreated event.
  2. payment-service: paisa kaata → PaymentCompleted (fail → PaymentFailed).
  3. inventory-service: stock reserve → StockReserved (khatam → StockFailed).
  4. order-service: StockReserved mila → order CONFIRMED.
  5. Agar StockFailed: payment-service refund kare (compensation) → order-service order CANCELLED.
StepActionCompensation
1 OrderCreate PENDINGMark CANCELLED
2 PaymentChargeRefund
3 InventoryReserve stockRelease stock

Choreography vs orchestration

Choreography: koi boss nahi, har service events sun kar react karti hai (upar wala flow). Orchestration: ek OrderSagaOrchestrator har service ko command bhejta hai (ChargePayment, ReserveStock) aur reply ke hisaab se aage badhta ya compensate karta hai.

ChoreographyOrchestration
ControlEvents se, distributedCentral orchestrator
Kab2-4 steps, simpleBade workflows, branching
Flow dekhnaKai services mein bikhraEk class / workflow mein
ToolsKafka / RabbitMQ eventsCustom state machine, Temporal, Camunda

Choreography ka code (payment-service)

@Component
class PaymentEventHandler {
    private final PaymentService payments;
    private final KafkaTemplate<String, Object> kafka;
    // constructor ...

    @KafkaListener(topics = "order-events", groupId = "payment-service")
    public void onOrderCreated(OrderCreated e) {
        try {
            payments.charge(e.orderId(), e.amount());               // local @Transactional
            kafka.send("payment-events", e.orderId().toString(), new PaymentCompleted(e.orderId()));
        } catch (PaymentDeclinedException ex) {
            kafka.send("payment-events", e.orderId().toString(), new PaymentFailed(e.orderId(), ex.getMessage()));
        }
    }

    @KafkaListener(topics = "inventory-events", groupId = "payment-service")
    public void onStockFailed(StockFailed e) {
        payments.refund(e.orderId());                               // compensating transaction
    }
}

Eventual consistency

Saga ke beech mein kuch second ke liye order PENDING hai aur paisa kat chuka hai. System thodi der inconsistent dikhta hai, par aakhir mein sab theek ho jaata hai: eventual consistency. UI mein ise dikhana padta hai: 'Order processing...' status, ya email baad mein.

SochoBank transfer bhi aisa hi hai: tumhare account se paisa turant kata, doosre bank mein thodi der baad aaya.

Dual-write problem aur Outbox pattern

Galat code: orderRepo.save(order); kafka.send(event);. DB commit hua aur Kafka send fail? Event kho gaya, payment kabhi nahi hoga. Ulta order: event gaya aur DB rollback? Bina order ke payment!

Transactional outbox: event ko bhi usi DB mein outbox table mein same transaction mein likho. Ek alag relay (scheduled poller, ya CDC tool jaise Debezium) outbox rows padhkar Kafka par bhejta hai aur sent mark karta hai.

@Transactional
public Order placeOrder(CreateOrder cmd) {
    Order order = orderRepo.save(Order.pending(cmd));
    outboxRepo.save(new OutboxEvent(UUID.randomUUID(), "OrderCreated",
            order.getId().toString(), json(order)));       // dono ek hi commit mein
    return order;
}

@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 1000)
@Transactional
public void relay() {
    for (OutboxEvent e : outboxRepo.findTop100BySentFalseOrderByCreatedAt()) {
        kafka.send("order-events", e.getAggregateId(), e.getPayload()).join();
        e.markSent();
    }
}

Idempotent consumer

Brokers at-least-once deliver karte hain: relay crash hua to same event dobara jaayega. Consumer ko duplicate safely handle karna chahiye, warna do baar charge.

@Transactional
@KafkaListener(topics = "order-events", groupId = "payment-service")
public void onOrderCreated(OrderCreated e) {
    if (processedRepo.existsById(e.eventId())) return;      // pehle dekh chuke
    payments.charge(e.orderId(), e.amount());
    processedRepo.save(new ProcessedEvent(e.eventId()));   // same TX mein mark
}
Yaad rakhoIdempotency ke tareeke: processed-event-id table, unique constraint (order_id par ek hi payment), ya natural idempotent operation (status = PAID set karna, balance -= x nahi).
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Database per service: data sirf API ya events se share.
  • 2PC avoid: locks, blocking, broker support nahi.
  • Saga = local transactions + compensating actions.
  • Choreography (events, chhota flow) vs orchestration (central, bada flow).
  • Outbox: business row + event row ek transaction mein; relay publish kare.
  • At-least-once delivery → consumer idempotent hona chahiye.

✅ Review questions (4): ab khud check karo

Q252

Why does each microservice have its own database?

Main Definition

  • Database per service keeps services loosely coupled: a service can change its schema, choose its own DB technology and scale independently, and no other service can read or write its tables directly.
  • Other services get the data only through its API or events.
  • The cost is that cross-service queries and transactions become harder.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • हर service का अपना database होता है ताकि कोई दूसरी service सीधे उसकी tables न छेड़े।
  • Schema बदलना हो या अलग DB (MongoDB, PostgreSQL) चुनना हो, सिर्फ़ उसी service पर असर होता है।
  • दूसरी service को data चाहिए तो API या event से माँगेगी।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Shared DB = hidden coupling, schema change sab tod deta hai
  • Polyglot persistence possible
  • Join nahi: API composition ya data copy (event se)
  • Har DB par sirf apni service ka access
Q253

How do you handle distributed transactions in microservices? What is the Saga pattern? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • A single ACID transaction across services' databases is avoided (2PC/XA blocks resources, needs all participants up, and most brokers/NoSQL do not support it).
  • Instead use the Saga pattern: a sequence of local transactions, one per service, each publishing an event or reply; if a step fails, earlier steps are undone by compensating transactions (e.g. refund payment, release stock).

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • कई services के databases पर एक साथ एक transaction नहीं चल सकता।
  • Saga में हर service अपना local transaction करती है और अगला step trigger करती है।
  • कोई step fail हुआ तो पिछले steps को compensating action से उल्टा किया जाता है, जैसे payment refund या stock वापस।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  1. Order service: order PENDING save + OrderCreated event
  2. Payment service: payment charge + PaymentCompleted (ya PaymentFailed)
  3. Inventory service: stock reserve + StockReserved (ya StockFailed)
  4. Order service: order CONFIRMED; kisi fail par compensate → refund, order CANCELLED
Important 89 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q250)★ Important listAgla important (Q256) → ★
Q254

Choreography vs orchestration saga?

Main Definition

  • In choreography there is no central controller: each service listens to events and publishes its own events, so the flow emerges from the reactions.
  • In orchestration a central orchestrator (e.g. an OrderSaga in order-service, or a tool like Temporal/Camunda) tells each participant what to do via commands and decides on compensation.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Choreography में कोई boss नहीं, हर service events सुनकर अपना काम करती है, जैसे dance में हर dancer music पर चलता है।
  • Orchestration में एक orchestrator हर service को बताता है कि अब क्या करना है।
  • Steps कम हों तो choreography, flow बड़ा और complex हो तो orchestration।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
PointChoreographyOrchestration
ControlDistributed, events seCentral orchestrator
CouplingServices ek doosre ke events jaanti hainParticipants sirf commands jaante hain
Flow samajhnaMushkil jab steps badheinEk jagah poora flow dikhta hai
Best for2-4 simple stepsBade, branching workflows
RiskCyclic events, 'kaun kya karta hai' confusionOrchestrator mein zyada logic
Q255

What is eventual consistency, the outbox pattern and an idempotent consumer?

Main Definition

  • Eventual consistency means services may be briefly out of sync but converge once all events are processed.
  • The transactional outbox pattern writes the business row and an event row in the same local transaction, and a relay (poller or CDC like Debezium) publishes outbox rows to the broker, avoiding the dual-write problem.
  • An idempotent consumer processes duplicates safely (e.g. by storing processed message ids), since brokers deliver at least once.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Eventual consistency: data थोड़ी देर के लिए अलग-अलग हो सकता है, पर आख़िर में सब match हो जाता है।
  • Outbox में order और event एक ही DB transaction में save होते हैं, फिर एक relay event को Kafka पर भेजता है, ताकि DB save हो और event miss हो जाए ऐसा न हो।
  • Message दो बार आ सकता है, इसलिए consumer idempotent होना चाहिए।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
@Transactional
public void placeOrder(Order o) {
    orderRepo.save(o);
    outboxRepo.save(new OutboxEvent("OrderCreated", o.getId(), toJson(o)));  // same TX
}
// relay: unsent outbox rows padho -> Kafka par bhejo -> sent mark karo
➡️ Agle topic mein: ek order 5 services se guzra aur kahin slow hua. Kahan? Logs, tracing, metrics, security aur deployment.Agla topic: Observability, security aur deployment →

43. Observability, security aur deployment

5 questions
🔗 Pichhle topic se jodo: Pichle topic mein saga se 5 services ek order ko milkar poora kar rahi hain. Customer bolta hai 'checkout 8 second le raha hai'. Kis service mein dhundho? Monolith mein ek log file thi. Ab 5 services x 3 instances = 15 log files. Aur in sab ko secure karke production tak kaise pahunchayein?
📖 Notes

Observability ke teen pillar

PillarSawaalTools
LogsKya hua? (error message, details)Logback JSON → ELK / EFK / Loki
MetricsKitna? (req/sec, latency, error %, JVM)Actuator + Micrometer → Prometheus → Grafana
TracesKahan? (kis service mein time gaya)Micrometer Tracing → Zipkin / Jaeger / Tempo

Centralized logging

Har service stdout par (12-factor) structured/JSON logs likhe. Ek agent (Filebeat, Fluent Bit, Promtail) unhe uthakar Elasticsearch/Loki mein bhejta hai, aur Kibana/Grafana mein sab services ke logs ek jagah search hote hain. Har line mein traceId ho to ek request ke saare logs ek query mein mil jaate hain.

# Boot 3.4+ built-in structured logging
logging.structured.format.console: ecs     # ya logstash / gelf

# Sample log line (Boot 3 default pattern mein traceId/spanId apne aap)
2026-10-14T10:15:02 INFO [order-service,6f1c2a9e4b7d8c01,a13b44f0e2c97d55] Placing order 981

Distributed tracing: request ka safar

Ek request = ek trace (traceId). Har hop / kaam = ek span (spanId, parent span ke saath). Gateway naya traceId banata hai, har outgoing HTTP call / Kafka message header (traceparent, W3C format) mein use aage bhejta hai. Zipkin UI mein waterfall dikhta hai: kaunsa span 7 second le raha hai.

Micrometer Tracing + Zipkin setup

Boot 3 mein Spring Cloud Sleuth hata diya gaya; ab Micrometer Tracing hai (Brave ya OpenTelemetry bridge).

<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
    <artifactId>micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.zipkin.reporter2</groupId>
    <artifactId>zipkin-reporter-brave</artifactId>
</dependency>

management:
  tracing.sampling.probability: 1.0        # dev 100%; prod mein 0.1 jaisa
  zipkin.tracing.endpoint: http://localhost:9411/api/v2/spans

# Zipkin chalao: docker run -d -p 9411:9411 openzipkin/zipkin
Common galtinew RestTemplate() / RestClient.create() se client banaya to trace headers propagate nahi honge. Hamesha Boot ka injected RestClient.Builder / WebClient.Builder use karo. Kafka ke liye spring.kafka.template.observation-enabled=true aur listener observation on karo.

Metrics aur health checks

  • Prometheus har 15s /actuator/prometheus scrape karta hai.
  • Grafana dashboard: request rate, p95 latency, error rate, JVM heap, circuit breaker state.
  • Alert: 'order-service 5xx > 2% for 5 min'.
  • Liveness fail = container restart; readiness fail = traffic band (restart nahi).
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
    <artifactId>micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
</dependency>

management:
  endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,prometheus,metrics
  endpoint.health:
    probes.enabled: true            # /actuator/health/liveness aur /readiness
    show-details: when-authorized
  metrics.tags.application: ${spring.application.name}

Security: JWT gateway par + har service par

Spring Security wala knowledge yahan bhi kaam aata hai, bas ab token ek authorization server (Keycloak, Okta, Auth0, Spring Authorization Server) deta hai. Flow: user login → JWT access token → har request Authorization: Bearer <token> ke saath gateway par.

Gateway token validate karta hai (signature, expiry) aur TokenRelay / header ke saath aage bhejta hai. Har service bhi OAuth2 Resource Server hai aur khud JWT verify karti hai, roles/scopes check karti hai (zero trust: andar ka network bhi bharosemand nahi).

  • Service-to-service (bina user ke): OAuth2 client credentials grant.
  • Transport: HTTPS; zyada strict ho to mTLS (service mesh jaise Istio/Linkerd).
  • Secrets: K8s Secret / Vault, Git mein kabhi nahi.
  • Internal services ko bahar expose mat karo, sirf gateway public.
<!-- gateway aur har service -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server</artifactId>
</dependency>

spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri: http://keycloak:8080/realms/shopkart

// order-service (servlet)
@Configuration
@EnableMethodSecurity
class SecurityConfig {
    @Bean
    SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        return http
            .csrf(csrf -> csrf.disable())                       // stateless API
            .sessionManagement(s -> s.sessionCreationPolicy(SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS))
            .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
                .requestMatchers("/actuator/health/**").permitAll()
                .requestMatchers(HttpMethod.POST, "/orders").hasAuthority("SCOPE_orders.write")
                .anyRequest().authenticated())
            .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()))
            .build();
    }
}

// gateway (reactive) mein: ServerHttpSecurity + .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(...))

Docker: har service ek image

Local par sab ek saath: docker compose up (postgres, kafka, zipkin, eureka, gateway, services). Boot 3.1+ ka spring-boot-docker-compose module dev mein compose file apne aap start kar deta hai.

# Dockerfile (simple)
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY target/order-service-1.0.jar app.jar
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "app.jar"]

# ya bina Dockerfile: Cloud Native Buildpacks
./mvnw spring-boot:build-image -Dspring-boot.build-image.imageName=shopkart/order-service:1.0

Kubernetes basics

Microservice zarooratSpring Cloud tareekaKubernetes tareeka
Discovery + LBEureka + LoadBalancerService (DNS + kube-proxy)
ConfigConfig ServerConfigMap / Secret
Health / restartActuatorProbes + auto restart
ScalingManually instancesreplicas + HorizontalPodAutoscaler
EdgeSpring Cloud GatewayIngress / Gateway API (gateway app bhi chala sakte ho)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: order-service }
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: order-service } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: order-service } }
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: order-service
          image: shopkart/order-service:1.0
          ports: [ { containerPort: 8080 } ]
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: { name: order-config }
            - secretRef:    { name: order-secrets }
          livenessProbe:  { httpGet: { path: /actuator/health/liveness,  port: 8080 } }
          readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /actuator/health/readiness, port: 8080 } }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: order-service }        # DNS: http://order-service
spec:
  selector: { app: order-service }
  ports: [ { port: 80, targetPort: 8080 } ]

12-factor app (short)

  • Ek codebase, kai deploys.
  • Dependencies explicit (pom.xml).
  • Config environment se (ConfigMap, env vars).
  • Backing services (DB, Kafka) attached resources, URL se badlo.
  • Build → release → run alag.
  • Stateless processes: session memory mein nahi, JWT/Redis mein.
  • Port binding (embedded Tomcat).
  • Scale out = aur instances.
  • Disposability: fast start, server.shutdown=graceful.
  • Dev/prod parity: same image.
  • Logs = stdout stream.
  • Admin tasks one-off (Flyway migration job).

Poore Part 6 ka safar ek line mein

Monolith todo (capability)→REST + events→Eureka + Gateway→Config + Resilience4j→Saga + Outbox→Tracing + Security + K8s
📌 Yaad rakho
  • Observability = logs + metrics + traces; traceId har log line mein.
  • Boot 3: Micrometer Tracing (Sleuth gaya) + Zipkin; Builder se client banao.
  • Actuator + Prometheus + Grafana; liveness = restart, readiness = traffic.
  • JWT: gateway par check + har service resource server (zero trust).
  • Docker image per service; K8s Deployment + Service + ConfigMap/Secret + probes.
  • 12-factor: config env mein, stateless, logs stdout.

✅ Review questions (5): ab khud check karo

Q256

What is distributed tracing and how does it work in Spring Boot 3? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Distributed tracing follows one request across many services.
  • A trace (one traceId) is made of spans (one spanId per unit of work, e.g. one HTTP call).
  • The ids travel in headers (W3C traceparent by default) and appear in every log line.
  • In Boot 3, Micrometer Tracing (replacement of Spring Cloud Sleuth) with the Brave or OpenTelemetry bridge reports spans to Zipkin or another backend.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Distributed tracing एक courier की tracking ID जैसा है: एक request कितनी services से गुज़री, हर जगह कितना time लगा, सब दिखता है।
  • पूरी request का एक traceId होता है और हर hop का अपना spanId।
  • Boot 3 में Micrometer Tracing यह काम करता है और data Zipkin में दिखता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
<dependency><groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId><artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId></dependency>
<dependency><groupId>io.micrometer</groupId><artifactId>micrometer-tracing-bridge-brave</artifactId></dependency>
<dependency><groupId>io.zipkin.reporter2</groupId><artifactId>zipkin-reporter-brave</artifactId></dependency>

management.tracing.sampling.probability: 1.0      # dev mein 100%, prod mein kam
management.zipkin.tracing.endpoint: http://localhost:9411/api/v2/spans
Dhyan doHeader propagation ke liye HTTP client Spring ke builder (RestClient.Builder, WebClient.Builder) se banao, new RestTemplate() se nahi, warna traceId aage nahi jaayega.
Important 90 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q253)★ Important listAgla important (Q258) → ★
Q257

How do you monitor microservices (logging, metrics, health checks)?

Main Definition

  • Three pillars of observability: logs shipped to a central store (ELK/EFK, Loki) with traceId in each line; metrics exposed by Spring Boot Actuator + Micrometer at /actuator/prometheus, scraped by Prometheus and shown in Grafana with alerts; traces in Zipkin/Jaeger/Tempo.
  • Health checks (/actuator/health, liveness/readiness groups) let the platform restart or stop routing to bad instances.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • 20 services के logs 20 machines पर ढूँढना असंभव है, इसलिए सारे logs एक जगह (ELK या Loki) भेजे जाते हैं।
  • Actuator और Micrometer metrics देते हैं, Prometheus उन्हें collect करता है और Grafana dashboard बनाता है।
  • Health endpoint से Kubernetes जानता है कि instance ठीक है या restart करना है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Logs: JSON logs + traceId, central store
  • Metrics: micrometer-registry-prometheus
  • Traces: Zipkin / Jaeger
  • Health: liveness vs readiness
management:
  endpoints.web.exposure.include: health,info,prometheus
  endpoint.health.probes.enabled: true   # /actuator/health/liveness, /readiness
Q258

How do you secure microservices? ★ Important

Main Definition

  • Use OAuth2/OIDC with JWT: an authorization server (Keycloak, Okta, Spring Authorization Server) issues tokens; the API Gateway validates the token and relays it (TokenRelay filter); each service is also an OAuth2 resource server that validates the JWT signature and checks scopes/roles itself (zero trust).
  • Add HTTPS/mTLS between services and keep secrets in a vault/K8s Secrets.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • User login authorization server पर करता है और उसे एक JWT token मिलता है।
  • Gateway token check करके request आगे भेजता है, और हर service भी खुद token verify करती है, क्योंकि अंदर का network भी पूरा भरोसेमंद नहीं है।
  • Passwords और keys Secret या Vault में रखो।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
<!-- har service -->
<dependency><groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId><artifactId>spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server</artifactId></dependency>

spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.issuer-uri: http://localhost:8080/realms/shop

@Bean SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
    return http.authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
            .requestMatchers("/actuator/health/**").permitAll()
            .anyRequest().authenticated())
        .oauth2ResourceServer(o -> o.jwt(Customizer.withDefaults()))
        .build();
}
Important 91 / 91
★ ← Pichhla important (Q256)★ Important listAb Must study →
Q259

How are microservices deployed with Docker and Kubernetes?

Main Definition

  • Each service is packaged as a container image (Dockerfile or ./mvnw spring-boot:build-image with Buildpacks).
  • Kubernetes runs the containers: a Deployment keeps N replicas (pods) running and does rolling updates, a Service gives a stable DNS name and load balances, ConfigMaps/Secrets inject config, probes use Actuator health, and the HorizontalPodAutoscaler scales on load.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • Docker हर service को एक image में pack करता है जिसमें Java, jar और सब कुछ होता है, तो 'मेरी machine पर चलता है' वाली problem ख़त्म।
  • Kubernetes इन containers को चलाता है: replicas रखता है, crash पर restart करता है, load पर scale करता है।
  • Kubernetes Service का DNS नाम discovery का काम भी कर देता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
K8s objectKaam
PodEk ya zyada container ka chalta hua instance
DeploymentReplicas + rolling update
ServiceStable naam + load balancing
ConfigMap / SecretConfig aur passwords
IngressBahar se traffic andar
HPACPU / metrics par auto scale
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
COPY target/order-service.jar app.jar
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-jar", "/app.jar"]
Q260

What is the 12-factor app methodology?

Main Definition

  • 12-factor is a set of practices for cloud-native services: one codebase per app, explicit dependencies, config in the environment, backing services as attached resources, separate build/release/run, stateless processes, port binding, scale out via processes, disposability (fast start, graceful shutdown), dev/prod parity, logs as event streams (stdout), and admin tasks as one-off processes.

Hindi mein samjho (आसान भाषा)

  • 12-factor cloud पर चलने वाली services के 12 नियम हैं।
  • सबसे ज़रूरी: config environment से आए, service stateless हो ताकि कोई भी instance request ले सके, और logs सीधे stdout पर जाएँ।
  • Spring Boot इनमें से ज़्यादातर नियम default में follow करता है।
Poora answer, code aur detail (click karke kholo)
  • Config env/ConfigMap se, code mein nahi
  • Stateless: session Redis/JWT mein, memory mein nahi
  • Logs stdout par, file mein nahi
  • Fast startup + graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful)
  • Dev/prod parity: same Docker image har jagah
➡️ Course yahin poora hota hai: Java basics se lekar Spring Boot, database aur ab microservices tak poora safar ho gaya. ShopKart ki 2-3 services (gateway + Eureka + Resilience4j + Zipkin ke saath) khud banake practice karo, aur questions dobara revise karo.

Last-minute must study

Revision ke time sirf yeh padho

Part 1: Spring Boot ki neev

Client-server → Q1
Client sends HTTP request, server returns response.
Client request भेजता है, server response देता है।
Status codes → Q3
2xx success, 4xx client error, 5xx server error.
2xx success, 4xx client की गलती, 5xx server की गलती।
Evolution → Q6
java.net → Servlet/Tomcat → Spring MVC → Spring Boot.
हर stage ने manual काम कम किया।
Servlet container → Q7
Tomcat listens on 8080, parses HTTP, manages threads and servlet objects.
Tomcat request सुनता है और servlets का पूरा ध्यान रखता है।
provided scope → Q8
Servlet API is needed to compile but Tomcat supplies it at runtime, so it is not packed in the WAR.
Compile के लिए चाहिए, WAR में नहीं जाती।
Servlet lifecycle → Q10
init() once, service() per request, destroy() once; object created lazily.
init एक बार, service हर request, destroy एक बार।
Spring vs Boot → Q12
Boot = Spring + starters + auto-config + embedded server.
Boot, Spring को आसान बनाता है, replace नहीं करता।
starter-web → Q14
Brings Spring MVC, Jackson and embedded Tomcat.
एक dependency में MVC, JSON और Tomcat।
@RestController → Q16
@Controller + @ResponseBody; return value becomes body.
Return value सीधे JSON बनता है।
Fat JAR vs WAR → Q18
Fat JAR has deps + Tomcat, runs with java -jar.
Fat JAR अकेले चल जाता है, WAR को external Tomcat चाहिए।
GAV → Q20
groupId, artifactId, version identify an artifact.
GAV project का पूरा address है।
Scopes (Maven) → Q21
compile, provided, runtime, test.
provided मतलब runtime पर server देगा।
Repositories → Q22
Local ~/.m2 → Central → private (Nexus).
पहले local, फिर Central से download।
Lifecycle → Q23
validate → compile → test → package → verify → install → deploy.
कोई phase चलाओ तो पहले वाले सब चलते हैं।

Part 2: Spring Core

Tight coupling → Q25
Class creates concrete deps with new.
new से बंधी class बदलना मुश्किल।
DI → Q26
Dependencies are given from outside; prefer constructor.
Dependency बाहर से मिलती है।
IoC vs DI → Q27
IoC is the principle, DI is the technique.
IoC क्या, DI कैसे।
Bean → Q29
An object created and managed by the IoC container.
Container जो object manage करे वो bean है।
@Component vs @Bean → Q31
Class-level scan vs method in @Configuration.
अपनी class पर @Component, third-party के लिए @Bean।
@Primary / @Qualifier → Q33
Default bean vs exact bean by name.
@Qualifier exact choice देता है।
Circular dependency → Q34
A needs B, B needs A; fix the design.
Common logic तीसरी class में निकालो।
Scopes (bean) → Q35
singleton = one per context, prototype = new each time.
Default singleton है।
Lifecycle (bean) → Q37
Instantiate → inject → @PostConstruct → use → @PreDestroy.
Injection के बाद @PostConstruct चलता है।
@SpringBootApplication → Q39
@SpringBootConfiguration + @EnableAutoConfiguration + @ComponentScan.
तीन annotations का combo।
Auto-config → Q40
Conditional beans based on classpath and missing beans.
तुम्हारा bean हो तो Boot पीछे हट जाता है।
properties vs yml → Q43
Both are supported; if both exist, .properties wins.
दोनों हों तो properties जीतती है।
Config + profiles → Q45
@Value for one key, @ConfigurationProperties for groups; profiles per env.
हर environment की अलग file, code वही।
Profiles → Q46
application-{profile} values override common application.properties.
Profile वाली file common को override करती है।
Activate profile → Q47
--spring.profiles.active=prod or SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE.
Command line या env variable से profile दो।

Bean सिर्फ़ उसी profile में बनता है।
Layers → Q49
Controller → Service → Repository → DB.
हर layer का अपना काम।

Part 3: Web layer (Spring MVC)

Front Controller → Q52
One DispatcherServlet receives all requests and delegates to controllers.
एक ही DispatcherServlet सारी requests लेता है।
MVC flow → Q53
Tomcat → DispatcherServlet → HandlerMapping → HandlerAdapter → Controller → Jackson / ViewResolver.
Mapping ढूंढता है, adapter चलाता है, result JSON या view बनता है।
@RestController → Q55
@Controller + @ResponseBody on every method.
हर method पर @ResponseBody वाला controller।
REST → Q57
Style: resource + URI + HTTP method + status code, stateless
REST एक style है: resource का URL, उस पर HTTP method, और सही status code।
Naming → Q60
Plural nouns, kebab-case, no verbs, filters in query

Idempotent → Q61
GET/PUT/DELETE idempotent; POST not
GET, PUT, DELETE बार-बार चलाओ तो result same, POST नहीं।
PUT vs PATCH → Q62
PUT replaces whole, PATCH changes given fields
PUT पूरा replace करता है, PATCH सिर्फ़ भेजी गई fields बदलता है।
Status codes → Q63
201+Location on POST, 204 on DELETE, 404, 409, 400
POST पर 201 और Location, DELETE पर 204, duplicate पर 409।
Versioning → Q64
Default /api/v1; bump only for breaking changes
Default /api/v1 रखो, version सिर्फ़ breaking change पर बदलो।
ResponseEntity → Q69
Control status, headers, body; created(uri)
ResponseEntity से status, header और body तीनों control होते हैं।
DTO → Q70
Never expose entities; records in/out
Entity सीधे मत भेजो, DTO में सिर्फ़ ज़रूरी fields रखो।
Validation → Q71
@Valid + jakarta constraints → 400
@Valid लगाओ, गलत data पर अपने आप 400 जाएगा।
Swagger → Q72
springdoc → /swagger-ui.html, /v3/api-docs
springdoc डालो, /swagger-ui.html पर docs मिल जाएंगे।

Classic blocking HTTP client (getForObject, postForEntity, exchange); maintenance mode, use RestClient for new code.
दूसरी API call करने का पुराना तरीका; नए code में RestClient।
Status codes → Q76
201 create, 200 read/update, 204 delete, 400 invalid, 404 missing, 409 duplicate, 500 server.
सही काम के लिए सही status code।
Global handler → Q81

Exceptions एक जगह पकड़ो, एक जैसा JSON भेजो।

@Valid failure throws MethodArgumentNotValidException; read getBindingResult().getFieldErrors().
@Valid fail होने पर field-wise errors निकालो।

Servlet level, before DispatcherServlet; does not know the controller.
Filter सबसे पहले चलता है, controller नहीं जानता।
Header timing → Q86
Set response headers before chain.doFilter(); after it the response may be committed.
Header chain.doFilter से पहले लगाओ।

Set 401/403 and return without calling the chain (filter) or return false (interceptor).
Chain मत बुलाओ, request वहीं रुक जाती है।

Reading the input stream in a filter consumes it; Jackson later fails.
Body stream एक बार ही पढ़ी जा सकती है।
OncePerRequestFilter → Q92

Cast नहीं, एक बार चलता है, skip भी आसान।

AOP terms → Q101
Aspect (code), Pointcut (where), Advice (when + what), JoinPoint (the call), Proxy (wrapper).

JDBC → Q120
Standard java.sql API; the driver gives the implementation.

PreparedStatement → Q124
? placeholders stop SQL injection and allow precompilation.
? placeholder से SQL injection रुकता है।
